| `options_privacy_lookup` | To check a game, the extension asks Valve's own store servers, without your cookies or account. | Privacy bullet. |
| `options_privacy_nothing_sent` | Nothing is sent to us or anyone else. No analytics. | Privacy bullet. |
| `options_privacy_backup` | Backups are files on your computer. They never pass through us. | Privacy bullet. |
| `options_unaffiliated` | Not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve Corporation. Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation. | Legal line; keep the names as they are. |
| `options_unaffiliated_short` | Not affiliated with Valve. Nothing leaves your browser except lookups to Valve's store. | Popup footer. |
| `options_all_settings` | All settings | Popup link to the full page. |
| `options_section_backup` | Backup | Section heading. |
| `options_backup_help` | Save your settings and game lists to a file, to restore them after reinstalling or in another browser. | Help under the heading. |
| `options_backup_download` | Download backup | Button that saves the file. |
| `options_backup_restore` | Restore from a backup | Button that opens the file picker. |
| `options_backup_summary_title` | Backup from `$date$` | Heading of the check shown before restoring. `date` is already formatted for the locale. |
| `options_backup_summary_settings` | Settings | First item of that check. |
| `options_backup_summary_allow_one` | 1 game you ignored | Plural, one. |
| `options_backup_summary_allow_other` | `$count$` games you ignored | Plural, other. |
| `options_backup_summary_history_one` | 1 checked game | Plural, one: a game the extension has already looked up. |
| `options_backup_summary_history_other` | `$count$` checked games | Plural, other. |
| `options_backup_restore_note` | Restoring replaces your settings and adds these games to your lists. Nothing already here is removed. | Under the check, before the buttons. |
| `options_backup_confirm` | Restore | Applies the backup. |
| `options_backup_cancel` | Cancel | Closes the check without changing anything. |

### `ext_`

| Key | English | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ext_name` | Tag Kit for Steam | Manifest `name` and the settings heading. The brand: keep "Tag Kit" as is and translate only "for". At most 75 characters (Chrome limit). |
| `ext_short_name` | Tag Kit | Manifest `short_name`, where space is tight. The brand, kept as is. At most 12 characters (Chrome recommendation). |
| `ext_description` | Tags Steam games: AI Generated Content Disclosure, Anti-Cheat (kernel level first), 3rd-party DRM, account and EULA, and PvP. | Manifest and userscript description. At most 132 characters; the English is 125. Name each tag as Steam's own store does in that language. |
| `ext_action_title` | Tag Kit for Steam settings | Toolbar button tooltip. Keep "Tag Kit for Steam" as in `ext_name`. |

### `userscript_`

| Key | English | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userscript_name` | AI Reporter for Steam | Userscript `@name`, kept from the first release. Lives in `userscript.json`, which only the userscript header reads. Keep as is. See [Renaming the userscript](../testing/userscript-install.mdx#renaming-the-userscript). |
| `userscript_menu_settings` | Settings | Entry in the script manager's menu. |
| `userscript_close` | Close | Closes the settings dialog. |
| `userscript_reload_note` | Changes apply on the next page load. | Shown when the manager cannot apply settings live. |

The backup check is the first place with plurals: `_one` and `_other` keys, chosen with `Intl.PluralRules`. A language with more categories adds its own suffixes.

## Contrast

WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for non-text. Grounds are the store's own, sampled on 2026-10-20: page `#1b2838`, React pages `#0f1924`, search row `#16202d` (20% black over the page). The store's row hover `#2a475e` is assumed, not sampled. Translucent tokens are composited over each ground before measuring. The banner wash runs from `#292258` to `#513dab` over the page; every banner pair is measured on the bright end, the worst case.

| Pair | Worst ground | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Limits that keep these true

- On the banner wash, text is `sar-banner-fg` only. `sar-color-text-muted` is 3.77:1 at the bright end, `sar-color-error` 4.21:1, and the store's own in-bubble link color `#c3c1c0` 4.49:1.
- The banner button's edge is white at 40%, the store's own, and 2.63:1 on our bright end. Its white label (8.06:1) identifies the button, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not ask 3:1 of the edge.
- `sar-color-text-subtle` only on page, row, panel, raised and sunken. On the store's row hover it is 3.32:1.
- `sar-accent-300` as link text only on solid grounds. On the store's row hover it is 4.45:1, so links there use `sar-accent-200`.
- The compact badge's surface stays at accent 900. A mid-tone flag color such as accent 700 would leave mid grey art with no boundary at 3:1 (surface 2.54, edge 1.11) and violet art at 2.01.
- None of this holds for a tag the person gave a color of their own (experimental): the tint, text, edge, surface and wash are mixed from the picked color, and nothing checks or adjusts them. The defaults keep every pair above; decision 49.
- The switch's off track is 1.55:1 against raised; its `sar-toggle-track-off-border` edge carries the 3:1.

### The mark on browser toolbars

The icon's `sar-accent-400` ink against toolbar grounds: Chrome light `#ffffff` 3.55, Chrome light toolbar `#f1f3f4` 3.19, Chrome dark `#202124` 4.53, Chrome dark toolbar `#3c3c3c` 3.11, Firefox dark `#2b2a33` 3.99, Firefox light `#f9f9fb` 3.38. Chrome light hover grounds fall below 3:1: `#e8eaed` 2.95 and `#dadce0` 2.59. The ink stays purple; re-sample the toolbar colors before submission.

```

`docs/design/decisions.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: Tag Kit for Steam UI design decisions (v1)
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-25
---

# Tag Kit for Steam UI design decisions (v1)

The choices behind `tokens.css`, `components.mdx` and `assets/icons/`, with the alternatives weighed, and what is still open. None of these is big enough for an ADR: the plan treats placement rules as tunable constants and copy changes as catalog edits. The published design system carries the same decisions.

## How the values were found

- Computed styles from live store pages on 2026-10-20, logged out, in English. At 1280px: the app page of 5072580, `/search/?term=ai`, a private wishlist URL and the home page. Then the app page of 1808500 for the notice bubbles, tag chips, corner flags and summary box (its tags block was not captured; see open question 16).
- The store's React pages ship their own scale on `:root` (spacing 4 to 32, radii 2, 4, 8, type 11 to 22, control heights 24, 36, 48), which became ours, so injected UI lines up with classic and React pages alike.
- Contrast uses the WCAG 2.x formula, compositing every translucent token over each sampled ground. Results are in the contrast section of `components.mdx`.
- Every page in `previews/` was rendered in Chrome: the compact badge over light, dark, striped, grey, sky and violet art, the list filter in both modes, and Spanish copy up to three times the English length.

## Decisions

1. **Match the store's look, carry no Valve branding.** Sampled neutrals, sizes and radii; "Motiva Sans" by name only. Rejected: using the store's brand assets (listings reject it, and it would look official); a fully foreign look (a seam on every page). The one Valve mark is the Steam glyph in the extension icon, wherever the icon is shown; no in-page component carries it (decision 40).
2. **Violet is the accent.** Rejected: teal (too close to the store's blue), amber or gold (collides with the store's own notices and reads as a warning), red or orange (reads as danger). Violet stays the default for every tag; decision 49 lets a person swap it per tag.
3. **Replaced by decision 36.**
4. **The compact badge sits top right on a solid surface.** The store's flags and live pill own the top-left and prices own the bottom edge. Rejected: a translucent or blurred surface (contrast depends on the art; blur is costly on carousels), bottom-left (where cover art puts the game's logo).
5. **Compact tiers are measured in script, not with container queries.** `container-type` would change how store containers size themselves.
6. **On search rows the full badge goes on the line under the title.** The title line clips.
7. **The banner sits above the purchase box, in a shadow root.** Rejected: the right column (326px wide, below the fold), under "About this game" (after the buying decision), a modal (what people asked to get away from), light DOM (store CSS styles bare `h2`, `p`, `button`).
8. **The banner attributes every word to the developer.** Nothing paraphrases or rates the notes.
9. **"Ignore this game", next to the store's own Ignore button.** The store's button sits just above. Ours only stops badges and the notice for one game in this extension and never calls the store's feature. The list is "Games you ignored" with "Stop ignoring".
10. **The list filter reads Show, Dim, Hide.** "Games that report AI use: Off" could read as turning the games off.
11. **Dim is opacity 0.4 only.** Rejected: grayscale (an effect layer per capsule, hundreds on a sale page).
12. **Settings are attributes on the root element; the list filter is pure CSS.** Rejected: toggling classes per host (one write per capsule, re-applied on every React re-render), inline styles (same cost, and they fight the store's).
13. **The banner collapses at 3 lines, without animation, and forgets the expanded state.**
14. **Replaced by decision 32.** The compact badge still takes the pointer only inside the capsule link.
15. **Settings pages are dark only, in a system font.** A light theme would need a second palette for no v1 gain.
16. **The 128px icon carries 16px of transparent padding** (Chrome Web Store guidance); 16, 32 and 48px are full bleed. The 16 and 32px renders are interim until hand-hinted reduced versions replace them.
17. **Tokens live on the store page's `:root`, all prefixed `sar-`.** Shadow roots inherit them.
18. **Every message is a catalog key** with a translator note. Labels that quote another label take it as a placeholder.
19. **Badges truncate; everything else wraps.** Rejected: shrinking type for long translations (unreadable at 11px), two-line badges (break the row rhythm, cover more art).
20. **Compact tiers depend on image size only,** so a capsule looks the same in every language.
21. **Logical properties and logical token names.** The switch thumb's `translateX` is the one physical value.
22. **A language picker on the full options page,** naming each language in itself through `Intl.DisplayNames`.
23. **Replaced by decision 41.**
24. **The prefix is `sar-`,** from the repo slug `steam-ai-reporter`, replacing the working name's `sfs-` before any code ships. Every class, attribute and custom property uses it.
25. **The banner is a store notice bubble in our hue.** Modeled on the DLC notice (`game_area_bubble`), sampled on 2026-10-20: a 135 degree wash at 80% from 10% to 100%, no border, radius or shadow, 8px 16px 12px padding, light Motiva type in `#d5d6d8`, the store's white-transparent button and underlined in-bubble links. Ours swaps the DLC plum for accent 800 to accent 600, keeps a 16px gap below (not 2px) so it never reads as part of the offer, sets the notes italic like the store's own disclosure section, and lifts the link color to `#d5d6d8` to stay AA. Its button matches the store's outlined buttons right below the banner: 11px regular, a 40% white edge, 2px 15px padding. It stays at least 24px tall for the target size, where the store's are 22px. The allow-listed note takes the DRM notice's geometry in neutral. Rejected: the first draft's card (a colored rule on one edge, 4px radius, drop shadow), which is generic callout chrome the store never uses; a neutral surface, which would pass as the store's own content; the DRM notice (one line, no room for notes or actions), the coming-soon and purchase boxes (rounded with shadows), the Early Access header (bordered), and the orange notice box (the store's warning tone, which judges).
26. **The full badge is a store tag chip in our hue.** Modeled on `.app_tag`: 19px tall, 7px padding, 2px radius, no border, a 20% tint. Text is accent 200 on accent 400 at 20%. It keeps the page font instead of the chips' Arial because it sits in Motiva rows. It carries no icon (decision 30); the violet hue and the wording set it apart from the store's blue tags, and it never sits in the store's tag row.
27. **The compact badge mirrors the store's corner flags.** Modeled on `.ds_flag`: 5px from the top, flush to the edge, 19px tall, square, solid. Ours sits at inline-end with accent 100 on accent 900, plus a 1px accent 400 edge and an outer ring. Rejected: a mid-tone flag color (accent 700), which left mid grey art with no boundary at 3:1 (surface 2.54, edge 1.11) and violet art at 2.01.
28. **Backups are a file the person keeps.** Download a JSON file; restore it after a check that shows its date and contents. Restore replaces settings and merges the game lists, so nothing on the current browser is lost. Full options page and userscript dialog only. Rejected: browser sync storage (stays within one browser family, needs a browser account, and its small quota cannot hold the lookup history); an account or server copy (the product sends nothing anywhere); a paste-in text box (clumsy for a large history); restoring the moment a file is picked (no chance to catch the wrong file). The check's Restore and Cancel row sits on the right with Restore first, like the store's own confirm dialogs.
29. **A summary-box row under Publisher, not a chip in the tag row.** (Superseded by decision 50: the row is gone.) The summary box at the top right is above the fold, while the banner usually is not. Steam's own reviews row there is a link that jumps to the reviews section, so a row whose violet chip jumps to our banner is a native pattern. Sampled on 2026-10-20: rows are flex label and value pairs in Arial 13/18, labels 35% wide, 11px uppercase. Rejected: first chip in the tag row (the row never wraps and Steam's own script hides tags that do not fit, so ours would overflow or force us to hide a store tag; it would also sit under "Popular user-defined tags" and read as a player tag); a floating bubble (covers content, against "never block"). The row holds only the badge label's chip, in the value column (decision 35).
30. **No icons in labels or the banner.** Badges, the tag section chips and the banner carry no spark or other icon. The store's own tags, corner flags and notice bubbles carry no icons either, and the violet hue plus the wording still mark our UI. Images under 180px wide get no compact badge, since that tier showed only the spark. Rejected: keeping the spark (dropped on 2026-10-20 in favor of labels without it); a short "AI" flag on small images (new copy, and a bare "AI" reads as a verdict rather than a report); squeezing the full label onto small images (it truncates to something like "AI use r...").
31. **The popup is flat and compact.** The toolbar popup shows its sections as flat groups split by a divider, captioned in small uppercase like the store's own section labels, with 4px rows and the store's 24px control height for the segmented control. An empty allow-list is left out there; the full page keeps its empty state. The full page keeps its cards, with 12px padding, 8px apart. Rejected: the same cards in the popup (padding and an empty card took most of its height); dropping the captions (the rows would lose their grouping).
32. **The badges' tooltip is a hover card built like the store's game hover popup.** One panel per page, sampled from `#global_hover` on 2026-10-21: `#344352`, the store's 20px shadow, 16px padding, 306px wide, square. It quotes the developer's notes verbatim, clamped to 6 lines, and names the AI service. Only the violet title marks it as ours. It sits 8px under the badge at z-index 2100, above the store's popup (1526), and it opens as a manual popover so it also clears the React hover layer, which sits in the browser's top layer, and a compact badge hangs it back over the capsule, away from where the store's popup opens. On the game's own page it drops the line that points to the store page (the summary row that once opened it is gone, decision 50). Rejected: the native `title` (cut at 200 characters, unstyled, delayed by the browser, and invisible to keyboard users); a custom tooltip without the store's surface (a seam next to the store's own popup); the store's arrow (ours sits right under its trigger); a violet accent edge (decision 30 removed edge chrome, and the violet title already marks it).
33. **The store's options arrow may cover the compact badge on hover.** On home capsules, `.ds_options` (z-index 15) appears in the badge's corner while the capsule is hovered and covers about 39px of its inline end. A store control wins over our label, the badge is clear at rest, and the hover card still opens from the uncovered part and by focus. Rejected: shifting the badge on hover (it jumps under the pointer) and a permanent wider inset (it reaches the store's top-left flags on small capsules).
34. **The store's game hover hides while the hover card is open.** On a search row the badge sits inside the row's link, so a pointer resting on it would open `#global_hover` beside the row and our card under the badge. While the card is open the root element carries `data-sar-hovercard="open"`, and one page rule sets `#global_hover` to `visibility: hidden`. Closing the card, `pagehide` and stopping remove the attribute, and the store's popup returns while the pointer stays on the row. It is the list filter's mechanism (decision 12): one attribute write and a CSS attribute selector, with no store node or script touched. The React hover layer gets no rule: it covers the capsule and takes the pointer, so the card closes after its grace, and its only hooks are a hashed class and `popover="manual"`, which our card shares. Rejected: removing or moving `#global_hover` (the store's script reuses that node on every row); `display: none` (it drops the popup's box while the store's script still places it); keeping the card off search rows (the notes would go unread there); leaving both open (two panels compete for one pointer).
35. **One label, "AI use reported", and a summary row with the chip alone.** (The summary row was replaced by decision 50.) Five surfaces named the verdict in four phrasings: "AI use disclosed" (full badge, hover card title), "AI disclosed" (compact badge), "Disclosed by the developer" (summary row chip, after an "AI use:" label) and "The developer discloses AI use" (banner heading). One catalog key, `badge_label`, now feeds all five; Spanish reads "Uso de IA declarado". The compact badge carries the full label: in the Arial fallback it grows from 71px to 87px, and on a 184px capsule it still leaves 33px beside a 64px store flag. The summary row drops its label column. Its chip starts 35% into the row, where Steam's labels end, so it shares the value edge of Developer and Publisher; the jump to the banner and the hover card stay. The developer stays named as the source: the hover card and the banner open with "In the developer's own words:". Rule 4 fixes the wording, so the choice has its own record: [ADR 0008 (one badge label)](../adr/0008-one-badge-label-ai-use-reported.mdx). Rejected: a short form for cover images (two labels again); "Developer reports AI use" (about 135px, which overlaps a store flag on a 184px capsule); a row label before the chip (it repeats the chip's first words).
36. **The mark is a Steam badge with a tag attached at its lower right** (decided 2026-10-24). The product tags Steam store pages with several kinds of fact: AI content disclosure, anti-cheat, third-party DRM, accounts and EULAs, and PvP. The old label tag with a spark named AI alone. The badge says where the tags live and the tag icon says what the product does, whatever the kind. The tag derives from Lucide's `tags` icon (ISC) and the badge from Simple Icons' Steam icon (CC0); the notices ship in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Replaces decision 3. Rejected: keeping the label tag and spark, which names AI alone.
37. **The ring is as thick as the tag's stroke.** Both measure 20 units on the 300 unit canvas, so ring and tag sit at one line weight. The tag leaves a transparent cut 8 units wide around itself where it crosses the ring. A transparent cut keeps the mark clean on light and dark toolbars.
38. **Four files, one ink each.** `mark.svg` is the master and paints in `currentColor`; a page can theme it. `mark-purple.svg` (`#8f73f3`, `sar-accent-400`) is the extension icon, the store listings and the README logo; the PNGs render from it. `mark-white.svg` and `mark-black.svg` serve grounds that cannot take purple. `mise run icons` generates the three color files from the master, and a test keeps them equal. The files carry no `role`: each consumer adds its own role and name.
39. **Components still carry no icons.** Decision 30 stands: badges, the tag section chips and the banner have no icon, and neither the mark nor the Steam glyph enters them. Whether chips for the other tag kinds get icons is a later design decision; it needs its own record before any component takes one.
40. **The Steam glyph appears wherever the extension icon is shown, and in no in-page component.** This replaces the older statement that no Valve mark appears anywhere. The extension icon includes an outlined Steam glyph, which is Valve's trademark, by decision on 2026-10-24. The Steam glyph appears in the extension icon and wherever the icon is shown: the README logo, the store listing images, the options and popup headers and the design previews. It appears in no in-page component: no chip, badge, banner or hover card. No Valve wordmark, image or font file ships. The "not affiliated with Valve" lines stay in the settings, the README and the listings. Open question 6 covers the listing policies.
41. **The name is Tag Kit for Steam** (short name Tag Kit; the Spanish name is Tag Kit para Steam), a working name until a store search ends. The product tags several kinds of fact, and "AI Reporter" named only one. Our name comes first and "for Steam" says only what it works with, so it does not read as an official Steam product, the pattern of decision 23. The name lives in the catalog keys `ext_name`, `ext_short_name` and `ext_action_title`, so changing it is a catalog edit. The repo slug `steam-ai-reporter` and the `sar-` prefix (decision 24) stay. Replaces decision 23. Rejected: keeping AI Reporter for Steam, which names AI alone.

42. **One compact banner per app page.** One entry per disclosed kind with Steam's line as its h2 (24px for one entry, 18px for several) and an outlined "Ignore for this tag" button. Only AI keeps the developer's own text. A foot link, "Ignore this game", ignores every tag. Steam's own notice boxes already carry the details.
43. **An ignored scope becomes a note with Undo.** The region is named by its h2 when it holds one entry and no note, else "Declared by the developer". Ignore and Undo buttons take their names from their own text and the heading or note (`aria-labelledby`).
44. **The summary row stays an AI summary.** It links to the banner when the banner holds the AI entry, else to the hover card. The hover card has no buttons. (Superseded by decision 50. The hover card still has no buttons.)
45. **The English app page draws AI from the live page at once.** Every other kind merges in when `GetItems` answers, and a failed request leaves the page as it is. When the live page and `GetItems` disagree on AI, `GetItems` wins and the disagreement is logged.
46. **Settings have one card per tag**, titled with Steam's line. The master switch hides the card's other controls. Writes patch what is stored at write time. The ignored list groups entries by scope, "All tags" first.
47. **PvP starts off.** It is common on rows and DLC, and the other six tags start on.
48. **Each tag's settings section closes, and remembers it.** Seven tag cards make the popup tall, and a person who sets up one tag rarely returns to it. A section is a native `details`: the browser gives the keyboard, the expanded state and the disclosure role, with no script or ARIA of ours. The summary keeps the tag's name and an "On" or "Off" cue for the master switch, which lives inside the card. Each section is remembered on its own, in a small separate `v2:ui` record shared by the popup, the page and the userscript dialog, and a section nobody toggled starts open. This differs from decision 13, where the banner forgets: the banner is a notice on a store page that should greet each visit, while settings are a place the person arranges once. Rejected: one open or closed state for all sections (hides what the person left open), remembering in settings (it is not a setting, and a backup would carry it), a button with `aria-expanded` and our own click handling (more code for the same result), animation (decision 13). Only the tag sections close; language, ignored games, backup and privacy are short and stay open.

49. **A tag can take a color of the person's choice (experimental).** One hex color per tag kind, typed into a plain text box on the full options page and in the userscript dialog, not in the toolbar popup (its sections are already tall, and the popup is for quick switches). It accepts `#rgb` and `#rrggbb`, with or without the `#`, in any case, shows the error as it is typed and stores lowercase `#rrggbb`. The setting is labelled "(experimental)" in every language. It colors every surface that carries the tag: the full badge, the compact badge, the chips of the Tag Kit section, the hover card entry's title and the banner's wash. Unset, a tag looks as it did, with the same violet and the same contrast. This lifts the AA and 3:1 guarantees of the Contrast section for the people who pick a color, and only for them. Nothing clamps, nudges or checks the color: the picked color is the one used, and the help text says that contrast is not checked. Rejected: clamping or auto-adjusting a pick to keep AA (it would change the color the person chose, and the right amount depends on art and pages we do not control); a warning that blocks a low-contrast pick (a refusal the person did not ask for, with no good threshold across the full badge's grounds); a native color picker (a browser dialog that differs everywhere and cannot be typed into or read back by a screen reader as a code); a free choice of every shade (seven tags times seven shades is a form nobody finishes). It extends decision 2 and the Color section's "Violet is ours": the hue is ours by default and the person's by choice, never ours to judge with, so Principle 1 (label the report, never judge it) still holds. It follows decision 12 and Principle 7: the color is one custom property per kind on the root element (`--sar-kind-color-<id>`), never a per-node style. The chips and entries carry `data-sar-kind`, one hand-listed rule per kind reads that kind's property, and the shades are `color-mix()` of it at fixed shares that put the violet scale's shape on any color (the color plays accent 400; the full badge text is 37% of it into white, the compact surface 22% into black, the wash stops 31% and 66% into black at 80%). Custom properties inherit into the banner's and the dialog's shadow roots, so a change applies live and a chip is not drawn again. A banner with one tag takes that tag's color for its wash, and a banner that lists several keeps the default violet. Text on the banner, the switches, buttons and focus rings keep their tokens. Forced colors still override the badges. The userscript dialog gets the fields through a form capability (`colors`) apart from the layout context, so it keeps the popup layout. Open question 18 asks for the real contrast of a few popular picks.
50. **A "Tag Kit tags for this product" section below the user-defined tags, instead of one AI chip under Publisher** (decided 2026-10-25). Supersedes decision 44 and amends decisions 29 and 35. The summary row held one AI chip. Next to a banner that lists three kinds it looked like a bug, since the other kinds were missing, and it sat off the page's tag grid: a violet chip in a box of label and value rows. The section goes right below Steam's "Popular user-defined tags for this product:" block, with a small muted heading and the chips shaped like that row (19px, 2px apart, wrapping). It lists one chip for every disclosed kind that is enabled, not ignored and has its badge switch on, in registry order, all of them and with no "+N" chip, so a game that declares only kernel anti-cheat gets a section too. With no such kind there is no section and no heading. It is a block of its own with its own heading and hue, so decision 29's reason against the tag row (it never wraps, Steam hides the tags that do not fit, a chip there reads as a player tag) does not apply. Each chip opens the hover card with its own kind and does nothing on click: the jump to the banner went with the row, because one link cannot stand for several kinds and a card over the click path was why the two never combined. The section follows `.popular_tags_ctn`; without it, the last `.dev_row`; without both, nothing. Rejected: keeping the row and adding chips to it (still off the tag grid, and it repeats the banner under Publisher); chips in the store's tag row (decision 29); a "+N" chip (the section wraps, and a hidden kind is a kind the player never sees); a chip click that jumps to the banner (the same chip already opens the card, which quotes the developer, and four chips would share one target).

## Ideas credited

Nothing was copied from prior-art extensions. Ideas that shaped this, to credit in the project README: a dismissible banner in the style of the store's DRM notice instead of a modal (requested in Augmented Steam issue 1913, shipped by Obvious Steam AI); dim or hide modes for lists (AI warning for Steam); falling back from hiding to highlighting where a list cannot hide (AI Generated Content Filter for Steam); a block of our own in the summary box (SteamDB's browser extension adds its rating row there).

## Open questions

1. **Wishlist anchor.** The wishlist is React and the sampled one was private; the full badge's exact anchor is unverified.
2. **Row hover color.** `#2a475e` is assumed. The badge passes on it (5.21:1), but confirm the live value.
3. **CSP for styles.** The banner and dialog use `adoptedStyleSheets`; badges rely on the content stylesheet or `GM_addStyle`. If the store's CSP blocks either, fall back to light DOM plus the badge reset.
4. **Line clamp with `pre-line` in Firefox.** Unchecked with notes that contain blank lines.
5. **Forced colors.** The rules are written but unchecked in Windows high contrast mode.
6. **"Steam" in the name, the description and the icon.** "Tag Kit for Steam" and `ext_description` use the trademark descriptively, and the extension icon holds the Steam glyph (decision 40), shown in the README logo, the store listing images and the settings headers too; check all of them against the listing policies.
7. **Language of the quoted notes.** The API does not say which language the developer wrote in, so the quote carries no `lang`.
8. **Dim distinctness.** 0.4 against the store's 0.3 is a small difference. If people confuse the two, profile a cheap second cue (a tinted outline on the host) on a sale page first.
9. **Banner next to the DLC bubble.** A game with DLC can carry a report too, so our banner may stack with the store's plum DLC bubble. Compare the two side by side on such a page.
10. **Compact badge and the store's flags.** Both share the 5px row, and the compact badge carries the full label (decision 35). On a 184px capsule the English label leaves 33px beside a 64px flag and the Spanish one 9px; a longer translation can reach a store flag at the other corner. Measure the widest flag and cap our label if needed.
11. **Banner button hover.** The 10% white hover wash is ours; the store's white-transparent hover state was not sampled.
12. **Restore: merge or replace.** Restore merges game lists by default. Decide whether to also offer "replace everything", for someone who wants this browser to match the backup exactly.
13. **History in backups.** Lookup history is the bulk of the file and refreshes itself anyway. Decide whether it stays in, becomes optional, and how large a file to accept.
14. **Tag section over background art.** The tag block sits on transparent layers: a column gradient (to the right, from 0 to 40% black) and the page's glow, over the game's background art when the page has some. Contrast is measured on the plain page color. On a page with custom art, measure the chips and the heading against the lightest pixel behind the block.
15. **Tag section in the narrow layout.** The store's responsive layout moves the summary box. Confirm the section still follows the tags block there.
16. **Anchor classes and heading style.** `.popular_tags_ctn` and `.dev_row` are the store's class names as known, and no captured fixture holds the summary box (the fixtures keep the description column only). Capture one page with user tags and one without, add them to `tests/fixtures/app-page/`, and sample the heading's size, color and spacing, which `tokens.css` approximates with the tag font and `sar-color-text-muted`. A game with two review rows and a publisher name that wraps makes the box taller; check that the section does not hang past the media's bottom edge.
17. **Hand-hinted 16px and 32px marks.** The interim renders are weak at 1x toolbar size, so hinted files are needed before store submission. Drop them in as `assets/icons/icon-16.svg` and `icon-32.svg`; `mise run icons` then renders from them. Fallback: a simplified 16px mark with ring and tag only, and cuts of at least 1px.
18. **Custom colors and contrast.** The color is used as given (decision 49). Measure the full badge, compact badge and banner for a few popular picks (pure red, yellow, white, black, a pastel) on the store grounds, and decide whether the help text should name the risk more plainly or whether the shares in `sar-kind-mix-*` need tuning.
19. **Banner with several tags.** The wash keeps the default violet while the color setting is experimental. A wash that blends the colors of its entries is the option to try later.

`docs/design/reference.css`:

```css
/*
 * Tag Kit for Steam reference component CSS (v1)
 *
 * Reference implementation of docs/design/components.mdx, rendered by docs/design/previews/ and
 * by the published design system. The UI step can lift these rules into src/core/ui/styles.css
 * as they are. Only tokens from tokens.css are used, and tokens.css loads first.
 *
 * Light-DOM components (badges, tag section, list filter) start from a reset, because store CSS
 * styles bare span, a, button and h2 in places. The banner lives in a shadow root in the real
 * build, so its rules work both inside a shadow root and in the light DOM.
 *
 * State lives in data-sar-* attributes, never in inline styles. Settings are attributes on the
 * root element (data-sar-filter, data-sar-badges), so changing a setting is one attribute write.
 *
 * i18n: no copy lives here (no content: strings). Labels truncate or wrap, so translations
 * about 40% longer than English fit. Directional spacing uses logical properties; the only
 * physical value left is the switch thumb's translate, marked below.
 */

/* Shared */

.sar-badge,
.sar-badge *,
.sar-compact,
.sar-compact *,
.sar-tag-section,
.sar-tag-section *,
.sar-hovercard,
.sar-hovercard * {
  all: unset;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

.sar-vh {
  position: absolute !important;
  width: 1px !important;
  height: 1px !important;
  margin: -1px !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  overflow: hidden !important;
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0) !important;
  white-space: nowrap !important;
  border: 0 !important;
}

/* Set by placements.ts on an image container that computed to position: static, after a
   batched read. Replaces an inline style write. */
[data-sar-anchor] {
  position: relative;
}

/* Badges turned off while the page is open: hide what exists without touching each node */
[data-sar-badges="off"] .sar-badge,
[data-sar-badges="off"] .sar-compact,
[data-sar-badges="off"] .sar-tag-section,
[data-sar-badges="off"] .sar-hovercard {
  display: none !important;
}

/* Full badge */

.sar-badge {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  block-size: var(--sar-badge-height);
  max-inline-size: var(--sar-badge-max-inline-size);
  min-inline-size: 0;
  padding-inline: var(--sar-badge-pad-inline);
  border-radius: var(--sar-badge-radius);
  background: var(--sar-badge-bg);
  color: var(--sar-badge-fg);
  font: var(--sar-badge-font);
  letter-spacing: normal;
  text-transform: none;
  white-space: nowrap;
  vertical-align: middle;
  flex: none;
  cursor: default;
}

/* The label is the part that gives way to a long translation */
.sar-badge-label,
.sar-compact-label {
  display: block;
  min-inline-size: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* Search rows: first item in the platform line, under the title */
.search_platforms > .sar-badge {
  margin-inline-end: var(--sar-space-2);
  flex-shrink: 1;
}

/* Compact badge */

.sar-compact {
  position: absolute;
  /* Mirrors the store's corner flags: 5px down, flush to the edge, square, solid */
  inset-block-start: var(--sar-compact-inset-block);
  inset-inline-end: var(--sar-compact-inset-inline);
  z-index: var(--sar-z-badge);
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  block-size: var(--sar-compact-height);
  max-inline-size: calc(100% - var(--sar-compact-inset-inline));
  padding-inline: var(--sar-compact-pad-inline);
  border: 1px solid var(--sar-compact-border);
  background: var(--sar-compact-bg);
  box-shadow: var(--sar-compact-shadow);
  color: var(--sar-compact-fg);
  font: var(--sar-compact-font);
  letter-spacing: normal;
  text-transform: none;
  white-space: nowrap;
  pointer-events: none; /* Default: clicks fall through to whatever is under the art */
}

/* Placed inside the capsule link: hovering it is hovering the link, so the hover card can
   open without stealing clicks or hover previews */
.sar-compact[data-sar-in-link="true"] {
  pointer-events: auto;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.sar-compact[data-sar-size="large"] {
  block-size: var(--sar-compact-height-lg);
  padding-inline: var(--sar-compact-pad-inline-lg);
  font: var(--sar-compact-font-lg);
}

/* Tag section: under the store's user-defined tags on the app page. The label is small and muted
   like the store's tags label; the chips are the full badge in the store's tag font, 2px apart,
   and wrap to more rows. */

.sar-tag-section {
  display: block;
  margin-block-start: var(--sar-space-2);
}

.sar-tag-section-label {
  display: block;
  margin-block-end: var(--sar-space-1);
  color: var(--sar-color-text-muted);
  font: var(--sar-summary-tag-font);
}

.sar-chips[data-sar-chips="full"] {
  display: inline-flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sar-space-0);
  max-inline-size: 100%;
  min-inline-size: 0;
  vertical-align: middle;
}

.sar-tag-section .sar-badge {
  font: var(--sar-summary-tag-font);
}

.sar-tag-section .sar-badge:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sar-focus-width) solid var(--sar-focus-color);
  outline-offset: var(--sar-focus-offset);
}

/* Hover card: the store's game hover popup in our type. One per page, fixed to the viewport;
   hover-card.ts sets its top and left. */

.sar-hovercard {
  position: fixed;
  z-index: var(--sar-z-hovercard);
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sar-hovercard-gap);
  box-sizing: border-box;
  inline-size: var(--sar-hovercard-inline-size);
  max-inline-size: calc(100vw - 2 * var(--sar-hovercard-offset));
  padding: var(--sar-hovercard-pad);
  background: var(--sar-hovercard-bg);
  box-shadow: var(--sar-hovercard-shadow);
  color: var(--sar-color-text);
  font: var(--sar-hovercard-meta-font);
  text-align: start;
  white-space: normal;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  pointer-events: auto;
  opacity: 1;
  transition: opacity var(--sar-duration-fast) var(--sar-ease);
}

@starting-style {
  .sar-hovercard {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}

/* The reset unsets the user agent's hidden rule */
.sar-hovercard[hidden],
.sar-hovercard [hidden] {
  display: none !important;
}

.sar-hovercard-title {
  display: block;
  color: var(--sar-badge-fg);
  font: var(--sar-hovercard-title-font);
}

.sar-hovercard-source,
.sar-hovercard-service,
.sar-hovercard-more {
  display: block;
  color: var(--sar-color-text-muted);
  font: var(--sar-hovercard-meta-font);
}

.sar-hovercard-notes {
  display: -webkit-box;
  overflow: hidden;
  color: var(--sar-color-text);
  font: var(--sar-hovercard-notes-font);
  white-space: pre-line;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  -webkit-line-clamp: var(--sar-hovercard-notes-lines);
  line-clamp: var(--sar-hovercard-notes-lines);
}

.sar-hovercard-service-name {
  color: var(--sar-color-text);
}

/* List filter
 *
 * The mode is one attribute on the root element (data-sar-filter="off|dim|hide"). Hosts carry
 * data-sar-state from the scanner and, where hiding would break a list,
 * data-sar-hideable="false". Allow-listed hosts carry data-sar-state="allowed", so they never
 * match. Opacity only, no filter, and no transition when the mode changes, so hundreds of
 * capsules flip in one style pass.
 */

[data-sar-filter="dim"] [data-sar-state="disclosed"],
[data-sar-filter="hide"] [data-sar-state="disclosed"][data-sar-hideable="false"] {
  opacity: var(--sar-dim-opacity) !important;
}

/* The fade back runs only on the one hovered host; leaving it snaps back */
[data-sar-filter="dim"] [data-sar-state="disclosed"]:is(:hover, :focus-within),
[data-sar-filter="hide"] [data-sar-state="disclosed"][data-sar-hideable="false"]:is(
    :hover,
    :focus-within
  ) {
  opacity: 1 !important;
  transition: opacity var(--sar-duration-fast) var(--sar-ease);
}

[data-sar-filter="hide"] [data-sar-state="disclosed"]:not([data-sar-hideable="false"]) {
  display: none !important;
}

/* App page banner
 *
 * Modeled on the store's own per-app notice bubbles (the DLC notice): a hue-coded 135 degree
 * wash with no border, no radius and no shadow, light Motiva type, the store's outlined button
 * and underlined in-bubble links. Our hue marks it as ours.
 */

.sar-banner {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: block;
  margin: 0 0 var(--sar-banner-margin-bottom);
  padding-block: var(--sar-banner-pad-block-start) var(--sar-banner-pad-block-end);
  padding-inline: var(--sar-banner-pad-inline);
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: var(--sar-banner-bg);
  box-shadow: none;
  color: var(--sar-banner-fg);
  font: var(--sar-banner-meta-font);
  text-align: start;
  overflow-wrap: break-word;
}

/* Title and button share a line in English. A longer translation wraps the title first, then
   moves the button under it, aligned to inline-end. */
.sar-banner-head {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  column-gap: var(--sar-banner-gap);

`docs/design/tokens.css`:

```css
/*
 * Tag Kit for Steam design tokens (v1)
 *
 * Every custom property the extension and userscript UI reads, generated from the published
 * design system (https://claude.ai/artifact/3xsXmaA5vjofhEWkL8nYsQ). The UI step of
 * docs/plans/steam-ai-reporter-v1.md (step 10) imports this file ahead of
 * src/core/ui/styles.css. Component rules reference only these tokens, never raw values.
 *
 * Sources: neutrals, type sizes, spacing and radii were sampled from store.steampowered.com on
 * 2026-10-20, so injected UI sits in the page without a seam. The violet accent is ours: it
 * stays clear of every hue the store already uses for meaning. See decisions.mdx.
 *
 * Contrast: every text pair a token's note names meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for
 * non-text) on the grounds it names. The full table is in components.mdx.
 *
 * Fonts: no font file is bundled. "Motiva Sans" is the store page's own, already loaded font,
 * referenced by name only.
 *
 * i18n: sizes leave room for translations about 40% longer than English. Spacing with a
 * direction is named for logical sides, so components use logical properties.
 */

:root {
  /* Grounds and surfaces */

  /* The store's classic page body, sampled 2026-10-20. A ground our injected UI sits on (badges,
     banner); we never paint it on store pages. */
  --sar-color-bg-page: #1b2838;
  /* The store's React page body (wishlist), sampled. A ground for the full badge; never painted by
     us. */
  --sar-color-bg-page-deep: #0f1924;
  /* A store search row (20% black over the page), sampled. The ground the full badge is checked on;
     never painted by us. */
  --sar-color-bg-row: #16202d;
  /* Segmented control, select and the backup summary backgrounds on extension pages. */
  --sar-color-bg-sunken: #0e141b;
  /* Options page and action popup background. */
  --sar-color-bg-panel: #171d25;
  /* Cards on the options page and popup. */
  --sar-color-bg-raised: #1f2630;
  /* Hover wash for rows on extension pages. Defined; no reference rule uses it yet. */
  --sar-color-bg-hover: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
  /* The store's game hover popup panel, sampled 2026-10-21. Hover card surface: white 10.14:1,
     sar-color-text 6.70:1, sar-color-text-muted 4.74:1, sar-accent-200 6.64:1. Not for subtle. */
  --sar-hovercard-bg: #344352;

  /* Text, edges and errors */

  /* Headings on extension pages: options and card titles, on panel and raised. */
  --sar-color-text-strong: #ffffff;
  /* Body copy on extension pages: 10.07:1 on raised, 12.24:1 on sunken. */
  --sar-color-text: #c6d4df;
  /* Meta lines on solid grounds and the allow-listed note (7.68:1 on its strip); 6.97:1 or more on
     page, row, panel and raised. Never on the banner wash (3.77:1 at its bright end). */

`docs/plans/steam-ai-reporter-v1.md`:

```md
---
title: AI Reporter for Steam v1 (MV3 extension + userscript)
status: active
issue: none
updated: 2026-10-20
---

# AI Reporter for Steam: MV3 extension and userscript from one core (v1)

**Ambiguities and the assumptions taken**

- Product name "AI Reporter for Steam" (`short_name` "AI Reporter"), slug `steam-ai-reporter`, Gecko ID `steam-ai-reporter@jdelavega.github.io`. The CSS and attribute prefix is `sar-` (internal, never shown to users). Wherever this plan writes `<slug>`, it means `steam-ai-reporter`.
- "Unknown" renders nothing, the same as "not disclosed". The only trace is a `data-sar-state` attribute, kept for debugging.
- The allow-list is per app ID only. Developer and publisher allow-lists are on the roadmap.
- The repo is MIT licensed. No code is copied from any prior-art project; ideas are credited in the README (see "Prior art and credits").
- Default TTLs: disclosed 7 days, not disclosed 12 hours, unknown `gated` or `missing` 6 hours. `error` and `rate-limited` are never persisted.
- Trunk-based: each step after step 1 lands as its own PR into `main`, from its own `<type>/<slug>` branch in its own worktree (a separate session per step where useful), squash-merged to give `main` one Conventional Commit per step. After a merge, the step's session is archived and its worktree and branch removed; any open branch the merge left behind is rebased onto `main`.
- steamcommunity.com is excluded. The wishlist is on the store host (`rq5-extension-constraints.md:33`), and spike spike 5 (surface map) confirmed that old community wishlist URLs redirect there (`rq6-verification-spikes.md`, spike 5 (surface map)).
- Formatting at 100 columns applies to every file the repo owns. Markdown and MDX are formatted for structure only; prose lines are not wrapped. Captured fixtures, the lockfile and `LICENSE` stay unformatted.

## Objective

Build a Chrome and Firefox MV3 extension and a Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey userscript, both driven by one framework-free TypeScript core. They mark every app-ID-bearing item on `store.steampowered.com` whose developer filled in Steam's AI content disclosure:

- a badge on capsules and rows
- a non-blocking banner on the app page that quotes the developer's text verbatim
- an opt-in dim or hide mode for lists
- a per-game allow-list for false flags

Detection calls `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` with `include_extra_details`, batched and in the page's language. A `?l=english` HTML parse is the fallback. There are three states (disclosed, not disclosed, unknown) and a local cache. There is no remote code, and nothing is sent anywhere except Valve's own endpoints.

## Current state

- The repo is `jrv97/steam-ai-reporter` on GitHub. `main` tracks `origin/main` and has two commits: `chore: init` (the wf docs scaffold, `AGENTS.md` and the research) and `chore: enforce lf line endings`.
  - `AGENTS.md` holds only a "working knowledge (docs/)" section: where plans, research, journal, drafts and ADRs live. ADRs are MADR in `docs/adr/`, which does not exist yet.
  - `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf` and `docs/journal/*.md merge=union`.
  - `docs/drafts/`, `docs/journal/` and `docs/plans/` exist with `.gitkeep`. `docs/TASKS.md` is untracked through `.git/info/exclude`. `.claude/settings.local.json` is ignored by the global Git ignore.
  - There is no `.gitignore`, no CI and no code.
- A Steam Web API key is available as the environment variable `STEAM_API_KEY`. v1 makes no keyed calls; the key is for development scripts only (see invariant 16).
- The recommendations this plan implements are at `docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure.md:69-76`. The three follow-ups that note asks for (`:78-81`) became the step 2 spikes, recorded in `rq6-verification-spikes.md` (spikes 1 to 7) and `rq7-library-study.md` (spike 8, library study).
- Detection evidence:
  - The request recipe and the "non-empty `content_survey_ai_notes`" rule: `rq2-data-surface.md:125-127`. The protobuf fields: `:99`.
  - First-hand verification: CORS from the store origin passes, 50 IDs came back in one call in about 1.3 s, the duplicate ID is confirmed, and a same-origin HTML fetch works (`rq2-data-surface.md:129-134`).
  - Batch ceiling (spike 1, batch ceiling): the limit is the URL length and has no fixed ID count. 250 IDs (6,886 characters) passed and 300 IDs (8,236 characters) failed. 30 back-to-back 50-ID calls all returned 200 and no 429 appeared. Error answers carry no CORS headers; JavaScript sees a `TypeError` and never a status or `Retry-After`.
  - Item states (spike 2, item states): the API ignores the age gate. Adult-only (339800), delisted and age-gated apps return `success: 1` with `extra_details` cookie-less. An invalid ID returns `success: 15`, `appid: 0` and no `extra_details`. Items come back in request order and duplicates are not merged. A 200 answer can still be a failure: `x-eresult: 8` with an empty `response` when `context` is missing.
  - Language (spike 2, item states): the set of disclosing apps is the same in every language, but the notes come back in the developer's translation where one exists.
  - CORS and runtime (rq6 spike 3 (CORS headers), spike 4 (extension fetch)): GetItems CORS is an allow-list of Valve origins, and `x-eresult` is exposed. A content script with no permissions reads GetItems in Chrome 155 and Firefox Nightly 160.
  - HTML fallback rules: `#game_area_content_descriptors` is duplicated (`rq2-data-surface.md:36`). Agecheck, login and home redirects mean unknown (`:62-68`). Spike 7 (HTML fallback) confirmed the `/login/` and `/` redirects and that a cookie-less `?l=english` fetch cannot change the store language. No `/agecheck/` redirect was reproducible from the spike's region, and the AI block came first on every sampled app with both blocks.
  - Still open: how stable the endpoint is (`rq2-data-surface.md:107`) and where the real rate limit lies (spike 1 (batch ceiling) never reached it).
- Extension constraints:
  - Content scripts can fetch same-origin and parse with `DOMParser` (`rq5-extension-constraints.md:23`).
  - Search infinite scroll and the React wishlist: `:89-98`. Surface map, app link shapes, the `<html lang>` table and the store CSP: rq6 spike 5 (surface map).
  - Rate-limit mitigations: `:105-107`.
  - Chrome limited-use and remote-code rules: `:127-128`.
  - AMO source submission (reviewer environment Node 24.14.0, npm 11.9.0) and `data_collection_permissions`: `:135-136`.
  - Userscript managers (spike 6, userscript managers): Tampermonkey 5.5 on Chrome and Firefox Nightly runs a plain `fetch` to GetItems without `@connect`, and the `GM.*` value calls, `GM_addStyle`, a plain `<style>`, `GM_addValueChangeListener` and the menu command all work. Violentmonkey was not tested.
  - Libraries and tooling: rq7 (spike 8, library study), summarized in "Tooling decisions" below.
- Release research: `docs/research/extension-release-pipeline.md`.
- Wording: show the developer's text, never say "uses AI" or "AI-free", and treat absence as neutral (`rq3-reliability.md:84`, `:94`). The January 2026 rewrite narrowed the scope (`rq1-policy.md:7`).
- Conventions adopted: a root `mise.toml` (this repo is one package), MADR ADRs in `.mdx`, and Conventional Commits. Git hooks run through mise, not prek (invariant 14).

## Architectural impact

The repo is greenfield and this change creates the invariants. Step 1 writes them into the root `AGENTS.md`, where every session working in the repo sees them before any code exists.

1. **Privacy.** App IDs leave the browser only for Valve hosts the user is on: `api.steampowered.com` GetItems and `store.steampowered.com` app pages. Every such request uses `credentials: "omit"`. No analytics, no third-party hosts, no seed lists.
2. **No remote code.** No `eval`, `new Function`, remote scripts or remote selector logic. Bundles are not minified. A build check enforces this.
3. **Permissions.** `storage` plus content-script matches on `https://store.steampowered.com/*`. No `host_permissions` and no background script. ADR 0003 records this content-script-only runtime, which spike 3 (CORS headers) and spike 4 (extension fetch) settled.
4. **Semantics.** Three verdict states. Unknown is never recorded or shown as not disclosed. The wording is "AI use reported", never "uses AI" or "AI-free". The developer text is rendered verbatim through `textContent`.
5. **Core purity.** `src/core` uses only DOM and web standards and never names `chrome`, `browser` or `GM`. `tsconfig.core.json` sets `"types": []` and never includes `gm.d.ts`; any such reference fails the type check.
6. **Originality and credit.** No code is copied from prior-art projects, and nothing from Augmented Steam (GPL-3.0) in any form. Ideas are credited in the README. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists the licenses of bundled dependencies only.
7. **One version source.** The `package.json` version feeds both manifests and the userscript header.
8. **Repo hygiene.** Repo text is ASCII with normal capitalization and no em dashes (non-English catalogs excepted). Branches are `<type>/<slug>`. Commits follow Conventional Commits 1.0.0 with the qoomon types (`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `perf`, `style`, `test`, `docs`, `build`, `ops`, `chore`; CI changes are `build`) and carry no trailers.
9. **i18n from day 1.** Every user-visible or logged message (UI copy, errors, warnings, success notices, empty states, ARIA labels, tooltips, the manifest name and description, the userscript `@name` and `@description`) lives in a message catalog, keyed and typed. English is the only shipped locale in v1. Code holds keys, never copy. Allowed literals are identifiers, selectors, URLs, storage keys, CSS class names, and detection constants such as Steam's own `AI Generated Content Disclosure` heading (matched, never displayed). The developer's disclosure text is data, shown verbatim and never translated. Lint rules and `check_i18n.py` enforce this.
10. **Strict static typing.** No `any`, explicit or implicit, anywhere. `unknown` is the only type for untrusted input, and it becomes a typed value only through a validation schema. No type assertions other than `as const`, no non-null assertions, no `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-nocheck`. Branded types for domain IDs (`AppId`), discriminated unions with exhaustive `never` checks, `readonly` by default. Enforced by the compiler flags and type-aware lint rules in step 4.
11. **SOLID and DRY.**
    - Single responsibility: one module, one reason to change (parser, throttle, cache, scanner, placement, renderer, composition root).
    - Open/closed: new surfaces are new `Placement` entries and new detection sources are new `Detector` links; the scanner and the chain are not edited.
    - Liskov: every port implementation passes the same shared contract test suite (memory, extension and GM stores; fake and real HTTP).
    - Interface segregation: small ports (`Http`, `KeyValueStore`, `Clock`, `Logger`, `SettingsSource`, `MessageCatalog`).
    - Dependency inversion: core depends only on ports; `content.ts` and the userscript `main.ts` are the only shipped composition roots (the dev-only `src/platform/dev/inject.ts` is never packaged).
    - DRY: before writing new code, check whether existing code can be refactored to cover the case. One build script for all targets, one manifest base with overlays, one catalog source, one placement engine, shared contract tests.
12. **Library check first.** Before building anything non-trivial, look for a library that does it and study it: size, types, maintenance, license, and whether it is needed at all. The outcome is recorded in the relevant ADR or PR description. Spike spike 8 (library study) did this for v1 (`rq7-library-study.md`).
13. **Efficiency: performance and memory.**
    - Network: one GetItems request per batch of up to 50 unseen app IDs; zero requests for cached verdicts.
    - CPU: after the initial pass, scan only `addedNodes` subtrees; batch DOM reads before writes in one `requestAnimationFrame`; dim and hide are CSS attribute selectors, not per-node style writes; no polling.
    - Memory: `WeakSet` and `WeakMap` keyed by elements; no per-node closures or listeners (one delegated listener per root); the in-memory verdict map is bounded (LRU, 2,000 entries); the observer disconnects on `pagehide`; daily storage sweep.
    - Budgets, enforced by `check_bundle.py` and tests: `content.js` at most 118 KB and the userscript at most 80 KB unminified; a 200-capsule fixture scan within a test budget; under 4 ms per mutation batch in a manual Chrome DevTools profile on a sale page (checklist).
14. **mise is the only toolchain manager and task runner.** Local development, Git hooks, CI and release pipelines all run `mise run <task>`. Every tool (Node, pnpm, Python, changie, web-ext, dprint, ruff, mypy, shellcheck, shfmt, actionlint, zizmor, gh) is pinned in `mise.toml`. JavaScript libraries that the build, lint and tests load from `node_modules` (esbuild, TypeScript, oxlint, valibot, vitest, happy-dom) are exact-pinned in `package.json` and the lockfile and installed by the mise-pinned pnpm (rq7 row 14). Non-trivial logic lives in `scripts/` as `.sh` (short glue) or `.py` (anything with logic), each exposed only through a mise task. `package.json` holds dependencies and no scripts. The pre-commit hook runs `mise run precommit` and the pre-push hook runs `mise run prepush`.
15. **Formatting from day 1.** Line width 100 for every file the repo owns: TypeScript, JSON, CSS, HTML, YAML, TOML, Python and shell. Markdown and MDX are formatted for structure only; prose is not wrapped. `precommit` formats the owned staged files and re-stages them; `prepush` and CI reject unformatted files. Excluded: `tests/fixtures/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `LICENSE`.
16. **Secrets.** `STEAM_API_KEY` is read only by development scripts (spikes, canary) and only from the environment. It is never committed, logged, written into fixtures or bundled; `check_bundle.py` fails if its value appears anywhere in `dist/` or `artifacts/`. Release secrets live in GitHub environments (step 15).

ADRs are warranted for five decisions. They are written in MADR `.mdx` in step 3:

- `0001` **Detection strategy**: GetItems as the primary source, queried in the page's language, a `?l=english` HTML fallback, no localized heading table, no seed lists, three states, and the TTL policy. The alternatives are real (per-app scraping, the localized DOM, SteamDB-derived lists, English-only detection with an extra banner call in the store language), and the choice rests on an undocumented endpoint.
- `0002` **Single codebase and tooling**: a core plus two thin platform adapters, built with esbuild driven by `scripts/build.py`, and the spike 8 (library study) outcomes: TypeScript 7, oxlint with type-aware rules, dprint, valibot, vitest with happy-dom, `@types/chrome`, a hand-written `gm.d.ts`, and actionlint plus zizmor. It also settles whether to pin `uv` and commit `mise.lock` (rq7 row 14).
- `0003` **Runtime topology**: content script only. Spike 3 (CORS headers) showed that GetItems CORS admits Valve origins only, and spike 4 (extension fetch) that a content script with no permissions reads GetItems in Chrome and Firefox. The runtime needs no background script and no `host_permissions`. The rejected alternative, a background relay for `api.steampowered.com`, would add a host permission and a background lifecycle; the record keeps it with the evidence that made it unnecessary.
- `0004` **i18n**: catalog format, runtime and locale resolution. Options considered: `chrome.i18n` with `_locales` only (cannot run in the userscript or in core, and cannot follow the Steam page language at runtime), i18next (about 40 KB and its own key conventions), ICU MessageFormat through `@formatjs/intl-messageformat` (rich plurals and selects, one more dependency), and the chosen default: Chrome `messages.json` as the single authored format (the extension needs it for `__MSG_*__` manifest strings, and Crowdin and Weblate read it natively) plus a dependency-free core runtime of about 60 lines: `$placeholder$` substitution, plurals through `_one` and `_other` key suffixes resolved with `Intl.PluralRules`, and an English fallback.
- `0005` **Release pipeline**: changie fragments, unpadded CalVer, the release app tag ruleset, nightly GitHub prereleases, prod promotion of the same artifacts to the stores on manual dispatch, and Chrome Web Store auth (OAuth refresh token or service account). Alternatives: manual store uploads (what most prior art does), rebuilding at prod time, and a signed beta channel (roadmap).

TTL numbers and placement rules are tunable constants and need no ADR. Copy changes are catalog edits.

### Tooling decisions

Decided by spike spike 8 (library study) on 2026-10-20 (`rq7-library-study.md`); ADR 0002 records them.

| Concern            | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Alternatives weighed in spike 8 (library study)                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Bundling           | esbuild 0.28 CLI, driven by `scripts/build.py`, one call per target; `--banner:js` only on the userscript call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | WXT plus vite-plugin-monkey; plain Vite (see below)                                                                                                          |
| Type check         | TypeScript 7 (`typescript@7.0.x`), `tsc --noEmit` on both configs; scripts test for a non-zero exit, not for a specific code; every tsconfig lists its `types`, since TypeScript 7 defaults them to `[]`                                                                                                                                                                 | TypeScript 6 `tsc` (about 2.3x slower, same diagnostics)                                                                                                     |
| Lint (TypeScript)  | oxlint 1.89 with type-aware rules (oxlint-tsgolint), every rule named in `.oxlintrc.json`, plus a custom `jsPlugins` rule `lint/restricted-syntax.mjs` for the literal-flow selectors                                                                                                                                                                                    | typescript-eslint `strictTypeChecked` and `stylisticTypeChecked` (caps `typescript` below 6.1; the fallback, see below); Biome (has no `no-unsafe-*` family) |
| Format             | dprint 0.64 with seven plugins (`npm:@dprint/typescript`, `npm:@dprint/json`, `npm:@dprint/markdown` with `textWrap: maintain`, `npm:@dprint/toml`, `npm:dprint-plugin-malva` for CSS, `npm:dprint-plugin-markup` for HTML, `npm:dprint-plugin-yaml`), line width 100, and `"markdown": { "associations": ["**/*.{md,mdx}"] }`, without which `.mdx` is silently skipped | Biome plus Prettier (Biome formats no Markdown, YAML or TOML; Prettier's MDX parser turned `2 * 3 * 4` into `2 _ 3 _ 4`)                                     |
| Runtime validation | valibot 1.5: `v.exactOptional` rather than `v.optional`, `v.readonly()` on every nested object, per-item validation of `store_items`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | zod 4 mini (37.3 KB unminified for the GetItems schema versus 10.8 KB); hand-written type guards (the fallback if the size budget fails)                     |
| Tests              | vitest 5 with happy-dom; jsdom per file only as a cross-check where a happy-dom divergence is suspected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | jsdom as the default (lacks `innerText`, observers, `popover`, `dialog`)                                                                                     |
| WebExtension types | `@types/chrome` 0.3.x, no polyfill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `chrome-types` (types storage values as `any`); `webextension-polyfill` (38 KB unminified, no release since 2024)                                            |
| Userscript types   | a hand-written `src/platform/userscript/gm.d.ts` for exactly the granted APIs, with non-generic signatures and `unknown` returns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `@violentmonkey/types`, `@types/tampermonkey` (neither compiles under the flags below; both make `GM.getValue<T>` an unchecked assertion)                    |
| Python scripts     | stdlib only; ruff (lint and format, line length 100); mypy `--strict`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | none                                                                                                                                                         |
| Shell scripts      | shellcheck and shfmt (`-i 2 -ci`; shfmt has no line width; 100 columns is a review rule)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | none                                                                                                                                                         |
| Workflows          | actionlint plus zizmor (`zizmor --offline` in `lint`; `prepush` needs no GitHub token)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | actionlint alone                                                                                                                                             |
| Package manager    | pnpm 12, installed by mise; `packageManager` in `package.json` matches, `pmOnFail: error` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `check_versions.py` fails when the two pins drift                                                                                                                                                                                                | none (user decision)                                                                                                                                         |

Bundler alternatives weighed:

- WXT plus vite-plugin-monkey. Two frameworks and two configs around one core, and a large transitive tree (Vite, Rollup, the WXT runtime, auto-import codegen) that AMO reviewers would have to rebuild. WXT's conventions leak into the core unless switched off, and its wins (HMR, manifest generation, a sources zip) are small for three entry points.
- Plain Vite plus vite-plugin-monkey. Content scripts must be IIFE, and Vite's library mode refuses multiple entries with the IIFE format; this still needs several build configs.
- esbuild (default). One package with no JavaScript dependencies beyond its platform binary. It builds several IIFE entries, gives byte-stable output for the same inputs and version, and `build.py` stays readable for reviewers. Costs: a hand-written userscript header and manifest overlays, both covered by checks, and no HMR. esbuild watch plus `web-ext run` reloads Firefox; Chrome is reloaded by hand.

TypeScript compiler flags (`tsconfig.json`, shared by the core config): `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `allowUnreachableCode: false`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `skipLibCheck: false`. TypeScript 7 defaults to `strict` and `"types": []`; the configs still set both explicitly. The extension config lists `"types": ["chrome"]`, and `gm.d.ts` is reached only from the configs that cover `src/platform/userscript/`.

Lint rules at `error` in `.oxlintrc.json`. oxlint has no presets; every rule is named under the `typescript` scope where typescript-eslint has it (for example `typescript/no-explicit-any`) and under the `eslint` scope otherwise:

- `no-explicit-any`; the `no-unsafe-*` family (`no-unsafe-assignment`, `no-unsafe-member-access`, `no-unsafe-call`, `no-unsafe-return`, `no-unsafe-argument`); `consistent-type-assertions` with `assertionStyle: "never"`; `no-non-null-assertion`; `ban-ts-comment` with `"ts-expect-error": true` as well, because its default allows a described `@ts-expect-error`.
- `strict-boolean-expressions`, `switch-exhaustiveness-check`, `explicit-module-boundary-types`, `prefer-readonly`, `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`.
- The oxlint equivalents of typescript-eslint's `strictTypeChecked` and `stylisticTypeChecked` rules. All exist except `no-unsafe-enum-assignment`, which the enum-free code does not need.
- oxlint has no `no-restricted-syntax`. `lint/restricted-syntax.mjs` (about 12 lines, loaded through `jsPlugins`, run by Node at lint time and never bundled) turns ESQuery selectors into reports. The selectors forbid string literals flowing into `textContent`, `innerText`, `title`, `placeholder`, `aria-*`, `alert`, `console.*`, `new Error` and `new SarError` (invariant 9). `JSON.parse` is wrapped once in `parseJson(text): unknown`; the same rule flags direct calls elsewhere. The file is lint configuration and lives in `lint/`; task logic lives in `scripts/` (invariant 14).

typescript-eslint stays the reference: where an oxlint rule behaves differently, its documentation is the spec. If the alpha JS plugin API proves flaky, the fallback is typescript-eslint with the documented alias pair (`typescript` as `npm:@typescript/typescript6`, `@typescript/native` as `npm:typescript@7`) keeps the type check on TypeScript 7.

AMO build-from-source instructions become: install mise (one documented command), then `mise install` and `mise run build`. mise pins Node 24.14.0 and pnpm; no corepack step is needed. Node stays at 24.14.0, the AMO reviewer environment (`rq5-extension-constraints.md:135-136`), although 24.22.0 is the latest 24.x release (rq7 row 14).

**Userscript header:**

- `@match https://store.steampowered.com/*`, `@noframes`, `@run-at document-idle`
- `@grant` for `GM.getValue`, `GM.setValue`, `GM.deleteValue`, `GM.listValues`, `GM_addStyle`, `GM.registerMenuCommand` and `GM_addValueChangeListener` (step 12 uses it for live settings)
- No `@connect`: Spike 6 (userscript managers) showed that a plain `fetch` to GetItems works without it in Tampermonkey on Chrome and Firefox Nightly. Violentmonkey was not tested; the manual checklist covers it (step 12)

## File operations

Nothing is deleted. `AGENTS.md` is extended (step 1); everything else is new. Layout:

```

Then `check_text.py` and `check_i18n.py` on the staged files. `precommit_format.sh` reads the staged list from `git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACMR`, not from the hook's `STAGED` variable, which splits paths with spaces.
     - `prepush`: `fmt-check` (rejects unformatted files), `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, `check`, and a branch-name check.
     - `ci`: everything `prepush` runs, plus `check-reproducible` and `lint-firefox`.

Task `change-new` wraps `changie new`. `changelog_gate.py` (CI job `changelog-fragment`) fails a PR that changes `src/` without a new `.changes/unreleased/*.yaml`, unless the PR carries the `no-changelog-fragment` label; it also checks that each new fragment names a known kind and has a body.

     - `src/locales/en/messages.json` in Chrome `messages.json` format. Keys are snake_case and grouped by prefix (`badge_`, `banner_`, `options_`, `error_`, `warn_`, `notice_`, `ext_`, `userscript_`). Every message has a `description` for translators.
     - `scripts/gen_i18n_keys.py` (run by `build` and `typecheck`) generates `src/core/i18n/keys.gen.ts`: a `MessageKey` union and per-key placeholder types; `t("missing_key")` or a wrong placeholder fails the type check. `build.py` copies catalogs to `_locales/<lang>/messages.json` for the extension and inlines them into the userscript bundle.
     - `t(key, params)`, `plural(baseKey, count, params)` and `createI18n(catalogs, locale)` live in core with no browser API. Locale resolution: the `locale` setting (default `auto`). On store pages `auto` follows the page's `<html lang>`, mapped through the table recorded in spike 5 (surface map) (for example `en` is `english`, `es-419` is `latam`, `pt-br` is `brazilian`, `zh-cn` is `schinese`); elsewhere it follows `navigator.language`. Anything without a catalog falls back to English. The same table, read in reverse, gives GetItems its `context.language` (step 5); one module in core owns it.
     - Errors are typed: `SarError` carries a `code` that is a `MessageKey` plus typed params, never prose. The logger takes keys; console output is catalog text with a `[sar]` prefix.
     - `scripts/check_i18n.py`: every locale has the same keys and placeholders as English, no catalog key is unused, every message has a `description`. The literal-flow rules live in the oxlint rule `lint/restricted-syntax.mjs`, which gives one AST check.
     - Commit `feat(core): add i18n catalogs, typed keys and the message runtime`.
