`docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq1-policy.md`:

```md
# RQ1: What does Steam's AI content disclosure policy require of developers?

Researched 2026-10-20. All fetches ran on that date unless noted. Wording of Valve text is quoted only in short fragments; everything else is paraphrase.

## Answer in short

- Valve announced the policy in the Steamworks news post "AI Content on Steam" (posted 2024-01-10 00:16 UTC, i.e. 2024-01-09 16:16 US Pacific): a new "AI disclosure" section in the Steamworks Content Survey, split into pre-generated and live-generated content. Much of the developer's disclosure is shown on the store page, under the heading "AI Generated Content Disclosure".
- The only documented rewrite since is in January 2026 (press coverage 2026-01-16 to 2026-01-20): the survey text now says it is about "content that ships with your game, and is consumed by players" and that efficiency gains from AI dev tools "[are] not the focus". Store page, community assets and marketing materials also count. No Valve blog post and no further revision turned up between February and 2026-10-20.
- Live-generated content adds three things: guardrails described in the survey, a Steam overlay path for players to report content that should have been blocked, and a hard ban on adult only sexual content made with live-generated AI ("at this time").
- Enforcement is review plus self-report: Valve compares survey answers with the build and store page before release and evaluates AI output like any other content, but the public docs state no penalty for lying or omitting, approved games are not re-reviewed on update, and some survey answers need Steam support to change after approval. The only stated sanction (app pulled from the store for missing guardrails) comes from one press quote of the login-gated form.

## Findings

### 1. What rules did Valve introduce, and have they changed since?

**The original announcement (January 2024).** The Steamworks development news post is titled "AI Content on Steam", gid 3862463747997849619, group (clan) ID 4145017. Steam's own event JSON endpoint gives posttime 1704845796, which is 2024-01-10 00:16:36 UTC (2024-01-09 16:16 Pacific) (source: https://store.steampowered.com/events/ajaxgetpartnerevent?clan_accountid=4145017&announcement_gid=3862463747997849619&l=english, fetched twice with consistent values). The same JSON gives an updatetime of 1705097438 (about 2024-01-12 22:10 UTC); the body may have been edited three days later, and what changed is unverified. Press dated it 2024-01-10 (https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/ai-content-reporting) and 2024-01-11 (https://dashfight.com/news/steam-adds-an-option-to-report-ai-content-4901). The canonical page https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/3862463747997849619 returned only its title to the fetcher; the body text above comes from the JSON endpoint.

What the 2024 post says, in order: Valve said it needed time to study "the fast-moving and legally murky space of AI technology" and was now changing how it handles AI games in order to release "the vast majority of games that use it" (source: ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above). The Content Survey gets "a new AI disclosure section" (same source). Developers describe their AI use in two categories, pre-generated and live-generated (definitions in sub-question 2). Valve uses the disclosure in pre-release review and will "include much of your disclosure on the Steam store page" (same source). Valve also launched a system for players to report illegal content in games with live-generated AI, reachable from the in-game overlay (same source). The one exception to the new openness is adult only sexual content made with live-generated AI (same source).

**The January 2026 rewrite.** No Steamworks news post announcing it turned up; it is an edit to the Steamworks Content Survey doc (and, per press, the in-app form). The exact date Valve made the edit is unverified. First press coverage and who flagged it:

- Game Developer, 2026-01-16, "Valve tweaks and clarifies AI disclosure rules for Steam" (source: https://gamedeveloper.com/business/valve-tweaks-and-clarifies-ai-disclosure-rules-for-steam).
- Video Games Chronicle, 2026-01-17, credits Simon Carless of GameDiscoverCo, who posted on LinkedIn (source: https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/valve-has-significantly-rewritten-steams-rules-for-how-developers-much-disclose-ai-use). PCGamesN also ran it 2026-01-17 (source: https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/new-gen-ai-disclosure-form).
- Outlook India 2026-01-18 (source: https://respawn.outlookindia.com/gaming/gaming-news/valve-clarifies-steam-ai-policy-focus-shifts-to-content-consumed); Dexerto and WNHub 2026-01-19 (sources: https://www.dexerto.com/gaming/steam-makes-major-change-to-ai-rules-for-games-3306274 and https://wnhub.io/news/stores-and-publishing/item-49836); Gigazine and GamingBible 2026-01-20 (sources: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260120-steam-updates-ai-disclosure-guidelines and https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platform/steam/steam-ai-changes-disclosure-rules-203740-20260120).
- Carless's framing, relayed by gigazine: Valve "significantly rewrote - but did NOT remove" the form (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260120-steam-updates-ai-disclosure-guidelines). Treat the disclosure duty as intact.

What the current Steamworks doc says (fetched twice on 2026-10-20): section 3 of the Content Survey, "Generative Artificial Intelligence Content", says the section is not about efficiency gains from AI-powered dev tools and "is concerned with the use of AI in creating content that ships with your game, and is consumed by players", with artwork, sound, narrative and localization as examples (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). The press quotes of the same sentences match (sources: https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/new-gen-ai-disclosure-form, https://www.gosugamers.net/entertainment/news/77861-steam-revises-ai-policy-while-keeping-generative-content-disclosure-intact).

What moved between 2024 and 2026:

- Scope narrowed from "any kind of content (art/code/sound/etc) created with the help of AI tools during development" (2024 post, ajaxgetpartnerevent URL) to content "that ships with your game and is consumed by players" (current doc). The word "code" no longer appears in the pre-generated example list in the doc text read; whether AI-written code that ships in the game still needs disclosing is unverified (one SEO blog claims Valve confirmed it still does; that blog was not opened).
- AI dev tools (code helpers, bug checkers, etc.) are explicitly not the focus (doc, above). Examples named in press: GitHub Copilot, automated bug-checking software, office productivity tools, and the Photoshop generative fill and ChatGPT questions raised by PC Gamer (source: https://respawn.outlookindia.com/gaming/gaming-news/valve-clarifies-steam-ai-policy-focus-shifts-to-content-consumed). The press supplied those examples.
- The form now covers AI content for the game, its store page, marketing materials and community assets, in a written explanation, plus a separate gameplay question (sources: https://www.dexerto.com/gaming/steam-makes-major-change-to-ai-rules-for-games-3306274, https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/new-gen-ai-disclosure-form). Kitguru quotes the gameplay question as "Do you use AI to live-generate content or code during gameplay?" (source: https://www.kitguru.net/desktop-pc/mustafa-mahmoud/steam-updates-its-gen-ai-disclosure-policies/). The form itself is behind the Steamworks login, and these are second-hand.
- Gamingbible says the form went from one broad question to three (source: https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platform/steam/steam-ai-changes-disclosure-rules-203740-20260120). Dexerto, game developer and PCGamesN describe two parts. Treat "three questions" as unverified.
- PCGamesN adds that the gameplay section now says players can report content they find inappropriate or copyright infringing (a paraphrase; no direct quote), where the 2024 post said "illegal" (source: https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/new-gen-ai-disclosure-form). Single source.

**Changes after January 2026.** None found. Targeted searches (standard and extended) for later Valve changes, new filters, or new store labels found only January 2026 coverage plus follow-on commentary (the conversation, 2026-02-11, says Steam still has no consumer search or filter for AI content; source: https://theconversation.com/are-video-game-developers-using-ai-players-want-to-know-but-the-rules-are-patchy-274850). The current doc carries no date stamps or changelog. An absence of found changes is no proof that none exist. No 2025 revision found either; the January 2026 coverage calls it the first revision since 2024 (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260120-steam-updates-ai-disclosure-guidelines).

**Store page wording.** The display heading is "AI Generated Content Disclosure" (named in the VGC January 2026 article, source: https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/valve-has-significantly-rewritten-steams-rules-for-how-developers-much-disclose-ai-use, and seen on the sample page, source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/Courage_and_Faith_Into_the_Dark_Woods/). On that sample page (one fetch, 2026-10-20) the section sits after "About This Game" and the features list and before "Mature Content Description" and "System Requirements". Its body is developer-written prose that itself uses the words pre-generated and live-generated (same source). The conversation describes the field as free text with no tag (source: https://theconversation.com/are-video-game-developers-using-ai-players-want-to-know-but-the-rules-are-patchy-274850). Valve's 2024 post only promises "much of" the disclosure. The shown text is a developer-supplied, Valve-selected subset; exactly what Valve trims is unverified. No change to the heading turned up in 2026.

### 2. Pre-generated vs live-generated, and extra obligations for live-generated

**Pre-generated.** Current doc: content that ships with the game, is consumed by players and was made with AI tools during development (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). The 2024 wording was "any kind of content (art/code/sound/etc) created with the help of AI tools during development" (source: ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above). Obligations: under the Steam distribution agreement the developer promises the game will not include illegal or infringing content and will be consistent with its marketing materials; Valve evaluates the AI output in prerelease review "the same way" as non-AI content (sources: ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above; https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). The full distribution agreement is not public; its exact clauses are unverified (https://partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect only mentions it and is access-restricted).

**Live-generated.** "any kind of content created with the help of AI tools while the game is running" (both the 2024 post and the current doc; sources above). It follows the same rules as pre-generated plus these:

- Guardrails: in the Content Survey the developer must say what guardrails stop the AI generating illegal content (sources: ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above; https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey).
- In-game player reporting: Valve built a Steam system for players to report illegal content in games with live-generated AI, submitted from the in-game overlay when they meet content that guardrails should have caught (source: ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above). This is a Valve-side system that the developer does not build; Outlook India wording ("developers must support a Steam overlay") is a loose paraphrase (source: https://respawn.outlookindia.com/gaming/gaming-news/valve-clarifies-steam-ai-policy-focus-shifts-to-content-consumed). The current Steamworks doc page does not mention the overlay or reporting at all (a keyword check found no "overlay" in body text). Valve has not said publicly what it does with reports (source: https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/ai-content-reporting).
- Adults-only restriction: adult only sexual content made with live-generated AI is not accepted. 2024: "we are unable to release that type of content right now" and Valve would "revisit this decision when necessary" (ajaxgetpartnerevent URL above). Current doc FAQ: Valve does not want to ship it "at this time", citing substantial legal and customer risk (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). Pre-generated adult content is not covered by this ban.
- Paid AI services: if the game calls a paid live-generated AI service with per-call cost, the developer must manage player access and take payment through a Steam-supported method: price it into the game, microtransactions, a subscription, or a single DLC (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). When this FAQ entry was added is unverified.
- Stated sanction for guardrails (single source): PCGamesN quotes the in-app form as saying it is the developer's responsibility to implement guard rails that keep users from exposure to inappropriate and illegal content, and "Failure to do so will result in your app being pulled from the store" (source: https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam/new-gen-ai-disclosure-form). This could not be confirmed in the public Steamworks doc (no match for "pulled from the store") or in a second independent outlet; letsdatascience repeats a softer version that looks derived (source: https://letsdatascience.com/news/valve-updates-steam-ai-disclosure-for-player-consumed-conten-15e5014d). Tag as unverified beyond PCGamesN.

### 3. How it is enforced

**Survey and review.** Every app must complete the Content Survey (general content, mature content, generative AI content) before the store page and build are submitted for review; after submission Valve's team "will compare the answers relative to the content in your build and on your store page" (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). The review pipeline doc (store page, build, adult content, trading cards) mentions no AI check of its own and states no penalties (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/review_process). Survey answers do not excuse content: products "must adhere to the content rules, regardless of whether it is disclosed in these surveys" (doc FAQ, same source as the survey).

**Lying or failing to disclose.** The public Steamworks docs state no specific penalty for a false or missing AI disclosure (checked: Content Survey, review process, releasing docs; sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/review_process, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/releasing). The survey's mature-content section asks for "honest and accurate disclosures" (same survey doc), which is the nearest wording to an accuracy duty; it is not specific to the AI section. The one stated sanction is the guardrail line above (PCGamesN only). The conversation says it is unclear what happens when a developer fails to disclose (source: https://theconversation.com/are-video-game-developers-using-ai-players-want-to-know-but-the-rules-are-patchy-274850).

Observed cases (all secondary):

- Call of Duty / Black Ops 6: a Steam note "Our team uses generative AI tools to help develop some in-game assets" appeared on 2025-01-27 per SteamDB, about a month after suspected AI content shipped; no removal and no Valve comment reported (source: https://hitmarker.net/news/activision-confirms-call-of-duty-features-ai-generated-content-via-steam-1275002).
- Crimson Desert (March 2026): Pearl Abyss added a generative AI note after launch when AI art was spotted; a Reddit user who refunded after about 4 hours was declined on playtime grounds; no special Valve action reported (sources, search-result summaries only because the pages returned 403: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Crimson-Desert-player-denied-Steam-refund-for-post-release-date-generative-AI-disclosure.1257901.0.html, https://www.techspot.com/news/111795-crimson-desert-dev-apologizes-ai-art-slop-promises.html).
- The Alters (11 bit studios): the studio apologised for undisclosed AI assets; no removal reported (search-result summary only, hitmarker).
- A techraptor analysis relayed by a newsletter says 18% of Steam's top 100 new 2025 releases used generative AI and fewer than half of those told players on the store page (source: https://pixelpnl.beehiiv.com/p/pixel-p-l-nearly-one-in-five-top-steam-games-now-use-ai). The original was not seen; unverified.
- No report of Valve delisting a game solely for failing to disclose AI turned up. The 2023 heard of the story removal predates the policy and was about an AI feature rather than a disclosure (search-result summary only).

**Editing disclosures later.** The doc FAQ says that once the build and store page are approved, some survey questions "cannot be edited without first contacting" Steam support, who want a summary of the change, which survey result it affects, and how a tester can reach the content (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey). Which questions are locked, and whether the AI questions are, is not stated: unverified. The store page text clearly can be updated after launch, as Call of Duty and Crimson Desert show (sources above). Approved games are not re-reviewed: "Once your game has been reviewed and approved, there is no need to go through review again" (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/review_process, fetched twice). Inference (Valve states no such thing): AI content added in a later build is not necessarily seen by review; the shipped game can drift from the disclosure.

**Is it purely self-reported?** Mostly. Valve's stated checks are the pre-release comparison of survey, build and store page (doc, above) and player reports for live-generated content (2024 post). Press characterises the policy as voluntary and not enforced by moderation (gigazine's summary of gamespot, https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260120-steam-updates-ai-disclosure-guidelines; the gamespot article itself was only seen as a search-result summary, https://www.gamespot.com/articles/valve-updates-ai-disclosure-guidelines-to-allow-for-ai-powered-tools/1100-6537483/). "Voluntary" is the press's word; Valve's doc makes the survey mandatory but does not describe independent verification. Community trackers exist because of the gap: SteamDB's "AI Content Disclosed" tag (12,284 games, 2025-10-21, https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/10/want-to-avoid-ai-gen-on-steam-this-browser-userscript-might-save-your-day/; more than 15,000 per the conversation, 2026-02-11) and the user-run "AI Check" curator group (the conversation).

## Caveats and version notes

- The Steamworks doc has no changelog; "current" means the page as fetched on 2026-10-20. Old wording comes from the 2024 post; no archived copy of the doc was available (web.archive.org was blocked to the fetcher).
- The in-app survey form (where the guardrail sanction and exact question text live) is behind the Steamworks login; all form text above is relayed by press and is not independently verified, except the sentences that also appear in the public doc.
- The JSON for the 2024 post includes an rtime32_last_modified of 1792301324 (about 2026-10-18), returned identically in two fetches. The value is unexplained; it may be a platform field, and it was not treated as evidence of an edit.
- Many search results are SEO blogs (tech-insider, legalmoveslawfirm, strayspark and similar); none were used as a source for a claim. One search result contained text that looked like an embedded instruction; it was ignored.
- These pages returned 403 or truncated content to the fetcher; claims about them rest on search-result summaries: GeekWire, TechPowerUp, Blue's News, Notebookcheck, TechSpot, and the PC Gamer January 2026 article (headline only).
- Sample game: Courage and Faith: Into the Dark Woods (app 5072580), developer and publisher Local Fire Games, release "coming soon" at fetch time; its disclosure says generative AI is used in both pre-generated and live-generated content (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/Courage_and_Faith_Into_the_Dark_Woods/). One fetch only.
- Incidental, outside RQ1 but relevant to the project: prior art exists. "AI warning for Steam" (repo seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam, file aiwarningforsteam.user.js) is a Firefox/Chrome extension and userscript that shows the disclosure in a modal on store pages and blurs or hides disclosed games in search (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/main/README.md). Its readme does not say how it detects disclosures. Gamespot covered it (title only seen in search results).
- Implications for the extension: the store signal only means the developer chose to disclose; dev-tool AI is exempt by design; the section text is free-form, and "pre-generated" and "live-generated" can only be inferred from developer wording, with no structured field to read (unverified whether the live-generated checkbox is rendered distinctly on the store page).
```

`docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq2-data-surface.md`:

```md
# RQ2: How does Steam's AI generated content disclosure show up on store pages and in machine-readable data?

## Answer in short

- On the app page the disclosure is a server-rendered block `<div id="game_area_content_descriptors" class="game_area_description">` holding `<h2>AI Generated Content Disclosure</h2>`, a fixed lead-in `<p>`, and the developer's free text inside `<p><i>...</i></p>`. The ID is duplicated: the mature content description uses the same ID and classes; the only discriminator is the localized h2 text (and document order: AI block came first on the one sample that had both).
- The heading is localized and Valve has edited translations after the fact (Russian 2026-02, French 2026-09); text matching on a localized page is fragile. Every existing tool fetches `?l=english` for detection in lists.
- A no-scrape source exists: `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` with `data_request.include_extra_details=true` returns `store_items[].extra_details.content_survey_ai_notes` (the same free text as the page) and, for some apps, `extra_details.ai_generation_service` (`name`, `url`). Seen working without an API key. `appdetails`, search rows, hover popups, tags and content descriptor IDs carry no AI marker.
- There is no Steam content descriptor ID and no Steam store tag for it (descriptor IDs seen are 1 to 5 only; the SteamDB "AI Content Disclosed" tag 1368160 is SteamDB's own and absent from Steam's tag list).
- Age gates matter: a cookie-less fetch of an app with violence descriptors (Call of Duty, 1938090) was redirected to `/agecheck/app/1938090/`, and an adult-only app redirected to login. Treat any response without `id="appHubAppName"` as "unknown" and never as "no disclosure".

## Findings

How the evidence was gathered (read this first): the only fetch tool available converts pages to markdown through a small summarizing model, which hid the raw HTML. Server HTML structure came from `api.microlink.io` (a third-party fetch API) with `prerender=false`, which returned CSS-selected fragments (`data.x.selector`, `attr=html|text|class`); the helper model then described them. Short strings quoted below were returned verbatim by that route; element skeletons are the helper's description of the returned HTML and are corroborated by the regexes and selectors used in three open source tools (sources below). JSON fields were read through the same helper; treat exact numeric values as "seen once". Re-confirm the snippets with curl or devtools before hard-coding anything.

### 1. Store page HTML: containing element, selectors, heading, free text

Sample with disclosure: app 5072580 (Courage and Faith: Into the Dark Woods), fetched as `https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/?l=english` through microlink with `prerender=false` (server HTML, no JavaScript run). The left column (`.game_description_column`) listed these direct children in order: `div#game_area_purchase`, `div#bannerCommunity`, `div.purchase_area_spacer`, `div[data-featuretarget="events-row"]`, `div#contentForThisGame_ctn`, `div#aboutThisGame.game_page_autocollapse` (holding `div#game_area_description.game_area_description`), then the AI block, then the mature content block, then `div.game_page_autocollapse.sys_req` (system requirements). (Source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F5072580%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.col.selector=.game_description_column&data.col.attr=html)

The AI block, server HTML skeleton (text shortened, attributes exact as reported):

```
<div class="game_page_autocollapse">
  <div id="game_area_content_descriptors" class="game_area_description">
    <h2>AI Generated Content Disclosure</h2>
    <p>The developers describe how their game uses AI Generated Content like this:</p>
    <p><i>Generative AI is used in both pre-generated and live-generated content. ...</i></p>
  </div>
</div>
```

(Source: same microlink route with `data.h.selectorAll=#game_area_content_descriptors > h2` and `data.p.selectorAll=#game_area_content_descriptors > p`, https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F5072580%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.p.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20p&data.p.attr=html&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=html)

- Heading: `<h2>` with no attributes, text exactly `AI Generated Content Disclosure` in English (31 chars). (Source: the microlink URL above; also the ARC Raiders check, https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F1808500%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.p.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20p&data.p.attr=html&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text)
- Lead-in paragraph: first `<p>`, no attributes, text `The developers describe how their game uses AI Generated Content like this:` (75 chars; identical on app 1808500). The mature content block uses `The developers describe the content like this:`. (Source: the two microlink URLs above)
- Developer free text: the second `<p>`, which wraps an `<i>`. The raw string starts `<i>\n\t\t\t\t\tGenerative AI is used in both pre-generated and live-generated content. AI-assisted tools w...`; expect leading newline and tabs inside the `<i>`. No `<br>` was present in the three samples (5072580: 465 chars, 1808500: 232 chars). (Source: microlink URLs above)
- No IDs or classes exist on `h2`, `p` or `i`. The usable hooks are `#game_area_content_descriptors`, `.game_area_description`, and the parent `.game_page_autocollapse`. The working selector in a shipped extension is `.game_page_autocollapse > #game_area_content_descriptors > h2`, filtered by heading text. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/main/aiwarningforsteam.user.js)
- The ID is not unique. On 5072580 there are two elements with `id="game_area_content_descriptors"`: the AI block (heading `AI Generated Content Disclosure`) first, the mature block (heading `Mature Content Description`, free text in its own `<p><i>`) second. In a javascript-rendered DOM the AI block was reported wrapped as `div.game_page_autocollapse_ctn > div.game_page_autocollapse[style="max-height: none;"]` followed by `div.game_page_autocollapse_fade > div.game_page_autocollapse_readmore` ("READ MORE"). A `querySelector("#game_area_content_descriptors")` call returns whichever block is first and can be either one; use `querySelectorAll` and test heading text. (Source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F5072580%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&data.page.selector=html&data.page.attr=html with offset 100000; the Pierre-Demessence banner script takes only the first `h2` of the first block, which would miss the AI block on pages where mature content comes first, see https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierre-Demessence/SteamAIGamesIndicator/main/steamAIBanner.user.js, summarized by the fetch helper)
- Single-block and zero-block cases: ARC Raiders (1808500) has the AI block and no mature block (appdetails `content_descriptors.ids` is `[]`, `notes` null). Stardew Valley (413150) has no `#game_area_content_descriptors` at all (microlink returned `null` for both `data.h` and `data.cd`). Absence of the element means no disclosure and no mature text. (Sources: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F413150%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text&data.cd.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors&data.cd.attr=html and https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=1808500&cc=us&l=english)
- App name hook: `#appHubAppName` exists on real app pages (used by the extensions as the "this is a real store page" check). (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierre-Demessence/SteamAIGamesIndicator/main/steamAIBadge.user.js, summarized by the fetch helper)
- Plain-text fetch of the app page also showed the section with the same heading and the developer text for 5072580 and for Call of Duty (1938090): `Our team uses generative AI tools to help develop some in game assets.` (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/Courage_and_Faith_Into_the_Dark_Woods/ and https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/Call_of_Duty/)

Detection strings the existing tools rely on, as a cross-check that the heading is literal server HTML:

- seeeeew fetches `https://store.steampowered.com/app/${appid}?l=english` and runs `text.match('<h2>AI Generated Content Disclosure</h2>')` on the raw response. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/main/aiwarningforsteam.user.js)
- Pierre-Demessence fetches `https://store.steampowered.com/app/{appId}/?l=english`, tests the case-insensitive pattern `AI Generated Content Disclosure` against the HTML, and only caches a negative when the page contains `id="appHubAppName"`. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierre-Demessence/SteamAIGamesIndicator/main/steamAIBadge.user.js, summarized by the fetch helper)
- SoBloxsy fetches `https://store.steampowered.com/app/${appId}/` (no `l` param) and flags if the HTML `includes("AI Generated Content Disclosure")`; it treats fetch errors as "not flagged". (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoBloxsy/AI-Content-Hider-for-Steam/main/content.js, summarized by the fetch helper)

A bare substring match on the whole HTML would also fire if a developer wrote that phrase in their own description; matching `<h2>` text inside the specific container avoids that (inference; untested).

### 1b. Is the heading localized?

Yes. Verified by microlink with the DOM selector on 5072580:

- `?l=german`: `["Offenlegung von KI-generierten Inhalten", "Beschreibung nicht jugendfreier Inhalte"]` (AI heading, then mature heading). (Source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F5072580%2F%3Fl%3Dgerman&meta=false&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text)
- `?l=spanish`: AI heading `Informaci\u00f3n sobre contenido generado por IA` (written with a \u escape to keep this note ascii), mature heading `Descripci\u00f3n del contenido para adultos`. (Source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F5072580%2F%3Fl%3Dspanish&meta=false&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text)
- Both match the translation table shipped in seeeeew's script, which lists a heading for 30 store languages (schinese, tchinese, Japanese, koreana, thai, indonesian, Malay, bulgarian, czech, danish, German, English, Spanish, latam, greek, French, italian, hungarian, dutch, norwegian, polish, portuguese, brazilian, romanian, Russian, finnish, swedish, turkish, vietnamese, ukrainian). (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/main/aiwarningforsteam.user.js)

The translations are not frozen:

- Russian: Steam changed the heading; detection broke; fixed 2026-02-25 (issue 1, commit "fixed detection on Russian store pages"). The new Russian string was not stated in the issue body (unverified here; the table in the current script holds it). (Sources: https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/issues/1 and https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/commits?per_page=20)
- French: on 2026-09-24 a user reported Steam changed the title from `Divulgation de contenu g\u00e9n\u00e9r\u00e9 par IA` to `Notification de contenu g\u00e9n\u00e9r\u00e9 par IA`; fixed in commit 1422d0851c81fd85950e435d31e399dc21b0c045 (version 1.1.1, announced as 1.1.2 on 2026-09-25). (Sources: https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/issues/13/comments and https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/commits/1422d0851c81fd85950e435d31e399dc21b0c045)
- Malay was missing until 2026-06-13 (issue 5). Issue 4 (open) proposes a script that checks whether headings changed in any language. (Source: https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/issues?state=all&per_page=30)

Consequence: only the English heading (fetched with `?l=english`) is a stable key to date; any localized table needs a refresh mechanism, and a localized-dom check should fall back to an English fetch when the heading is unknown.

### 1c. Age gates, login walls, redirects that affect fetching

- App 5072580 and 1808500: server HTML returned directly, no gate (microlink, `prerender=false`, no cookies). (Sources: microlink URLs above)
- Call of Duty (1938090; search row shows `data-ds-descids` `[2,5]`): the same cookie-less microlink fetch (both `?l=german` and `?l=english`) ended at `https://store.steampowered.com/agecheck/app/1938090/` with title "Call of Duty" and no `#game_area_content_descriptors`. The agecheck page itself returned HTTP 200 and its DOM IDs were `valve-ssr-data`, `StoreTemplate`, `searchSuggestions_...`, `footer` (a react shell; none of the old age form IDs). By contrast, the plain-text fetch tool got the full store page for the same app; the gate depends on the client (cookies, location). (Sources: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F1938090%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text&data.form.selector=%23agegate_box&data.form.attr=html&data.title.selector=title&data.title.attr=text , https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fagecheck%2Fapp%2F1938090%2F&meta=false&prerender=false&data.ids.selectorAll=%5Bid%5D&data.ids.attr=id , https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/Call_of_Duty/)
- Adult-only app HuniePop (339800): both the fetch tool and microlink landed on `https://store.steampowered.com/login/?redir=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fagecheck%2Fapp%2F339800%2F` (title "Sign In"). (Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/app/339800/HuniePop/ and https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F339800%2F&meta=false&prerender=false&data.title.selector=title&data.title.attr=text&data.h.selectorAll=%23game_area_content_descriptors%20%3E%20h2&data.h.attr=text&data.ageform.selector=%23ageYear&data.ageform.attr=html)
- Nonexistent appid 99999999: microlink reported a 302 and a final URL of `https://store.steampowered.com/` (title "Welcome to Steam"); a delisted or invalid app also yields a 200 HTML page with no `#appHubAppName`. (Source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F99999999%2F&meta=false&prerender=false&data.title.selector=title&data.title.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text)
- Practical rule: `fetch()` follows redirects silently with a 200 at the end; check `response.url` for `/agecheck/` or `/login/` and/or the presence of `id="appHubAppName"`; Pierre-Demessence does the latter and keeps "age gates, login walls, or error pages" out of the negative cache. An extension fetching from the user's own logged-in browser sends the user's cookies and sees the user's view; a background fetch with `credentials: "omit"` does not (inference; not tested here). Ways to spoof age cookies were not researched and the note does not cover them.
- Region: no store-page region redirect was found or tested beyond `StoreItem.unvailable_for_country_restriction` (a bool in the GetItems proto, field 5; spelling as in the proto). `cc` only influenced price in the calls made. (Source for the proto field: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, offset 200000 via the fetch helper). Unverified for HTML pages.
- Whether a fetch with `?l=english` writes a language cookie that flips the user's own store language is unverified. Forum posts say a `?l=` link tends to "stick" for the user, but nothing fetched confirmed it for a background `fetch`. (Source: web search results, e.g. https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/1729828401709606496)

### 2a. `store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails`

- Request: `https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=5072580` (also with `cc=us&l=english`). Response is keyed by the appid string with `success` and `data`. (Source: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=5072580&cc=us&l=english)
- `data` keys for 5072580 (31 listed): `type, name, steam_appid, required_age, is_free, dlc, detailed_description, about_the_game, short_description, supported_languages, header_image, capsule_image, capsule_imagev5, website, pc_requirements, mac_requirements, linux_requirements, developers, publishers, demos, package_groups, platforms, categories, genres, screenshots, movies, release_date, support_info, background, background_raw, content_descriptors, ratings`. No key named for AI, generative or disclosure. (Source: same URL)
- `content_descriptors.ids` is `[5]`; `content_descriptors.notes` starts `The game contains dark fantasy violence, combat involving weapons and supernatural creatures, descrip...` and is the mature-content free text and holds no AI text. (Source: same URL)
- The strings `Generated Content Disclosure` and `Generative AI is used in both pre-generated` do not occur anywhere in the 5072580 response; for ARC Raiders neither `Generated Content Disclosure` nor `AI-based tools to assist with content creation` occurs (its `content_descriptors` is `ids: []`, `notes: null`). Appdetails therefore cannot be used for detection. The only AI wording is incidental, e.g. `short_description` "AI-generated narration reacts to your decisions" and a `pc_requirements` note about live AI features. (Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=5072580&cc=us&l=english and https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=1808500&cc=us&l=english)
- Tooling note: the fetch helper would not print the full JSON verbatim; key lists came from its enumeration, and two separate fetches of the 5072580 response gave the same key list and `ids`.

### 2b. `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` (api.steampowered.com)

This is the endpoint that does expose the disclosure.

Request shape that worked with no API key (decoded `input_json`):

```
{"ids":[{"appid":5072580}],"context":{"language":"english","country_code":"US"},"data_request":{"include_extra_details":true}}
```

URL: `https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=<urlencoded json above>` (source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A5072580%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D)

Response layout: `response.store_items[]`, each with `item_type, id, success, visible, name, store_url_path, store_url_slug, appid, type, related_items, content_descriptorids, categories, is_coming_soon, extra_details` when only `include_extra_details` is set. (Source: same URL)

The AI fields, in `store_items[].extra_details`:

- `content_survey_ai_notes` (string): the developer's free text. For 5072580 it begins "Generative AI is used in both pre-generated and live-generated content." and continues with the artwork, music, sound effects and live narrative text description, i.e. the same text shown in the page's `<i>`. For Call of Duty (1938090) the whole value was `Our team uses generative AI tools to help develop some in game assets.` (matching the page text); for ARC Raiders (1808500) it begins "During the development process, we may use procedural- and AI-based tools to assist with content cre" (matching the page's `<i>` start). Absent for Stardew Valley (413150). (Sources: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A5072580%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1808500%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1938090%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D and https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D)
- `ai_generation_service` (object with `name`, `url`): seen only on 5072580 as `{"name":"OpenAI API","url":"https://openai.com/api/"}`; absent for 1808500, 1938090 and 413150. It appears to be a live-generation service declaration; its meaning and when it is shown on the page are unverified (the sample page did not render it in the block structure seen). (Source: the 4-app GetItems URL above, plus a separate single-app fetch of 5072580 that listed `.ai_generation_service.name` and `.ai_generation_service.url`)
- `content_survey_notes` (string) is the mature-content free text, separate from the AI notes. (Same URLs)
- Other keys seen under `extra_details`: `vetted, controller_wizard_complete, interactive_elements, links_and_info, system_requirements` (5072580); the set varies per app (ARC Raiders also had `steam_award, anticheat, eula, section, legal_notice_bbcode, press_review, partner_awards_bbcode`). There is no boolean or enum for "pre-generated" vs "live-generated"; only the free text and the optional service object. (Same 4-app URL)
- Protobuf confirmation: `StoreBrowseItemDataRequest` has `optional bool include_extra_details = 18;` and `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` declares `optional .StoreItem_ExtraDetails_AIGeneratedContentService ai_generation_service = 11;` and `optional string content_survey_ai_notes = 17;`; the service message has `name = 1` and `url = 2`. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, offset 200000, via the fetch helper)
- Full list of request flags in `StoreBrowseItemDataRequest`: `include_assets, include_release, include_platforms, include_all_purchase_options, include_screenshots, include_trailers, include_ratings, include_tag_count (int32), include_reviews, include_basic_info, include_supported_languages, include_full_description, include_included_items, included_item_data_request, include_assets_without_overrides, apply_user_filters, include_links, include_extra_details, include_best_purchase_option, include_optin_registration_tags`. (Same proto source)
- Batching: four appids in one request worked. The maximum IDs per call is unverified.

What the other flags return for 5072580 (no AI marker anywhere in them):

- With `include_basic_info`, `include_tag_count`, `include_ratings`: `content_descriptorids: [5]`, `categories.supported_player_categoryids [2]`, `categories.feature_categoryids [35, 62]`, `basic_info.short_description` (the "AI-generated narration reacts to your decisions" text is just the marketing blurb), `basic_info.developers/publishers[].name`, `tags[]` as `{tagid, weight}` (20 entries when `include_tag_count` is 20; first tagids 10695, 11014, 6426, 4325, 1742), and `game_rating.content_survey_notes` (the mature text). (Source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A5072580%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_basic_info%22%3Atrue%2C%22include_tag_count%22%3A20%2C%22include_ratings%22%3Atrue%7D%7D)
- With the broad flag set (assets, release, platforms, purchase options, screenshots, trailers, ratings, tags, reviews, basic info, languages, full description, links): additionally `tagids`, `reviews.summary_filtered`, `assets`, `release`, `platforms`, `screenshots`, `trailers`, `supported_languages`, `full_description_bbcode`. `game_rating` held only `content_survey_notes` there. The string `AI Generated Content Disclosure` appears nowhere in that response and `full_description_bbcode` is the "About This Game" bbcode only. (Source: the broad-flag GetItems call, input_json with all `include_*` flags true and `include_tag_count` 5, same endpoint)
- `StoreGameRating` in the proto has `type, rating, descriptors, interactive_elements, agency, banned, esrb_online_*, survey_interactive_elements, required_age, use_age_gate, descriptor_images, content_survey_notes (13), image_url, image_target`; no AI field. (Source: proto above)
- Stability: `GetItems` is a Valve web UI endpoint described only by reverse engineered protobufs (SteamDatabase/Protobufs); no Valve documentation for `include_extra_details` turned up. Steam could rename or gate it. (The xPaw API index page did not list method details in the fetched content, https://steamapi.xpaw.me/)

### 2c. Content descriptor IDs and user tags

- Content descriptor IDs seen: `[5]` (5072580), `[2, 5]` (Call of Duty, both in GetItems and in search row `data-ds-descids`), `[]` (ARC Raiders). A community post lists the enum as 1 NudityOrSexualContent, 2 FrequentViolenceOrGore, 3 AdultOnlySexualContent, 4 GratuitousSexualContent, 5 AnyMatureContent, and says it may be incomplete (unofficial, posted 2024-05-01). A Substack analysis independently says games with mature classification start with `ids=[5]` (reverse engineered). There is no AI ID in this set, and ARC Raiders discloses AI with an empty list, which rules out descriptors as a carrier of the disclosure. (Sources: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/4362375816113312079 and https://fredericksen.substack.com/p/steam-video-game-ratings-and-mature; absence of a newer ID is unverified beyond the apps sampled)
- Steam tag list: `https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetTagList/v1/?language=english` returned 446 tags, first `9 Strategy`, `19 Action`, `21 Adventure`; none is an AI-disclosure tag, and tagid 1368160 is not in it. `https://store.steampowered.com/tagdata/populartags/english` (429 entries) likewise has only `Artificial Intelligence` (tagid 7926), which is a gameplay-topic tag and no disclosure. (Sources: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetTagList/v1/?language=english and https://store.steampowered.com/tagdata/populartags/english)
- SteamDB runs its own tag "AI Content Disclosed" with ID 1368160 at https://steamdb.info/tag/1368160/; per the search snippet it is applied automatically when the disclosure statement appears on the store page. Direct fetch of that page returned HTTP 403; the description is from a search result only (single source). Destructoid says `&tagid=-1368160` is a steamdb.info search option that store.steampowered.com lacks. (Sources: https://steamdb.info/tag/1368160 (403), web search result for that URL, https://www.destructoid.com/how-to-filter-out-generative-ai-games-with-steamdb/)

### 3. Is the disclosure visible anywhere other than the app page?

- Search results page: the rows carry no AI marker. Each `a.search_result_row.ds_collapse_flag` has `data-ds-appid`, `data-ds-itemkey`, `data-ds-tagids`, `data-ds-descids`, `data-ds-crtrids` and children `.search_capsule`, `.responsive_search_name_combined`, `.search_platforms`, `.search_released`, `.search_reviewscore`, price blocks; nothing about AI. Checked on the JSON variant `https://store.steampowered.com/search/results/?query&start=0&count=10&dynamic_data=&sort_by=_ASC&term=Call%20of%20Duty&infinite=1&l=english&cc=us` (fields `success, results_html, total_count, start`); Call of Duty's row had `data-ds-descids` `[2,5]`. (Source: that URL)
- Hover popup `https://store.steampowered.com/apphoverpublic/<appid>`: 5072580 showed title, availability and user tags; 1938090 showed release date, review summary and tags; no AI wording in either. (Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/apphoverpublic/5072580?l=english&cc=us and https://store.steampowered.com/apphoverpublic/1938090?l=english&cc=us)
- Home page capsules, wishlist, tab lists, sale capsules: not shown natively, inferred from the fact that the existing tools add their own badges after a per-app page fetch. Pierre-Demessence targets `.CapsuleDecorators`, `.ds_flagged`, `.tab_item`, `.search_result_row`, wishlist `input[data-appid]` and `[data-rfd-draggable-id^="WishlistItem-"]`, `[data-ds-appid].store_capsule`, `[data-ds-appid].sale_capsule`, `.home_area_spotlight[data-ds-appid]`, `.tab_row_item[data-ds-appid]`, `.Panel[data-ds-appid]:has(> img)`; SoBloxsy handles wishlist rows as `div[role="button"][tabindex="0"]` containing `a[href*="/app/"]` and avoids obfuscated class names. (Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierre-Demessence/SteamAIGamesIndicator/main/steamAIBadge.user.js and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoBloxsy/AI-Content-Hider-for-Steam/main/content.js, both summarized by the fetch helper; no logged-in wishlist was opened)
- Discovery queue and the Steam desktop client library: not tested (no logged-in session). Issue 3 on seeeeew's repo (open) asks for desktop client support, and the maintainer says he cannot test it, which suggests nothing native exists there, but that is inference. Unverified. (Source: https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/issues?state=all&per_page=30)
- Coverage gaps in the one mature tool: category pages (issue 10) and search suggestions (issue 7) are not handled, and issue 9 asks for curator review feed support. (Same issues source)
- No first-party Steam AI filter in the store search turned up; the extension author added a client-side "Narrow by AI Generated Content Disclosure" panel in 2026-06 (commit "Added search filter by AI disclosure"), implying none existed. (Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/main/aiwarningforsteam.user.js and the commits API URL above; absence of a native filter in the current store is otherwise unverified)

What a per-app request looks like (for the extension):

1. Preferred: batch `GET https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json={"ids":[{"appid":A},{"appid":B},...],"context":{"language":"english","country_code":"US"},"data_request":{"include_extra_details":true}}`; disclosed iff `store_items[i].extra_details.content_survey_ai_notes` is a non-empty string. One call can cover a whole search page or wishlist (batch ceiling unverified). No age gate or cookie dependence was seen in the JSON route (4 apps incl. Call of Duty returned data from the fetch tool; a cookie-less check of an age-gated app through this endpoint was not run).
2. Fallback: `GET https://store.steampowered.com/app/<appid>/?l=english`, check the final URL and `id="appHubAppName"`, then look for `<h2>AI Generated Content Disclosure</h2>` inside `#game_area_content_descriptors`, and read the free text from the `<i>` of the second `<p>`.
3. On the app page itself the block is already in the DOM; query `.game_page_autocollapse > #game_area_content_descriptors > h2` with all headings known, and fall back to option 1 or 2 if no heading matches but the page may still disclose.

## First-hand verification (2026-10-20, built-in browser, no Steam login, no API key)

- `GetItems` with `include_extra_details: true` for 5072580 and 413150 returned `extra_details.content_survey_ai_notes` (the full English disclosure text) and `ai_generation_service` `{"name":"OpenAI API","url":"https://openai.com/api/"}` for 5072580. Both keys were absent for Stardew Valley 413150, whose `extra_details` keys were `vetted, press_review, partner_awards_bbcode, links_and_info, points_shop_eligible, metacritic, system_requirements`.
- From a page on `https://store.steampowered.com`, a plain `fetch()` to `api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1` returned 200 with a readable body, which shows that CORS permits the store origin. `access-control-allow-origin` cannot be read from JS, so whether it is a wildcard or echoes the origin is unknown.
- Batch ceiling: the 50 rows of `store.steampowered.com/search/?term=roguelike` (IDs from `#search_resultsRows a[data-ds-appid]`) went out in one request (encoded `input_json` about 1.7 KB) and returned 50 items in about 1.3 s, 10 of them with `content_survey_ai_notes`. Larger batches were not tried.
- DOM on the sample app page (`?l=english`): exactly two `#game_area_content_descriptors.game_area_description` elements, both children of `.game_page_autocollapse`. The first has `<h2>AI Generated Content Disclosure</h2>` and the second has `<h2>Mature Content Description</h2>`. This confirms the duplicate ID.
- A same-origin `fetch('/app/413150/?l=english')` from the search page returned 200, contained `appHubAppName`, and did not contain the AI heading.

## Caveats and version notes

- All HTML structure came through a third-party headless fetch API plus a summarizing model; no byte-exact copy of the page source was read. Snippets above are faithful to what was returned, but whitespace, attribute order and any extra classes could differ. Re-verify with devtools before shipping selectors.
- The JSON route result for `ai_generation_service` is based on one app. Do not depend on it for detection.
- `content_survey_ai_notes` text is the English-context value; whether it varies with `context.language` is unverified.
- Whether `content_survey_ai_notes` can exist on an app whose page does not render the section (for example not yet approved) is unverified. The sample app was "coming soon" and showed both.
- Policy context: Valve rewrote its disclosure rules around 2026-01-17 (what must be disclosed; the article does not say the page section changed), and the Steamworks Content Survey has a "Generative Artificial Intelligence Content" section with pre-generated and live-generated parts and a guardrails question; that doc page does not say where the text is shown or whether an API exposes it. (Sources: https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/valve-has-significantly-rewritten-steams-rules-for-how-developers-much-disclose-ai-use and https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey)
- False positives come from policy: a publisher's AI upscaling disclosure triggers the section (issue 12). (Source: issues API URL above)
- The Steam announcement "AI Content on Steam" (https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/3862463747997849619) returned only navigation text; the original 2024 statement was not read.
- The web search tool declined to explain age-cookie workarounds; none were researched or recorded here.
- CORS and MV3 behavior (service worker with host permissions vs content script) for `api.steampowered.com` was not tested.
```
