`docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq5-extension-constraints.md`:

```md
# RQ5: Technical and policy constraints for a Chrome + Firefox MV3 extension and a userscript that flag AI-disclosing Steam games

Research date 2026-10-20. A sibling note covers the exact Steam markup and endpoints; this note covers extension mechanics, dynamic injection, rate limits and store/steam policy. Tags: `unverified` means not confirmed by a primary source in this run; `inference` means a deduction from cited facts.

## Answer in short

- Content scripts on store.steampowered.com can fetch same-origin store pages themselves, but any cross-origin call (api.steampowered.com, other hosts) is subject to CORS in both Chrome and Firefox MV3 and must go through the background (service worker in Chrome, event page in Firefox) with `host_permissions`. Ship one manifest per browser, or one with both `background.service_worker` and `background.scripts`.
- Storage.local is 10 MB in Chrome (5 MB before Chrome 114), content-script readable, and extendable with `unlimitedStorage`; Firefox follows indexeddb limits with no fixed number published. A per-app flag cache fits easily; MV3 Chrome service workers die after 30 s idle; persist queue state.
- App capsules on classic store pages carry `data-ds-appid` / `data-ds-packageid` or an `/app/<id>` href; Augmented Steam keys off those. Search infinite scroll is handled by hooking Steam's own page globals and firing a custom event; the react wishlist needs a MutationObserver and uses build-hashed class names that break on deploys.
- The 200 requests per 5 minutes figure for `appdetails` comes from community lore; Valve publishes no rate limit for store endpoints. 429s are per IP and can last hours on other store endpoints. Design for a throttled, cached, backoff-aware fetcher.
- Publishing blockers: Chrome Web Store limited use and no-remote-code rules (keep all logic in the package, do not send viewed appids to a server), and AMO source-code submission for bundled builds plus the mandatory `data_collection_permissions` key for new Firefox extensions. The Steam Subscriber Agreement has no explicit scraping clause; section 4.C bans bots/scripts that interact with Steam in ways listed there (accounts, fake stats, rewards, peer review).

## Findings

### 1a. Content script versus background for fetching store.steampowered.com pages

Content scripts send requests as the web origin they are injected into, and the same-origin policy applies to them; Chrome states cross-origin requests are always treated as cross-origin in content scripts, even with host permissions. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/network-requests)

Chrome 85 removed the ability for content scripts to bypass CORS; they get "the same request rules as the page they are running within", requests to the page's own origin work as before, cross-origin ones need a matching `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Chromium recommends moving cross-origin fetches to the background and relaying results by messaging, and fetching only fixed intended URLs rather than URLs supplied by the content script. (Source: https://www.chromium.org/Home/chromium-security/extension-content-script-fetches/)

Chrome docs advise the content script send a limited value (such as an item ID) and let the extension build the URL itself. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/network-requests)

Firefox MV3 is the same: since Firefox 101 content scripts follow the page's CORS policy, host permissions do not apply to content scripts but do apply to extension pages, and only background scripts have elevated cross-domain privileges. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/mozilla/add-ons/webextensions/content_scripts/index.md) The MDN `host_permissions` page agrees that the unrestricted xhr/fetch grant does not apply to requests from content scripts. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/mozilla/add-ons/webextensions/manifest.json/host_permissions/index.md)

Consequence for this project (inference): a content script on `https://store.steampowered.com/*` can fetch `/app/<id>` pages and `/api/appdetails` as ordinary same-origin requests (page cookies sent by default fetch semantics) and parse the HTML with the page's `DOMParser`, with no background hop. Anything on `api.steampowered.com` or another host must be proxied through the background, where host permissions lift CORS.

Reference implementations route through the background: SteamDB's extension accepts messages only from tabs and routes by `request.contentScriptQuery`, doing all Steam and SteamDB fetches there (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/BrowserExtension/master/scripts/background.js); Augmented Steam's `SteamStoreApi` runs in the background and fetches pages with `fetch(url, {credentials: "include"})` and `/api/appdetails/` with `credentials: "include"` and an optional `filter` (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Background/Modules/Store/SteamStoreApi.ts).

### 1b. HTML parsing in the background (Chrome service worker has no DOM)

Chrome MV3 service workers cannot access the DOM or `window`; Chrome points to offscreen documents for DOM work. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/to-service-workers) Augmented Steam does exactly this: on chrome/edge builds it creates an offscreen document with reason `DOM_PARSER` to parse fetched HTML, on Firefox it uses a native parser. (Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Background/Modules/Dom/DomParserFactory.ts, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Background/Modules/Dom/OffscreenDomParser.ts) The offscreen helper there creates and closes the document around every parse call, and the fetch summary flagged a possible race when parses run concurrently (read from a single fetch of the file).

Inference: if the disclosure lives only in the app-page HTML, the simplest cross-browser design is to have the background return raw HTML text (or fetch same-origin in the content script) and parse in a context that has `DOMParser`, avoiding the offscreen permission and its reviewer justification.

### 1c. steamcommunity.com and the wishlist

The wishlist badge code in Augmented Steam lives under `Features/Store/Wishlist/` (store host), and the community side only has a profile link feature (source: file tree, https://api.github.com/repos/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/git/trees/master?recursive=1). Inference: a `steamcommunity.com` match is not needed for wishlist flagging; `store.steampowered.com/wishlist/*` is covered by the store match. Both Augmented Steam and SteamDB list steamcommunity.com for unrelated community features. (Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/scripts/tools/manifest.mjs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/BrowserExtension/master/manifest.json)

### 1d. CORS of store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails and api.steampowered.com

No official Valve documentation on CORS for these hosts was found. What exists is anecdotal: a 2019 Steam community thread reports browser calls to `api.steampowered.com` failing for lack of `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and recommends a server-side proxy (source: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/1743358239838884448); a userscript on Greasy Fork fetches store pages via `GM_xmlhttpRequest` with `anonymous: true` to sidestep page CORS (source: search result summary, https://greasyfork.org/scripts/587297-steam-gamestatus). Cloudflare radar scans show CORS errors for third-party pages calling `store.steampowered.com/dynamicstore/saledata/` (source: search result summary, https://v2.radar.cfdata.org/es-la/scan/f2d5c21b-a13c-4fb8-8696-9298134f0f57/security).

`unverified`: the actual response headers of `/api/appdetails` for a foreign `Origin`. No HTTP request could be issued in this run. Test with a one-off posting request, then also test from inside an extension service worker, before relying on either result. Make the fetch path independent of the result: same-origin from the store content script, or background fetch with host permission.

### 1e. Firefox MV3 differences that matter

- Background: Firefox does not support `background.service_worker` (bug 1573659); it supports `background.scripts` as a non-persistent event page. Chrome uses `service_worker` and (from Chrome 121) ignores `scripts`. MDN's recommended cross-browser manifest lists both keys. Firefox before 120 failed to start the background page if `service_worker` was present; from 121 it starts regardless. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/mozilla/add-ons/webextensions/manifest.json/background/index.md)
- SteamDB ships one manifest with both `scripts` and `service_worker` pointing at `scripts/background.js`, `gecko.strict_min_version` 128.0 (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/BrowserExtension/master/manifest.json). Augmented Steam instead generates a per-browser manifest: `service_worker` for chrome/edge, `scripts` for Firefox, gecko ID, `strict_min_version` 140.0 (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/scripts/tools/manifestBuilder.mjs).
- Event pages in Firefox: listeners must be registered synchronously at top level, state kept in storage, timers replaced by alarms. (Source: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/manifest-v3-migration-guide/)
- Host permissions: MDN says most browsers treat `host_permissions` as optional because users can grant or revoke per host. Through Firefox 126 MV3 host permissions were not shown in the install prompt and effectively had to be granted by the user afterwards; from Firefox 127 permissions from `host_permissions` and `content_scripts` appear in the prompt and are granted at install. Chrome shows them at install. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/mozilla/add-ons/webextensions/manifest.json/host_permissions/index.md) Because the user can revoke them later, check with `permissions.contains` and handle the revoked case. (Source: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/manifest-v3-migration-guide/)
- Registered content scripts only run if the extension has host permission for the matched domain in Firefox. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/mozilla/add-ons/webextensions/content_scripts/index.md; read via one fetch summary)
- `world: "MAIN"` content scripts: SteamDB's manifest uses one with `strict_min_version` 128 and Augmented Steam's manifest sets `world: "MAIN"` on its Steam scriptlet, built for Firefox too. (Sources: SteamDB and Augmented Steam manifests above) Inference: main-world scripts work in Firefox 128 and later; the MDN page read did not state the Firefox version; confirm on the compat table before depending on it.
- Chrome and Firefox match-pattern rules: `https://store.steampowered.com/*` matches only that host over HTTPS; `https://*.steampowered.com/*` matches any subdomain; the page does not confirm whether the wildcard form matches the bare apex. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/match-patterns) Both reference extensions request `*://*.steampowered.com/*` for host permissions; the narrower single-host pattern better fits the Chrome "narrowest permissions" policy (see 4d).

### 1f. Chrome service worker lifetime

Chrome typically terminates an extension service worker after 30 s idle, when a single request takes longer than 5 minutes, or when a `fetch()` response takes longer than 30 s. Extension events and API calls reset the idle timer (API calls since Chrome 110); a long-lived port keeps it alive from Chrome 114. Global variables are lost, `localStorage` is unavailable; docs recommend `storage` APIs and saving queue progress after each step. (Sources: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/service-workers/lifecycle, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/to-service-workers)

Consequence (inference): a throttled backfill of many appids must be a persisted queue that resumes on wake, driven by messages or `chrome.alarms`, not an in-memory loop with `setTimeout`.

### 1g. Storage quotas for caching per-app results

- `chrome.storage.local`: 10,485,760 bytes (5 MB in Chrome 113 and earlier); `unlimitedStorage` permission removes the cap; exposed to content scripts by default; `setAccessLevel` can restrict it to trusted contexts. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage)
- `chrome.storage.sync`: about 100 KB total, 8 KB per item, 512 items, 120 writes per minute and 1800 per hour; unsuitable for a per-app cache. (Same source)
- `chrome.storage.session`: 10 MB, memory only, not exposed to content scripts by default. (Same source)
- Firefox `storage.local`: "the same storage limits as applied to IndexedDB databases"; `unlimitedStorage` needed for more; writes can still fail with quota exceeded at the global disk limit; no fixed figure given. (Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/storage/local) Note: that MDN page still says "in Chrome ... 5MB", which is stale against the Chrome reference above (10 MB since Chrome 114); trust the Chrome docs.
- Precedents: SteamDB caches in `storage.local` with TTLs (user data 1 hour, family data 6 hours); Augmented Steam uses indexeddb in the background with a 86,400 s TTL for package-to-app maps, localStorage for currency (1 day). (Sources: SteamDB background.js and Augmented Steam SteamStoreApi.ts above)
- Sizing (inference, an estimate not a measurement): a record of appid, tri-state flag, fetch time and a short evidence hash is on the order of tens of bytes per app; tens of thousands of apps fit inside 10 MB. Add an expiry/TTL and negative caching ("no disclosure section") to avoid refetching unchanged apps.

### 2a. Userscript variant: GM APIs, @connect, caching, @match

What was fetched: the Tampermonkey documentation index page only lists section names and links (`@connect`, `@grant`, `GM_xmlhttpRequest(details)`, `GM_setValue`/`GM_getValue`, `@match/@include/@exclude`, `@run-at`, `@require/@resource`); it contains no semantics. (Source: https://www.tampermonkey.net/documentation.php) The detail pages (`?q=connect`, `?q=GM_xmlhttpRequest`, `?q=GM_values`, `?q=include`, `?q=run_at`, `?q=externals`) were not read.

The following come from background knowledge and are all `unverified` until the detail pages and the Violentmonkey and Greasemonkey docs are read:

- `GM_xmlhttpRequest` / `GM.xmlHttpRequest` is the manager's CORS-free request API; Tampermonkey requires `@connect` entries for target hosts and prompts the user otherwise; `@grant` must list each `GM_*` or `GM.*` function used.
- `GM_setValue`/`GM_getValue` persist per script in the manager's storage, no fixed small quota known; use a ttl-wrapped cache like the extension's.
- Same-origin `fetch` from a script running on `store.steampowered.com` needs no `@connect` (inference from web standards; confirm).
- Greasemonkey 4+ exposes the promise-based `GM.*` namespace; Tampermonkey and Violentmonkey support both `GM_*` and `GM.*`.

Observed in the wild: a Greasy Fork Steam userscript uses `GM_xmlhttpRequest` with `anonymous: true` for store pages. (Source: https://greasyfork.org/scripts/587297-steam-gamestatus, via search summary)

### 2b. Sharing one codebase between extension and userscript

- `vite-plugin-monkey` builds userscripts for Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey, Greasemonkey and ScriptCat, injects the metadata block, collects the `GM_*` APIs the code imports to produce `@grant` automatically, and supports `@require`/`@resource` and a single-file output. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lisonge/vite-plugin-monkey/main/README.md) The readme does not describe browser-extension output.
- WXT and plasmo: not researched in this run; any claim about their cross-browser manifest generation or userscript support is `unverified`.
- Precedent for one tree, many targets: Augmented Steam is one typescript/svelte source tree built per browser with build-time flags (`__CHROME`, `__EDGE`) and a `manifestBuilder.mjs` that emits per-browser manifests. (Sources: https://github.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Background/Modules/Dom/DomParserFactory.ts, manifestBuilder.mjs above)
- Recommended shape (inference): a pure `core` module (appid discovery from the DOM, disclosure parsing, cache TTL logic, throttling queue) with two thin adapters behind one interface: `fetchText(url)` and `kv.get/set`. Extension adapter = `runtime.sendMessage` to the background plus `storage.local`; userscript adapter = `GM.xmlHttpRequest` (or plain same-origin `fetch`) plus `GM.setValue`. Build the extension with a vite-based tool and the userscript with vite-plugin-monkey from the same `core`.

### 3a. Which pages are server-rendered versus react, and how known extensions attach badges

Augmented Steam's current selector list for classic store capsules (from a file marked `@deprecated`, with a successor `HighlightsTagsUtils2.ts` not read): `.tab_item`, `.newonsteam_headercap`, `.comingsoon_headercap`, `.store_capsule`, `.dailydeal_ctn`, `.special.special_img_ctn`, `.store_main_capsule`, `.home_marketing_message[data-ds-appid]`, `.home_area_spotlight`, `.curator_giant_capsule`, `.home_content_item`, `.search_result_row`, `.small_cap`, `.game_area_dlc_row`, `.browse_tag_game`, `.similar_grid_item`, `.recommendation`, `.recommendation_carousel_item`, `.app_header`, and others. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Content/Modules/Highlights/HighlightsTagsUtils.ts) The list covers home, tag/browse, discovery/recommendation and search surfaces, which implies those surfaces still expose classic markup; it is not proof of which are react (inference).

ID extraction: `AppId.fromElement` reads `element.dataset.dsAppid` first, then falls back to the `href` attribute parsed with a regex matching `store.steampowered.com|steamcommunity.com` followed by `/app/`, `/games/` or `/market/listings/` plus digits; images fall back to cdn URLs, `data-image-url`. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Core/GameId/AppId.ts; the fetch summary garbled the regex in places; re-read the file before copying it)

Attaching the badge: for each node, take the node or its first `<a>`, resolve app/sub/bundle ID, mark the node with class `es_highlight_checked` to make later passes skip it, create or find a `div.es_tags` container whose placement depends on the node class (for `.tab_item`, prepend into `.tab_item_details`), and append a `<span class="es_tag_<tag>">`. A `clearDisconnectedTags()` pass removes tags whose host nodes have left the DOM. `data-ds-tagids` is read for tag checks. (Sources: HighlightsTagsUtils.ts above; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Content/Features/Store/Wishlist/FWishlistHighlights.ts)

SteamDB's extension does not badge capsules in the files read: its `appicon.js` handles one icon on an app page with a single `querySelector` and no observer. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/BrowserExtension/master/scripts/appicon.js) Augmented Steam is the relevant precedent for list-page badging.

### 3b. Search results and infinite scroll

`FSearchHighlights` does not use a MutationObserver. It queries `.search_result_row[data-ds-appid],.search_result_row[data-ds-packageid]` and re-runs on a `searchCompleted` event dispatched on `document`. That event is dispatched by a main-world scriptlet (`executeSearchOverride.js`) which wraps Steam's own `window.ExecuteSearch` and `window.SearchCompleted` and replaces `InitInfiniteScroll.oController.SetPageChangedHandler` to make infinite-scroll page loads also dispatch it. Each run re-queries every row, including old ones. (Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Content/Features/Store/Search/FSearchHighlights.ts, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/scriptlets/Store/Search/executeSearchOverride.js) That explains why its manifest has a `world: "MAIN"`, `run_at: document_start` content script on store and community. (Source: manifest.mjs above)

Tradeoff (inference): hooking Steam's globals is exact but brittle and needs main-world injection (Firefox 128+, see 1e); a debounced `MutationObserver` on a stable container plus an `a[href*="/app/"]` scan works in a userscript with no page-global access and survives renames of Steam's functions.

### 3c. React surfaces (wishlist) and mutation observers

The wishlist is client-rendered. Augmented Steam's `WishlistDOM` finds the list through build-hashed class names (section `section.jGMVnjZbmZM-`, list `.PLkUpk974nY-.Panel`, row `.PE-3oq-yIvg-.Panel`, title link `a.I8vuMMV-osE-[href*='/app/']`), observes the section with `{subtree: true, childList: true, characterData: true}` (no `attributes`), rebuilds a snapshot and dispatches `onUpdate` on any mutation with no debounce. The hashed names are literal selectors; a Steam redeploy that changes them breaks it; the observer is bound to the original section node and would watch a detached node if react replaced it; its own DOM edits can retrigger it. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsThereAnyDeal/AugmentedSteam/master/src/js/Content/Features/Store/Wishlist/Utils/WishlistDOM.ts; class names are a snapshot of the master branch at fetch time and may already be stale)

Design consequences (inference): anchor on the stable `/app/<id>` href rather than hashed classes; observe a high container (`document.body` or the nearest stable ancestor) with `childList + subtree`; debounce; mark processed nodes with a data attribute and re-verify on each pass because react can re-render and drop injected children; ignore mutations caused by the extension's own badge nodes.

`unverified`: which of the store home carousels, discovery queue, tag/category hubs and sale/event pages are react-rendered in October 2026. Not checked directly; the Augmented Steam selector list suggests classic markup on several, and sale/event pages are widely reported to be react, but no source was fetched. Inspect each surface in devtools before choosing a strategy per page.

### 4a. Rate limits on store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails

There is no official Valve statement of a rate limit for `/api/appdetails` in the sources read. The "about 200 requests per 5 minutes" figure appears in (1) a community wiki page (https://github.com/Revadike/InternalSteamWebAPI/wiki/Get-App-Details) and (2) a blog post that says "i read somewhere" it is around 200 per 5 minutes and recommends caching (https://blog.kartones.net/post/steam-web-api-introduction/, published 2019-12-01). These count as one unofficial claim with no independent confirmation, `unverified` against Valve. One search summary of an apis.io profile claims storefront endpoints are unofficial and 429 quickly above roughly 1 request per second per IP (https://apis.io/rate-limits/steam/steam-rate-limits/); also `unverified`. The two numbers conflict (200 per 300 s is about 0.67 per second); design for the stricter.

Other `appdetails` facts from the same community wiki: `appids` accepts a comma list up to 100 only when `filters=price_overview`; otherwise multiple appids return a 400 with a `null` body; the disclosure lookup costs one request per app. (Source: https://github.com/Revadike/InternalSteamWebAPI/wiki/Get-App-Details; read via one fetch summary)

Consequences of hitting limits: HTTP 429. SteamDB's extension backs off on 429 using `Retry-After` (default 60 s) plus up to 10 s of random jitter, and returns a "Rate limited" error to callers during the wait. (Source: SteamDB background.js above) Augmented Steam's `SteamStoreApi.ts` shows no 429 handling in the file read. Forum reports describe per-ip 429 blocks on other store/community endpoints (market, inventory) lasting hours and refreshing on repeated hits; applicability to `appdetails` is `unverified`. (Source: search result summary of Steam community threads, e.g. https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/6670425060412516194) Browser extensions that issue extra requests share the user's IP budget with the user's own Steam browsing; a heavy crawler in every user's browser can degrade the user's own Steam session (inference).

Mitigations: lazy fetch only for capsules in or near the viewport, global concurrency of 1 to 2, a minimum spacing of about 1 s (stricter than the 200/5 min claim), persistent negative and positive cache with long TTLs, a persisted queue, jittered exponential backoff honoring `Retry-After`, and a circuit breaker that pauses all fetching for several minutes after a 429.

### 4b. Steam web API terms (api.steampowered.com)

The terms cap use at 100,000 calls per day, allow distributing Steam Data to end users only for their personal use through a registered "Application", require a privacy policy and disclosure of what Steam Data is stored, forbid presenting the application as endorsed by or affiliated with Valve, forbid uses that violate the Steam Subscriber Agreement or degrade Steam, and let Valve revoke access at its sole discretion. They do not mention scraping or browser extensions. (Source: https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms) The official webapi overview mentions neither a daily cap nor store-host limits. (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi_overview)

Applicability (inference): these terms bind users of a keyed Steam Web API application. An extension that only calls store-host endpoints from the user's browser without a key is not clearly inside them, but the "no implied endorsement" and "no degrading Steam" principles are sensible constraints either way. If the project ever adds a keyed `api.steampowered.com` call, the key cannot be embedded in a public extension or userscript (the overview says do not share keys: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi_overview).

### 4c. Steam Subscriber Agreement

Last updated September 10, 2026 per section 11 of the agreement page (confirmed by two fetches of the page and a third-party capture dated 2026-09-11 at https://conductatlas.com/platform/steam/steam-subscriber-agreement/provision/CA-P-029839/prohibition-on-all-forms-of-automation-on-steam/).

- Section 4.C (automation): "you may not use any form of scripts, bots, macros, or other non-human-controlled systems" for a listed set of purposes: automating account creation, faking gameplay statistics, earning rewards or progress without genuine user input, and automated participation in peer review/overwatch. (source: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ and https://store.steampowered.com/agreement)
- Section 4.D: Valve may enforce using automated detection and human review and may restrict accounts without notice. (Same source)
- Section 2.G: no copying, modifying, decompiling, reverse engineering or creating derivative works of the Content and Services without consent. (Same source)
- The agreement text contains no occurrence of "scrap", "crawl", "spider" or "data mining" (per a fetch search of the English page). (Source: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/english/)

Reading (inference, not legal advice): a read-only overlay that adds a badge in the user's own browser is not one of the section 4.C purposes, and two long-lived store-listed extensions (Augmented Steam, SteamDB) do far more on the same pages, but a mass crawler that fetches thousands of app pages is closer to "non-human-controlled" access. Keep fetching user-driven (pages the user is looking at), throttled and cached.

### 4d. Chrome Web Store policy

- Single purpose: "an extension must have a single purpose that is narrow and easy to understand." (source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies)
- Use of permissions: request the narrowest permissions; avoid future-proofing. Match `https://store.steampowered.com/*` rather than every Steam subdomain. (Same source)
- Privacy: if the product handles any user data an accurate privacy policy must be posted linked in the dashboard; prominent disclosure and affirmative consent are needed for collection. (Sources: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/privacy, policies page above) The privacy page does not define whether reading the appids a user browses counts as user data (`unverified`).
- Limited use: use of user data limited to the single purpose; "collection and use of web browsing activity is prohibited" except as required by a user-facing feature; the restrictions "also apply to scraped content or otherwise automatically gathered user data"; an affirmative limited-use statement must be on a site belonging to the extension. (Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/limited-use) Design implication: do not transmit viewed appids to any server; if a shared flag database is ever added, fetch from it with a fixed request that does not leak browsing history, and write the privacy policy accordingly.
- MV3 code rules: all logic in the package; no script tags to outside resources, no `eval` on fetched strings, no interpreters of remote commands; loading external data and remote config is allowed provided logic stays local; the full functionality must be discernible from submitted code and obfuscation is banned (minification is fine). (Sources: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/mv3-requirements, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/improve-security) Fetching Steam html/json for parsing by packaged code is a data request, not remote code. A remotely updated JSON list of disclosure patterns or selectors is allowed as data, but a remote script of selector logic is not.
- Impersonation and IP: do not represent the product as authorized or endorsed by another company; using "Steam" in the name or the Valve logo is a trademark question the policy excerpt does not settle (`unverified`; add an unaffiliated notice and avoid Valve branding). The working repo name contains profanity; whether that conflicts with listing/metadata policy was not checked (`unverified`). (Source: policies page above)
- Anything that would block publishing (summary): obfuscated or remotely-loaded logic; permissions broader than needed; missing or inaccurate privacy disclosures; transmitting browsing activity; misleading name or endorsement implication. None is inherent to the concept.

### 4e. Mozilla add-on policies (addons.mozilla.org)

- Remote code: add-ons must be self-contained and must not load remote code for execution; request only necessary permissions; do not relax page security headers. (Source: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/publish/add-on-policies/; section numbers as summarized from a single fetch, `unverified`)
- Obfuscation: not allowed; minification allowed but reviewers need the pre-minified source. (Same source)
- Source submission: required for minifiers, bundlers (webpack, browserify; by extension vite), template engines and custom preprocessing. Matching source must be attached to each version with build instructions (readme with OS, tool versions, every command), a lockfile, and open-source local build tools only; reviewers rebuild and compare output to the submitted package, which must match exactly. Default reviewer environment per the page is Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS desktop, node 24.14.0, npm 11.9.0, arm64, 10 GB ram, 6 vcpus, 35 GB disk (two fetches agree; state the build environment in the readme if different, or the submission may be rejected). (Sources: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/publish/source-code-submission/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/extension-workshop/master/src/content/documentation/publish/source-code-submission.md)
- Data collection key: all new extensions from November 3, 2025 must declare `browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions`; use `"required": ["none"]` when nothing is collected or transmitted; built-in consent exists in Firefox desktop 140+ and Android 142+; older versions need `strict_min_version` set accordingly or a custom consent flow; the page does not say what happens if the key is omitted. (Sources: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/firefox-builtin-data-consent/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/extension-workshop/master/src/content/documentation/develop/firefox-builtin-data-consent.md) Augmented Steam declares `required: ["none"]`, `optional: ["websiteContent"]` and `strict_min_version` 140.0. (Source: manifestBuilder.mjs above)
- Add-on ID: an ID at `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id` is required to publish. (Source: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/manifest-v3-migration-guide/)
- The add-on policies do not address scraping third-party sites; closest rules are the data transmission and privacy sections (limit transmission to what is necessary, explicit opt-in for personal data). (Source: policies page above)

## Caveats and version notes

- No HTTP request tool was available; CORS headers, response codes and the real behavior of `/api/appdetails` were not tested; every CORS statement about Steam hosts is from forum and scan reports.
- The userscript half (Tampermonkey `@connect`, `GM_*` semantics, Violentmonkey and Greasemonkey differences) and wxt/plasmo were not read from primary docs. The Tampermonkey documentation index page was all that loaded.
- Augmented Steam files were read from the `master` branch at fetch time; the hashed wishlist class names and the deprecated `HighlightsTagsUtils.ts` may be out of date. The successor `HighlightsTagsUtils2.ts` and `DynamicStore.ts` were not read.
- Several fetch tool outputs were summaries by a small model; where a regex or quote looked garbled (the `AppId` href regex) it is flagged. The Subscriber Agreement 4.C text and date, the AMO source-code environment and the Firefox data-consent dates were each confirmed by at least two fetches.
- `store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails` rate limit: only unofficial figures exist.
- Legal readings in 4b and 4c are not legal advice.
- The 5 MB vs 10 MB Chrome quota conflict between MDN and the Chrome reference is resolved in favor of the Chrome reference.
```

`docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq6-verification-spikes.md`:

```md
# RQ6: Verification spikes 1 to 7 (S1 to S7)

Spikes from step 2 of `docs/plans/steam-ai-reporter-v1.md`, run on 2026-10-20. Spike 8 (S8, libraries and tooling) is in `rq7-library-study.md`.

Environment: the Claude desktop app's built-in Chromium browser, from a European location (prices in EUR). Unless a section says otherwise, the session was logged out and every request used `credentials: "omit"`. Calls ran from a `store.steampowered.com` page through the browser's JavaScript console, spaced at least 0.7 s apart. Fixtures captured during the spikes are listed in `tests/fixtures/README.md`.

## Answer in short

| Spike                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default the code takes                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Spike 1 (S1): batch ceiling and 429 | The ceiling is the URL length: 250 IDs (6,886 characters) passed, 300 IDs (8,236 characters) failed with an unreadable answer. 30 back-to-back 50-ID calls all returned 200; no 429 was triggered. Error answers carry no CORS headers and surface as `TypeError`                     | 50 IDs per call plus a 4,000-character URL guard, one call in flight, 1 s spacing; a `TypeError` opens the breaker like a 429                                                       |
| Spike 2 (S2): item states           | Adult-only, delisted and age-gated apps all return `success: 1` with `extra_details` cookie-less; an invalid ID returns `success: 15` and no `extra_details`; notes are localized when the developer translated them, but the set of disclosing apps did not change with the language | Key results by `id`; missing `extra_details` or `success != 1` is unknown `missing`; dedupe IDs before the call; treat `x-eresult != 1` or a missing `store_items` as a batch error |
| Spike 3 (S3): CORS headers          | CORS is an allow-list of Valve origins: store and community pages can read GetItems, a foreign origin (wikipedia.org) cannot; `x-eresult` is exposed. Steam sends no CORS headers to non-browser clients (posting), whatever the `Origin`                                             | Content script calls GetItems directly where its requests carry the store origin; backoff without `Retry-After` unless spike 1 (S1) shows it                                        |
| Spike 4 (S4): extension fetch       | A content script with no permissions reads GetItems in Chrome 155 and Firefox Nightly 160 (`type: "cors"`, 200); same-origin app page fetches work; `content.fetch` does not exist in MV3                                                                                             | Content script only (ADR 0003, content-script-only runtime): no background, no `host_permissions`                                                                                   |
| Spike 5 (S5): surface map           | Classic surfaces carry `data-ds-appid`; React surfaces (tag, category, specials, developer, wishlist, search suggestions) carry only `/app/<id>` links; the wishlist is a virtualized list                                                                                            | Link-based host finding with the refinements in "Proposed plan changes"; wishlist `hideable: false`                                                                                 |
| Spike 6 (S6): userscript managers   | Tampermonkey 5.5 on Chrome 155 and Firefox Nightly 160: plain `fetch` to GetItems works without `@connect`; `GM.*` values, `GM_addStyle`, a plain `<style>`, `GM_addValueChangeListener` and the menu command all work. Violentmonkey could not be tested                             | Plain `fetch`, no `@connect`; `GM_addStyle` with a `<style>` fallback                                                                                                               |
| Spike 7 (S7): HTML fallback         | `?l=english` cookie-less fetch returns the full page and cannot change the store language; redirects to `/login/` and `/` confirmed; no `/agecheck/` redirect reproducible from this location; the AI block came first on every app with both blocks                                  | Fallback as planned: final URL plus `#appHubAppName` guard, all `#game_area_content_descriptors`, heading match, notes from `p > i`                                                 |

## Spike 1 (S1): batch ceiling and 429

Method: Run last with a VPN on and in a Chrome 155 Incognito window on `https://store.steampowered.com/` while logged out, which kept any account and the home IP out of it. A console script refused to run off the store origin or with a signed-in session. Each call was `fetch(GetItems, {credentials: "omit", cache: "no-store"})` with synthetic IDs (multiples of 10, many invalid). Sequence: a 3-ID baseline; batches of 100, 200, 250, 300 and 400 IDs, 2 s apart; then 30 calls of 50 distinct IDs back to back with no delay, stopping at the first non-200. When a call threw, a second `mode: "no-cors"` request showed whether the server had answered at all.

Result:

| IDs | Encoded URL length | Outcome                                                                | Time     |
| --- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| 3   | 333                | 200, 3 items                                                           | 216 ms   |
| 100 | 2,836              | 200, 100 items                                                         | 551 ms   |
| 200 | 5,536              | 200, 200 items                                                         | 953 ms   |
| 250 | 6,886              | 200, 250 items                                                         | 1,490 ms |
| 300 | 8,236              | `TypeError: Failed to fetch`; the `no-cors` retry got an opaque answer | 277 ms   |
| 400 | 10,936             | Same as 300                                                            | 55 ms    |

- The ceiling is the URL length: 6,886 characters passed and 8,236 failed, which fits the common 8 KB request-line limit of the `nginx` front end (the status was not captured; 414 is the likely code). With real 7-digit app IDs each ID costs about 31 encoded characters; the same limit falls at about 250 IDs.
- Error responses are unreadable. The over-long request was answered without CORS headers; JavaScript saw only a `TypeError` and no status. A 429 from the same front end would very likely look the same, and `Retry-After` will not be readable in practice.
- No rate limit hit. All 30 back-to-back 50-ID calls returned 200 (1,500 IDs in about 17 s, average 557 ms, range 226 to 1,167 ms). No 429 and no `Retry-After` header appeared. Where the real limit lies stays unknown; it is above about 1.8 calls per second sustained for 30 calls from one IP.
- Earlier, a 50-ID call with real IDs (the 50 rows of `/search/?term=roguelike`) returned 50 items in request order in 1.16 s; its URL was 1,741 characters and its body 99,315 bytes (`content-length: 5187`; gzip shrinks it about 19 times). Responses carry `cache-control: private, max-age=120`.

Default the code takes:

- Batches of at most 50 IDs, as planned, with a guard that splits any batch whose encoded URL would exceed 4,000 characters (half the observed limit); the limit is never reached even with longer IDs or a larger context.
- One call in flight, 1 s spacing. Spike 1 (S1) shows ample headroom; these stay as safety margins for the user's own browsing on the same IP, and none is a measured limit.
- A `TypeError` from GetItems counts like a 429: open the breaker with the fixed backoff (60 s plus up to 10 s of jitter) and treat the batch as unknown `rate-limited`. `Retry-After` is read only if it ever becomes readable.

## Spike 2 (S2): age gate and item states

Method: Cookie-less GetItems calls with `data_request.include_extra_details: true` and context `english`/`US` for 1938090 (violence descriptors), 339800 (adult only), 99999999 (invalid), 50300 and 241560 (delisted), then 5072580, 1808500 and 1938090 in `english`, `german`, `french`, `japanese` and `schinese`, then the 50-row roguelike batch in `english`/`US` and `german`/`DE`. Edge cases: duplicate IDs, an empty `ids` list, no `context`, and malformed `input_json`.

Result:

| App                          | `success` | `visible` | `extra_details`                                         | Notes                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | --------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1938090 Call of Duty         | 1         | true      | yes, with `content_survey_ai_notes`                     | Not gated in the API                                         |
| 339800 HuniePop (adult only) | 1         | true      | yes, no AI notes; mature text in `content_survey_notes` | Not gated in the API, although its page redirects to sign-in |
| 99999999 (invalid)           | 15        | false     | absent                                                  | `id` echoes the request, `appid` is `0`, `name` is empty     |
| 50300, 241560 (delisted)     | 1         | true      | yes                                                     | Extra key `unlisted: true`                                   |

- For 5072580 and 1808500 the notes were identical in all five languages. Call of Duty returned translated notes in each language (German 85 characters, Japanese 33, Simplified Chinese 29, English 70) and a localized `name`. In the 50-row batch the same 10 apps disclosed in English and German; 3 of the 10 had different German text. Presence does not depend on the language; the text does when the developer translated it.
- Items come back in request order. Duplicate IDs are not merged: `[413150, 413150]` returned two items.
- `ids: []` returns 200 `{"response":{}}` with `x-eresult: 1`. A request without `context`, or with no `input_json` at all, returns 200 `{"response":{}}` with `x-eresult: 8`. A malformed `input_json` returns 400 with an HTML body ("Invalid input_json parameter").
- Headers readable from the store origin: `cache-control`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `expires`, `x-eresult`. The last one is not CORS-safelisted; the server exposes it.
- Notes can contain `\r\n` line breaks, trailing spaces and zero-width spaces (`U+200B`), for example 5269270 in the roguelike batch.

Default the code takes:

- Map results by `id` (the requested ID), never by `appid`, which is `0` for invalid items.
- Disclosed when `success === 1` and `extra_details.content_survey_ai_notes` is non-empty after trimming whitespace (including `U+200B`). Not disclosed when `success === 1` and `extra_details` is present without notes. Unknown `missing` otherwise.
- Dedupe IDs before building a batch.
- A 200 response is a batch error when `x-eresult` is present and not `1`, or when `store_items` is missing although IDs were sent.
- Normalize `\r\n` to `\n` before rendering; render with `white-space: pre-line`.
- GetItems runs in the page's language (decided; see "Proposed plan changes", item 5); presence is the same in every language, and the notes come back in the developer's translation where one exists.

Fixtures: `getitems/mixed-states.json`, `getitems/german-context.json`, `getitems/search-roguelike-50.json`, `getitems/empty-response.json`.

## Spike 3 (S3): CORS headers

Method: The `posting/` collection (`posting/README.md`) ran, and its `on_response` hook saved every response's headers: GetItems with `Origin` set to `https://store.steampowered.com`, `https://example.com`, `moz-extension://<uuid>`, `chrome-extension://<id>` and none, plus two app page requests with redirects not followed. Because posting cannot send a browser's `Sec-Fetch-*` headers, the CORS decision was then checked in the built-in browser, which does enforce CORS: from a store page, a `help.steampowered.com` or `steamcommunity.com` HTML fetch fails. GetItems was then called from pages on three origins.

Result:

- posting: every GetItems response was 200 with the same headers (`server`, `content-type`, `x-eresult`, `vary: Accept-Encoding`, `content-encoding`, `content-length`, `cache-control: private, max-age=120`, `expires`, `date`, `connection`) and no `access-control-*` header for any Origin, the store origin included. Since a browser on the store origin does pass CORS (below), Steam must decide from request headers that a browser sends and posting does not, such as `Sec-Fetch-*` or `Referer` (inference; the exact trigger was not isolated). Posting therefore cannot show the allow-list.
- Browser:

| Page origin                      | `fetch(GetItems)`                  | `mode: "no-cors"` | Meaning                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `https://store.steampowered.com` | 200, `type: "cors"`, body readable | n/a               | Allowed                                  |
| `https://steamcommunity.com`     | 200, `type: "cors"`, body readable | n/a               | Allowed                                  |
| `https://www.wikipedia.org`      | `TypeError: Failed to fetch`       | 200 opaque        | Blocked by CORS (the network path works) |

CORS on GetItems is an allow-list of Valve origins; a wildcard `*` would have admitted wikipedia.org. A content script whose requests carry the store page's origin can read GetItems; a request carrying a `moz-extension://` or `chrome-extension://` origin falls outside the list; only a host permission (which lifts CORS for extension pages and background scripts) would make it readable.

- Exposed headers readable from the store origin: `cache-control`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `expires` (all CORS-safelisted) and `x-eresult`. The `access-control-expose-headers` header therefore names `x-eresult`. Whether it names `retry-after` cannot be seen without a 429 (see spike 1).
- On the cookie-less app page, `/app/413150/?l=english` returned 200 and set only the `steamCountry` and `sessionid` cookies, no language cookie. `/app/339800/?l=english` returned 302 with `location: https://store.steampowered.com/agecheck/app/339800/?l=english`, which then leads to sign-in (spike 7). The `content-security-policy` header matches spike 5 (S5).

Default the code takes: The content script calls GetItems directly with `credentials: "omit"` wherever its requests carry the store origin (Chrome, per spike 4). `x-eresult` is read for batch errors (spike 2). 429 backoff uses a fixed delay unless spike 1 (S1) shows that `Retry-After` is readable. ADR 0003 (content-script-only runtime) depends on spike 4 (S4): content script only if Firefox content-script requests carry the page origin, otherwise a background relay with `host_permissions: ["https://api.steampowered.com/*"]` for Firefox.

## Spike 4 (S4): extension fetch

Method: A throwaway MV3 extension (kept outside the repo) with no permissions and one content script on `https://store.steampowered.com/*`. On `/app/1808500/` it called GetItems for 5072580, 1808500 and 413150 with `fetch(url, {credentials: "omit"})`, tried Firefox's `content.fetch`, and fetched `/app/413150/?l=english` same-origin. Loaded unpacked in Chrome 155 and as a temporary add-on in Firefox Nightly 160 (the project's Firefox; see AGENTS.md "Development browsers").

Result:

| Probe                                | Chrome 155                                             | Firefox Nightly 160                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `fetch` GetItems                     | 200, `type: "cors"`, 3 items, 2 disclosed, 237 ms      | 200, `type: "cors"`, 3 items, 2 disclosed, 298 ms            |
| Readable headers                     | safelisted plus `x-eresult`                            | same                                                         |
| `content.fetch`                      | not available                                          | not available (no `content` global in an MV3 content script) |
| Same-origin `/app/413150/?l=english` | 200, `type: "basic"`, `#appHubAppName` present, 412 ms | 200, `type: "basic"`, `#appHubAppName` present, 312 ms       |

Given spike 3 (S3), where CORS admits only Valve origins, a readable `cors` response means both browsers sent the content script's request with the store page's origin; an extension origin would have failed. The request header itself was not inspected.

Default the code takes: ADR 0003 (content-script-only runtime) picks that runtime: no background script, no `host_permissions`, permissions exactly `["storage"]`, as invariant 3 (permissions) already states. Plain `fetch` in both browsers; `content.fetch` is not used.

## Spike 5 (S5): surface map

Method: Each surface was opened in the built-in browser, first logged out, then logged in for the wishlist, the discovery queue and the logged-in home page. A console script counted `[data-ds-appid]` elements and `a[href*="/app/"]` links, read `<html lang>` and the `content-security-policy` header (same-origin `HEAD`), and tested three host rules (see "Host finding"). Capsule containers were cut out of the live DOM, sanitized and saved under `tests/fixtures/surfaces/`. Selectors below come from these observations only.

Result:

| Surface                                          | Rendering                                                            | IDs on capsules                                                                     | Capsule element                                                                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App page `/app/<id>/`                            | Classic server HTML with React islands (`[data-featuretarget]`)      | `data-ds-appid` on DLC rows                                                         | `a.game_area_dlc_row`                                                                       | Banner anchor: `.game_description_column` starts with `#game_area_purchase` on released, coming-soon and demo pages. The right column shows a `.DRM_notice` "Connects to 3rd-Party Service for AI Content Generation" when `ai_generation_service` is set (5072580)               |
| Search `/search/`                                | Classic                                                              | `data-ds-appid` (single IDs only)                                                   | `a.search_result_row` in `#search_resultsRows`                                              | Infinite scroll appends the next 50 rows to the same container                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Home `/`                                         | Classic, plus React rows                                             | `data-ds-appid`; comma lists only next to `data-ds-packageid` or `data-ds-bundleid` | `a.store_main_capsule` (CSS background image, no `img`), `a.sale_capsule`, `a.tab_row_item` | The React rows (`discounts-and-events`, `discovery-queue-home`, `personal-calendar-home`) stayed empty in the automated session, logged in or out, and they go to the manual checklist. Logged in, owned and wishlisted capsules get `ds_flagged`                                 |
| Tag hub `/tags/en/<tag>/`                        | React `sale-display`, hashed class names                             | Links only                                                                          | `div.Panel` grid capsule; large `LibraryAssetExpandedDisplay` carousel capsule              | Stable semantic classes next to the hashed ones: `CapsuleImageCtn`, `CapsuleDecorators`, `SaleSectionContainer`, `HeroCapsuleImageContainer`                                                                                                                                      |
| Category hub `/category/<name>/` and `/specials` | Same React `sale-display` template as the tag hub                    | Links only                                                                          | Same as the tag hub                                                                         | Covered by the tag hub fixture                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Developer `/developer/<name>`                    | React creator home                                                   | Links only                                                                          | `StoreSaleWidgetOuterContainer`                                                             | Publisher pages use the creator home template too (not visited)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Wishlist `/wishlist/`                            | React, virtualized                                                   | Links only; the drag row ID is `WishlistItem-<appid>-0`                             | `div.Panel[data-index]`                                                                     | Redirects to `/wishlist/id/<vanity>/`. An inner scroll container holds an absolutely positioned list moved with `translateY`; with 602 items only 16 to 28 rows are mounted. Rows scrolled out are unmounted and new elements are mounted (no element was reused for another app) |
| Discovery queue `/explore/`                      | Classic                                                              | Link only                                                                           | `.discovery_queue_static` preview                                                           | The queue overlay was not opened, because stepping through it changes the account's queue                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Search suggestions                               | React, inside the header root `[data-featuretarget="store-menu-v7"]` | Links only                                                                          | `a` with an `img` per result                                                                | Results come from `api.steampowered.com/IStoreQueryService/SearchSuggestions`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Old `steamcommunity.com/profiles/<id>/wishlist/` | Redirect                                                             | n/a                                                                                 | n/a                                                                                         | Redirects to `store.steampowered.com/wishlist/id/<vanity>/`; no community match needed                                                                                                                                                                                            |

- App links take four shapes: `/app/<id>/<slug>/?snr=...` (classic), `/app/<id>/<slug>?snr=...` (React, no trailing slash), `/app/<id>?snr=...` (no slug) and `/app/<id>/?snr=...#app_reviews_hash` (review score links). Every one was absolute on `https://store.steampowered.com`.
- `<html lang>` follows the Steam language: `english` en, `german` de, `french` fr, `spanish` es, `latam` es-419, `portuguese` pt, `brazilian` pt-br, `schinese` zh-cn, `tchinese` zh-tw, `japanese` ja, `koreana` ko, `russian` ru, `ukrainian` uk, `polish` pl, `turkish` tr, `thai` th, `vietnamese` vi, `indonesian` id, `arabic` ar, `czech` cs, `danish` da, `dutch` nl, `finnish` fi, `greek` el, `hungarian` hu, `italian` it, `norwegian` no, `romanian` ro, `swedish` sv, `bulgarian` bg.
- The CSP is identical on the app page, search, home, tag, category, specials and developer pages: `default-src blob: data: https: 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'`, with `script-src`, `object-src`, `connect-src`, `frame-src` and `frame-ancestors`, and no `style-src`. Inline styles therefore fall back to `default-src`, which allows them: a `<style>` element inserted from the console applied. `connect-src` lists `https://api.steampowered.com/`; page-context code (a userscript injected into the page) may call GetItems.
- On logged-in pages, `#application_config[data-userinfo]` holds the Steam ID and account name. The fixture sanitizer removes that element; product code must never read it.

Three rules for finding hosts were compared on the tag hub (56 app links, 27 apps):

- The plan's rule, "highest ancestor up to 8 levels whose links all name one app", gave the right capsule in most cases but climbed into a 1326 x 663 px `SaleSectionTabListContainer` when a tab section showed a single app.
- "Lowest ancestor that contains an image" never overshot, but on carousel capsules the image link and the title block are siblings; it produced two hosts for one capsule.
- "Lowest image-bearing ancestor, then climb at most 3 more levels while the links still name one app, then drop hosts nested in another host of the same app" gave one host per capsule and no section-sized host. It returned the same host counts as the plan's rule (43 hosts for 27 apps; repeats are carousel clones and apps listed in several sections).
- The home main carousel capsule has no `img`; its image is a CSS `background-image` on a child `div`. An "image" test must accept an inline `background-image` too.
- The header root holds the search suggestions; the scanner cannot skip the header wholesale. Its navigation links have no images, and the image test drops them.

Default the code takes: Candidates come from `[data-ds-appid]` with a single numeric ID, then from `a[href]` whose URL is on `store.steampowered.com` with a path matching `^/app/(\d+)(?:[/?#]|$)`. Hosts follow the third rule above. Wishlist rows are `hideable: false`. Locale `auto` maps `<html lang>` through the table above.

Fixtures: `surfaces/search/rows.html`, `surfaces/home/capsules.html`, `surfaces/tag-hub/capsules.html`, `surfaces/developer/widgets.html`, `surfaces/wishlist/rows.html`, `surfaces/search-suggestions/popup.html`, plus the DLC rows in `app-page/1808500-ai-only.html`.

## Spike 6 (S6): userscript managers

Method: A throwaway userscript (kept outside the repo) with `@match https://store.steampowered.com/*`, `@noframes`, `@run-at document-idle`, no `@connect`, and `@grant` for `GM.getValue`, `GM.setValue`, `GM.deleteValue`, `GM.listValues`, `GM_addStyle`, `GM.registerMenuCommand`, `GM_addValueChangeListener` and `GM_info`. On `/app/1808500/` it called GetItems with plain `fetch`, round-tripped an object through the `GM.*` value calls, injected a rule with `GM_addStyle` and another through a plain `<style>` element, registered a value change listener and a menu command, and reported `GM_info.injectInto` and `GM_info.sandboxMode`.

Result:

| Check                                                     | Chrome 155, Tampermonkey 5.5.1      | Firefox Nightly 160, Tampermonkey 5.5.0 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Plain `fetch` to GetItems, no `@connect`                  | 200, 2 items                        | 200, 2 items                            |
| `GM.setValue` / `getValue` / `listValues` / `deleteValue` | all pass; objects stored as objects | same                                    |
| `GM_addStyle`                                             | applies                             | applies                                 |
| Plain `<style>` element                                   | applies                             | applies                                 |
| `GM_addValueChangeListener`                               | fires locally with `remote = false` | same                                    |
| `GM.registerMenuCommand`                                  | the menu entry runs its callback    | same                                    |
| Context                                                   | `sandboxMode: "raw"` (page context) | `sandboxMode: "raw"`                    |

Violentmonkey was not tested. Its `@inject-into` fallback therefore stays unverified; Steam's CSP allows inline scripts (`script-src 'unsafe-inline'`, spike 5); Violentmonkey's default page injection should not need the fallback.

Default the code takes: Plain `fetch` with no `@connect` and no `GM.xmlHttpRequest`; `GM_addStyle` with a `<style>` element fallback (both work under Steam's CSP); settings apply live through `GM_addValueChangeListener` where it exists.

## Spike 7 (S7): HTML fallback

Method: From a store page: `fetch("/app/<id>/?l=english", {credentials: "omit"})` for 413150, 5072580, 1808500, 1938090, 339800, 99999999, 50300 and 4618750, plus six more apps with mature descriptors (271590, 1174180, 782330, 1091500, 1245620, 2050650) to look for an age check. Language stickiness: a top-level visit to `/app/1808500/?l=german`, then a visit without `l`. Block order: every app with both blocks among those sampled.

Result:

- 413150 returned 200, no redirect, 136 KB, `lang="en"`, `#appHubAppName` present, in about 1.4 s. Pages ran from 104 KB to 351 KB. One HTML fetch costs about as much as a 50-item GetItems call.
- The top-level `?l=german` visit rendered German (`lang="de"`); the next visit without `l` was English again, and no language cookie was readable. A `credentials: "omit"` fetch neither sends nor stores cookies and cannot change the store language, logged in or not.
- 339800 (adult only) ended at `/login/?redir=...%2Fagecheck%2Fapp%2F339800%2F%3Fl%3Denglish` with a 200 "Sign In" page. 99999999 ended at `/` (the 960 KB home page). `Response.redirected` was true for both. Delisted 50300 served a normal page with `#appHubAppName` and no block.
- None of the seven mature apps redirected to `/agecheck/` from this location; even a direct `/agecheck/app/1938090/` bounced back to the app page. rq2 saw the redirect through a third-party fetcher in another region; the redirect depends on the region. The agecheck fixture is synthetic.
- The AI block came before the mature block on all four apps that have both (5072580, 1938090, 4431800, 4461450). The mature-first fixture is synthetic.
- After Steam's scripts run, the block sits in `.game_page_autocollapse_ctn > .game_page_autocollapse[style="max-height: none;"]` with a `.game_page_autocollapse_fade` "READ MORE" sibling. `#game_area_content_descriptors > h2` still matches.
- 4618750's notes are `...product.\r\n\r\nThe game does not use AI...` in GetItems. The page renders `<br>` tags, each followed by a newline in the source; `textContent` keeps the breaks. The text inside `<i>` starts with a newline and five tabs and ends with four tabs.
- The app page's `apppage-store-browse-cache` mount carries GetItems data for the current app, but without `include_extra_details`; it has no AI notes.

Default the code takes: As planned: unknown `gated` when the final URL is under `/agecheck/` or `/login/` or not under `/app/<id>`, or when `#appHubAppName` is missing; otherwise collect every `#game_area_content_descriptors`, keep the one whose trimmed `h2` is `AI Generated Content Disclosure`, and read the notes from `p > i` with trimming. At most 10 HTML fetches per page view.

Fixtures: everything under `tests/fixtures/app-page/`.

## Proposed plan changes

Each item names the plan section it touches.

1. Step 5, parser: key results by `id`, dedupe IDs before the call, and treat `x-eresult != 1` (readable cross-origin) or a missing `store_items` as a batch error.
2. Step 9, host finding: replace "highest ancestor, at most 8 levels" with "lowest ancestor that contains an `img` or an inline `background-image`, then at most 3 more levels while every link names the same app; drop a host nested in another host of the same app". Do not skip `[data-featuretarget="store-menu-v7"]` wholesale (it hosts the search suggestions); the image test drops navigation links.
3. Step 9, app link parsing: accept `/app/<id>` followed by `/`, `?`, `#` or the end; React links have no trailing slash.
4. Step 13, placements: the wishlist is virtualized; set `hideable: false`. Its rows also expose the app ID as `data-rfd-draggable-id="WishlistItem-<appid>-0"`, a second source next to the links.
5. Step 10, display language (decided on 2026-10-20): spike 2 (S2) showed that notes are localized when the developer translated them, but that the set of disclosing apps does not change. Of the two options:
   - As planned: detect in English; on the app page, one extra GetItems call in the store language for the banner.
   - Query every batch in the page's language (`<html lang>` mapped back to the Steam name): no extra banner call, and badge tooltips are localized too. The cache record stores the language; the banner re-fetches only that one app if the cached language differs.
     The second option won: GetItems runs in the page's language. Step 10's "detection always uses English" line and the matching review decision ("detection stays on English") change accordingly; the HTML fallback still fetches `?l=english`, because it matches the English heading.
6. Step 8, locale mapping: use the `<html lang>` table in spike 5 (S5) for `auto`.
7. Risks: add "the adult-only app page redirects to sign-in cookie-less, but GetItems answers for it"; the old risk "adult-only apps may stay unknown" no longer holds for the API path. Mark "Firefox content-script fetch may fail CORS" as resolved (spike 4), and "`Retry-After` is probably unreadable" as confirmed in practice (spike 1: error answers carry no CORS headers).
8. Step 3, ADR 0003 (content-script-only runtime): spikes 3 and 4 (S3, S4) pick the content-script-only runtime; the relay branch in step 3 ("If spike 3 or 4 showed ...") can be dropped. Invariant 3 stands as written.
9. Steps 5 and 7, batching and backoff: keep 50 IDs per call, and add a guard that splits a batch whose encoded GetItems URL would exceed 4,000 characters (spike 1 found the server limit between 6,886 and 8,236). Treat a `TypeError` from GetItems like a 429 (breaker, fixed backoff), because error answers are unreadable cross-origin.
10. Step 12, userscript: spike 6 (S6) confirms no `@connect` and no `GM.xmlHttpRequest` for Tampermonkey on Chrome and Firefox Nightly; the "manager that failed in spike 6" branch is not needed for Tampermonkey. Violentmonkey stays untested and goes on the manual checklist.

## Caveats

- One browser, one region, one day. The age check redirect and the CSP may differ elsewhere.
- Logged-in checks used a personal account in the built-in browser. To capture wishlist rows without publishing the account's wishlist, two neutral apps (5072580 and 3664320) were added, captured and removed again with permission; the wishlist count returned to its earlier value.
- React sections that render only when scrolled into a visible viewport (home rows) were not captured.
- Spike 1 (S1) ran over a VPN exit IP with synthetic IDs (many invalid), once. Steam may rate-limit residential IPs, other regions or heavier items differently; the 429 behaviour itself was never observed.
- Spikes 3, 4 and 6 (S3, S4, S6) ran on a local machine; their results come from the text the throwaway scripts printed, with no request-header inspection.

## Sources

- `https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1` with `input_json` as described per spike (keyless, cookie-less).
- `https://store.steampowered.com/app/<id>/?l=english` for the apps named in spike 7 (S7); `https://store.steampowered.com/login/?l=<language>` for the `<html lang>` table.
```
