`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds.md`:

```md
# Steam store disclosure kinds

## Executive summary

Steam publishes all four disclosure kinds in `extra_details`, the object that `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` returns when `include_extra_details` is set. The extension makes that request today, and the new kinds need no new host, permission or request. Kernel-level anti-cheat has an explicit flag (`kernel_mode`). Third-party DRM, EULA and third-party account or launcher are free text or links typed by the publisher, and no field names a launcher. Every kind is self-reported, and an absent key means "not declared", never "none". The page text is localized in every language checked, while `GetItems` values are language-neutral. Detection should read `GetItems` first, and the page only for what `GetItems` omits, such as custom anti-cheat names and the activation limit. The Oct 22 change was real but removed only the old reviews endpoint; nothing found touches these fields. Community datasets track Linux compatibility, carry no kernel field and live on non-Valve hosts. Every icon set checked allows commercial use, and Lucide and Phosphor fit best.

## Research questions

### RQ1: What does Steam record per kind, and who declares it?

Steam keeps all four kinds in one object, `extra_details`, which `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` returns when `include_extra_details` is set. Anti-cheat is the only kind with a public Valve rule (a Steamworks post of 2024-10-30). Every kind is self-reported. Note: [rq1-declarations.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq1-declarations.md).

- The fields are `anticheat` (an object with `kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection`, `boot_protection_name`, `name` and `name_loc`), `drm_third_party_type` and `drm_activation_limit` (strings), `user_account_third_party` (a string) with `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (a bool), and `eula` (a list of name and URL). Every field is optional: a missing key means "not recorded" and never "none".
- No field names a required launcher. It appears inside the DRM or account free text. The publisher types those values, and "Denuvo", "Denuvo Anti-tamper" and "Denuvo Anti-Tampering" all name one vendor. Plain text matching is fragile.
- Press reports the anti-cheat declaration as mandatory for new submissions with a client-side kernel-mode anti-cheat, and optional for other anti-cheat. Valve contacts partners of older games, with no deadline found. No public Valve rule or start date turned up for DRM, account or EULA.
- Nothing shows Valve inspecting binaries. Press says Valve checks that anti-cheat notices are present and correct. No penalty was found for any kind.
- Unverified: the original 2024-10-30 post (its body would not load, and everything about it comes from press), the second anti-cheat checkbox and its polarity, the rules and dates for DRM, account and EULA (partner pages sit behind a login), and the sources of the "RICOCHET" and activation-limit examples.

### RQ2: Where does each kind appear in data?

`GetItems` with `include_extra_details` carries all four kinds as typed fields in `store_items[].extra_details`, and any surface that batches IDs can read them with no new request. The app page and `appdetails` add detail that `GetItems` omits. 32 apps and one 63-ID batch were read. Note: [rq2-data-surface-by-kind.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq2-data-surface-by-kind.md).

- A key is omitted when nothing is declared. No `false` or empty string showed up; there was one empty object (`anticheat: {}`, Marvel Rivals). Without `include_extra_details` the whole `extra_details` object is absent. In the 63-ID batch, 35 items came back with `success: 15` and no `extra_details`. The existing detector chain already treats that case as unknown. A follow-up request on 2026-10-24 covered 13 apps in one batch, nine of them with no declaration of any kind: Animal Well, Hades, Stardew Valley, Celeste, Hollow Knight, Balatro, Terraria, Portal 2 and Half-Life 2. All nine returned `success: 1` with an `extra_details` object that lacks all four kinds. The Animal Well page has no `.DRM_notice`, `.anticheat_section` or `/eula/` link. An omitted key under a present `extra_details` therefore reads as "not reported".
- `anticheat` has three states in the data: `kernel_mode: true`; an `anticheat` object without `kernel_mode` (Counter-Strike 2 and Dota 2 carry a VAC `name` and `name_loc`, Marvel Rivals carries `{}`); and no `anticheat` key. `kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely` and `boot_protection` are booleans. Only `true` ever appeared, and false looks omitted (an inference from protobuf defaults). `boot_protection_name` was only ever `secureboot_tpm2`.
- Denuvo shows up in two fields on different apps: `drm_third_party_type` (9 apps, 5 spellings, for example "Denuvo Anti-tamper") and `anticheat.name` (ARC Raiders, with the token `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo`). No app showed both.
- Launchers and accounts are free text: 12 distinct strings across 9 publishers, plus a bool that says whether the account links to Steam. `anticheat.name` is a closed set of tokens. A custom anti-cheat leaves `name` out, and its name ("EA Javelin Anticheat", "NetEase Game Security") appears only in the page HTML.
- On the page, DRM, account, EULA and kernel anti-cheat are `div.DRM_notice` children of `#category_block`. Kernel anti-cheat is `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice`, non-kernel anti-cheat is `.anticheat_section.anticheat_nonkernel_notice`, and the EULA block is `.DRM_notice[role=button]` with an `/eula/` link. The DRM and account blocks share one class and differ only by their text prefix.
- `appdetails` has `drm_notice` and `ext_user_account_notice` and nothing for anti-cheat or EULA. The DRM activation limit is in the page and `appdetails`, in no `GetItems` field read.
- A 63-ID request returned 63 items, which makes the 50-ID figure a project choice and not the server limit. The true ceiling stayed unknown, because the fetch tool rejected a 120-ID URL.
- Unverified: the protobuf field types, the boot-protection selector and other boot tokens, Vanguard, several single-read strings (such as "Denuvo Anti-Temper"), and why `GetItems` omits a custom anti-cheat name. The researcher also passed its fetch cap (about 46).

### RQ3: What changed around 2026-10-22?

The Oct 22 change is real, and it is narrower than "the store APIs". Valve announced on 2026-10-02 that it would disable `store.steampowered.com/appreviews/<appid>?json=1` on October 22, and it did. On 2026-10-24 that URL returns the store home page as HTML. The replacement is `api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/`, and it answers without a key. Nothing found changes `GetItems`, `appdetails` or the app page for the four disclosure kinds. Note: [rq3-oct-2026-changes.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq3-oct-2026-changes.md).

- The project does not call the reviews endpoint, and the removal does not touch it.
- In the protobuf tracker, the field numbers, names and scalar types of `anticheat`, `eula`, `drm_third_party_type` and `user_account_third_party` are identical at every October checkpoint read.
- One drift is live: `GetItems` now returns `extra_details.has_community_hub` (field 33, added to the protobuf on 2026-10-21). No fixture captured on 2026-10-20 has it. The project's `GetItems` schema (`getitems.schema.ts`) names only the fields it uses, so an extra key is harmless today.
- The announcement says the new endpoint needs a key and the docs say it does not. A keyless call worked on 2026-10-24.
- Unverified: live app-page markup (class names) was not compared with the fixtures, no baseline exists for `appdetails`, the Steam news, SteamDB changelist and Steamworks API changelog were not checked, and the protobuf comparisons come from summaries, not raw diffs.

### RQ4: How stable and localized are the signals?

Every notice string on the app page is localized. Text cannot serve as a detection key. `GetItems` returns language-neutral values for all four kinds. Note: [rq4-stability-localization.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq4-stability-localization.md).

- Seven store languages were checked on one app, and german and spanish also on a kernel anti-cheat app. Each notice string differs per language, and latam is a separate translation from spanish. The stable page hooks are `.anticheat_section` (with `DRM_notice` for kernel, `anticheat_nonkernel_notice` for non-kernel), `.anticheat_name`, `.anticheat_uninstalls` and `a[href*="/eula/"]`. `.DRM_notice` also holds the account line, the EULA line and the AI-service line. Its count says nothing per kind.
- `GetItems` `extra_details` stayed language-neutral under a german context for every field these kinds use. `anticheat.name_loc` is a token, and five were seen: vac, easyac, battleye, ace and denuvo. Only the content survey text and item names localize.
- `GetItems` is a subset of the page. The activation-limit line and custom anti-cheat names show on the page and are absent from `GetItems` for the apps tested. Older titles also keep anti-cheat names inside `drm_third_party_type`.
- Coverage: apps, DLC, demos and software return `extra_details`. Packages return none. A missing app and bundle 1 return `success: 15`. A delisted app stays `success: 1` with `unlisted: true`. Some mature apps redirect cookie-less page fetches to `/agecheck/` for some clients and adult-only apps go to login. `GetItems` was never gated.
- History: the anti-cheat declaration tool dates from 2024-10-30. The DRM, account and EULA notices are older, but the only evidence is a 2014 forum thread.
- Unverified: markup history (the Wayback Machine was blocked), the markup of the DRM and activation lines, region-restricted and valid-bundle behavior, and when the public protobuf gained `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` (it is absent through 2025-08-29). The researcher passed its fetch cap (about 60) and read element classes through a third-party selector API until it hit a rate limit.

### RQ5: What do Steam's fields miss, and how do other tools cover it?

Steam holds all four kinds as developer-typed fields, and Steam's own `kernel_mode` flag is the only explicit kernel marker anywhere. Nothing is detected from game files. An absent key cannot separate "not declared" from "none". The community datasets track Linux compatibility, carry no kernel field and live on non-Valve hosts. Note: [rq5-gaps-and-community-data.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq5-gaps-and-community-data.md).

- Gaps seen on 2026-10-24: Elden Ring and Rainbow Six Siege have no `anticheat` key, though AreWeAntiCheatYet lists Easy Anti-Cheat for Elden Ring and Valve's Steam Deck report flags an unsupported anti-cheat for Siege. Battlefield 6, Call of Duty and PUBG carry `kernel_mode: true` with no vendor name. Marvel Rivals has an empty `anticheat` object. DOOM: The Dark Ages still carries a Denuvo string months after reports of its removal.
- Steam has no store tag for any of the four kinds (446 tags checked). The one anti-cheat category, id 8, covers Valve's own VAC only.
- The Steam Deck report returns anti-cheat tokens only for tested apps with an unsupported result. It says "does not work on Linux" and never "kernel-level".
- AreWeAntiCheatYet is MIT licensed, with 1,167 games, about 59 percent with a Steam ID and about 60 spellings of vendor names. PCGamingWiki is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and has anti-cheat and DRM fields, but anonymous `cargoquery` was denied. No machine-readable Denuvo or launcher list turned up. The Steam curator "Denuvo Watch" is the one maintained Denuvo tracker found.
- Community sources need a vendor name to derive kernel status. Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, FACEIT and Vanguard are documented kernel drivers. Ricochet, nProtect GameGuard, XIGNCODE3 and Denuvo Anti-Cheat rest on press or vendor statements.
- Unverified: Steam's full list of vendor tokens, SteamDB (it returned 403), PCGamingWiki row data, and kernel status for VAC, Hyperion and the East Asian vendors. The researcher used about 55 fetches, well over its cap.

### RQ6: Which icon set fits chip icons at 12 to 16 px?

All eleven candidate sets allow commercial use, and none has a copyleft, non-commercial or share-alike clause. Lucide covers every concept we need, with outline strokes only. Phosphor is the closest to solid glyphs for every concept but has no crossed swords. Note: [rq6-icon-sets.md](steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq6-icon-sets.md).

- Licences: Lucide is ISC with a second MIT notice for icons derived from Feather (`lock` and `key` are among them). Tabler, Phosphor, Heroicons, Bootstrap Icons, Iconoir and Radix Icons are MIT. Material Symbols and Carbon are Apache 2.0. Font Awesome Free icons are CC BY 4.0, which makes attribution mandatory, and its sparkles, swords and shield-alert are Pro only. Remix Icon 4.9 ships a custom licence (January 2026) that bars distributing the icons as a standalone product or building a competing icon set, while its npm record still says Apache 2.0.
- Coverage of eight concepts (AI, kernel anti-cheat, anti-cheat, DRM, account, EULA, PvP, launcher): Lucide has all eight (`sparkles`, `shield-alert`, `shield`, `lock`, `user`, `scroll-text`, `swords`, `app-window`). Tabler has eight but no `scroll`. Phosphor and Heroicons have seven, because Phosphor offers a single `sword` and Heroicons has none.
- Weight: Lucide is outline only. Phosphor and Material Symbols come closest to a solid variant for every concept, and Heroicons has a dedicated 16 px solid set.
- Bundling: eight icons cost about 2 to 5 KB in any set. Lucide's modules are `[tag, attrs]` arrays and its `createElement` calls `createElementNS`, with no `innerHTML`. The other sets ship SVG files and need a build-time path extraction.
- Maintenance: Lucide 1.61.0 (2026-10-21) and Tabler 3.49.0 (2026-10-05) release often. Phosphor core 2.1.1 (2024-03) and Heroicons 2.2.0 (2024-11) have had no npm release for about two years, though their repos show 2026 commits.
- The researcher's ranking (judgment): Phosphor fill, Lucide, then Heroicons 16 solid, with Lucide first if an outline look is acceptable.
- Unverified: rendering at 12 to 16 px was not tested, byte sizes are estimates except Heroicons (3,534 B for seven icons), the Material sparkle icon is missing from the SVG package, and several names were read through the Iconify mirror. The researcher used about 150 fetches against a cap of 25.

## Conclusions

What we now know.

- All four kinds sit in `extra_details` of the request the extension makes today (`GetItems` with `include_extra_details`). The new kinds need no new host, permission or request.
- Everything is developer-declared. Nothing is detected, and no source shows Valve checking binaries. Press reports Valve checking that anti-cheat notices are present and correct. A verdict can say "reported". It cannot say a game lacks the feature.
- Kernel-level anti-cheat has an explicit boolean, `anticheat.kernel_mode`. It can be true with no vendor name (Battlefield 6, Call of Duty, PUBG). No community source carries a kernel field.
- Third-party DRM, EULA and account or launcher are weaker. DRM and account are free text with spelling drift, `eula` is a list of name and URL, and no field names a launcher. Denuvo appears in two fields on different apps.
- A game that declares nothing still returns `extra_details`, with all four kinds absent (nine apps from 2004 to 2024, Animal Well among them). An item without `extra_details` is unknown.
- The page localizes every notice, while `GetItems` values are language-neutral. The extension sends the page's Steam language as `context.language` (`getitems.ts`), and these fields do not change with it. The stable page hooks are `.anticheat_section`, `.anticheat_name` and `a[href*="/eula/"]`. DRM and account blocks share one class and differ only by text. Only `GetItems` tells them apart.
- `GetItems` omits custom anti-cheat names and the activation limit. Both show on the page and in `appdetails`.
- The Oct 22 reviews change removed one old endpoint and is irrelevant to these fields. The only drift found is the new `has_community_hub` key.
- Only anti-cheat has a public Valve rule (2024-10-30). No public rule or start date turned up for DRM, account or EULA.
- Every icon set checked allows commercial use. Lucide covers all eight icon concepts, and its icon data builds SVG without `innerHTML`.

What stays open.

- Whether every app that declares nothing returns `extra_details`. Nine did, and the sample is small.
- The original 2024-10-30 post, and the Steamworks rules for DRM, account and EULA (partner pages sit behind a login).
- The `GetItems` batch ceiling above 63 IDs, live app-page markup against the fixtures, and an `appdetails` baseline.
- Boot-protection selectors and tokens, kernel status of VAC, Hyperion and the East Asian vendors, and why `GetItems` omits custom anti-cheat names.

## Recommendations

- Treat `GetItems` as the source for all four kinds. Parse the page only for what `GetItems` lacks, and key on classes and links, never on notice text.
- Capture fixtures before any code. The repo has no DRM or account notice fixture, none of the 2026-10-20 captures has `has_community_hub`, and there is nothing for packages, delisted apps or an app with no declarations. `scripts/capture_fixtures.py` is the tool.
- Widen the "declares nothing" check beyond the nine apps seen: sample about 30 apps across ages and publishers, plus a package and a delisted app, and keep them as fixtures. The three-state mapping for every new kind rests on it.
- Write an umbrella ADR for the scope change before code. It must say how rule 4 (semantics and wording) extends to the new kinds, and that free text from developers renders verbatim through `textContent`.
- Needs another `/wf:research`: the Steamworks partner-admin rules for DRM, account and EULA, which need a partner login the researchers lack. Also the batch ceiling, if the 50-ID budget ever matters.
- Icons: if the design session approves chip icons, use Lucide as an exact-pinned dependency and import only the icons we draw. Its outline style matches the new extension mark. Phosphor's fill weight sits closer to Steam's flat glyphs but has no crossed swords. Record the library check in the ADR (rule 12).
- Ship the licence notices in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`: Lucide (ISC) with the Feather MIT notice, and Tabler (MIT) for the Steam outline the extension mark derives from.

```

`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq1-declarations.md`:

```md
# RQ1: What does Steam record per kind, and who declares it?

Researched 2026-10-24. Tags: `verified from source` means the cited page or API response was read and says it; `search-summary` means the claim comes only from a web search result summary; `unverified` means a single weak source or an inference. Web fetches went through a small summarizing model, so API values read that way are "seen once through a helper" even when tagged verified; the local fixtures under tests/fixtures are first-hand captures from 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21. The Valve announcement of 2024-10-30 and all Steamworks partner pages behind a login were unreachable, so every statement about what that post says is a press report.

## Answer in short

- Steam stores all four kinds in one object, `extra_details` of IStoreBrowseService/GetItems (proto `StoreItem_ExtraDetails`): `anticheat` (object), `drm_third_party_type` and `drm_activation_limit` (strings), `user_account_third_party` (string) with `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (bool), and `eula` (list of name plus url). Every field is optional, so a missing key means "not recorded", never "none". There is no field for a required third-party launcher; it shows up inside the DRM or account free text.
- Anti-cheat is the only kind with a public Valve rule: Steamworks post "New Tool for Describing Anti-Cheat in Games", 2024-10-30. Press reports it as mandatory for new submissions that install a client-side kernel-mode anti-cheat, optional for every other anti-cheat, with Valve contacting partners of existing games. The Steamworks Store Page doc lists an "Anti-Cheat Declaration" under the Basic Info tab.
- For third-party DRM, third-party account and EULA no Valve announcement, rule text or start date was found in public sources. The values are free text typed by the publisher (for example "Denuvo", "Denuvo Anti-tamper" and "Denuvo Anti-Tampering" for the same vendor).
- All four are self-reported. No source says Valve inspects binaries. Press says Valve checks that anti-cheat notices are present and correct; no penalty or enforcement action was found for any kind. As far as public sources show, developers can omit DRM, account and EULA data, and non-kernel anti-cheat; records with an absent key are common, but whether each such game really has the feature was not checked.

## Findings

### 1. Anti-cheat: what developers must or may declare, and since when

Date and status of the primary source.

- Valve's Steamworks Development post "New Tool for Describing Anti-Cheat in Games" is dated 2024-10-30 by press (source: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/10/steam-games-will-now-need-to-fully-disclose-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/), and a Slashdot story of the same day carries the date in its path (source: https://tech.slashdot.org/story/24/10/30/212206/, search result only). `verified from source` for the date via press.
- The post body did not load in five attempts: steamcommunity.com returned only the title and site navigation, the `?l=english` variant the same, store.steampowered.com/news/group/4145017/view/4547038620960934857 the same, the Steamworks group RSS lists only ten recent posts without it, and the Wayback Machine is blocked in this environment (source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/4547038620960934857). `unverified` against the original.

What press reports Valve wrote.

- Valve's quoted lines: developers are "looking for the right way to share anti-cheat information"; players "have been requesting more transparency around the anti-cheat services used in games"; "we generally think that any game that makes use of anti-cheat technology would benefit from letting players know" (source: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/10/steam-games-will-now-need-to-fully-disclose-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/). `verified from source` (press quotes). A second read of the same page found no quoted Valve text for the mandatory rule, the existing-games rule or the accuracy checks, so those are the article author's summary there.
- Mandatory: kernel-level anti-cheat must be declared. AlternativeTo says the field is mandatory for new game submissions whose game installs a client-side, kernel-mode anti-cheat (source: https://alternativeto.net/news/2024/10/steam-will-now-require-developers-to-disclose-kernel-mode-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/). GIGAZINE says disclosure is mandatory for new games with kernel-level anti-cheat (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20241031-steam-tool-describing-anti-cheat). PC World says such games "now have to declare" it (source: https://www.pcworld.com/article/2507080/steam-will-show-when-games-use-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages.html). Three press reads agree; `verified from source` for the press, original post unread.
- Optional: client-side or server-side anti-cheat that is not kernel-level is optional, though Valve encourages it (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20241031-steam-tool-describing-anti-cheat). PC World reports server-side systems that use no separate client software are exempt (source: https://www.pcworld.com/article/2507080/steam-will-show-when-games-use-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages.html). The exemption is stated once and is `unverified` elsewhere.
- Form: a new field in the "Edit Store Page" section where the developer specifies the anti-cheat software (source: https://alternativeto.net/news/2024/10/steam-will-now-require-developers-to-disclose-kernel-mode-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/). GIGAZINE adds a pre-populated list of several tools and a custom entry for tools not on the list, and describes one checkbox for kernel-level tools (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20241031-steam-tool-describing-anti-cheat). A search summary of other press describes two checkboxes, kernel-level integration and whether users must remove residual files after uninstall (source: web search summary of the Neowin, Tom's Hardware and Techspot items, none readable: Neowin returned 403 and Tom's Hardware returned only its headline). The second checkbox is `search-summary`; the stored fields `kernel_mode` and `uninstall_completely` (section 3) match it.
- Existing games: GIGAZINE quotes Valve as saying it will "review existing games and contact partners whose games fall into this category" (source: https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20241031-steam-tool-describing-anti-cheat). AlternativeTo says Valve is contacting partners with existing games that use such software (source: https://alternativeto.net/news/2024/10/steam-will-now-require-developers-to-disclose-kernel-mode-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/). Press differs on scope: a first read of GamingOnLinux summarized "new and existing games", a second read of the same article found no such sentence. No deadline for existing games appeared anywhere. Net: mandatory for new submissions from 2024-10-30; for existing games enforced by Valve outreach, timing unknown.
- Steamworks docs: the Store Page doc lists "Anti-Cheat Declaration - Share anti-cheat information about your game" under the "Basic Info" tab, with a link to more info that sits behind the partner site (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page). `verified from source`. The doc "Anti-cheat and Game Bans" tells developers to warn customers that an anti-cheat system exists and has nothing on the store-page declaration (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/anticheat). `verified from source`.

### 2. Third-party DRM, third-party account and EULA: what developers must or may declare

- No public Valve rule found. The Store Page doc's Basic Info tab lists accessibility support, controller support, social media links and the anti-cheat declaration; nothing on DRM, third-party accounts, EULAs or legal information (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page). `verified from source`. The Steam DRM doc covers the Steam wrapper and using it with other DRM, and has no store-page disclosure text and no mention of Denuvo (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/drm). `verified from source`. The Steamworks doc index has no entry for EULA, launcher or release checklist (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc). `verified from source` (navigation only; the Steam Distribution Agreement, review process pages and release checklist sit behind login and were not read).
- A search for a Steamworks doc on adding a EULA found only Steam-hosted publisher EULA pages at store.steampowered.com/eula/ and the Workshop EULA call in ISteamUGC; no developer instruction page (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamUGC). `search-summary`.
- Community claims, none from Valve. A forum commenter, thread not identified, says Steamworks gives publishers two flags, "3rd-Party Account" and "3rd-Party DRM", and that nobody forces them to set them (source: web search summary). `unverified`; the "Requires 3rd-Party Account" thread, read for 15 of its 20 replies, does not contain it (source: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/10/601901188455074095/). A 2018 thread's top reply says publishers are not obliged to state third-party DRM (source: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/1736595227852911346, search summary). `unverified`. A Steam group says Valve policy is to disclose DRM on relevant store pages, with inconsistent results (source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/nodrm, search summary). `unverified`. A forum remark that the Steam Distribution Agreement sits under NDA means its terms on these notices cannot be checked (source: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/1755779919109939706, search summary). `unverified`.
- Start dates: none found for any of the three. A 2014-era forum thread says older games list such requirements in the system requirements text because they predate when listing third-party accounts or DRM was required; that is a user inference and the thread was not pinned down (source: web search summary, no stable URL). `unverified`. The notices exist on pages today (see section 4).
- Who writes the text: a forum commenter says everything on a store page comes from the developer or publisher, not Valve (source: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/1736595227852911346, search summary). `unverified`; consistent with the free-text values in section 3.

### 3. Stored fields and what they mean

Where the data lives.

- `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` declares `drm_third_party_type` (string, 5), `drm_activation_limit` (string, 6), `user_account_third_party` (string, 7), `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (bool, 8), `anticheat` (`StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat`, 9) and repeated `eula` (`StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Eula`, 10) (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, read at offset 200000). `verified from source`. Standalone `StoreItem_Anticheat` and `StoreItem_Eula` messages with the same fields are referenced in comments, which suggests a refactor. DRM and account data are plain fields on the parent, not nested messages.
- `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat`: `kernel_mode` bool 1, `uninstall_completely` bool 2, `boot_protection` bool 3, `boot_protection_name` string 4, `name` string 5, `name_loc` string 6. `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Eula`: `name` string 1, `url` string 2 (same source). `verified from source`.
- The request flag is `include_extra_details` in `data_request`; the live JSON uses the same key names. 25 apps were sampled on 2026-10-24 plus 7 in the 2026-10-20 fixture (source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1 with `input_json` `{"ids":[{"appid":N}],"context":{"language":"english","country_code":"US"},"data_request":{"include_extra_details":true}}`; local fixture tests/fixtures/getitems/mixed-states.json). `verified from source`. In the sections below, "GetItems v1 URL" means this call.

anticheat.kernel_mode and uninstall_completely.

- `kernel_mode: true` is the "kernel-level" checkbox. Seen true for Call of Duty (1938090), Battlefield 2042 (1517290), HELLDIVERS 2 (553850), Delta Force (2507950), Destiny 2 (1085660), Apex Legends (1172470), Grand Theft Auto V (271590) and ARC Raiders (1808500) (source: GetItems v1 URL; fixture mixed-states.json). `verified from source`.
- `uninstall_completely: true` is the second checkbox, read from the field name as "the anti-cheat is removed on uninstall"; the key is absent when not set. The ARC Raiders record has no `uninstall_completely`, and its page appends " - Requires manual removal after game uninstall" (source: tests/fixtures/app-page/1808500-ai-only.html lines 70-72). The Call of Duty record has it true and the live page block lists no removal line (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english). `verified from source` for both observations. The polarity (true means clean uninstall, so the warning shows when the key is false or unset) is inferred from these two apps: `unverified` as a rule. The press describes the second checkbox the other way round ("users need to remove any residual files"), and the Steamworks UI label was not seen.
- False booleans appear to be omitted: Counter-Strike 2 (730) has `{"name":"VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)","name_loc":"#Store_AntiCheat_Type_vac"}` with no `kernel_mode` (source: GetItems v1 URL). So "unset" and "false" cannot be told apart in the JSON. `verified from source`.
- Empty and bare objects occur: Marvel Rivals (2767030) returned `anticheat: {}`; Battlefield 2042 returned `{"kernel_mode":true,"uninstall_completely":true}` with no name (source: GetItems v1 URL). `verified from source` (one read each). An empty object is an unexplained state; do not read it as "no anti-cheat".

anticheat.name versus name_loc.

- `name` is the display string. When the developer picked an entry from Valve's list, `name_loc` holds a localization token of the form `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_<id>`: `denuvo` (ARC Raiders, name "Denuvo"), `easyac` ("Easy Anti-Cheat"), `battleye` ("BattlEye"), `ace` ("Anti-Cheat Expert (ACE)"), `vac` ("VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)") (source: GetItems v1 URL; fixture mixed-states.json). `verified from source`.
- The API does not resolve the token: with `language: german` and `country_code: DE` HELLDIVERS 2 and Delta Force returned the same English `name` and the same token (source: GetItems v1 URL, german request). `verified from source` (one read). Whether the store page localizes the name through the token was not tested.
- Records exist with neither `name` nor `name_loc` (Call of Duty, Battlefield 2042). No record with a `name` but no `name_loc` was found, so the claim that a custom entry has no token is `unverified`. The press says a custom entry is allowed (GIGAZINE, section 1).
- "Denuvo" in `anticheat.name` is the vendor's anti-cheat product. The DRM field uses the same vendor name for a different product. Treat them as separate facts.
- Open discrepancy: the Call of Duty store page lists "RICOCHET Anti-Cheat" as a notice line, but its GetItems record (read twice on 2026-10-24 and once in the 2026-10-20 fixture) has no `name`. The page may take that line from another source (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english). `unverified` as to where it comes from.

anticheat.boot_protection and boot_protection_name.

- `boot_protection: true` with `boot_protection_name: "secureboot_tpm2"` was seen only on Call of Duty (1938090) (source: GetItems v1 URL; fixture german-context.json). `boot_protection_name` is a key, not display text: the page renders "Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0" and, when the visitor's PC lacks them, a warning box "Secure Boot & TPM 2.0 Not Detected" saying both "must be enabled to play some or all parts of this game" (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english). `verified from source` (two page reads, one app). Other key values are unknown; only one value was seen.

drm_third_party_type and drm_activation_limit.

- `drm_third_party_type` is free text typed by the publisher. Observed: "Denuvo Anti-Tampering" (Hogwarts Legacy 990080), "Denuvo" (Black Myth: Wukong 2358720), "Denuvo Anti-tamper" (Metaphor: ReFantazio 2679460, Street Fighter 6 1364780, Assassin's Creed Shadows 3159330), "EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use required." (Star Wars Jedi: Survivor 1774580) and "EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use required. Denuvo Anti-tamper" (EA Sports FC 25 2669320) (source: GetItems v1 URL). `verified from source` (one read). The field is a mix of vendor name and prose, so values are not an enum; a required third-party launcher is expressed here (the EA app) or in the account field, not in a dedicated field.
- `drm_activation_limit` (string) was absent in every record sampled. The Street Fighter 6 page nonetheless shows "5 different PC within a day machine activation limit" beside its DRM notice (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364780/?l=english). `unverified` as to which field feeds that line.

user_account_third_party and user_account_third_party_link_to_steam.

- `user_account_third_party` is the free-text name of the required account: "Activision Account" (Call of Duty), "Rockstar Games" (Red Dead Redemption 2 1174180, Grand Theft Auto V), "PlayStation Network" (HELLDIVERS 2), "Xbox Live" (Forza Horizon 5 1551360), "Capcom ID" (Street Fighter 6), "Ubisoft Account" (Assassin's Creed Shadows), "EA Account" (Jedi: Survivor, FC 25), "LEVEL INFINITE PASS" (Delta Force) (source: GetItems v1 URL and fixture mixed-states.json). `verified from source`.
- `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam: true` means the third-party account can be linked to the Steam account. The page renders it as a parenthetical: "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Activision Account (Supports Linking to Steam Account)" and "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Capcom ID (Supports Linking to Steam Account)" (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english and https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364780/?l=english). `verified from source`. When the flag is absent (EA Account on Jedi: Survivor and FC 25) the page wording was not fetched; that it then omits the parenthetical is `unverified`.

eula.

- `eula[]` is a list of `{name, url}` objects, one per EULA, for example `{"name":"Resident Evil Village EULA","url":"https://store.steampowered.com//eula/1196590_eula_1"}` (source: GetItems v1 URL). `verified from source`. The URL pattern is `store.steampowered.com//eula/<appid>_eula_<n>` (double slash as served; n was 0 or 1 in the sample), so the EULA page is hosted on Steam. The ARC Raiders EULA page is a Steam-hosted shell that links out to the publisher's terms (source: https://store.steampowered.com/eula/1808500_eula_0). `verified from source` (one read).
- The field says the game shows a EULA to accept; it does not mark whether the EULA is "third-party" versus the developer's own. The page wording is fixed: "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" (section 4). Resident Evil Village, Resident Evil 4, Tekken 8 and Dragon Age: The Veilguard each carry an `eula` entry but no account or DRM, so the EULA is declared independently of the other kinds. `verified from source`.

### 4. Store-page wording per kind

- Anti-cheat block (ARC Raiders fixture): a div with classes `anticheat_section DRM_notice` holding "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat", then a div `anticheat_name` with the name and a span `anticheat_uninstalls` reading " - Requires manual removal after game uninstall" (source: tests/fixtures/app-page/1808500-ai-only.html lines 70-73). `verified from source`. The class `DRM_notice` is shared by every notice, including anti-cheat.
- EULA block: a `DRM_notice` div with `role="button"` holding "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" and a link whose text is the `eula[].name` (same fixture lines 74-77). `verified from source`.
- Third-party account line: "Requires 3rd-Party Account: <name> (Supports Linking to Steam Account)" (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364780/?l=english). `verified from source`.
- DRM line: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper" (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364780/?l=english). `verified from source` (one read); an earlier search summary paraphrased it as "Includes", so exact verb wording needs a raw HTML check. The Call of Duty page had no DRM notice and its record has no DRM field (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english).
- Boot protection: "Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0" (source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1938090/?l=english). `verified from source`.
- The notices use English text only in the captures; other-language wording was not checked here (RQ4 covers it).

### 5. Self-reported or verified, enforcement, old games, omission

- Self-reported: the data lives in the developer's Steamworks store page configuration, and the free-text, publisher-specific values (section 3) are consistent with developer entry. No public source describes Valve detecting kernel drivers, Denuvo wrapping, account walls or EULAs on its own. For anti-cheat the Steamworks doc names the declaration as something the developer shares (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page). `verified from source` for the doc line; the absence of any verification statement is a negative finding, not proof.
- Valve checking: press says new games will be checked so that the notices are present and accurate (source: web search summary of PC World, GamingOnLinux and others; GamingOnLinux's second read did not confirm it). `search-summary`. No source says how, and none describes an audit result.
- Penalties: none found for any kind. The public Steamworks pages read contain no enforcement language for these declarations (sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/anticheat, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/drm). `verified from source` for the absence on those three pages; the partner review pages and Distribution Agreement were not reachable.
- Old games: for anti-cheat, Valve contacts partners of existing games (section 1). Live data shows old apps do carry declarations: Grand Theft Auto V (appid 271590, a legacy listing) has `anticheat` `{"kernel_mode":true,"name":"BattlEye","name_loc":"#Store_AntiCheat_Type_battleye"}` and an account entry (source: GetItems v1 URL). `verified from source`; when each record was added is unknown. Developers can edit the store page themselves after release and changes go live on publish (source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page). `verified from source`. No retroactive sweep was found for DRM, account or EULA.
- Omission: as far as public sources show, developers may omit DRM, account and EULA data. A Steam forum report describes a 2024 case where a game's third-party DRM info was missing at first and was added to the requirements text after launch (source: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2291060/discussions/0/4509876314624602448, search summary). `search-summary`. Records with an absent key include apps often reported to use the feature, but this was not checked against each game, so it is only a pointer: Elden Ring (1245620), NARAKA: BLADEPOINT (1203220) and Black Desert (582660) have no `anticheat`; Dragon Age: The Veilguard (1845910) has an EULA but no account or DRM entry while the other EA titles sampled have EA entries (source: GetItems v1 URL). `unverified` as evidence of omission; whether each game ships kernel-mode anti-cheat or needs an EA account was not verified.
- Optional declarations do occur: Counter-Strike 2 declares VAC with no kernel flag, and Valve is its developer (source: GetItems v1 URL). `verified from source`.

### 6. What stayed unreachable or unanswered

- The original Steamworks announcement text (all fetch routes returned navigation only); the exact field labels and checkbox wording in the Steamworks UI; the "more info" link behind "Anti-Cheat Declaration".
- Any Valve statement on DRM, third-party account or EULA declaration rules, their start dates, and whether the Steamworks admin pages make them mandatory; the Steam Distribution Agreement, review guidelines and release checklist (login required).
- Whether Valve audits any declaration and any penalty applied; whether `drm_activation_limit` is ever populated; whether a custom anti-cheat name lacks `name_loc`; localized page wording of the notices.

## Caveats and version notes

- Data values are a 2026-10-24 snapshot of live records, read through a summarizing helper; the 2026-10-20 fixtures agree for the apps they cover (1808500, 1938090), and the fixture files are the byte-exact source for those two. Records change when developers edit store pages. The question of what changed around 2026-10-22 belongs to RQ3 and is not covered here.
- Press accounts of the 2024-10-30 post differ on whether existing games were covered, and on one versus two checkboxes. Treat "mandatory for new submissions with kernel-mode client anti-cheat" as the stable core.
- `drm_third_party_type` and `user_account_third_party` are free text, so any classification (for example Denuvo or not) needs string handling with spelling variants; `name_loc` tokens are the only stable anti-cheat identifiers and cover only list entries.
- Two page-versus-API gaps are unexplained: the RICOCHET line on the Call of Duty page and the activation-limit line on the Street Fighter 6 page. A page-only notice may exist that GetItems does not carry.
- The Call of Duty and Street Fighter 6 page reads came from the helper's markdown view of the full page; the helper capped quotes at 125 characters, so surrounding text was described, not quoted.
- Search results for forum claims were summaries and several were not pinned to a single thread; each is tagged accordingly.
```

`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq2-data-surface-by-kind.md`:

```md
# RQ2: Where does each non-AI disclosure kind appear in Steam's data?

Researched 2026-10-24. Scope: four kinds shown on Steam store pages: (1) kernel-level anti-cheat, (2) third-party DRM such as Denuvo, (3) a required third-party EULA, (4) a required third-party account or launcher. Facts only.

Method and tags. Every web read went through WebFetch, which hands the page to a small summarizing model; JSON values below are that model's transcription of the response, requested verbatim. "verified from source" means read first-hand from the cited URL or local fixture (items that matter were read two or three times, noted per claim). "search-summary" means seen only in a search result. "unverified" means a single indirect read or an inference. Citation labels (G-..., A-..., M-..., P-..., H-..., F-..., PROTO) each map to exactly one URL or file in the Sources list; the GetItems labels spell out the appids.

## Answer in short

- GetItems with `include_extra_details` carries all four kinds as typed fields in `store_items[].extra_details`: `drm_third_party_type` (free text), `user_account_third_party` (free text) with `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (bool), `eula[]` (`{name,url}`), and `anticheat` (`kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection`, `boot_protection_name`, `name`, `name_loc`). A key is omitted when nothing is declared; no `false` or empty string was seen, and one empty object (`anticheat: {}`). Without `include_extra_details` the whole `extra_details` object is absent. 32 apps and a 63-ID batch were read.
- Denuvo is in both fields, on different apps: `drm_third_party_type` for anti-tamper DRM (9 apps, 5 spellings, for example "Denuvo Anti-tamper") and `anticheat.name` ("Denuvo", `name_loc` "#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo") on ARC Raiders. No app showed both. Launchers and accounts are free text (12 distinct strings across 9 publishers). `anticheat.name` is a closed set of tokens (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Denuvo, VAC seen); a custom anti-cheat leaves `name` out and the name appears only in the page HTML ("EA Javelin Anticheat", "NetEase Game Security").
- App page: DRM, account, EULA and kernel anti-cheat are `div.DRM_notice` children of `#category_block`; the anti-cheat one is `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice` with `.anticheat_name` and `.anticheat_uninstalls`; a non-kernel anti-cheat is `.anticheat_section.anticheat_nonkernel_notice` and is not a `.DRM_notice`. DRM and account blocks have no class other than `DRM_notice`; they differ only by their text prefix. The EULA block is `.DRM_notice[role=button]` with an `<a href=".../eula/<appid>_eula_<n>">`.
- appdetails has `drm_notice` and `ext_user_account_notice` (when declared) and nothing for anti-cheat or EULA. The DRM activation limit ("5 activations within 24 hours machine activation limit") is in appdetails and the HTML but in no GetItems field read.
- Batching: all GetItems fields are batchable by appid; 63 IDs in one request returned 63 items (35 with `success: 15` and no `extra_details`). The 50-ID figure is not a server limit at 63; the true maximum is above 63 and was not found (WebFetch rejected a 120-ID URL as invalid). Only the page or appdetails carry custom anti-cheat names, the activation limit, the rendered boot-protection sentence and the EA Play terms line.

## Findings

### 1. Per kind: which field carries it in each source

Summary table (all rows verified from source unless marked):

| Kind                             | GetItems `extra_details`                                                                                                  | App-page HTML                                                                                                                         | `/api/appdetails`                                               |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Kernel-level anti-cheat          | `anticheat.kernel_mode: true`, plus `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection`, `boot_protection_name`, `name`, `name_loc` | `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice`: "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat", `.anticheat_name`, `.anticheat_uninstalls`; boot-protection sentence | no key                                                          |
| Non-kernel anti-cheat (adjacent) | `anticheat` object without `kernel_mode` (`{name,name_loc}` or `{}`)                                                      | `.anticheat_section.anticheat_nonkernel_notice`: "Uses Anti-Cheat Software." plus `.anticheat_name`                                   | no key                                                          |
| Third-party DRM                  | `drm_third_party_type` (string)                                                                                           | `.DRM_notice`: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: <text>" plus activation-limit text                                                        | `drm_notice` (string, may hold `<br>` and the activation limit) |
| Third-party EULA                 | `eula[]` of `{name,url}`                                                                                                  | `.DRM_notice[role=button]`: "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" plus `<a href>`                                                  | no key                                                          |
| Third-party account or launcher  | `user_account_third_party` (string), `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (bool)                                      | `.DRM_notice`: "Requires 3rd-Party Account: <text>" and "(Supports Linking to Steam Account)" when the flag is true                   | `ext_user_account_notice` (string; link text appended)          |

Assassin's Creed Shadows (3159330): Denuvo, Ubisoft account with link flag, EULA. `anticheat` and `content_survey_ai_notes` absent. Full `extra_details` key list: vetted, controller_wizard_complete, drm_third_party_type, user_account_third_party, user_account_third_party_link_to_steam, eula, section, legal_notice_bbcode, content_survey_notes, links_and_info, points_shop_eligible, system_requirements, has_community_hub. (verified from source: G-3159330)
```

```
Battlefield 6 (2807960): account, kernel anti-cheat with boot protection, EULA; no `drm_third_party_type`; `anticheat` has no `name`. Two reads (a single-app request and a two-app request) gave the same anti-cheat object, and a search of the second response for "Javelin" and "name_loc" found neither. #### 1.2 App-page HTML: selectors and text actually observed
```

```
Raw structure, from a fixture captured 2026-10-20 (ARC Raiders, `?l=english`, cookie-less). The two blocks sit directly inside `#category_block`, after `div.game_area_features_list_ctn` and the controller-support placeholder. Whitespace was collapsed by the fixture sanitizer. (verified from source: F-1808500-page)

```
<div class="block responsive_apppage_details_left" id="category_block">
  <div class="game_area_features_list_ctn">...</div>
  <div data-featuretarget="store-sidebar-controller-support-info"></div>
  <div class="anticheat_section DRM_notice">
    <div>Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat</div>
    <div class="anticheat_name">Denuvo<span class="anticheat_uninstalls"> - Requires manual removal after game uninstall</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="DRM_notice" role="button">
    <div>Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA</div>
    <div><a href="https://store.steampowered.com//eula/1808500_eula_0">ARC Raiders EULA</a></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

The same container holds a `DRM_notice` for the AI-content service on the AI sample: `<div class="DRM_notice">Connects to 3rd-Party Service for AI Content Generation:&nbsp;<a href="https://openai.com/api/">OpenAI API</a></div>`. (verified from source: F-5072580-page)

DRM and account blocks, read by CSS selector on `.DRM_notice` (class attribute and text). Both carry only the class `DRM_notice`; the first words are the only discriminator. (verified from source: M-2878980, M-1295660, M-1240440)

- NBA 2K25 (2878980) class list `["DRM_notice", "anticheat_section DRM_notice"]` plus the EULA block; texts: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper5 Activations per 24 hours machine activation limit", "Requires 3rd-Party Account: 2K Sports Account", "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat Easy Anti-Cheat", "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA NBA 2K25 EULA". The concatenated "Anti-tamper5" shows the activation limit is a separate element (line break or tag) after the DRM text; its markup was not read. (verified from source: M-2878980)
- Civilization VII (1295660) class list `["DRM_notice"]`; texts: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper5 activations within 24 hours machine activation limit", "Requires 3rd-Party Account: 2K Account for Online Interactions (Not Required for Offline Play) (Supports Linki..." (cut by the 110-character limit; full string in appdetails below), "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA Sid Meier's Civilization VII EULA". `role` attribute list: `["button"]` (one element, the EULA block); link list: the `/eula/1295660_eula_0` URL. (verified from source: M-1295660)
- Halo Infinite (1240440): "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Xbox Live" (plain `DRM_notice`) and "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat Easy Anti-Cheat - Requires manual removal after game uninstall" (`anticheat_section DRM_notice`); no `<a>` inside any `.DRM_notice` and no EULA block, matching the absent `eula` in GetItems. (verified from source: M-1240440)
- EA SPORTS FC 25 (2669320): six `.DRM_notice` blocks: DRM "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use...", account "Requires 3rd-Party Account: EA Account", anti-cheat "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat EA Javelin Anticheat - Requires manual removal after game uninstall", EULA "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA EA SPORTS FC 25 EULA", "EA Play subscription requires acceptance of EA Play Terms", "Steam refunds will consider EA account playtime". `.anticheat_name` text: "EA Javelin Anticheat - Requires manual removal after game uninstall". Links inside `.DRM_notice a`: `https://store.steampowered.com//eula/2669320_eula_0` and `https://store.steampowered.com//eula/1289670_eula_0` (the EA Play terms link, a different appid). (verified from source: M-2669320)
- The link flag renders as appended text: the Battlefield 6 page line reads "Requires 3rd-Party Account: EA Account linking required (Supports Linking to Steam Account)", from the plain store page (markdown conversion, so no selectors). (verified from source: P-2807960)

Anti-cheat block variants. Kernel: `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice`, first child "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat". Non-kernel: class `anticheat_section anticheat_nonkernel_notice`, first child "Uses Anti-Cheat Software.", then `<div class="anticheat_name">NetEase Game Security<span class="anticheat_uninstalls"></span></div>` (Marvel Rivals, verbatim excerpt) or "VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)" (Counter-Strike 2). Counter-Strike 2 had no `.DRM_notice` at all; Marvel Rivals had one, the EULA block. (verified from source: M-2767030, M-2767030-sec, M-730, M-730-sec)

Mapping between GetItems and the rendered anti-cheat block (inferred from consistent pairs, no counterexample among the apps named):

- `kernel_mode: true` goes with `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice` and the "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat" line; no `kernel_mode` goes with `.anticheat_nonkernel_notice` (Counter-Strike 2, Marvel Rivals). (verified from source: G-G, M-730-sec, M-2767030-sec; the mapping itself is an inference)
- `uninstall_completely` absent goes with the suffix " - Requires manual removal after game uninstall" inside `.anticheat_uninstalls` (ARC Raiders, Halo Infinite, EA FC 25); `uninstall_completely: true` goes with no suffix (NBA 2K25 page text; Battlefield 6 page lines). (inferred from G-B, G-D, G-F, M-1240440, M-2669320, M-2878980, P-2807960)
- `boot_protection: true` with `boot_protection_name: "secureboot_tpm2"` goes with the page line "Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0" (Battlefield 6, one page read; Call of Duty's page was not readable cookie-less from the fetch location). (verified from source: G-2807960, P-2807960)
- The boot-protection line's selector or class was not captured (markdown read only): unverified.

Whether the same blocks appear elsewhere on the page (for example near the purchase area) was not checked: unverified.

#### 1.3 /api/appdetails

Request: `https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=<id>&cc=us&l=english`. (verified from source: A-2669320, A-1295660, A-1808500)

- EA SPORTS FC 25 (2669320): top-level `data` keys include `legal_notice`, `drm_notice`, `ext_user_account_notice`. `drm_notice` is "EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use required. Denuvo Anti-tamper", identical to GetItems `drm_third_party_type` for the same app. `ext_user_account_notice` is "EA Account " (trailing space). `legal_notice` begins "Internet connection; EA Account; Steam Account; acceptance of the EA User Agreement (terms.ea.com); and download & insta". No key containing "anticheat" or "eula". (verified from source: A-2669320, G-D)
- Civilization VII (1295660): `drm_notice` is "Denuvo Anti-tamper<br>5 activations within 24 hours machine activation limit" (a `<br>` inside the string, activation limit included) and `ext_user_account_notice` is "2K Account for Online Interactions (Not Required for Offline Play) (Supports Linking to Steam Account)". The link flag becomes appended text; there is no separate link key (`ext_user_account_link`, a name guessed in the brief, is absent). (verified from source: A-1295660)
- ARC Raiders (1808500), which has a kernel anti-cheat and an EULA in GetItems: no `drm_notice`, no `ext_user_account_notice`, no anti-cheat or EULA key; `legal_notice` present. (verified from source: A-1808500)
- `categories` descriptions for EA FC 25 and ARC Raiders list player-mode and feature entries (Single-player, Multi-player, Online PvP, Steam Achievements, In-App Purchases and so on) and have no DRM, anti-cheat, account or EULA entry. (verified from source: A-2669320, A-1808500)

### 2. Representation: enum, free text or link flag; distinct values observed

#### 2.1 Denuvo

Denuvo appears in two different fields on different apps. No app read had both. (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1)

- `drm_third_party_type` (free text): 9 apps, 5 distinct strings: "Denuvo Anti-tamper" (Assassin's Creed Shadows, Civilization VII, NBA 2K25, Monster Hunter Wilds, Street Fighter 6), "Denuvo" (Black Myth: Wukong), "Denuvo Anti-Temper" (Far Cry 6, single read, may be a transcription slip), "Denuvo Anti-Tampering" (Hogwarts Legacy), and a long string "EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use required. Denuvo Anti-tamper" (EA SPORTS FC 25, three reads). The spelling variation shows the field is typed text, not an enum. (verified from source: G-3159330, G-2358720, G-D, G-E, G-F, G-G, G-H, G-I)
- `anticheat.name`: "Denuvo" with `name_loc` "#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo" on ARC Raiders; the page shows `.anticheat_name` "Denuvo". (verified from source: F-mixed-states, F-1808500-page)
- Denuvo is therefore not one field: DRM-type Denuvo is `drm_third_party_type`; anti-cheat-type Denuvo is `anticheat.name`. A text search of `drm_third_party_type` for "Denuvo" misses the ARC Raiders anti-cheat entry, and a search of `anticheat.name` misses all nine anti-tamper apps. (verified from source: G-B, G-F)
- EA FC 25 has a composite `drm_third_party_type` that bundles EA's own activation and app requirement with Denuvo in one string. (verified from source: G-D, G-I, A-2669320)

#### 2.2 Launchers and accounts

`user_account_third_party` is free text; `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` is a separate bool, omitted when false. The 12 distinct strings read (9 publishers): "Ubisoft Account" (AC Shadows, Far Cry 6), "Ubisoft Connect launcher" (Rainbow Six Siege), "EA Account" (Apex Legends, EA FC 25), "EA Account linking required" (Battlefield 6), "Rockstar Games" (GTA V Legacy, RDR2), "Activision Account" (Call of Duty), "Battle.net Account" (Diablo IV, Overwatch), "Xbox Live" (Halo Infinite, Forza Horizon 5), "Bethesda.net" (Fallout 76, DOOM Eternal), "2K Account for Online Interactions (Not Required for Offline Play)" (Civilization VII), "2K Sports Account" (NBA 2K25), "Capcom ID" (Street Fighter 6). (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1)

- One publisher can have several strings: EA ("EA Account", "EA Account linking required"), 2K (two strings), Ubisoft ("Ubisoft Account", "Ubisoft Connect launcher"). The same string repeats across games of one publisher ("Xbox Live", "Battle.net Account", "Bethesda.net", "Rockstar Games"). The field is not an enum and carries no launcher or store identifier. (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1)
- The link flag is `true` on 13 of the 18 apps with an account string and omitted on the other 5 (Diablo IV, Overwatch, Halo Infinite, EA FC 25, NBA 2K25); no explicit `false` appeared in any response. (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1; counts from the table)
- The account string is not translated in a `german` context: `user_account_third_party` stays "Activision Account" in the German-context fixture (language `german`, country `DE`). (verified from source: F-german-context)
- Call of Duty is "Activision Account", not "Battle.net". Battle.net strings were seen only on Diablo IV and Overwatch. (verified from source: F-mixed-states, G-D, G-G)
- The page prefix "Requires 3rd-Party Account:" is page text; the JSON field holds only the name, for example "Rockstar Games" with no launcher name. (verified from source: M-1240440, G-A)

#### 2.3 Anti-cheat

`anticheat` is a nested object. `kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection` are bool flags (omitted when false). `boot_protection_name` is a token-like string ("secureboot_tpm2", the only value seen). `name` is human text and `name_loc` is a Steam localization token ("#Store_AntiCheat_Type_<id>"). (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1)

- Tokens seen: easyac ("Easy Anti-Cheat"), battleye ("BattlEye"), denuvo ("Denuvo"), vac ("VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)"). Vanguard was not seen: no Riot title was tested and none is known to be on Steam (unverified, general knowledge).
- Custom or unnamed anti-cheat: `name` and `name_loc` are omitted while the page still names the anti-cheat. EA SPORTS FC 25 (JSON `{"kernel_mode":true}`) and Battlefield 6 (JSON with no `name`) both render "EA Javelin Anticheat"; Marvel Rivals (JSON `{}`) renders "NetEase Game Security". PUBG (`{"kernel_mode":true,"uninstall_completely":true}`) and Call of Duty also have no `name` in JSON; their page names were not readable. In every GetItems response read, "Javelin" and "NetEase" never occurred. (verified from source: G-I, G-J, M-2669320, P-2807960, M-2767030)
- A working reading of the three cases is that `name` and `name_loc` carry only the closed token set and a custom name is rendered from a source GetItems does not expose; that reading is an inference (unverified).
- Presence of the `anticheat` key does not mean kernel level: Counter-Strike 2 (`{name, name_loc}` without `kernel_mode`) and Marvel Rivals (`{}`) show the non-kernel block. (verified from source: G-G, M-730-sec, M-2767030-sec)
- `anticheat: {}` is the only empty-object value seen; it was read twice (two different requests) for Marvel Rivals. (verified from source: G-G, G-J)

#### 2.4 EULA

`eula` is a repeated `{name, url}`. Observed URL forms: `https://store.steampowered.com//eula/<appid>_eula_<n>` (note the double slash), with n = 0 on most apps and n = 1 on Apex Legends, PUBG and Rainbow Six Siege (the Siege entry also uses `http://`, one read). Elden Ring has two entries (`_eula_0` "ELDEN RING EULA", `_eula_1` "ELDEN RING EULA (JP)"). (verified from source: G-1172470, G-A, G-C; the Siege scheme is a single read)

- EULA presence is common without any other kind: Starfield, Borderlands 3, Elden Ring, Resident Evil 4, Hogwarts Legacy, Monster Hunter Wilds and Marvel Rivals have `eula` and no account or DRM string. (verified from source: G-A, G-B, G-E, G-F, G-G, G-H)
- The page link set can be larger than `eula[]`: EA FC 25 shows a second `/eula/1289670_eula_0` link under "EA Play subscription requires acceptance of EA Play Terms" while `eula[]` holds one entry; Battlefield 6 shows the same EA Play line with a one-entry `eula[]`. The JSON source of the EA Play line was not found in the responses read. (verified from source: M-2669320, P-2807960, G-D, G-I)
- The related `refund_checks_ea_playtime` key (present on EA FC 25) matches the page line "Steam refunds will consider EA account playtime"; the match is inferred. (verified from source: G-D for the key, M-2669320 for the line)

### 3. Absent vs false vs empty; known vs unknown

GetItems, a game with no declaration. The item has `success: 1` and an `extra_details` object but none of the kind keys: Stardew Valley `extra_details` holds `vetted, press_review, partner_awards_bbcode, links_and_info, points_shop_eligible, metacritic, system_requirements, has_community_hub` (and the raw fixture, `vetted, points_shop_eligible, metacritic`). Hades is the same. (verified from source: G-H, F-mixed-states)

- Absent is the normal "not declared" form. In all responses (32 apps), `false` never appeared for `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam`, `kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely` or `boot_protection`, and no empty-string `drm_third_party_type` or empty `eula` array appeared. A false bool is represented by omission (5 account strings lack the link flag; the mechanism is an inference from proto3 default handling, unverified). (verified from source: G-sets in section 1.1)
- Empty object: `anticheat: {}` (Marvel Rivals) is a present-but-empty value and the only one read; the page shows an anti-cheat name for it. (verified from source: G-G, G-J, M-2767030)
- Without `include_extra_details`: the item has no `extra_details` key and no occurrence of Denuvo, anticheat, anti-cheat, Javelin, EULA, "EA Account", "user_account" or "drm" anywhere (EA FC 25 request with `include_basic_info`, `include_assets`, `include_release`, `include_platforms`, `include_links`, `include_full_description`, `include_tag_count` 20, `include_ratings`; 19 item keys). (verified from source: G-noextra)
- Unknown vs nothing, GetItems: `success` separates them. `success: 1` with `extra_details` is a known record. `success: 15`, `visible: false`, `name: ""` and no `extra_details` appears for invalid or non-store IDs: 35 of 63 sequential IDs (10 to 630 step 10) and ID 99999999. A delisted app (50300, Spec Ops: The Line) returns `success: 1`, `unlisted: true` and `extra_details`. An adult-only app (339800) returned `success: 1` with the mature text in `content_survey_notes` (per the fixture README). (verified from source: G-63, F-mixed-states, F-fixtures-README)
- Inside a `success: 1` record nothing separates "developer declared nothing" from "not applicable" from "field not exposed". Observed cases where the page has information the JSON lacks: custom anti-cheat names (section 2.3), the DRM activation limit (section 4), the EA Play terms line (section 2.4). Rainbow Six Siege and Elden Ring have no `anticheat` key; whether either game ships an anti-cheat was not checked here (both are commonly reported to use one: unverified). (verified from source for the key absence: G-C, G-A)
- Age gate: GetItems returned `extra_details` for the mature apps tested (Call of Duty, Battlefield 6, GTA V, Wukong, Assassin's Creed Shadows) with no cookie or login. The app-page route differs: the microlink fetcher (cookie-less, location unknown, `prerender=false`) was redirected to `https://store.steampowered.com/agecheck/app/<id>/` for 3159330, 2807960, 271590, 2358720 and 1938090 and returned null for `.DRM_notice` and `#appHubAppName` (578080, PUBG, returned the same nulls; the gate there is presumed). The same fetcher got full pages for 2669320, 1240440, 1295660, 2878980, 730 and 2767030, and WebFetch itself read the Battlefield 6 page. Captured from an EU location on 2026-10-20, no app redirected cookie-less (1938090, 271590, 1245620 and others served the full page). The gate therefore depends on the client, and an empty `.DRM_notice` result on a gated fetch does not mean "nothing declared". (verified from source: M-gated, M-2669320, P-2807960, F-fixtures-README)
- appdetails, no declaration: ARC Raiders has neither `drm_notice` nor `ext_user_account_notice`; the keys are omitted, not null or empty. appdetails behavior for unknown IDs was not re-tested (unverified). (verified from source: A-1808500)
- App page, no declaration: no `.DRM_notice` element at all (Counter-Strike 2). The earlier AI-disclosure note established that a page with no `#appHubAppName` is not a store page (gate, login or invalid ID), so such a response is unknown (local note, not re-read: F-prior-rq2).

### 4. Batchable data vs full-page-only data; the batch ceiling

Batchable through GetItems (one request, any appids, no cookie): `drm_third_party_type`, `user_account_third_party`, `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam`, `eula[]` (names and URLs), and the whole `anticheat` object. Any surface that yields appids (search rows with `data-ds-appid`, wishlist rows, capsules, tag hubs, Next Fest cards) can be resolved this way; the surfaces themselves carry none of the kinds. The hover popup for EA FC 25 lists title, release date, review summary and user tags and mentions no DRM, account, anti-cheat or EULA (checked for this one app); search rows carry `data-ds-*` attributes for appid, tag IDs and descriptor IDs and no kind (earlier note); appdetails categories have no entry (section 1.3). (verified from source: H-2669320, A-2669320, F-prior-rq2)

Only on the full app page or appdetails, not in any GetItems field read:

- Custom anti-cheat names: "EA Javelin Anticheat" (EA FC 25, Battlefield 6), "NetEase Game Security" (Marvel Rivals). (verified from source: M-2669320, P-2807960, M-2767030)
- DRM activation limit: "5 Activations per 24 hours machine activation limit" (NBA 2K25 page) and "5 activations within 24 hours machine activation limit" (Civilization VII page and appdetails `drm_notice`, `<br>` separated). GetItems `drm_third_party_type` for both is just "Denuvo Anti-tamper"; the response had no "activation" substring and no `drm_activation_limit` key, read twice for each app. The differing wording between the two apps suggests the limit is developer text, not a fixed template (inference). (verified from source: M-2878980, M-1295660, A-1295660, G-F, G-K)
- The rendered boot-protection sentence ("Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0"); GetItems carries only the token `secureboot_tpm2`. (verified from source: P-2807960, G-2807960)
- The EA Play terms line and its EULA link (section 2.4).
- appdetails `legal_notice` prose: account and EULA requirements in publisher text, for example EA FC 25's "acceptance of the EA User Agreement". GetItems has a similarly named `legal_notice_bbcode` key in `extra_details` of several apps (AC Shadows, Wukong, Apex); its content was read only as a description by the summarizer. (verified from source: A-2669320, G-3159330, G-2358720, G-1172470)

Batch ceiling with `include_extra_details`: a request with 63 appids (10 to 630 step 10) returned 63 `store_items` in a single response: 28 with `success: 1` and `extra_details`, 35 with `success: 15` and no `extra_details`; no error, truncation or message field at the top level. The local fixture from 2026-10-20 holds a 50-ID response with 50 items in request order. A 120-ID URL (about 4.3 KB) failed in WebFetch with "Invalid URL" before any request reached Steam, so the real ceiling above 63 is unknown. The project's 50 is therefore not a limit observed on the server at 63. (verified from source: G-63, F-search-roguelike-50; the URL failure is a tool limit)

### 5. Every StoreItem_ExtraDetails field related to these kinds

Source: `webui/common.proto` in SteamDatabase/Protobufs, read at two character offsets (150000 and 200000) by the summarizing model, which listed names and field numbers and agreed across both reads; types were not reported by either read except where the JSON shows them. (verified from source: PROTO)

Directly the four kinds:

- `drm_third_party_type` = 5 (string in JSON)
- `drm_activation_limit` = 6 (type not reported by the read; never seen in a GetItems response)
- `user_account_third_party` = 7 (string in JSON)
- `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` = 8 (bool in JSON)
- `anticheat` = 9, message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat`: `kernel_mode` = 1, `uninstall_completely` = 2, `boot_protection` = 3, `boot_protection_name` = 4, `name` = 5, `name_loc` = 6
- `eula` = 10 (repeated), message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Eula`: `name` = 1, `url` = 2

Adjacent, same notice family on the page:

- `ai_generation_service` = 11, message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_AIGeneratedContentService`: `name` = 1, `url` = 2 (renders as a `.DRM_notice` "Connects to 3rd-Party Service for AI Content Generation")
- `refund_checks_ea_playtime` = 12 (seen as a key on EA FC 25; the page line "Steam refunds will consider EA account playtime" is inferred to be its rendering)

Possible carriers of related legal or account prose, content not read as structured data:

- `section` = 13 (repeated `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_PageSection`: `label` = 1, `content_bbcode` = 2, `banner` = 3 enum), present on many apps
- `legal_notice_bbcode` = 14
- `links_and_info` = 22, message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_LinksAndInfo`: includes `privacy_policy_url` = 5 and `available_documents` = 6 (repeated enum)

Not related: `steam_award`, `vetted`, `no_mouse_keyboard_support`, `controller_wizard_complete`, `interactive_elements`, `content_survey_notes`, `content_survey_ai_notes` (AI), `press_review`, `partner_awards_bbcode`, `early_access`, `season_pass`, `item_store_eligible`, `points_shop_eligible`, `metacritic`, `cast_and_crew`, `system_requirements`, `running_time_minutes`, `episode`, `seasons`, `video_extras_note`, `has_community_hub`.

The request flag `include_extra_details` is field 18 of `StoreBrowseItemDataRequest` per the earlier AI-disclosure note, not re-read here. (verified from source in the earlier note: F-prior-rq2)

## Caveats and version notes

- All reads were made on 2026-10-24, after the 2026-10-22 date named in this topic's RQ3; nothing here shows what the data looked like before. Local fixtures are from 2026-10-20 and agree with the fresh reads for ARC Raiders and Call of Duty (byte-exact JSON), so no change between those two dates was seen for those two apps.
- Summarizer risk: values are the helper model's transcription. Cross-reads agree for Battlefield 6, EA FC 25, Marvel Rivals, PUBG, Rainbow Six Siege, NBA 2K25, Civilization VII and the fixture-backed apps. Single reads: "Denuvo Anti-Temper" (Far Cry 6), the Rainbow Six Siege `http://` EULA scheme, Wukong's and Hogwarts Legacy's DRM strings, and every HTML read through microlink. Treat single-read strings as unverified in spelling.
- The microlink fetches went through the third-party service api.microlink.io from a location not shown; its age-gate behavior differs from the EU captures in the local fixtures. Page structure for gated apps (Assassin's Creed Shadows, GTA V, Call of Duty, Wukong) therefore comes from other apps and from the plain-text read of Battlefield 6.
- Not tested: the `language` effect on `name`, `name_loc` and `drm_third_party_type` (only the account string was seen untranslated in a German fixture); boot-protection tokens other than `secureboot_tpm2`; Riot Vanguard, ESEA or other anti-cheats; an app with Denuvo anti-tamper plus an anti-cheat in the same record; wishlist, discovery queue and other logged-in surfaces; appdetails for gated apps; field types in the proto; the markup of the activation-limit text; the JSON source of the EA Play line.
- Lead checks (second-hand claims from the brief): `drm_third_party_type` as free text "Denuvo Anti-tamper" confirmed, with four other spellings; `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` is a bool, confirmed; Call of Duty's string is "Activision Account", not Battle.net; Elden Ring has no `anticheat` key (confirmed absent in JSON; the game's actual anti-cheat was not checked); `.DRM_notice` is the generic class and the anti-cheat block is `.anticheat_section.DRM_notice` for kernel mode only; appdetails has `drm_notice` and `ext_user_account_notice` and no anti-cheat or EULA (confirmed on three apps); the Battlefield 6 "EA Javelin Anticheat" gap is confirmed and also affects EA FC 25 and Marvel Rivals ("NetEase Game Security").
- The 120-ID batch test was blocked by the tool's URL length, not by Steam, so "no ceiling at 50" is bounded at 63.
```
