`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq3-oct-2026-changes.md`:

```md
# RQ3: What changed around 2026-10-22?

Researched 2026-10-24. Every web fetch went through a small summarising model, so "verified from source" means "fetched and read through the summariser", not a byte-level check. Tags used below: `verified from source`, `search-summary` (seen only in a search result summary, or a page that failed to fetch), `unverified`. Live API calls were made on 2026-10-24 from the research tooling (location unknown, probably the US), not from the project's European capture setup.

## Answer in short

- The belief is confirmed, with one correction. Valve announced on 2026-10-02 (21:19 UTC) that it would disable the store-domain reviews endpoint `store.steampowered.com/appreviews/<appid>?json=1` on October 22, and it did: on 2026-10-24 that URL returns the store home page, and the replacement `api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/` answers keyless. It is a removal and move of one endpoint, announced 20 days ahead, and not a push of changes to the store APIs.
- Nothing was found that changes GetItems, appdetails or the app page for the four disclosure kinds (anticheat, eula, drm_third_party_type, user_account_third_party) around 2026-10-22. No Steamworks announcement in the window mentions them, and in `webui/common.proto` their field numbers, names and scalar types are identical at every October checkpoint read.
- One real drift: live GetItems now adds `extra_details.has_community_hub` (bool), absent from every fixture captured on 2026-10-20. The protobuf tracker first shows it (field 33 of `StoreItem_ExtraDetails`) in a commit dated 2026-10-21 00:15 UTC.
- Two quieter protobuf edits landed earlier in October and are not wire changes: the types of fields 9, 10 and 11 were renamed from `StoreItem_*` to `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_*` (between 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-05), and fields 28 to 32 were added (between 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-14).
- Fixture values for anticheat and user-account fields on 1808500 and 1938090 match live responses; the app-page notice wording for 1808500 matches its fixture. Markup (class names) of live pages could not be compared with the tooling used.

## Findings

### 1. What Valve announced and shipped for the reviews API (2026-10-02 to 2026-10-24)

The announcement. The Steamworks Development group feed lists "Changes to Steam User Reviews API", published Fri 2026-10-02 21:19:11 +0000 (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/rss/). Per the feed body, the bulk user reviews endpoint moves off the store domain for reliability and a higher call-frequency limit; developers must update their bookmarks and tools by October 22 to avoid disruption; on that day `store.steampowered.com/appreviews/<appid>?json=1` is disabled; the replacement is the WebAPI `IUserReviewsService` method `GetAppReviews`; and the post says requests must include the WebAPI key associated with the game (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/rss/). The announcement's own detail page returned only the title and site navigation to the summariser, so the body text above comes from the feed, not the detail page (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/676258795703241581). A news article dated 2026-10-05 gives the same announcement date and the October 22 shutdown (verified from source: https://mixed-news.com/en/steam-user-reviews-api-october-22-replacement-no-key/). A gamedev.net repost of the notice exists but returned HTTP 403 on fetch (search-summary: https://gamedev.net/news/6178/).

The docs. The Steamworks page for the old method now carries the notice that the endpoint is deprecated and to use `IUserReviewsService#GetAppReviews`; it gives no removal date (verified from source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/getreviews). The new service page documents `GET https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/` with parameters in `input_json`, the key as optional ("does not require a key"), anonymous responses cacheable for up to 10 minutes, and HTTP 429 on rate limiting (verified from source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IUserReviewsService). The docs list these differences from `/appreviews`: string filter values become enums, `language` becomes `languages` (list), the response has no `success` field, `author.num_games_owned` is gone, `weighted_vote_score` is a number instead of a string, each review gains `refunded`, hardware strings are no longer profanity-filtered, and `total_matching` and `day_range_used` are new (verified from source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IUserReviewsService).

The key conflict. The announcement says the key must be passed; the docs say it is optional (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/rss/ versus https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IUserReviewsService). A keyless call to the new endpoint for app 413150 on 2026-10-24 returned JSON, so the docs match behaviour at least for anonymous reads (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/?input_json=%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%2C%22num_per_page%22%3A1%7D). One search summary says a PR needed its own key sent as an `x-webapi-key` header; this is unattributed and conflicts with the keyless result: unverified.

Live behaviour on and after the cutoff.

- A GET to `https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/413150?json=1&num_per_page=1` on 2026-10-24 returned an HTML page opening with "Welcome to Steam", not JSON (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/413150?json=1&num_per_page=1).
- A downstream repository reports the same: from 22 October 2026 the old URL answered HTTP 200 with the store home page, and its first scan on 23 October (UTC) failed with a JSON parse error on a `<!DOCTYPE` body (verified from source: https://github.com/Statusnone420/Crimson-Desert-Report-Hub/pull/50). The Content-Type of that response was not stated.
- The new endpoint on 2026-10-24 returned `response` keys `query_summary`, `reviews`, `cursor`, `day_range_used`, `total_matching`; `query_summary` keys `num_reviews`, `review_score`, `review_score_desc`, `total_positive`, `total_negative`, `total_reviews`; and review keys `recommendationid`, `author`, `language`, `review`, `timestamp_created`, `timestamp_updated`, `voted_up`, `votes_up`, `votes_funny`, `weighted_vote_score`, `comment_count`, `steam_purchase`, `received_for_free`, `written_during_early_access`, `primarily_steam_deck`, `refunded` (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/?input_json=%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%2C%22num_per_page%22%3A1%7D).
- A search summary of a third-party migration PR says some test apps returned HTTP 200 with empty bodies and `x-eresult=42` after the cutoff (search-summary: https://github.com/draknorr/piq/pull/135, seen only as a search result).
- An open-source tool opened a migration issue on 2026-10-12 citing the October 22 date; it does not mention appdetails or any other store endpoint changing (verified from source: https://github.com/TMHSDigital/steam-mcp/issues/23).

### 2. Other Valve announcements and news in the window

The Steamworks Development feed lists these items for 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-23, newest first (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/rss/):

- 2026-10-23, "Steam's Personal Calendar Full Release": the Personal Calendar leaves Steam Labs and becomes a store feature with the Steam update of 23 October.
- 2026-10-15, "Updated Achievement System": a rebuilt achievement editor in Steamworks.
- 2026-10-08, "Pricing Conversion Updates": refreshed data behind the regional pricing tools.
- 2026-10-02, "Changes to Steam User Reviews API": section 1.
- 2026-10-01, "Steam Deck Framerate data": a partner dashboard chart, expanded on 2026-10-21.
- 2026-09-29, "Upcoming Changes to the Discounts & Events Section on Steam": curated placements replaced by dynamic recommendations, curated calendar to stop in early 2027.
- 2026-09-02, "Improvements to the Financial Reporting Site", and 2026-07-24, "Steamworks SDK 1.65 has been released".

None of these concerns GetItems, appdetails, app-page markup or the anti-cheat, EULA, DRM or third-party account fields (verified from source: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/rss/). The summariser read the item bodies from the feed; the feed returned ten items, so older items are not shown.

Other places searched, with outcomes:

- Hacker News: one Algolia story query ("steam reviews api") returned nine unrelated or old stories and nothing about the endpoint change (verified from source: https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search_by_date?query=steam%20reviews%20api&tags=story). A single query is weak evidence.
- SteamDB blog: the page returned HTTP 403 (https://steamdb.info/blog/). A web search for "SteamDB blog October 2026" surfaced no post about store APIs; it returned news about a concurrent-user record and the Nexus Mods acquisition of SteamDB (search-summary: https://tech-insider.org/steam-43-million-concurrent-users-record-2026/).
- Not checked: Valve developer forums (partner forums sit behind sign-in), the Steam news hub, SteamDB changelist pages, and any Steamworks API changelog page (none was located). The dated Steamworks documentation notices that exist are the two in section 1.

### 3. Protobuf history: StoreItem_ExtraDetails before and after 2026-10-22

Where the message lives. `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` is defined in `webui/common.proto`, not in `webui/service_storebrowse.proto` (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, characters 200000 onward; the other file holds only `CStoreBrowse_*` request and response messages: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/service_storebrowse.proto). The GitHub API reports commit URLs under `SteamTracking/Protobufs` while the raw URLs under `SteamDatabase/Protobufs` still resolve; why is not established (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commits?path=webui/common.proto&since=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z&per_page=100).

The four kinds, current definition (master, after the last commit of 2026-10-23 05:30 UTC):

- `drm_third_party_type`: field 5, string. `drm_activation_limit`: field 6, string.
- `user_account_third_party`: field 7, string. `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam`: field 8, bool.
- `anticheat`: field 9, message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat` with `kernel_mode` (1, bool), `uninstall_completely` (2, bool), `boot_protection` (3, bool), `boot_protection_name` (4, string), `name` (5, string), `name_loc` (6, string).
- `eula`: field 10, repeated message `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Eula` with `name` (1, string) and `url` (2, string).

All of this is from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto (verified from source). Related fields from the same file: `content_survey_notes` 16, `content_survey_ai_notes` 17, `ai_generation_service` 11. No message named for DRM or user accounts exists; those are plain fields of `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` (same source).

Checkpoints. I read the `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` field table at these commits of `webui/common.proto`; fields 1 to 27 (including 5 to 10) have the same numbers and names, and the same scalar types, at all of them:

- bb294c34, committed 2026-10-02 02:39 UTC (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/bb294c34f5f4704b10da5a8ed51e898a8cbbf31c/webui/common.proto).
- 78c82519, 2026-10-05 22:17 UTC (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/78c82519b58d748a4f99dac78cf624fc5cea6282/webui/common.proto).
- 5805db06, 2026-10-08 01:31 UTC (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/5805db068b7d348eda0ffd322c598fe69957c206/webui/common.proto).
- 184badc2, 2026-10-14 00:46 UTC (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/184badc242dae6153ce875eeb8217c14b1ce3f3c/webui/common.proto).

- master as read on 2026-10-24 (source in the previous paragraph). The tables are summariser output, not diffs.

What did change, in order:

1. Between bb294c34 (2026-10-02) and 78c82519 (2026-10-05): the types of fields 9, 10 and 11 changed from `StoreItem_Anticheat`, `StoreItem_Eula` and `StoreItem_AIGeneratedContentService` to `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat`, `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Eula` and `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_AIGeneratedContentService`; the member fields of each type are the same (verified from source: the bb294c34 and 78c82519 raw files above). The common.proto commits in that window are bd8f82df (2026-10-04, a descriptor.proto reorganisation) and 78c82519; I did not read which one made the edit (verified from source for the commit list: https://api.github.com/repos/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commits?path=webui/common.proto&since=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z&per_page=100). Message type names are not part of the JSON response (unverified general protobuf-JSON knowledge).

Between 5805db06 (2026-10-08) and 184badc2 (2026-10-14): fields 28 `system_requirements`, 29 `running_time_minutes`, 30 `episode`, 31 `seasons` and 32 `video_extras_note` appear (verified from source: the 5805db06 and 184badc2 raw files above). The commits in that window are 42cc5a96, 2d1c5e5f and 184badc2; not narrowed further.

In 94546e80, dated 2026-10-21 00:15:53 UTC: `optional bool has_community_hub = 33;` is added to `StoreItem_ExtraDetails`; the same commit adds `CMsgKeyValuePair` and `CMsgKeyValueSet` to common.proto, `is_public` to a cloud upload request, and `include_all_free_games` to `CPlayer_GetOwnedGames_Request`, and no line touches anticheat, eula, drm, user account or content survey fields (verified from source: https://github.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commit/94546e8057dc80a155d4c52f05f6b230a97919e4.patch). The 89b77382 table lacks field 33 and the 94546e80 table has it, and 94546e80 is the only common.proto commit between them (verified from source: the two raw files and the commit list above).

The commit of 2026-10-22 00:23:01 UTC (5c2b73b2) changes only remote play and streaming messages in webui/common.proto (adds `CSetSupportedColorspacesMsg` and a few streaming fields, removes `CInputLatencyTestMsg`) (verified from source: https://github.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commit/5c2b73b2.patch). The next commit, 6c35e1ad of 2026-10-23 05:30 UTC, lists only audio protos (verified from source for the file list: https://api.github.com/repos/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commits?since=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z&per_page=100).

Request side. `StoreBrowseItemDataRequest` has `include_extra_details` as field 18 on master, next to `include_best_purchase_option` (19) and `include_optin_registration_tags` (20) (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, characters 150000 onward). Related store protos. `webui/service_storequery.proto` changed on 2026-10-08 (e621d3f0: new `compatibility_filter` field 18 on `CStoreQueryFilters` and a nested `CStoreQueryFilters_CompatibilityFilter` with `device` and `categories`) and on 2026-10-16 (6a6f9a36: `use_name_match_scoring` field 11 on `CStoreQuery_SearchSuggestions_Request`); neither touches the four kinds (verified from source: https://github.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commit/e621d3f0946c0033dea4a357b53af95724cb74b3.patch and https://github.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commit/6a6f9a368079d9069a656e4f3786e8c6e9b14ded.patch). Timing caveat. A protobuf commit date is when the tracker saw a new Steam web build, not when the server began to emit a field. The commit of 2026-10-21 and the fixture capture of 2026-10-20 bracket the first sighting of `has_community_hub`, but the server could have started earlier or later (unverified inference).

### 4. Live GetItems against the captured fixtures

Fixtures. `tests/fixtures/getitems/*.json` were captured on 2026-10-20 from a European location with `include_extra_details: true`, keyless, cookie-less; `scripts/capture_fixtures.py` strips `related_items` and `best_purchase_option` from each item and `system_requirements`, `early_access`, `partner_awards_bbcode`, `links_and_info`, `press_review`, `legal_notice_bbcode`, `eula` and `section` from `extra_details` (read from the repo: `tests/fixtures/README.md` and `scripts/capture_fixtures.py`). Because `eula` is stripped, the fixtures hold no EULA baseline. They also hold no `drm_third_party_type` or `drm_activation_limit` value.

Method. I re-issued the capture request for the seven `mixed-states.json` IDs (5072580, 1808500, 1938090, 413150, 339800, 99999999, 50300; `english`, `US`) on 2026-10-24 and compared key lists and values (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A5072580%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1808500%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1938090%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A339800%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A99999999%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A50300%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). The summariser returned key lists, not byte-identical bodies, so the comparison is on keys and the values listed below.

Result, net of the keys the capture script strips:

- Top-level item keys are unchanged for all seven IDs. 99999999 still returns `success: 15`, `visible: false`, an empty name and `store_url_path: "app/0/"` with no `extra_details`; 50300 still returns `unlisted: true`.
- Added: `extra_details.has_community_hub` appears on every item that has `extra_details`. Raw dumps show `"has_community_hub":true` for 413150 and 339800 (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A413150%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A339800%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D) and for 3159330 (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A3159330%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). Before this note was written, no fixture and no other file in the repo contained the string `has_community_hub` (read from the repo with a grep). The field is not in the capture script's removal list, so it was not in the 2026-10-20 responses unless it is region or request dependent (unverified; the live calls came from a different location).
- Removed or renamed: no field was removed or renamed in any of the seven items.
- Values that match the fixtures: `anticheat` for 1808500 is `{"kernel_mode":true,"name":"Denuvo","name_loc":"#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo"}`; `anticheat` for 1938090 is `{"kernel_mode":true,"uninstall_completely":true,"boot_protection":true,"boot_protection_name":"secureboot_tpm2"}`; 1938090 `user_account_third_party` is "Activision Account" with `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam: true`; 5072580 `ai_generation_service` is `{"name":"OpenAI API","url":"https://openai.com/api/"}`; the first 80 characters of `content_survey_ai_notes` match for 1808500, 1938090 and 5072580 (verified from source: the first URL above, compared with `tests/fixtures/getitems/mixed-states.json`).
- Not re-fetched: `german-context.json`, `search-roguelike-50.json` and `empty-response.json`; no drift claim is made for them.

Baseline for the four kinds on 2026-10-24 (no fixture exists for these apps, so this is a starting point and not drift). All six come from one request (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A3159330%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2807960%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2358720%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1172470%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A271590%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1245620%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D):

- 3159330 Assassin's Creed Shadows: `drm_third_party_type` "Denuvo Anti-tamper"; `user_account_third_party` "Ubisoft Account" with link true; one `eula` entry; no `anticheat`.
- 2807960 Battlefield 6: `anticheat` `{"kernel_mode":true,"uninstall_completely":true,"boot_protection":true,"boot_protection_name":"secureboot_tpm2"}`; `user_account_third_party` "EA Account linking required" with link true; one `eula`.
- 2358720 Black Myth: Wukong: `drm_third_party_type` "Denuvo"; one `eula`; no account or anticheat.
- 1172470 Apex Legends: `anticheat` `{"kernel_mode":true,"name":"Easy Anti-Cheat","name_loc":"#Store_AntiCheat_Type_easyac"}`; `user_account_third_party` "EA Account" with link true; one `eula` whose URL ends `_eula_1`.
- 271590 Grand Theft Auto V Legacy: `anticheat` `{"kernel_mode":true,"name":"BattlEye","name_loc":"#Store_AntiCheat_Type_battleye"}`; `user_account_third_party` "Rockstar Games" with link true; one `eula`; `unlisted: true`.
- 1245620 ELDEN RING: two `eula` entries ("ELDEN RING EULA" and "ELDEN RING EULA (JP)"); no `anticheat`, DRM or account field.

`drm_activation_limit` is absent from all twelve valid items checked across both requests, including 3159330, even though that app's page and appdetails show an activation-limit line (section 5). The `eula` URL form is `https://store.steampowered.com//eula/<appid>_eula_<n>` (with a double slash) in the live responses, and the same form appears in the 1808500 app-page fixture (verified from source: the request above and `tests/fixtures/app-page/1808500-ai-only.html`).

### 5. appdetails and app-page markup

appdetails. On 2026-10-24, appdetails for 3159330 returns the keys `drm_notice` ("Denuvo Anti-tamper<br>5 a day machine activation limit") and `ext_user_account_notice` ("Ubisoft Account (Supports Linking to Steam Account)") and has no key for EULA or anti-cheat (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=3159330&cc=us&l=english). For 1938090 it returns `ext_user_account_notice` ("Activision Account (Supports Linking to Steam Account)") and no `drm_notice` (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=1938090&cc=us&l=english). For 1808500 it returns neither notice key and no EULA or anti-cheat key (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=1808500&cc=us&l=english). A request for two app IDs at once returned HTTP 400; the cause was not investigated (https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=1938090,1808500&cc=us&l=english). The repo holds no appdetails baseline from before 2026-10-22, so no appdetails drift can be asserted; only the present shape is recorded.

App-page text. The live 1808500 page text matches the fixture `1808500-ai-only.html` for the anti-cheat notice ("Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat", then "Denuvo - Requires manual removal after game uninstall"), the EULA notice ("Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" with link text "ARC Raiders EULA" and the `//eula/1808500_eula_0` URL), and the AI block (heading "AI Generated Content Disclosure", opening line "The developers describe how their game uses AI Generated Content like this:") (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1808500/?l=english, compared with the fixture file). The live 3159330 page shows, after the Features list and before Languages: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper" with "5 a day machine activation limit", "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Ubisoft Account (Supports Linking to Steam Account)" and "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" with "Assassin's Creed Shadows EULA" (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=english). No fixture covers the DRM or third-party account notices, so these wordings are a baseline.

App-page markup. The fetch tool returned plain text, so class names, element nesting and roles of the live pages were not compared. The fixture records `div.anticheat_section.DRM_notice` holding a `div` with the notice and `div.anticheat_name` with a `span.anticheat_uninstalls`, and `div.DRM_notice[role=button]` for the EULA notice (read from the repo: `tests/fixtures/app-page/1808500-ai-only.html`, lines 70 to 77). Whether that markup is unchanged since 2026-10-20 is unverified.

One cross-source fact for the uninstall wording: the live 1808500 GetItems `anticheat` object has no `uninstall_completely` key while the page says removal is manual after uninstall, and the 1938090 object has `uninstall_completely: true`. This suggests an absent key renders the manual-removal text; that is an inference from two data points and is unverified (sources: the first GetItems request above and https://store.steampowered.com/app/1808500/?l=english).

## Caveats and version notes

- Scope of the "reviews API" change: it covers the bulk review list only. The old URL is gone; the review summary values that appdetails carries (the `reviews` key for 1808500) were not examined for change.
- The announcement and the docs disagree on whether a key is required; on 2026-10-24 a keyless call worked. A future enforcement change would not show up in this note.
- All "same at every checkpoint" claims for the protobuf rest on summariser tables of seven file versions, not diffs. A subtle change (for example a default value or an option) could be missed. The four patches I read (5c2b73b2, 94546e80 and the two storequery commits) are the only diffs.
- The repo-wide commit list was truncated by the fetch (25 commits read, back to 2026-10-04); the path-filtered list for webui/common.proto (23 commits since 2026-09-01) came back whole.
- Not examined: the large October commits 78c82519 (32 files), 184badc2 and 89b77382 (58 files) beyond the `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` table, and any change to `StoreBrowseItemDataRequest` before the checkpoints.
- Live calls came from the research tooling, not from the capture location; region-dependent fields would show as false drift. The `has_community_hub` observation was repeated across three separate requests that all agree.
- The fixture README states captures from 2026-10-20 for GetItems and app pages; the next-fest surface capture is dated 2026-10-21 and is not a GetItems capture (read from the repo: `tests/fixtures/README.md`).
- No claim here covers the Steam client, the Steam Deck UI or other Valve products.
```

`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq4-stability-localization.md`:

```md
# RQ4: How stable and localized are the signals?

Researched 2026-10-24. Every web read went through a small summarizing model (WebFetch), so strings are as that model reproduced them, not byte-exact page source. Element classes and counts came from a third-party CSS-selector fetch API (microlink, `prerender=false`) until it answered HTTP 429 late in the session. Tags at the end of a claim: "verified from source" means read on the cited page or API response (through the summarizer); "search-summary" means seen only in a search result; "unverified" means inferred or not checked. The fetch tool refused web.archive.org, so no Wayback snapshot could be read (see caveats). Non-ASCII characters are written as `\uXXXX` escapes to keep the note ASCII. Test apps: 3159330 (Assassin's Creed Shadows), 2807960 (Battlefield 6), 1172470 (Apex Legends), 2358720 (Black Myth: Wukong), 271590 (GTA V Legacy), 1808500 (ARC Raiders), 1245620 (Elden Ring), 570 (Dota 2).

## Answer in short

- Every notice string on the app page is localized and differs per `?l=` language (seven languages checked on one app; german and spanish also on a kernel anti-cheat app). Latam is a separate translation from spanish. Text is no usable key; the stable hooks are classes and hrefs: `.anticheat_section` (plus `DRM_notice` for kernel, `anticheat_nonkernel_notice` for non-kernel), `.anticheat_name`, `.anticheat_uninstalls`, `a[href*="/eula/"]`. `.DRM_notice` is a mixed bucket (account, kernel anti-cheat, EULA, AI service), so its count is no per-kind signal.
- GetItems `extra_details` is language-neutral for every field the four kinds use: `anticheat.kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection`, `boot_protection_name` (token `secureboot_tpm2`), `anticheat.name_loc` (five tokens seen: vac, easyac, battleye, ace, denuvo), `drm_third_party_type`, `user_account_third_party`, `eula[]`. Only the content survey free text (when translated) and item names localize.
- GetItems is a subset of the page: the activation-limit line ("5 a day") and custom anti-cheat names ("EA Javelin Anticheat") show on the page and are absent from GetItems for the apps tested. Older titles also keep anti-cheat names inside `drm_third_party_type`.
- Coverage: apps, DLC, demos and software return `extra_details`; packages return none; missing apps and bundle 1 return `success: 15`; delisted apps stay `success: 1` with `unlisted: true`. Some mature apps redirect cookie-less page fetches to `/agecheck/` for some clients and adult-only apps go to login; GetItems was never gated.
- History: the anti-cheat declaration tool was announced 2024-10-30; the DRM, account and EULA notices are older (forum evidence from 2014, search-summary); markup history could not be read because Wayback is blocked; the public protobuf has no `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` through 2025-08-29.

## Findings

### 1. Are the page notice strings localized?

Yes, all of them. Cookie-less fetch of `https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=<language>`, features sidebar, 2026-10-24 (verified from source for each line below):

- english: "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper"; "5 a day machine activation limit"; "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Ubisoft Account (Supports Linking to Steam Account)"; "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=english)
- german: "Drittanbieter-DRM: Denuvo Anti-tamper"; "5 a day Aktivierungslimit (Ger\u00e4te)"; "Ben\u00f6tigt einen Drittanbieteraccount: Ubisoft Account (Unterst\u00fctzt Verkn\u00fcpfung mit Steam-Account)"; "Erfordert Zustimmung einer Drittanbieter-EULA" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=german)
- spanish: "DRM de terceros: Denuvo Anti-tamper"; "5 a day equipo(s) como l\u00edmite de activaci\u00f3n"; "Requiere una cuenta de terceros: Ubisoft Account (permite la vinculaci\u00f3n a una cuenta de Steam)"; "Es necesario aceptar un ALUF de terceros" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=spanish)
- latam: DRM, activation and EULA lines identical to spanish; the account line ends "(Soporta la vinculaci\u00f3n a una cuenta de Steam)" instead of "(permite ...)". So latam is its own translation and can differ by a word from spanish (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=latam)
- schinese, japanese, russian: all four lines differ again and are non-Latin except the data values. Glosses only (script not reproduced here): schinese "includes third-party DRM: ...", "5 a day - machine activation limit", "requires third-party account: ... (supports linking to Steam account)", "requires agreement to a third-party end user license agreement"; japanese the same four meanings in its own wording; russian "third-party DRM protection: ...", "5 a day - maximum number of devices", "additional registration required: ... (can be linked to Steam account)", "requires accepting a third-party user agreement:" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=schinese, https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=japanese, https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=russian)

Kernel anti-cheat and related lines on app 2807960 (Battlefield 6), same method (verified from source):

- english: "Requires 3rd-Party Account: EA Account linking required (Supports Linking to Steam Account)"; "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat"; "EA Javelin Anticheat"; "Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0"; "Requires agreement to a 3rd-Party EULA"; a second EULA block "EA Play subscription requires acceptance of" with link "EA Play Terms" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/2807960/?l=english)
- german: "Verwendet Anti-Cheat-Software auf Kernel-Ebene"; "Abonnement von EA Play erfordert Zustimmung von:"; the boot protection line was read as run-together text ("Sicherer Start" followed by "Erfordert sowohl Sicherer Start als auch TPM 2.0"), so its exact label is uncertain (https://store.steampowered.com/app/2807960/?l=german)
- spanish: "Utiliza antitrampas a nivel de kernel"; "Protecci\u00f3n de arranque - Requiere tanto arranque seguro como TPM 2.0"; "Tu suscripci\u00f3n a EA Play requiere la aprobaci\u00f3n de" (https://store.steampowered.com/app/2807960/?l=spanish)
- Non-kernel declaration (Dota 2, VAC): english "Uses Anti-Cheat Software", german "Verwendet Anti-Cheat-Software" (verified from source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F570%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.ac.selectorAll=.anticheat_section&data.ac.attr=html and the same URL with `l%3Dgerman`)
- Uninstall suffix inside `.anticheat_uninstalls`: english " - Requires manual removal after game uninstall" (hyphen), german "\u2013 Erfordert nach der Deinstallation des Spiels eine manuelle Entfernung" (an en dash inside the translation). The separator is part of the translated string (verified from source: https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F1172470%2F%3Fl%3Dgerman&meta=false&prerender=false&data.drm.selectorAll=.DRM_notice&data.drm.attr=html&data.acn.selectorAll=.anticheat_name&data.acn.attr=html)
- Secure Boot warning block in the Links and info area: english "Secure Boot & TPM 2.0 Not Detected", german "Sicherer Start und TPM 2.0 nicht erkannt", spanish "Arranque seguro y TPM 2.0 no detectados", linking to https://help.steampowered.com/faqs/view/7451-A8FE-3867-6A2E (verified from source on the three 2807960 URLs above). Whether "Not Detected" depends on the visitor's machine or is a server default was not tested (unverified).

Parts that stay constant across languages (verified from source, same pages): the data values `Denuvo Anti-tamper`, `Ubisoft Account`, `EA Account linking required`, `EA Javelin Anticheat`, `Easy Anti-Cheat`, `VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)`; the activation value `5 a day` (the proto field `drm_activation_limit` is a string, so this is publisher text and no number); the EULA link text (`Assassin's Creed Shadows EULA`); and the EULA href `https://store.steampowered.com//eula/<appid>_eula_<n>` with a double slash as served (3159330 `_eula_0`, 1172470 `_eula_1`, BF6 `2807960_eula_0` plus `1289670_eula_0` for EA Play Terms). The Mature Content Description heading is localized too: german "Beschreibung nicht jugendfreier Inhalte", spanish and latam "Descripci\u00f3n del contenido para adultos", schinese, japanese and russian each their own (verified from source, same 3159330 pages).

Retranslation risk, evidence from outside these notices: Valve changed the AI heading in Russian (fixed in a third-party tool 2026-02-25) and French (2026-09-24), per this repo's RQ2 note (docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq2-data-surface.md, citing https://api.github.com/repos/seeeeew/aiwarningforsteam/issues/13/comments; not re-read here: search-summary level for this note). No retranslation event for the four notices above was found, and the absence of past changes is unverified. Spanish versus latam differing by a word shows the strings are kept per locale file (verified from source for the difference).

### 2. Which structural hooks stay constant?

Server HTML, class names and counts (microlink, cookie-less, `prerender=false`; the committed fixtures cross-check):

- Kernel anti-cheat: `<div class="anticheat_section DRM_notice">` holding a plain `<div>` with the localized "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat" text and `<div class="anticheat_name">` with the name followed by `<span class="anticheat_uninstalls">...</span>`. Seen in the ARC Raiders fixture, lines 70 to 73, captured 2026-10-20 (tests/fixtures/app-page/1808500-ai-only.html, tests/fixtures/README.md), and as the second `.DRM_notice` of Apex Legends (https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F1172470%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.drm.selectorAll=.DRM_notice&data.drm.attr=html&data.acn.selectorAll=.anticheat_name&data.acn.attr=html). Verified from source.
- Non-kernel anti-cheat: the class list is exactly `anticheat_section anticheat_nonkernel_notice` with no `DRM_notice` class; Dota 2 had `.DRM_notice` null while `.anticheat_section` matched, in english and german, with an empty `<span class="anticheat_uninstalls"></span>` (https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F570%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.drm.selectorAll=.DRM_notice&data.drm.attr=html&data.ac.selectorAll=.anticheat_section&data.ac.attr=class&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text). Verified from source. PCGamesN reported the launch images as gold for kernel and blue for regular anti-cheat, which fits the two class names (https://www.pcgamesn.com/valve/kernel-anti-cheat-flags; the article gives no class names, so the link is inference: unverified).
- Third-party account: a plain `.DRM_notice` element with text and `&nbsp;` around the account name and no inner classes (Apex Legends, first of three `.DRM_notice`, same Apex microlink URL as above). Verified from source.
- Third-party EULA: a `.DRM_notice` (the fixture shows `role="button"`) with a label `<div>` and a second `<div>` holding `<a href="https://store.steampowered.com//eula/..." onclick="ShowEULA( this ); return false;">`, so `a[href*="/eula/"]` matches and a click opens a modal (Apex microlink above; ARC Raiders fixture lines 74 to 77). Verified from source.
- `.DRM_notice` count per page: Apex Legends 3 in both english and german (account, kernel anti-cheat, EULA); ARC Raiders 2 (kernel anti-cheat, EULA); Dota 2 0; app 5072580 1, and that one is the AI service notice "Connects to 3rd-Party Service for AI Content Generation:" with a link (tests/fixtures/app-page/5072580-ai-first.html lines 75 to 77). So `.DRM_notice` also carries the AI service line, and counting it says nothing about the DRM kind. Verified from source. The count was compared across languages for Apex only (identical); other apps were not compared.
- Third-party DRM line and activation-limit line: markup not captured. The microlink run for Assassin's Creed Shadows ended on the age check page and the run for Black Myth: Wukong returned HTTP 429, so the classes of "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM" and "5 a day machine activation limit" are unverified. They appear as separate sidebar lines in the text fetch (https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=english).
- One page can carry two EULA links with different lead-in labels (Battlefield 6: "Battlefield 6 EULA" and "EA Play Terms"), so a count of `a[href*="/eula/"]` is no count of agreements per kind (https://store.steampowered.com/app/2807960/?l=english). Verified from source.

### 3. Does GetItems return language-neutral values? Every name_loc token found

Request: `https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json={"ids":[{"appid":...}],"context":{"language":"<lang>","country_code":"<cc>"},"data_request":{"include_extra_details":true}}`, keyless.

Neutral under a language change (verified from source): apps 2807960, 2358720, 1172470, 271590, 1808500 and 1245620 returned identical `anticheat` objects, `drm_third_party_type`, `user_account_third_party`, `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` and `eula[].name` under `english/US` and `german/DE` contexts; app 3159330 returned the same `drm_third_party_type` "Denuvo Anti-tamper", `user_account_third_party` "Ubisoft Account" and eula under `english`, `german` and `spanish` contexts (example read: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A3159330%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22german%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22DE%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). The repo fixture agrees for Call of Duty under german: `user_account_third_party` stays "Activision Account" and the `anticheat` booleans equal the english capture (tests/fixtures/getitems/german-context.json against tests/fixtures/getitems/mixed-states.json). Compared fields only; other keys were not diffed.

Localized in GetItems (verified from source): item `name` (the demo 4616220 returned a Chinese-script name under a spanish context) and the content survey free text when the publisher supplied a translation (Call of Duty returned a German `content_survey_ai_notes` while 5072580 stayed English; tests/fixtures/getitems/german-context.json, tests/fixtures/README.md). The translation of the four kinds happens in Valve's page templates, not in the API.

Anti-cheat object, from the protobuf (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, offsets 150000 and 200000, two reads agree; verified from source): `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat { bool kernel_mode = 1; bool uninstall_completely = 2; bool boot_protection = 3; string boot_protection_name = 4; string name = 5; string name_loc = 6; }`. Related fields of `StoreItem_ExtraDetails`: `drm_third_party_type = 5` (string), `drm_activation_limit = 6` (string), `user_account_third_party = 7` (string), `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam = 8` (bool), `anticheat = 9`, `repeated eula = 10` with `name = 1` and `url = 2`, `ai_generation_service = 11`, `legal_notice_bbcode = 14`, `content_survey_notes = 16`, `content_survey_ai_notes = 17`. There is no enum for anti-cheat types; `name_loc` and `boot_protection_name` are plain strings.

Every `name_loc` token found, over 26 apps in english context (verified from source; GetItems with ids 730, 252490, 578080, 359550, 381210, 1085660, 1599340, 2507950, 2767030, 1203220, 1517290, 346110, 2073850, 1172620, 553850, 582660, 216150, 570, 221100, 552500 plus the six-app read above):

- `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_vac`, `name` "VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)": apps 730 and 570, which carry no `kernel_mode`.
- `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_easyac`, `name` "Easy Anti-Cheat": apps 252490, 381210, 1599340, 553850, 552500, 1172470.
- `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_battleye`, `name` "BattlEye": apps 1085660, 221100, 271590.
- `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_ace`, `name` "Anti-Cheat Expert (ACE)": app 2507950.
- `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo`, `name` "Denuvo": apps 2073850, 1808500.

The Steamworks form's pre-populated list is login-gated, so these five are the tokens that occurred in the sample; others very likely exist (unverified). The pattern is `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_<lowercase vendor key>`. The page shows the vendor name unchanged in german ("Easy Anti-Cheat", "VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)"), so only the surrounding sentence is translated.

`boot_protection_name` is a second neutral token without a leading `#`: `secureboot_tpm2` (Battlefield 6, Call of Duty). The page renders it as the localized "Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0" line (section 1). Verified from source.

Other values seen (verified from source):

- `kernel_mode` true with `name` and `name_loc` absent: PUBG 578080, MapleStory 216150, Battlefield 2042 1517290, Call of Duty 1938090, Battlefield 6 2807960.
- False booleans are omitted instead of sent as false (ARC Raiders has only `kernel_mode` and `name`/`name_loc`), so absent reads as false (inference from the sample).
- Free-text `user_account_third_party`: "EA Account", "EA Account linking required", "Rockstar Games", "Ubisoft Account", "Ubisoft Connect launcher", "Embark ID", "PlayStation Network", "Xbox Live", "Black Desert Online", "LEVEL INFINITE PASS", "Activision Account".
- Free-text `drm_third_party_type`: "Denuvo", "Denuvo Anti-tamper", "XIGNCODE3" (Black Desert), "Easy Anti-Cheat" (Sea of Thieves), and a long sentence for Battlefield 2042 ("EA online activation and EA app software installation and background use required. Denuvo Anti-tamper"). A "third-party DRM" detector keyed on that field would flag Easy Anti-Cheat and XIGNCODE3 as DRM, because anti-cheat names also sit there for titles that predate the declaration form.

### 4. Where the page and GetItems disagree

- Activation limit: the page for 3159330 shows "5 a day machine activation limit" in all seven languages, while `extra_details` for 3159330 has no `drm_activation_limit` key in english, german and spanish reads (keys: vetted, controller_wizard_complete, drm_third_party_type, user_account_third_party, user_account_third_party_link_to_steam, eula, section, legal_notice_bbcode, content_survey_notes, links_and_info, points_shop_eligible, system_requirements, has_community_hub; spanish read: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A4616220%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A3159330%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22spanish%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22ES%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). The proto declares the field. Verified from source; why the response omits it is unverified.
- Custom anti-cheat name: the page for 2807960 shows "EA Javelin Anticheat" in english, german and spanish, while GetItems `anticheat` for 2807960 holds `kernel_mode`, `uninstall_completely`, `boot_protection` and `boot_protection_name` and no `name` or `name_loc` (same key set as the Call of Duty fixture). Verified from source; the cause is unverified.
- Uninstall suffix: `uninstall_completely` true produced no "Requires manual removal" line (Battlefield 6 page); absent produced the suffix on kernel entries (Apex Legends, ARC Raiders); the non-kernel entry (Dota 2, `uninstall_completely` absent) renders an empty suffix span. The suffix depends on both flags (verified from source on four apps).
- Second EULA: the page for 2807960 carries "Battlefield 6 EULA" and "EA Play Terms", while the GetItems read listed one eula name for 2807960 (the prompt asked for names, so a second entry may have been dropped by the summarizer): unverified.

Consequence for the extension: for the four kinds GetItems gives language-neutral booleans for kernel anti-cheat and neutral strings for account, DRM type and EULA, while the page is a superset for the activation limit and custom anti-cheat names.

### 5. Coverage by item type and state

GetItems with `include_extra_details`, english context (verified from source, plus the repo fixture tests/fixtures/getitems/mixed-states.json captured 2026-10-20):

- Game (type 0): `success: 1` and `extra_details` present; the four kinds appear only when the publisher declared them. Elden Ring (1245620) returned two EULA entries ("ELDEN RING EULA", "ELDEN RING EULA (JP)") and no anticheat key; Stardew Valley's `extra_details` holds no eula, drm, account or anticheat keys (fixture).
- DLC: Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree (2778580) returned `type: 4`, `success: 1`, `extra_details` keys vetted, controller_wizard_complete, legal_notice_bbcode, interactive_elements, press_review, links_and_info, points_shop_eligible, metacritic, system_requirements: no eula, drm or anticheat (https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A2778580%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A365670%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A228980%7D%2C%7B%22packageid%22%3A320795%7D%2C%7B%22bundleid%22%3A1%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A4618750%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). Whether DLC pages inherit the parent's notices on the HTML page was not tested: unverified.
- Software: Blender (365670) returned `type: 6`, `success: 1`, `is_free: true`, `extra_details` keys vetted, legal_notice_bbcode, links_and_info, system_requirements, has_community_hub (same URL).
- Demo: Dice Tavern: Farkle Roguelike Demo (4616220) returned `type: 1`, `success: 1`, `extra_details` keys vetted, controller_wizard_complete, links_and_info, system_requirements (spanish-context read URL in section 4); the type value also appears in tests/fixtures/getitems/search-roguelike-50.json. This demo carries no notices.
- Package: `{"packageid":320795}` (Batman: Arkham Collection) returned `item_type: 1`, `success: 1`, `visible: true`, `store_url_path: "sub/320795/"`, `type: 0`, no `appid` and no `extra_details` key (same URL as DLC).
- Bundle: `{"bundleid":1}` returned `item_type: 2`, `success: 15`, `visible: false`, empty name, `store_url_path: "bundle/1/"`, no `extra_details`. A valid bundle was not tested, so the shape of an existing bundle is unverified.
- Missing or hidden app: appid 99999999 returned `success: 15`, `visible: false`, `appid: 0`, `store_url_path: "app/0/"` and no `extra_details` (fixture mixed-states.json); appid 228980 (Steamworks Common Redistributables) returned the same shape (DLC URL above). The response is a normal 200 with the item present in `store_items`, so the failure signal is `success != 1` and no array entry goes missing.
- Delisted or unlisted: Spec Ops: The Line (50300) and GTA V Legacy (271590) return `success: 1`, `visible: true`, `unlisted: true`, with `extra_details` still present; GTA V Legacy keeps its BattlEye anticheat object, Rockstar account and EULA.
- Adult-only: HuniePop (339800) returns `success: 1` with `extra_details` (vetted, content_survey_notes, points_shop_eligible) even though its page needs login (fixture). Assassin's Creed Shadows (content descriptors 2 and 5) returned full `extra_details` while the page redirected one client to the age check (section 6).
- Old titles: titles that were already on sale long before 2024 carry the fields when the publisher set them (GTA V Legacy anticheat, Black Desert drm type); other older titles carry no notice keys (Spec Ops). A missing key cannot tell "none" from "never entered" (inference).
- Region-restricted titles: the proto has `unvailable_for_country_restriction` in `StoreItem` (spelling as in the proto, per this repo's RQ2 note citing https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto); no title unavailable in a test country was queried and no `country_code` variation was run: unverified.
- Response shape: the root `response` holds only `store_items`; order equals request order (tests/fixtures/README.md); a 20-id request worked in this session and 50 ids per this repo's RQ2 note.
- Rule that follows (inference): treat `success != 1` and a missing `extra_details` as "unknown"; treat a present `extra_details` without a key as "not declared" and never as "none".

### 6. Which apps need cookies or redirect to /agecheck/?

- Assassin's Creed Shadows (3159330, descriptors 2 and 5): the cookie-less microlink fetch for `?l=english`, `?l=german` and `?l=spanish` ended on `https://store.steampowered.com/agecheck/app/3159330/` with no `#appHubAppName`, and the `<html lang>` of that page followed the `l` parameter (en, de, es). The summarizer's description of the redirect chain was ambiguous (it also mentioned a 302 to the app URL). The plain WebFetch client got the full app page for the same app in seven languages (https://api.microlink.io/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F3159330%2F%3Fl%3Denglish&meta=false&prerender=false&data.drm.selectorAll=.DRM_notice&data.drm.attr=text&data.name.selector=%23appHubAppName&data.name.attr=text and https://store.steampowered.com/app/3159330/?l=english). The gate therefore depends on the client; location is the likely driver (unverified). Verified from source for the split.
- This repo's RQ2 note recorded the same split for Call of Duty (1938090), and tests/fixtures/README.md says a European capture got full pages for 1938090, 271590, 1174180, 782330, 1091500, 1245620 and 2050650 (verified from source, repo files).
- Adult-only HuniePop (339800): redirect to `/login/?redir=.../agecheck/app/339800/...` for both clients (tests/fixtures/app-page/339800-login-redirect.html, RQ2 note). Verified from source.
- Not gated in this session: 2807960 (text fetch), 1172470 and 570 (microlink, empty redirect list).
- GetItems was never gated or cookie dependent in any call (about 30 distinct ids, all keyless, no cookies). Content descriptor IDs 2 and 5 as the agecheck trigger is inference.

### 7. History: when did each notice and field appear?

- Kernel anti-cheat declaration: Valve's Steamworks post "New Tool for Describing Anti-Cheat in Games" (title read at https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/4547038620960934857; the body was not returned by the fetch). Date and content from coverage: GamingOnLinux dated 30 October 2024 says kernel-level anti-cheat must be listed, other anti-cheat is optional, older games are included and Valve will check during release review (https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/10/steam-games-will-now-need-to-fully-disclose-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/); PCGamesN confirms the 30 October announcement and says Valve will review older games with missing data and contact their developers (https://www.pcgamesn.com/valve/kernel-anti-cheat-flags). Verified from source (two outlets agree on the date).
- Form details from a search summary: two checkboxes (kernel-level integration; leftover files after uninstall) and a requirement that anti-cheat information previously kept elsewhere on the page be migrated into the new field (search-summary: https://alternativeto.net/news/2024/10/steam-will-now-require-developers-to-disclose-kernel-mode-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/). The checkboxes match `kernel_mode` and `uninstall_completely`; the migration claim matches the anti-cheat names still sitting in `drm_third_party_type` today (section 3).
- Steamworks documentation: the Store Page doc lists "Anti-Cheat Declaration - Share anti-cheat information about your game" under the Basic Info tab and links the announcement at https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/4145017/view/4547038620960934856 (https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/page). That doc and the application doc (https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application) say nothing about the third-party DRM, account, activation limit or EULA store fields. Verified from source for these two pages; other doc pages were not searched.
- Third-party DRM, account and EULA notices: no official Valve changelog or date was found. Forum evidence only (search-summary): a 2014 thread asks that third-party DRM be stated on store pages and a 2014 reply suggests listing third-party accounts and DRM had only recently become expected; an undated thread quotes the label "Incorporates 3rd-party DRM: Denuvo Antitamper" on the right side of store pages; a 2016 thread complains that some Denuvo games show nothing about it; a 2018 thread shows the third-party EULA box; a 2023 post says the PAYDAY 3 page was updated to show Denuvo (https://forum.glasswire.com/t/steam-extra-info-in-store-page/2898, https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/1736595227852911346; the individual thread dates were not opened). The same search summary says Steamworks has separate "3rd-Party Account" and "3rd-Party DRM" flags with nothing forcing accuracy (single anecdotal source: unverified).
- Markup history: not recoverable here. The fetch tool refuses web.archive.org (the Wayback CDX call failed with a tool-level refusal). One microlink-wrapped attempt on a December 2013 snapshot of app 200260 returned null for `.DRM_notice` with page title "200260" and is inconclusive; no further Wayback attempt was made once the refusal was seen. The live kernel and non-kernel class split (`anticheat_section DRM_notice` versus `anticheat_section anticheat_nonkernel_notice`) fits a form that has a kernel flag (October 2024), but whether the pre-2024 notice used the same classes is unverified. The AI service notice reuses `.DRM_notice` (fixture 5072580); its class history is unverified.
- Protobuf history (https://api.github.com/repos/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/commits?path=webui/common.proto): `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` and `StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat` were absent from `webui/common.proto` in reads at commit aff537efac (2024-10-29, the day before the announcement), 8a2f6ef4913e3dd71664b9c727b756e38957375d (2025-02-22) and 4a4ea7b18b1c61f92594824b06601caf9b33948a (2025-08-29); each read listed the `StoreItem_*` messages in the 100000+ character region and none was `ExtraDetails` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/aff537efac/webui/common.proto and the other two shas; verified from source, one summarized read each). The patches of aff537efac and 4923293d6c (2024-11-06) showed no lines mentioning anticheat, kernel_mode or ExtraDetails, as summarized. Both messages are present on master as read 2026-10-24 (section 3). Reads at 2025-12-17 (f5c63bcba4d60670a680e2141f6ebffffdc5238c) and 2026-05-22 (33f30cb8850a55d877b47dd2a7fba1476751c7d6) were inconclusive: the page lengths reported (119,796 and 133,871 characters) were shorter than the window assumed, so the StoreItem region may not have been in view. The public proto therefore first exposes `extra_details` after 2025-08-29 at the earliest. That bounds when SteamDB's extraction saw it and says nothing about when the API began returning it (unverified).
- A search for SteamDB blog posts or Steamworks announcements about later field changes (for example a `name_loc` addition) found only the 2024-10-30 post and its coverage (search-summary).

## Caveats and version notes

- Fetch count: about 60 calls, above the 25 asked for, because three sub-questions needed API, page, markup and protobuf-history reads. The last microlink call (Black Myth: Wukong) was cut off by HTTP 429.
- All page text and JSON came through a summarizing model that cannot print long strings verbatim; key lists and short strings are reliable, long strings (the German boot protection line, the 2807960 EULA list) are flagged where doubtful. Class names and counts came from microlink and this repo's committed fixtures.
- Section 1 strings cover three apps and seven languages. Non-kernel anti-cheat text in languages beyond english and german, and the latam, schinese, japanese and russian anti-cheat lines, were not fetched.
- The five `name_loc` tokens come from 26 apps in english context; the full vocabulary is unknown. Custom anti-cheat entries appear to produce no token (Battlefield 6, Call of Duty) but their page rendering was seen only for "EA Javelin Anticheat".
- A trusted pattern for the extension: rely on GetItems booleans and `name_loc`; never match page text. Page-only data (activation limit, custom anti-cheat name) needs an HTML read with class hooks, and those classes were verified only for anti-cheat, account and EULA.
- Not answered: classes of the DRM and activation-limit lines; behavior for region-restricted titles, valid bundles and DLC pages inheriting parent notices; age-gate trigger conditions; markup history before 2024 (Wayback blocked); the exact start of the `.DRM_notice` family; when the public proto began to expose `StoreItem_ExtraDetails`.
- No instruction-like text was found in any fetched page.
```
