`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq5-gaps-and-community-data.md`:

```md
# RQ5: What do Steam's fields miss, and how do other tools cover it?

Researched 2026-10-24. Every fetch went through a small summarising model; quoted values are what that model reported from the page. Tags: `verified from source` means the primary page, file or API response was fetched and the claim read from it; `search-summary` means a search result snippet only; `unverified` means no source was reached. Project rules (Valve hosts only at runtime, no seed lists) are not argued here; the note records facts about fields and datasets.

## Answer in short

- Steam stores the four kinds as developer-typed fields in the store item (`extra_details`): `anticheat` (with a `kernel_mode` flag), `drm_third_party_type`, `user_account_third_party` and `eula`. Valve says it checks anti-cheat declarations at release and will contact developers of existing games; nothing is detected from the game files. An absent key can mean "not declared" or "none", and the two cannot be told apart.
- Gaps seen first-hand on 2026-10-24: Elden Ring and Rainbow Six Siege have no `anticheat` key although AreWeAntiCheatYet lists Easy Anti-Cheat for Elden Ring and Valve's own Steam Deck report flags an unsupported anti-cheat for Siege; Battlefield 6, Call of Duty and PUBG say `kernel_mode` true with no vendor name; Marvel Rivals has an empty `anticheat` object; DOOM: The Dark Ages still carries a Denuvo string months after reports of its removal. The DRM and account fields are free text ("Denuvo Anti-Tamper" vs "Denuvo Anti-Tampering").
- The Steam Deck report (`ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=<id>`) returns anti-cheat tokens only for tested apps with an unsupported result (seen: `UnsupportedAntiCheat_Other`, `UnsupportedAntiCheatConfiguration`). It says "does not work on Linux" and never "kernel-level"; an untested app returns category 0 with empty item arrays.
- Community data: AreWeAntiCheatYet (MIT, `games.json`, 469,569 bytes, 1,167 games, about 59 percent with a Steam ID, about 60 distinct anti-cheat spellings, no kernel field) and the GamingOnLinux anti-cheat table (271 games, Steam app IDs, no kernel field, no license shown) track Linux compatibility. PCGamingWiki (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) has a `Middleware.Anticheat` string and `Availability.Uses_DRM`, but anonymous `cargoquery` returned `permissiondenied`. No Wikipedia list, no machine-readable Denuvo list and no launcher-requirement list was found; the Steam curator "Denuvo Watch" is the one maintained Denuvo tracker found.
- Kernel status is explicit only in Steam's own `kernel_mode` flag. Every community source requires deriving it from a vendor name. Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, FACEIT and Vanguard are documented kernel drivers; Ricochet, nProtect GameGuard, XIGNCODE3 and Denuvo Anti-Cheat rest on press or vendor statements; Steam's data flags Javelin as kernel-level for Battlefield 6 while EA's page never says it.

## Findings

### 1. What Steam holds per kind (the declared fields)

The reverse-engineered `StoreItem_ExtraDetails` message defines, among others: `drm_third_party_type` (field 5, optional string), `drm_activation_limit` (6, string), `user_account_third_party` (7, string), `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` (8, bool), `anticheat` (9, message) and `eula` (10, repeated message with `name` and `url`) (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteamDatabase/Protobufs/master/webui/common.proto, read at offset 200000).

`StoreItem_ExtraDetails_Anticheat` has `kernel_mode` (1, bool), `uninstall_completely` (2, bool), `boot_protection` (3, bool), `boot_protection_name` (4, string), `name` (5, string) and `name_loc` (6, string) (verified from source: same URL). The type name is `Anticheat` with a lowercase c.

There is no Steam store tag for any of the four kinds. The tag list returned 446 tags; a name search for cheat, kernel, DRM, Denuvo, EULA, launcher, account and always online matched only "Online Co-Op" (3843) (verified from source: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetTagList/v1/?language=english). The one anti-cheat store category is id 8, "Valve Anti-Cheat enabled", seen on Counter-Strike 2 (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=730&filters=categories&l=english). That category covers Valve's own VAC only.

### 2. Valve's anti-cheat declaration rule

- Valve announced it in a Steamworks group post titled "New Tool for Describing Anti-Cheat in Games" (verified from source for the title only; the fetch returned navigation text without the body: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/announcements/detail/4547038620960934857).
- GamingOnLinux, 2024-10-30: developers must list kernel-level anti-cheat on the store page; disclosure is mandatory only for kernel-level anti-cheat and optional for other client-side or server-side anti-cheat; existing games are covered; Valve will check games during the release process for present and accurate notices; older games that leave components after uninstall will be noted (verified from source: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/10/steam-games-will-now-need-to-fully-disclose-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/).
- PCGamesN, 2024-10-31: the flag sits next to the existing DRM and third-party launcher notices; kernel-level shows in gold and other anti-cheat in blue in Valve's images; Valve will review older games with missing data; no effective date given ("soon") (verified from source: https://www.pcgamesn.com/valve/kernel-anti-cheat-flags).
- Search coverage adds a pre-populated vendor list with custom entries, two checkboxes (kernel-level integration, residual files after uninstall) and an exemption for server-side systems with no client software (search-summary: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/10/steam-games-will-now-need-to-fully-disclose-kernel-level-anti-cheat-on-store-pages/page=1/).
- The Steamworks store editing doc lists an "Anti-Cheat Declaration" field under Basic Info ("Share anti-cheat information about your game") and says nothing about kernel level, boot protection, DRM, EULA or accounts (verified from source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/editing).
- No source found describes Valve verifying a declaration beyond that release-process check, and none reports a penalty for a wrong one (unverified).

### 3. Gaps between what Steam declares and what ships (documented cases)

All Steam values below come from `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems` with `include_extra_details`, read on 2026-10-24 through the summariser. Where a case matters it was read twice (single-app and batch). The proto fields are `optional`; a missing key means unset.

Anti-cheat missing or incomplete:

- Elden Ring (1245620): the `extra_details` key list has `eula` and no `anticheat` (verified from source, read twice: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A1245620%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). AreWeAntiCheatYet lists the game as Supported with Easy Anti-Cheat and Steam ID 1245620 (verified from source: https://areweanticheatyet.com/game/elden-ring). Easy Anti-Cheat loads a kernel driver per a 2024 academic study (section 8), but neither source says the driver is active in this game.
- Rainbow Six Siege (359550): no `anticheat` key, only `user_account_third_party` "Ubisoft Connect launcher" (verified from source, read twice: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A359550%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). Valve's own Deck report for the same app carries `#SteamDeckVerified_TestResult_UnsupportedAntiCheatConfiguration` (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=359550). Two Valve surfaces therefore disagree. A search snippet says BattlEye protects Siege (search-summary: https://alternativeto.net/software/battleye).
- Battlefield 6 (2807960), Call of Duty (1938090) and PUBG (578080): `kernel_mode` true with no `name` and no `name_loc`. Battlefield 6 and Call of Duty also carry `boot_protection` true and `boot_protection_name` "secureboot_tpm2" (verified from source, single batch read: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A1808500%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1245620%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1172470%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2807960%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A730%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A578080%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A359550%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1085660%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2767030%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A381210%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D; Call of Duty comes from the second batch below). The vendor name is optional in practice; Javelin and Ricochet do not appear by name in Steam's data for these games.
- Marvel Rivals (2767030): `anticheat` is the empty object `{}` (verified from source, same batch URL). AreWeAntiCheatYet lists NetEase Game Security for the same Steam ID (verified from source: https://areweanticheatyet.com/game/marvel-rivals).
- On Counter-Strike 2 (VAC) the `kernel_mode` key is unset (verified from source, same batch URL). A consumer cannot tell "not kernel" from "not declared".

Third-party DRM:

- DOOM: The Dark Ages (3017860) returned `drm_third_party_type` "Denuvo Anti-Tamper" on 2026-10-24 (verified from source, second batch: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A1771300%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A3017860%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2515020%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1778820%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A990080%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2050650%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1938090%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A553850%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A1174180%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A271590%7D%2C%7B%22appid%22%3A2215430%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D). GamingOnLinux reported on 2026-07-13 that Steam forum and Reddit reports say Denuvo was removed while the store page "still" states it, and that the Digimon Story Time Stranger page was corrected (verified from source: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2026/07/doom-the-dark-ages-and-digimon-story-time-stranger-have-denuvo-drm-removed/). Whether Denuvo is present in the shipped build today was not established.
- Hogwarts Legacy (990080) returned "Denuvo Anti-Tampering", a different string from DOOM's "Denuvo Anti-Tamper" (verified from source, second batch URL above). The field is free text; matching needs normalisation.
- Final Fantasy XVI (2515020) has no DRM string, consistent with the Denuvo removal GamingOnLinux reported in March 2025 (verified from source for the empty field, second batch URL; the 2025 report was seen as a search result only: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/03/final-fantasy-xvi-removed-denuvo-anti-tamper/page=1/).
- Older undisclosed cases, all from search summaries: Denuvo found in Sword Art Online Fatal Bullet, NieR: Automata and Code Vein without a store-page mention, the notice sitting in the EULA instead, and a reverse case where Persona 5 Strikers listed Denuvo although the downloadable build lacked it. Which DSOGaming article covers which game is not known (search-summary: https://www.dsogaming.com/?p=151436, one of several DSOGaming results). A claim that Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 lacked a Denuvo label at launch came from an article that returned HTTP 403 on fetch (search-summary: https://itc.ua/en/news/kingdom-come-deliverance-2-will-get-denuvo-list-on-steam). The Steam value for that app is empty today (verified from source, second batch URL), which does not show whether it ever had Denuvo.

Third-party account or launcher:

- The field is free text with no vocabulary: "EA Account" (Apex Legends, 1172470), "EA Account linking required" (Battlefield 6), "Activision Account" (Call of Duty), "PlayStation Network" (HELLDIVERS 2, 553850), "Rockstar Games" (Red Dead Redemption 2, 1174180, and GTA V Legacy, 271590), "Ubisoft Connect launcher" (Siege) and "PlayStation Network (Online Multiplayer, PlayStation overlay)" (Ghost of Tsushima, 2215430). `user_account_third_party_link_to_steam` was true for all of them (verified from source, batch URLs above).
- The text can carry an "optional" scope (the Ghost of Tsushima string names online multiplayer and the overlay); a non-empty value does not mean the account is required to play (verified from source for the string, second batch URL; the interpretation is mine).
- Forum users name games that gained a launcher or account after release (GTA V, Stellaris, DOOM Eternal's Bethesda account) and say some store pages omit the notice (search-summary: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/10/601901188455074095/). No documented, dated case of Valve correcting a missing third-party account label was found (unverified).
- Destiny 2 (1085660) returned no `user_account_third_party` (verified from source, first batch URL). Whether it should have one was not checked.

EULA:

- `eula` is a repeated name and URL, hosted at `store.steampowered.com/eula/<appid>_eula_<n>`: Elden Ring has two (English and JP), ARC Raiders one (verified from source, GetItems reads above). Counter-Strike 2 has none (verified from source, first batch URL). The proto has no flag for "third-party" EULA; whether an entry is a third-party license (for example a vendor's anti-cheat or middleware EULA) must be read from the document text. No dataset of third-party EULA presence was found (unverified).

### 4. Steam's own anti-cheat compatibility signal: the Deck report

- Endpoint `https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=<id>` returns JSON with `appid`, `resolved_category`, `resolved_items[]` (each `display_type` and `loc_token`), and parallel `steamos_*`, `machine_*` and `frame_*` pairs (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=1172470).
- Apex Legends (1172470): category 1 with `#SteamDeckVerified_TestResult_UnsupportedAntiCheat_Other`, and the matching `#SteamOS_...` and `#SteamMachine_...` tokens; the `frame_*` pair held `#SteamFrame_TestResult_UnsupportedAntiCheatConfiguration` (verified from source, URL above).
- Rainbow Six Siege (359550): category 1 with `#SteamDeckVerified_TestResult_UnsupportedAntiCheatConfiguration` (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=359550).
- Battlefield 6 (2807960): category 1 with `#SteamDeckVerified_TestResult_SteamOSDoesNotSupport`, which is not an anti-cheat token, while Steam's store data for the app says kernel anti-cheat with Secure Boot (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=2807960).
- Elden Ring (1245620): category 3, four Deck test items (controller, glyphs, text legibility, performance) and no anti-cheat item, though Easy Anti-Cheat is listed for it elsewhere (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=1245620).
- Untested app (5072580): all four `*_resolved_category` values 0 and empty item arrays (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID=5072580).
- Coverage rule: the report exists only for apps Valve has tested; it names a result for Linux-based Valve devices and carries no vendor and no "kernel-level" wording. Valve's Deck doc says some anti-cheat providers are currently unsupported and that an unsupported provider yields the Unsupported category (verified from source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamdeck/compat). The page did not use the word kernel (verified negative, same URL). Valve's Proton statement that kernel-space anti-cheat is unsupported was not located (unverified).
- "One app per call" is the observed usage (every call above took one `nAppID`); whether the endpoint accepts a list is unverified.
- Category numbers seen: 0, 1 and 3 for the main category, and 2 for `steamos_resolved_category` on Elden Ring. The usual mapping (0 unknown, 1 unsupported, 2 playable, 3 verified) fits these values and no page read states it (unverified).

### 5. AreWeAntiCheatYet

- Repository `AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet`, default branch `master`, created 2021-10-09, pushed 2026-10-24T13:22:19Z, 511 stars, description "A comprehensive and crowd-sourced list of games using anti-cheats and their compatibility with GNU/Linux or Wine" (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet). License MIT, copyright Starz0r and Curve, 2021 (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/master/LICENSE). The LICENSE is repo-wide; no separate data license was seen (unverified).
- Format and size: `games.json` at the repo root, a JSON array of objects, 469,569 bytes (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/contents/). Keys: `url`, `name`, `logo`, `native`, `status`, `reference`, `anticheats` (array of strings), `notes` (array of text and link pairs), `updates` (array of name, date, reference), `storeIds` (object), `slug`, `dateChanged` (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/master/games.json).
- Hosting and cadence: raw JSON on raw.githubusercontent.com; the site is a Next.js app (`next.config.js` in the repo listing) rebuilt on each commit, with an RSS feed at https://areweanticheatyet.com/feed.rss; changes arrive through GitHub issues (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/master/README.md). The repo was pushed to on the day it was read.
- Size: 1,167 games on the front page: Supported 196, Running 278, Planned 2, Broken 638, Denied 53 (verified from source: https://areweanticheatyet.com/). Reading the whole file in five chunks gave 179, 230, 280, 284 and 190 complete entries, 1,163 in total, which matches within the partial entries at chunk edges (manual tallies by the summariser; verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/master/games.json, offsets 0 to 400000).
- Steam app ID coverage: `storeIds` is an object keyed by store; the Steam value is a string app ID (`"steam": "976730"`), Epic is `{namespace, slug}`, and some entries are empty. Counting entries with a non-empty Steam value in each chunk gave 152, 154, 173, 129 and 79, about 687 of 1,163 or 59 percent (manual tallies, treat as plus or minus a few; same URL). The status field holds Linux/Proton compatibility and the file has no kernel field.
- Kernel status: not stored. The only anti-cheat information is the vendor string in `anticheats`; kernel status has to be derived from the name (verified from source: key list above).
- The file also records games from other stores; a Steam-scoped consumer would filter on `storeIds.steam` (verified from source: same URL).

### 6. GamingOnLinux anti-cheat table, PCGamingWiki and other datasets

GamingOnLinux anti-cheat table (https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/):

- Lists 271 games "with some form of anti-cheat". Columns are Game Title, Compatibility (Works, Broken, Single Player Only, Steam Deck / SteamOS only, Reports Needed), Developer and Anti-Cheat Used. Entries link to an item page carrying the Steam app ID. Per-entry "Updated" timestamps fall in October 2026. There is an RSS feed and a "Report Changes" link for user submissions. No kernel field, no API or export and no license were shown (verified from source for the first 100,000 of 120,438 characters: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/).
- Vendor filter pages exist, for example Bellring Anti-Cheat with one game and no kernel flag (verified from source: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/vendor/bellring-anti-cheat/). Search snippets of older snapshots counted 226 and 231 games; the table grows over time (search-summary: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/).

PCGamingWiki (PCGW):

- License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 per the Wikipedia infobox; about 48,000 content pages in October 2022; the Wikipedia article says nothing about an API (verified from source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCGamingWiki).
- Cargo tables listed by the API: AI, API, Audio, Availability, Cloud, Company, Controller, Engine, GFWL, Game, GameData, GameEngine, Input, L10n, Middleware, Mods, Multiplayer, SafeDisc, Software, StarForce, StoreFeature, StoreKeys, Tags, VR, Video, XDG, `_pageData` and some internal PCGW_* tables (verified from source: https://www.pcgamingwiki.com/w/api.php?action=cargotables&format=json).
- Relevant fields: `Game.Steam_AppID` (string, list with comma delimiter), `Middleware.Anticheat` (string) and `Middleware.Removed_Anticheat`, `Availability.Uses_DRM`, `Availability.Removed_DRM` and one DRM field per store such as `Steam_DRM` (verified from source: https://www.pcgamingwiki.com/w/api.php?action=cargofields&table=Game&format=json, and the same URL with `table=Middleware` and `table=Availability`). None of the three tables read has a field for a third-party launcher or account, a EULA or kernel mode; other tables were not read.
- Access: anonymous `cargoquery` calls returned `{"error":{"code":"permissiondenied","info":"You don't have permission to run arbitrary Cargo queries."}}` for four different queries on 2026-10-24, while `cargotables` and `cargofields` answered (verified from source: https://www.pcgamingwiki.com/w/api.php?action=cargoquery&tables=Middleware&fields=_pageName%3DPage%2CAnticheat&where=Anticheat%20IS%20NOT%20NULL&limit=5&format=json). A PCGW forum post reports the same message for logged-out visitors and names the groups that can run such queries (search-summary: https://community.pcgamingwiki.com/topic/5740-list-of-games-that-support-xinput-compatible-controllers-page-is-broken/). The api.php help page cites a usage-etiquette document that was not retrieved (verified from source: https://www.pcgamingwiki.com/w/api.php). Other PCGW pages returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher.
- Row counts, update cadence and Steam app ID coverage: not found (unverified). A community thread says editors sometimes record a store's DRM option without validating it, and that PCGW records "DRM-free*" by hand (search-summary: https://community.pcgamingwiki.com/topic/6230-drm-listing-question).

SteamDB:

- SteamDB change logs reportedly record when a game adds or removes a third-party DRM line, for example a Resident Evil 3 entry "Removed 3rd-Party DRM - Denuvo Anti-tamper" (search-summary: https://www.pcgamesn.com/resident-evil-3/denuvo). The SteamDB pages needed to confirm an anti-cheat or DRM listing, a search or a tag could not be read (the AI-disclosure research recorded HTTP 403 for steamdb.info). No SteamDB anti-cheat list was found (unverified).

Wikipedia:

- The Denuvo article names about 27 protected titles in prose, with no table and no app IDs, and was last edited 2026-10-16 (verified from source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denuvo). It records Denuvo Anti-Cheat as announced in March 2019 and first used by DOOM Eternal in May 2020, and does not say whether it is a kernel driver (verified from source, same URL). No Wikipedia list of games by anti-cheat or by DRM was found (unverified; only this article and the PCGW and GameGuard articles were read).

Denuvo trackers:

- Steam curator "Denuvo Watch" (https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26095454) reads as tracking Denuvo Anti-Tamper games on Steam, with 51,934 followers, review-type filters (148 Informational, 293 Not Recommended; the Recommended count was unreadable) and two lists of games that had Denuvo removed; the newest entry date shows no year (verified from source: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26095454). A 2023 forum thread calls it "Denuvo Games" (search-summary: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/4030223299342092022). Whether a machine-readable endpoint for curator lists exists was not checked (unverified).
- gamestatus.info answered with an Anubis bot-protection page; its content is unknown (verified from source for the block: https://gamestatus.info/). CrackWatch (a 2020 article) and a pinned list on r/crackwatch are named in secondary posts, with a warning that the list colour-codes "Denuvo removed" and "cracked" alike (search-summary: https://gigazine.net/news/20200917-crackwatch/ and https://lemmy.linuxuserspace.show/comment/812316). Current status of both is unverified. One unsourced comment puts 229 Denuvo releases since 2020, fewer than 30 cracked and 119 with Denuvo removed (search-summary, unreliable: https://lemmy.linuxuserspace.show/comment/812316).
- No GitHub JSON of Denuvo games with Steam IDs turned up in the search (unverified).

Launcher or account requirement lists:

- No maintained list of games that require an EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Rockstar or PSN account was found; the search returned PCGW's DRM-free lists (the inverse) and forum threads (search-summary: https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/10/601901188455074095/). Steam's own `user_account_third_party` is the only per-app source found.

### 7. Vendor-name coverage: Steam's field versus the community lists

Steam side:

- `anticheat.name` is an optional string and `name_loc` a localisation token (section 1). Tokens observed in the 21 apps sampled: `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_easyac` (Apex Legends, Dead by Daylight, HELLDIVERS 2) with name "Easy Anti-Cheat"; `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_battleye` (Destiny 2, GTA V Legacy) with name "BattlEye"; `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_vac` (Counter-Strike 2) with name "VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)"; and `#Store_AntiCheat_Type_denuvo` (ARC Raiders) with name "Denuvo" and `kernel_mode` true (verified from source, reads in section 3; the ARC Raiders record was read twice with the same result: https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=%7B%22ids%22%3A%5B%7B%22appid%22%3A1808500%7D%5D%2C%22context%22%3A%7B%22language%22%3A%22english%22%2C%22country_code%22%3A%22US%22%7D%2C%22data_request%22%3A%7B%22include_extra_details%22%3Atrue%7D%7D).
- The full pre-populated list of Steam vendor tokens was not found. Searches for the `Store_AntiCheat_Type_` strings returned nothing, and the Steamworks docs name no vendors (verified negative for https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/editing and https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/anticheat). Tokens for Vanguard, Javelin, Ricochet, FACEIT, nProtect and XIGNCODE3 were not seen; the games that use Javelin and Ricochet carry no name at all (section 3).

Community side, distinct names:

- AreWeAntiCheatYet `anticheats` strings, merged from the five chunk reads (summariser tallies, about 60 spellings; verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AreWeAntiCheatYet/AreWeAntiCheatYet/master/games.json): Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Vanguard, Hyperion, Arbiter, FairFight, EA anticheat, Zakynthos, UNCHEATER/Uncheater, VAC/Valve Anti-Cheat, XIGNCODE3, PunkBuster/Punkbuster, Treyarch Anti-Cheat, FACEIT, ESEA, NEAC Protect, miHoYo Protect, nProtect GameGuard, RICOCHET/Ricochet, Denuvo Anti-Cheat, EQU8, Anti-Cheat Expert, Nexon Game Security, Mail.ru Anti-Cheat, SARD, X-Trap, Saberclaw, EMAC LAB, Warden, Crackproof/CrackProof, WFSDrv, AhnLab HackShield, AnyBrain, NetEase Yidun, NetEase Anti-Cheat Expert, NetEase Game Security, KSophon, GuardenAC, IronShield, Tavern, ESL Wire, Esportal, MY.GAMES Anti-Cheat, Proxima Game Anti Cheat, Seasun Protect, VIOLET, Active Anticheat, 4game Guard / Frost Security, Arkos, TenProtect, Fredaikis Anti-Cheat, RedKard, SCUE4, Packman, GuardingPearSoftware's Anti Cheat Pro, ROO In-House Anti-Cheat, PlayStation Overlay, Anti-Cheat Solution, Cheat Blocker, R6 ShieldGuard, Enforcer, and "Unknown (Custom)" / "Custom (Unknown)". Case and spelling variants exist; exact-match lookups would miss entries.
- "Javelin" does not appear in the AreWeAntiCheatYet strings read; EA's system is stored as "EA anticheat" (verified from source: the Battlefield 2042 entry in the first chunk of the same file). Ricochet, Vanguard, FACEIT, nProtect GameGuard, XIGNCODE3 and Denuvo Anti-Cheat do appear.
- GamingOnLinux table vendor names: Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, RICOCHET Anti-Cheat, Vanguard, Anti-Cheat Expert (ACE), Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC), EA Javelin Anticheat, PunkBuster, XIGNCODE3, nProtect GameGuard, Denuvo Anti-Cheat, NEAC Protect, Nexon Game Security, Treyarch Anti-Cheat, Hyperion, miHoYo Protect, GamersFirst Anti-Cheat, Bellring Anti-Cheat, Defense Matrix, RedKard, Ironshield, Arbiter, Broken Arrow Anti-Cheat System, Uncheater, EXens, NetEase Yidun, plus "Unknown" (verified from source for the first 100,000 characters: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/). This list names Javelin and AreWeAntiCheatYet does not.
- PCGW `Middleware.Anticheat` is a plain string field; sample values were not retrieved because `cargoquery` is blocked (section 6).

### 8. Which vendors are kernel-mode, and how that is known

Kernel-mode status per vendor, with the strength of the evidence:

- BattlEye: loads the kernel driver BEDaisy.sys, mandatory on server and client, started with the game (verified from source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00500v1). Steam: `kernel_mode` true on Destiny 2 and GTA V Legacy (verified from source, batch URLs in section 3).
- Easy Anti-Cheat: loads a kernel driver (unnamed in the paper), started with the game (verified from source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00500v1). A search snippet of unclear origin says EAC runs in user space under Wine or Proton on Linux (unverified). Steam: `kernel_mode` true on Apex Legends, Dead by Daylight and HELLDIVERS 2 (verified from source, batch URLs).
- FACEIT Anti-Cheat: kernel driver FACEIT.sys, loads at boot, needs TPM 2.0, DEP and Secure Boot (verified from source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00500v1). No Steam token seen.
- Vanguard (Riot): kernel driver vgk.sys, loads at boot, the game refuses to start without it (verified from source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00500v1). Steam coverage not checked (unverified).
- Javelin (EA): EA's Secure Boot page (2025-08-04) calls Javelin customizable, says Secure Boot is required for Battlefield 6 on PC and lists kernel-level cheats among threats, but does not say Javelin runs in the kernel (verified from source: https://www.ea.com/games/battlefield/battlefield-6/news/secure-boot-information). A German report calls it kernel-based (search-summary: https://www.igorslab.de/battlefield-6s-anti-cheat-javelin-hat-bereits-330-000-cheater-gebannt-und-begruendet-die-pflicht-von-secure-boot/). Steam's Battlefield 6 record says `kernel_mode` true (verified from source, first batch URL).
- Ricochet (Activision): Activision announced a PC kernel-level driver in October 2021, first for Warzone, running only while a Call of Duty game plays (search-summary: https://www.thesixthaxis.com/2021/10/14/cod-vanguard-warzone-ricochet-anti-cheat-revealed-with-controversial-kernel-level-pc-driver/). Activision's support page says Ricochet moved to a unified security platform with Modern Warfare II; the current driver state was not confirmed (search-summary: https://support.activision.com/content/atvi/support/web/en/articles/ricochet-overview.html). Steam's Call of Duty record says `kernel_mode` true with Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 (verified from source, second batch URL).
- nProtect GameGuard: Wikipedia says it "uses rootkits" and cites a driver file npptnt2.sys tied to a privilege-escalation flaw; the article does not use the words kernel mode (verified from source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameGuard). Treat as kernel-driver based (inference).
- XIGNCODE3 (Wellbia): a CVE record for a privilege-escalation flaw in the xhunter1.sys kernel driver, and a game-specific test that saw the driver start with the game and stop after exit (search-summary: https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/cve-2026-3609 and https://trovesaurus.com/xigncode3).
- Denuvo Anti-Cheat: Denuvo's own Q&A argues kernel-mode drivers are needed and says Denuvo follows Microsoft's guidance (search-summary: https://irdeto.com/denuvo/qa-about-denuvo-anti-cheat-and-windows-kernel-mode-drivers). Steam's ARC Raiders record says name "Denuvo" with `kernel_mode` true (verified from source, ARC Raiders read in section 7). No independent analysis of the driver was found.
- VAC: Valve's anti-cheat; the Steam record for Counter-Strike 2 has name and token and no `kernel_mode` key (verified from source, first batch URL). No source read states VAC is user-mode (unverified).
- Hyperion, PunkBuster, FairFight, ESEA, Treyarch Anti-Cheat, miHoYo Protect, NetEase Game Security, Anti-Cheat Expert and EQU8: kernel status not researched (unverified).

Two limits shape any vendor-to-kernel map. The academic paper studies four systems only and records that a kernel driver may start at boot or with the game (verified from source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00500v1). A vendor can ship user-mode and kernel-mode variants, and a game can run the vendor in a reduced mode, so a vendor name proves less than Steam's per-game `kernel_mode` flag (inference).

## Caveats and version notes

- Fetch method: pages were summarised by a small model. Values from the `GetItems` JSON (Steam `anticheat`, DRM and account strings) are what the model reported. The Elden Ring, Rainbow Six Siege and ARC Raiders records were each read twice with matching results; the other apps were read once in two batches. Re-read raw JSON with a shell request or devtools before relying on any single string.
- All Steam values were read on 2026-10-24 for the US store in English. Per-country, per-language and per-login variation was not tested. Whether `name_loc` resolves to a different display string by language is unverified.
- The Steamworks announcement body, SteamDB, gamestatus.info and most PCGW pages were not readable (navigation only, HTTP 403 or bot protection). Claims that rest on them are marked.
- AreWeAntiCheatYet counts are manual tallies across five reads of one 469,569-byte file; entries split across chunk boundaries were skipped. The site and file change daily.
- The sample of 21 Steam apps is small and picked by recognisable names; it shows that gaps exist and gives no estimate of their rate.
- Valve's wording is "check" for declarations; no page read documents enforcement or a penalty for a wrong declaration.
- Dates: Valve's anti-cheat rule is from 2024-10-30; the Steam, AreWeAntiCheatYet, GamingOnLinux and PCGW readings are from 2026-10-24. Changes around 2026-10-22 (RQ3) were not examined here.
- The sources behind the search-summary tags were not opened.

Not answered:

- The full list of vendor tokens in Steam's pre-populated anti-cheat picker: no page or localisation file found.
- PCGW row counts and anti-cheat or DRM values: anonymous `cargoquery` is blocked.
- SteamDB's own DRM or anti-cheat data: pages returned 403.
- Any machine-readable Denuvo or launcher-requirement list: none found.
- Kernel status for VAC, Hyperion, PunkBuster, FairFight and the East Asian vendors: not researched.
- Valve's Proton or Deck statement on kernel anti-cheat: the Deck doc fetched does not contain it.
```

`docs/research/steam-store-disclosure-kinds/rq6-icon-sets.md`:

```md
# RQ6: Which open-source icon set fits 12 to 16 px chip icons in a no-minify, no-remote-asset browser extension?

Researched 2026-10-24. Facts first; every judgment is labelled "judgment". This note reports licence clauses and does not give legal advice. About 150 fetches were issued, far over the suggested 25, but in parallel batches; most were small registry, GitHub and CDN reads. Fetches went through a small summarising model, which sometimes answered "I cannot check existence" while still showing the file content; an explicit HTTP 404 was treated as "absent", and content shown was treated as "present".

Tag scheme. "verified from source" means read on the set's own registry record, repo, LICENSE or shipped package file. "search-summary" means seen only in a search result. "unverified" means not confirmed. A trailing "(m)" means the fact was read only on the Iconify API (https://api.iconify.design), a third-party mirror that republishes the sets; names read there matched upstream names wherever a second read was possible, but treat "(m)" cells as one level weaker. Byte figures marked "est" were counted by the summariser and are rough.

## Answer in short

- All eleven candidates allow commercial use and none has a copyleft, non-commercial or share-alike clause, but three need a closer look. Remix Icon 4.9.x ships a custom "Remix Icon License v1.0" (January 2026) that forbids selling or distributing the icons as a standalone product and building a competing icon set, while its npm record still says Apache-2.0. Font Awesome Free icons are CC BY 4.0, so attribution is mandatory and its per-icon JS files carry no attribution comment. Lucide is ISC with a second MIT notice for Feather-derived icons (`lock` and `key` are on that list). The rest are MIT or Apache-2.0 (verified from source, section 1).
- Concept coverage (8 concepts): Lucide 8 of 8 (`sparkles`, `shield-alert`, `shield`, `lock`, `user`, `scroll-text`, `swords`, `app-window`); Tabler 8 of 8 but no `scroll`; Phosphor 7 of 8 (only a single `sword`); Heroicons 7 of 8 (no swords); Material Symbols has `swords` but its sparkle icon `auto_awesome` is absent from the SVG package; Font Awesome Free lacks sparkles, swords and a shield with alert (Pro-only); Radix lacks shield, key, cpu and swords.
- Solid variants for every needed icon: only Material Symbols and Phosphor come close (Phosphor's PvP glyph is one sword); Heroicons has a dedicated 16 px solid set but no swords; Tabler fills exist for 6 of 8; Lucide is outline only.
- Bundling: Lucide, Carbon and Font Awesome ship per-icon JS data; Lucide's modules are plain `[tag, attrs]` arrays and its own `createElement` uses `createElementNS` (no `innerHTML`). The others ship SVG files only (needs a text loader or a build-time path extraction). Eight icons cost roughly 2 to 5 KB in every set, so bytes do not separate the candidates; Heroicons is exact at 3,534 B for seven icons.
- Ranking (judgment): 1 Phosphor (fill weight), 2 Lucide, 3 Heroicons (16 solid); Tabler is the first alternate. If the owner accepts an outline look, Lucide becomes first. Details in section 6.

Points that need a human decision, stated as facts:

- Lucide. The MIT part covers icons "derived from the Feather project"; against that list the summariser reported `lock` and `key` as listed, and `sparkles`, `shield`, `shield-alert`, `cpu`, `user`, `scroll`, `scroll-text`, `swords`, `app-window`, `file-text` as not listed (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucide-icons/lucide/main/LICENSE; the membership check was done by the summariser, so re-read the list before relying on it). The ISC header sits inside each module as `@license lucide v1.61.0 - ISC` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide@1.61.0/dist/esm/icons/scroll-text.mjs). GitHub reports the repo licence as "Other" because the file holds two licences (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/lucide-icons/lucide).
- Remix. The registry says Apache-2.0 for remixicon 4.9.1, and the package's own License file says Remix Icon License v1.0 (verified from source, both URLs above). Iconify still shows Remix Icon 4.8.0 as Apache-2.0 (verified from source: https://api.iconify.design/collections?prefixes=ri). That the licence changed between 4.8.0 and 4.9.x is an inference from these records, not a stated fact. Whether "Remix Icon License" is an SPDX identifier: unverified. The `@remixicon/react` record lists "Remix Icon License 1.0" (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=remixicon&size=3).
- Font Awesome Free. The summarised LICENSE.txt says downloaded files "already contain embedded attribution comments" and asks users not to strip them (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons@7.3.1/LICENSE.txt). The per-icon module faShieldHalved.js showed no header comment and begins with 'use strict' (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons@7.3.1/faShieldHalved.js), so a bundle built from per-icon files carries no attribution by itself.
- Apache-2.0 sets (Material, Carbon). Carbon's per-icon modules carry an Apache header comment generated by `@carbon/icon-build-helpers` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@carbon/icons@11.91.0/es/security/16.js). Material SVGs appear to carry no header comment (unverified: the summariser reported attributes only for https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material-symbols/svg-400@0.48.1/outlined/gpp_maybe-fill.svg), so the Apache notice would have to come from the project's own notices file.

### 2. Style and rendering at 12 to 16 px

Facts per set (grid, weights, variants):

- Lucide: outline only, 24 grid, `stroke-width` 2 in every body, round caps (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide@1.61.0/dist/esm/icons/shield-alert.mjs for the data shape; stroke 2 from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucide-icons/lucide/main/icons/swords.svg). The stroke scales with the SVG size, so a 2-unit stroke on 24 draws about 1.33 px at 16 px and 1 px at 12 px (arithmetic). The docs describe `absoluteStrokeWidth` to keep the on-screen stroke fixed; current framework docs rename it `nonScalingStroke` (verified from source: https://v0.lucide.dev/guide/basics/stroke-width; rename seen as search-summary: https://lucide.dev/guide/react/basics/stroke-width). A CSS alternative, `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`, was named in the same search result (search-summary). No fill variant exists.
- Tabler: 6,238 icons, 5,184 outline and 1,054 filled, 24 grid, 2 px stroke (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler-icons/main/README.md). Outline files carry `stroke-width` 2 (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons@3.49.0/icons/outline/swords.svg). Filled files use `fill="currentColor"` and include an invisible 24 by 24 helper path (`fill="none"`), so a filled file has one more element than the glyph needs (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons@3.49.0/icons/filled/shield.svg and .../filled/sparkles.svg, 2 and 4 path elements).
- Phosphor: six weights, thin, light, regular, bold, fill, duotone (the npm exports map lists bold, fill, thin, light, duotone, regular: https://registry.npmjs.org/@phosphor-icons/core/latest; the 9,072 Iconify entries equal 1,512 icons x 6 weights, arithmetic on https://api.iconify.design/collections?prefixes=ph). Assets live at `/assets/<weight>/<kebab-name>-<weight>.svg` (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phosphor-icons/core/main/README.md; the regular weight has no suffix, as in assets/regular/shield-warning.svg). Every file read had `viewBox` "0 0 256 256", `fill="currentColor"` on the root, one `<path>` and no stroke attributes, even for the regular weight, so weights are baked into outlines and there is no stroke-scaling knob (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@phosphor-icons/core@2.1.1/assets/regular/shield-warning.svg, .../assets/fill/sparkle-fill.svg, .../assets/fill/sword-fill.svg).
- Heroicons: four sets, 24 outline, 24 solid, 20 solid, 16 solid (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tailwindlabs/heroicons/master/README.md; the README does not use the names "mini" or "micro", those names come from the brief). The 16 solid set is a separate drawing at `viewBox` "0 0 16 16" with `fill="currentColor"` and one path for `sparkles` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/heroicons@2.2.0/16/solid/sparkles.svg). Each set has 316 icons (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/tailwindlabs/heroicons/git/trees/master:optimized/16/solid).
- Material Symbols: variable font axes FILL 0 to 1, wght 100 to 700, GRAD, opsz 20 to 48 dp (verified from source: https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/material_symbols). The optical size axis starts at 20, above the 12 to 16 px range. The SVG package is weight 400 only, with `outlined`, `rounded` and `sharp` folders and `<name>.svg` plus `<name>-fill.svg` files; the two files read have `viewBox` "0 -960 960 960", width and height 48 and no fill attribute (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material-symbols/svg-400@0.48.1/ and the two files fetched under it). Not every icon has a `-fill` file (see section 3, `auto_awesome`).
- Font Awesome Free 7.x solid: single filled style per package (this note read only the solid package). Per-icon canvases are not square: faWandMagicSparkles is 576 by 512, faShieldHalved 512 by 512, and Iconify normalises the set to 640 (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons@7.3.1/faWandMagicSparkles.js and https://api.iconify.design/fa7-solid.json).
- Bootstrap Icons: drawn on a 16 by 16 grid (`viewBox` "0 0 16 16", `fill="currentColor"`, one path) and ships outline and `-fill` icons as separate names; `window-fill` does not exist (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.13.2/icons/shield-fill-exclamation.svg and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/twbs/icons/main/font/bootstrap-icons.json).
- Iconoir: 24 grid, stroke 1.5, no fill on the root (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/iconoir@7.12.1/icons/regular/shield-alert.svg). A `solid` folder exists, but of 13 candidate names tested only `sparks-solid`, `web-window-solid` and `warning-triangle-solid` exist (m) (https://api.iconify.design/iconoir.json?icons=shield-alert-solid,cpu-solid,lock-solid,key-solid,user-solid,page-solid,shield-solid,app-window-solid,sparks-solid,web-window-solid,warning-triangle-solid,empty-page-solid,cpu-warning-solid).
- Remix Icon: `-line` and `-fill` names for each icon tested, 24 grid (m) (https://api.iconify.design/ri.json?icons=sparkling-fill,sparkling-line,sparkling-2-fill,sparkling-2-line,magic-fill,shield-fill,shield-line,shield-keyhole-fill,shield-flash-fill,shield-check-fill,shield-cross-fill,alert-fill,cpu-fill,cpu-line,lock-fill,lock-line,key-fill,key-2-fill,user-fill,user-line,file-text-fill,file-text-line,file-paper-fill,file-paper-2-fill,article-fill,sword-fill,sword-line,window-fill,window-2-fill,app-store-fill).
- Carbon: the 16 px modules reuse 32 grid artwork (`viewBox` "0 0 32 32", width and height 16) for `security` and `ai-generate`, so no dedicated 16 px redraw was seen for those two (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@carbon/icons@11.91.0/es/security/16.js and .../es/ai-generate/16.js).
- Radix Icons: 15 by 15 grid by design (verified from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/radix-ui/icons/master/README.md), 332 icons (m) (https://api.iconify.design/collection?prefix=radix-icons).

Which sets have a solid or fill version of every icon needed (8 concepts):

- Material Symbols: fill files confirmed for `gpp_maybe` and `swords`; `shield`, `lock`, `key`, `person`, `memory` have fill names on the mirror (m); the sparkle icon is the gap (section 3).
- Phosphor: fill exists for all but the crossed swords, which is absent; `sword-fill` is a single sword.
- Heroicons: solid for all 7 present concepts at 16 px; no swords.
- Tabler: filled exists for sparkles, shield, shield-check, shield-lock, lock, key, user, file-text, app-window (m except shield and sparkles); filled `cpu` and `swords` are 404 in the package, and the mirror shows no `shield-exclamation-filled`. So 6 of 8 concepts have a filled form (verified from source for the two 404s: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons@3.49.0/icons/filled/cpu.svg and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons@3.49.0/icons/filled/swords.svg).
- Bootstrap: fill for shield, shield-exclamation, cpu, lock, key, person, file-text; no `window-fill`; no sparkle (only `stars` and `magic`) and no swords.
- Remix: fill for every concept it has; no shield-with-alert and only a single `sword`.
- Font Awesome Free solid: everything is solid, but three concepts are missing (section 3).
- Lucide, Carbon, Iconoir, Radix: no fill variant for the needed set.

How each set renders at 12 to 16 px is a visual question; no rendering test was run. Facts that bear on it: Heroicons 16 solid and Bootstrap are drawn at 16 px, Radix at 15 px, Material Symbols' optical size starts at 20 dp, Carbon reuses 32 grid art, and outline sets with a 2-unit stroke on a 24 grid draw 1 to 1.33 px lines. Judgment: solid glyphs hold up at 12 to 16 px better than 2-unit strokes, and solid also matches Steam's own flat glyphs, per the owner's description.

Concepts: AI (sparkle), KAC kernel-level anti-cheat (shield with alert, or cpu), AC anti-cheat (shield), DRM (lock or key), ACCT third-party account (user), EULA (scroll or contract text), PVP (crossed swords), APP optional launcher (app window). "missing" means no such icon found. "(m)" means mirror read only. Which Material icon replaces it: unverified.
- Iconify search results are capped at 128 hits, so negative results from searches were not used as proof of absence; absence claims above come from `not_found` arrays, package 404s, the Bootstrap key map or the Heroicons file tree.
- Phosphor `swords` is in the mirror's not_found array and `swords-fill.svg` is 404 in the package, so two reads agree on absence.

### 4. Consumption under the extension's constraints

Facts about esbuild (the bundler named in the brief):

- Tree shaking is on by default when bundling or when the output format is `iife`; the documentation section does not make it depend on minification (verified from source: https://esbuild.github.io/api/, Tree shaking section). The `sideEffects` field marks files removable when all imports from them are unused (verified from source: same page, Ignore annotations text).
- The default for legal comments is `eof` when bundling (verified from source: https://esbuild.github.io/api/). So a license comment in a source module (Lucide, Carbon) reaches the end of the output file; a set with no header comment (Font Awesome per-icon files, likely Material and Heroicons SVGs) leaves nothing to carry.
- No built-in `.svg` loader exists; the `text` loader is on by default only for `.txt` and exports the file as a string; `dataurl` would produce a Base64 data URL (verified from source: https://esbuild.github.io/content-types/). Importing SVG files therefore needs a loader mapping for `.svg` set to `text` in the build config.

Per set: what the package ships, whether per-icon import tree-shakes, rough size of the eight concept icons, and how to build elements.

- Lucide. Ships JS data. Each icon is a module `dist/esm/icons/<name>.mjs` with a default export that is an array of `[tag, attrs]` pairs (shield-alert: three `path` pairs; app-window: one `rect` plus three `path`; no imports) (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide@1.61.0/dist/esm/icons/shield-alert.mjs and .../app-window.mjs). The package has `sideEffects: false`, `module: dist/esm/lucide.mjs` and no `exports` field, so deep file imports are not blocked by a map (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/lucide/latest; the consequence for deep imports is an inference from the missing field). Module sizes with license header and source map comment: shield-alert about 580 characters, scroll-text 500 to 550, app-window about 440, sparkles about 800 (est). Path data for sparkles, shield-alert, shield, lock, user, scroll-text, swords, app-window sums to about 2,100 characters (est, Iconify bodies: https://api.iconify.design/lucide.json?icons=sparkles,shield-alert,shield,cpu,lock,key,user,scroll-text,swords,app-window). DOM: the package's own `createElement` builds nodes with `document.createElementNS` and `setAttribute`, recursing over `[tag, attrs, children]`, with no `innerHTML` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide@1.61.0/dist/esm/createElement.mjs). Per-icon import with no minification should work under esbuild's rules above (judgment; no test build was run).
- Tabler. Ships SVG files (`icons/outline`, `icons/filled`) and two JSON dumps of all icon nodes, `tabler-nodes-outline.json` and `tabler-nodes-filled.json`; no `dist/` JS (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tabler/icons@3.49.0/). Its exports map is `"./*"` to `./icons/*` and it has `sideEffects: false` (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@tabler/icons/latest). Files are about 0.5 KB outline (swords about 510 B, shield-exclamation about 550 B, est) and about 0.76 to 0.8 KB filled (shield about 800 B, sparkles about 760 B, est), so eight icons are roughly 4 to 5 KB as files. Whether esbuild drops unused keys from a large JSON import: unverified; do not rely on it.
- Phosphor. Ships SVG files only under `assets/<weight>/`; `dist/` holds metadata (name lists, types). The exports map lists `./<weight>/*.svg` and `./assets/<weight>/*.svg` (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@phosphor-icons/core/latest and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@phosphor-icons/core@2.1.1/). Fill files measured by the summariser: sparkle-fill about 500 B, shield-warning-fill about 380 B, scroll-fill about 600 B, cpu-fill about 700 B, app-window-fill about 281 B, sword-fill about 890 B (est, files under https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@phosphor-icons/core@2.1.1/assets/fill/). Adding shield-fill, lock-fill and user-fill at an assumed 300 to 350 B each (unverified) puts the eight concept icons near 3.6 KB.
- Heroicons. Ships SVG files only (`16`, `20`, `24` folders, LICENSE, README). Exact bytes of the optimized 16 solid files (GitHub tree API sizes): sparkles 976, shield-exclamation 490, shield-check 514, cpu-chip 726, lock-closed 348, key 409, user 272, document-text 466, window 468, scale 891. For the seven concepts that exist (sparkles, shield-exclamation, shield-check, lock-closed, user, document-text, window) that is 3,534 B; adding cpu-chip gives 4,260 B (verified from source: https://api.github.com/repos/tailwindlabs/heroicons/git/trees/master:optimized/16/solid; folder layout https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/heroicons@2.2.0/). The unoptimized `src/16/solid` copies are larger (sparkles 2,012 B), so use the package copies.
- Material Symbols. Ships SVG files only in the data package (23,595 files in @material-symbols/svg-400); the `material-symbols` package is a font plus CSS (`main` is index.css) and is the wrong shape for this extension (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@material-symbols/svg-400/latest and https://registry.npmjs.org/material-symbols/latest). Measured files: gpp_maybe-fill about 300 B and swords-fill about 620 B (est). Other bodies on the mirror run 100 to 480 characters (m), so eight icons are roughly 3 KB (est, unverified). Width and height attributes are 48 and must be overridden.
- Font Awesome Free. Ships JS data. Per-icon CommonJS modules `faX.js` export `definition` with `icon: [width, height, aliases, unicode, svgPathData]`; `index.mjs` re-exports all icons for ESM, and the exports map has `"./*"` to `"./*.js"`; `sideEffects: false` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons@7.3.1/faShieldHalved.js and https://registry.npmjs.org/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons/latest). faShieldHalved is about 1,000 characters with about 260 characters of path; faWandMagicSparkles about 1,900 characters (est). Path bodies for ten candidate icons sum to about 5,450 characters (est, https://api.iconify.design/fa7-solid.json?icons=wand-magic-sparkles,triangle-exclamation,shield-halved,microchip,lock,key,user,scroll,file-contract,window-maximize). DOM: read `icon[4]` and create one `path` with `createElementNS`.
- Bootstrap Icons. Ships SVG files, a sprite and fonts; no JS path data (the `types` file only lists font names) (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/bootstrap-icons/latest). shield-fill-exclamation is about 700 B as a file (est). Path bodies for ten candidates sum to about 3,650 characters (est, https://api.iconify.design/bi.json?icons=stars,shield-fill-exclamation,shield-fill,lock-fill,key-fill,person-fill,file-text-fill,window,app-indicator,cpu-fill).
- Iconoir. SVG files only, exports map for `icons/regular/*.svg` and `icons/solid/*.svg` (verified from source: https://registry.npmjs.org/iconoir/latest). shield-alert is about 665 B with 3 paths (est).
- Remix Icon. SVG files and fonts in `remixicon`; a React package exists separately (`@remixicon/react`). File layout inside the package was not read: unverified.
- Carbon. Ships JS data. Per-icon ES modules `es/<name>/<size>.js` default-export a descriptor `{ elem: "svg", attrs, content: [{ elem: "path", attrs: { d } }], name, size }`, with an Apache header and no imports; `sideEffects: false` (verified from source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@carbon/icons@11.91.0/es/security/16.js and https://registry.npmjs.org/@carbon/icons/latest). security/16 is about 1,000 characters (2 paths); ai-generate/16 about 2,000 characters (6 paths) (est).
- Radix Icons. The npm package ships React components (React as a peer dependency, 332 files in dist); standalone SVG files in the package: unverified (verified from source for the React shape: https://registry.npmjs.org/@radix-ui/react-icons/latest).

Turning the data into SVG elements without `innerHTML`:

- For Lucide, Carbon and Font Awesome the data is already structured; a few lines of `createElementNS` and `setAttribute` suffice, and Lucide's `createElement` shows the pattern (verified from source: the createElement.mjs URL above).
- For SVG-only sets (Phosphor, Heroicons, Tabler, Bootstrap, Material, Iconoir, Remix) two routes work: extract the path `d` strings and root attributes at build time into a typed constant and build elements with `createElementNS`; or import the file as text and parse it with `DOMParser` as `image/svg+xml`, then `importNode`. The first avoids a runtime parser and fits the repo's `scripts/` rule; this is judgment.
- Size does not separate the sets: eight icons weigh about 2 to 5 KB in every set that was measured, from the exact 3,534 B Heroicons figure to the roughly 5 KB Font Awesome estimate (judgment from the figures above).

### 5. Where each candidate fails a stated criterion

- Remix Icon: custom licence with standalone-product and competing-library restrictions, and a registry SPDX field that disagrees with the shipped file (section 1). Fails "open source" in the OSI-style sense unless the owner accepts a custom licence; whether the OSI or SPDX list includes it: unverified.
- Font Awesome Free: attribution is mandatory (CC BY 4.0), the per-icon JS carries none, and sparkles, swords and a shield-with-alert are Pro-only or absent (section 3).
- Radix Icons: missing shield, key, cpu, swords; React-only package (sections 3 and 4).
- Carbon: no crossed swords, 32 grid art at every size seen, Apache notice duties.
- Iconoir: no swords, solid forms for few icons, stroke 1.5.
- Bootstrap Icons: no sparkle (`stars` is the nearest), no swords, no filled window.

### 6. Shortlist (judgment)

Ranking against the owner's four criteria (open source, commercially safe, looks good small, cheap to bundle) plus the eight concepts:

1. Phosphor, fill weight. MIT with a one-line notice; flat solid glyphs like Steam's; 7 of 8 concepts exact and PvP as a single sword; one-path SVG files of 0.3 to 0.9 KB; six weights so a hover state or outline form needs no second set; 5 open issues. Costs: SVG-only (build-time path extraction), npm version dates from March 2024 although the repo is active, and no crossed swords.
2. Lucide. Best consumption: per-icon JS arrays, `sideEffects: false`, a DOM builder that avoids `innerHTML`, 8 of 8 concepts including `shield-alert` and `swords`, releases within days. Costs: outline only (1 to 1.33 px lines at 12 to 16 px unless stroke width is raised or non-scaling stroke is used), two licences (add the MIT notice if `lock` or `key` is used).
3. Heroicons 16 solid. MIT; the only set with a dedicated 16 px solid drawing; exact total 3,534 B for seven icons; 4 open issues. Costs: no swords, a small pool of 316 icons if the tagging kinds grow, last npm release November 2024.

First alternate: Tabler (MIT, 6,238 icons, 8 of 8 with `file-text` for EULA, active releases; mixed outline and filled forms, filled `cpu` and `swords` absent). Material Symbols is the only set with a fill form for swords but has the unresolved sparkle gap, Apache duties, and the optical size floor of 20 dp.

What would change the ranking:

- If outline is acceptable on chips: Lucide moves to first.
- If crossed swords for PvP is mandatory in a solid style: Material Symbols (if the sparkle issue resolves) moves up; Tabler outline or Lucide outline are the only other full matches; Phosphor and Heroicons drop.
- If no build-time extraction step is wanted: Lucide, Carbon and Font Awesome move up because their data is JS.
- If the owner wants no attribution duty beyond a notices file: Font Awesome Free drops out; if only MIT or ISC text is acceptable, Material Symbols and Carbon (Apache) fall behind the MIT sets.
- If many more kinds of chip are expected: pool size favours Tabler (6,238), Lucide (1,903) and Phosphor (1,512 icons) over Heroicons (316) and Radix (332).
- If a rendering test at 12 and 16 px shows Lucide with a raised stroke width reads better than Phosphor fill, swap ranks 1 and 2; no such test was run.

## Caveats and version notes

- Dates are single-source (npm registry search endpoint). GitHub "open issues" includes open pull requests. The Carbon and Font Awesome repo counts cover the whole monorepo or project, not only icons.
- Names marked (m) were read on Iconify, which is a third-party mirror of upstream data; the Iconify copy can lag (Remix shows 4.8.0 against npm 4.9.1) or normalise (each set re-based to one viewBox; Tabler's "-filled" names are Iconify's, the package files drop the suffix).
- Byte figures marked "est" were counted by a summarising model and are rough (Phosphor sword-fill came out at about 890 B on a file read and about 450 characters on a body read, so expect +/- 50 percent). The Heroicons figures are exact tree sizes. No test bundle was built, so no figure is a measured esbuild output.
- Lucide is at 1.61.0; the current framework docs rename `absoluteStrokeWidth` to `nonScalingStroke`, so check the installed version before writing config (search-summary: https://lucide.dev/guide/react/basics/stroke-width).
- The Lucide Feather list and the licence summaries came from a summariser reading the raw files; quoted fragments are short on purpose.
- The Heroicons README names four sizes but not "mini" or "micro".
- Leads from the brief: Phosphor MIT with six weights, Heroicons MIT with outline, solid 20 and 16, Material Symbols Apache 2.0 with a fill axis, Font Awesome Free icons CC BY 4.0, Tabler MIT with some filled icons (1,054), Lucide ISC with Feather-derived MIT parts and outline only. All were confirmed above.
- Not answered: which Material Symbols icon replaces `auto_awesome` in the 0.48.1 SVG package; the file layout of the Remix package; whether Radix ships standalone SVG files; whether a plain `shield` exists in Heroicons; real rendering quality at 12 to 16 px; exact byte totals for sets other than Heroicons.
```

`docs/store/listing.mdx`:

```mdx
# Store listing copy

Source text for the Chrome Web Store and addons.mozilla.org (AMO) listings of "Tag Kit for Steam" (short name "Tag Kit"). The listing text is English; the extension also ships a Spanish catalog (name "Tag Kit para Steam", short name "Tag Kit"). The userscript has no store listing; its text is the `@description` in the userscript header, which comes from the same message catalog as the manifests. Its `@name` stays "AI Reporter for Steam" for now; see [Renaming the userscript](../testing/userscript-install.mdx#renaming-the-userscript).

Wording follows the project's semantics rule: a badge says "AI use reported". Nothing here says a game "uses AI" or is "AI-free", because developers report their AI use themselves.

Limits to respect when pasting: the Chrome name is at most 75 characters and the manifest description at most 132 (both come from `src/locales/en/messages.json`); the Chrome Web Store summary field is the manifest description.

## Name

Tag Kit for Steam

Short name: Tag Kit

## Summary (manifest description, 132 characters at most)

Tags Steam games: AI Generated Content Disclosure, Anti-Cheat (kernel level first), 3rd-party DRM, account and EULA, and PvP.

## Short description for AMO (250 characters at most)

Tags Steam store items: AI Generated Content Disclosure, Anti-Cheat (Kernel Level first), 3rd-party DRM, 3rd-Party Account, 3rd-party EULA and PvP. It reads only what Steam reports and sends no reports anywhere. Not affiliated with Valve.

## Detailed description

Tag Kit for Steam tags items on the Steam store: AI Generated Content Disclosure, Kernel Level Anti-Cheat and Anti-Cheat Software, 3rd-party DRM, 3rd-Party Account, 3rd-party EULA and PvP.

It only reads what Steam's store data and developers report there. It sends no reports, collects nothing and has no server of its own.

What it does:

- Adds a badge to capsules and rows in search, wishlist, home, tag and category hubs, sale pages, developer pages and search suggestions for items that carry one of those tags. The AI tag reads "AI use reported".
- On a game's page, shows a banner that quotes the developer's AI report word for word.
- Optionally dims or hides those items in lists. This is off by default.
- Lets you ignore a game you consider a false flag, with a per-game allow-list.

What each tag means, in Steam's words:

- AI Generated Content Disclosure: the developer reported generative AI use. The badge reads "AI use reported".
- Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: the game's anti-cheat runs at the kernel level.
- Anti-Cheat Software: the game uses anti-cheat software.
- 3rd-party DRM: the game uses DRM from a third party.
- 3rd-Party Account: the game needs an account with a third party.
- 3rd-party EULA: the game needs agreement to a third party's EULA.
- PvP: the game has player-versus-player play.

The AI tag is self-reported. It does not say how much AI a game uses, and a game without a badge is not guaranteed to be free of AI, because developers may not have reported anything, and Steam may not have the information for every item.

Privacy: nothing is collected. To check the items on the page you are viewing, their app IDs go to Valve's own hosts that your browser uses (api.steampowered.com and store.steampowered.com), without cookies. Results and your settings stay in your browser. The full policy is in PRIVACY.md in the project repository.

Open source (MIT). Source and build steps: https://github.com/jrv97/steam-ai-reporter

Tag Kit for Steam is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Valve Corporation. Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks of Valve Corporation.

## Single-purpose statement (Chrome Web Store)

Tag Kit for Steam has one purpose: to show, on Steam store pages, which items carry tags for AI content disclosure, anti-cheat, 3rd-party DRM, account and EULA, and PvP, by marking those items.

## Permission justifications

The extension asks for one permission and no host permissions. It has no background script.

- `storage`: keeps the cache of results (an app is not requested again until its entry expires), your settings, the per-game allow-list, and a small record used to back off if Steam is limiting requests. All of it stays on your device in the extension's local storage.
- Site access (content script matches `https://store.steampowered.com/*`): the content script runs only on the Steam store, because that is where the items to mark are. Its requests to `api.steampowered.com` and `store.steampowered.com` are made from the store page's own origin, so no `host_permissions` entry is needed. Both are Valve hosts the user is already on, and every request is made with `credentials: "omit"`.
- Remote code: none. No `eval`, no remote scripts and no remote selectors. The bundles in the package are not minified and are built from the public source.

## Privacy answers

These match PRIVACY.md.

- Does it collect or transmit user data to the developer or any third party? No. There is no analytics, no telemetry, no account and no server of the developer.
- Does it send any data off the device? Only app IDs of the items on the page being viewed, to Valve's own hosts `api.steampowered.com` (GetItems, in batches of up to 50) and `store.steampowered.com` (a few app pages as a fallback), without cookies. Valve sees the IP address and the app IDs, as for any store request.
- What is stored locally? Results per app ID (which tags the store data gives the item, check time, the developer's AI report text and language, the name of a named AI service if any, the game's name), the settings, the allow-list, and a back-off record. In `storage.local`.
- Does it read the Steam account, wishlist contents, library, cookies or browsing history? No.
- Is data sold or used for purposes unrelated to the single purpose? No.
- Chrome Web Store data usage categories: none are collected. Certify the three limited-use statements (not sold, not used for unrelated purposes, not used for creditworthiness or lending).
- AMO `data_collection_permissions`: `required: ["none"]`, set in the Gecko manifest overlay (`manifest.gecko.json`).
- Privacy policy URL: https://github.com/jrv97/steam-ai-reporter/blob/main/PRIVACY.md

## AMO reviewer notes

The package is built from source, unminified. Build steps are in the README under "Build from source", and the source archive is `steam-ai-reporter-source-<version>.zip`:

1. Install mise (`curl https://mise.run | sh`) on Linux or macOS, or see the mise install guide for Windows.
2. In the unpacked source folder run `mise trust`, then `mise install`, then `mise run build`.
3. `dist/gecko` is the submitted add-on.

The extension has no background script, requests no host permissions and makes no network request other than the two Valve hosts above.

## Screenshots

`docs/store/screenshots/` holds the listing screenshots, 1280 x 800 JPEG, in upload order. The Chrome Web Store takes five and AMO takes any number.

1. `01-search.jpg`: search results for "roguelike" with three badged rows.
2. `02-app-banner.jpg`: the banner on app 1808500, with its badged DLC rows.
3. `03-hover-card.jpg`: the panel that opens on a search badge. While it is open, Steam's own game hover stays hidden.
4. `04-next-fest.jpg`: Next Fest sale cards with the compact badge on the game image.
5. `05-options.jpg`: the options page with the list filter on Dim and one game in the allow-list.

`list-dim.jpg` (Dim mode in search) and `popup.jpg` (the toolbar popup, 360 px wide) appear in the README only.

They were captured on 2026-10-22 in headless Chrome with a fresh, signed-out profile, a 1280 x 800 viewport and Steam's cookie banner hidden. The store pages run the dev bundle (`dist/dev/inject.js`) built from main at commit 59417c5. The options page and the popup are `dist/chromium/options.html` with `chrome.storage` stubbed in memory. Prices show in euros because of the capture location.

## Assets still needed

- Chrome Web Store small promo tile 440 x 280 (optional).
- The store icon is `assets/icons/icon-128.png`, which the build also ships.
```

```mdx
# Manual test checklist

Run before each release, after `mise run canary` passes. Automated tests cover the parsers, the scanner and the placements against captured fixtures; this list covers what only a real browser and a live store show.

## Setup

Targets, each tested logged out and logged in:

| Target            | How to load it                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chrome extension  | `mise run build`, then `chrome://extensions`, Developer mode, "Load unpacked", pick `dist/chromium`. Or `mise run run-chromium`.      |
| Firefox extension | `mise run run-gecko`, which uses `SAR_GECKO_BIN` and the dedicated profile in `SAR_GECKO_PROFILE`. Personal profiles stay off limits. |
| Tampermonkey      | Install `steam-ai-reporter.user.js` from `artifacts/` (or `dist/userscript/`) in Chrome and in Firefox.                               |
| Violentmonkey     | Same file, in Chrome and in Firefox.                                                                                                  |

Before starting:

- Sign in to Steam in the dedicated Firefox profile and in Chrome for the logged-in column; use a private window or a clean profile for the logged-out column.
- Have one wishlist with at least 30 items, including at least one item whose developer reported AI use (one known to work on the day: 5072580 or 1808500; one without a report: 413150).
- Open the page console on every store page and keep it open. Any error from `sar-` code fails the cell.
- Enable the `debug` setting once to confirm the verbose log appears, then turn it off.

## How to read a cell

A surface cell passes when all of these hold:

1. An item with a report shows the badge "AI use reported"; an item without one shows nothing; no item shows an "AI-free" or "uses AI" wording.
2. The badge sits on the capsule, the page section around it carries none, and the layout stays intact.
3. Content added later (infinite scroll, carousel, React re-render, tab switch) gets badges without a reload and without duplicates.
4. The Network tab shows no request to any host other than `api.steampowered.com` and `store.steampowered.com`, no cookies sent on them, and one GetItems call per batch of up to 50 new IDs.
5. Reloading the page issues no new GetItems call for IDs already checked (the cache works).

Mark each cell with P (pass), F (fail, with a note and an issue), or N/A.
```

`docs/testing/userscript-install.mdx`:

```mdx
# Installing the userscript for testing

The userscript is `dist/userscript/steam-ai-reporter.user.js`, written by `mise run build`. A userscript manager runs it on every `https://store.steampowered.com/*` page. Test in Chrome and in Firefox Nightly only; the regular Firefox is personal and stays untouched.

Run `mise run build` first. The file lives in your clone, for example `C:\path\to\steam-ai-reporter\dist\userscript\steam-ai-reporter.user.js`.

## Tampermonkey

1. Install Tampermonkey in Chrome (Chrome Web Store) or in Firefox Nightly (addons.mozilla.org).
2. Chrome only: open `chrome://extensions`, click Details on Tampermonkey, turn on "Allow access to file URLs". Also turn on "Allow User Scripts" if Chrome shows that switch.
3. Open the built file in a tab by its `file:///` address, for example `file:///C:/path/to/steam-ai-reporter/dist/userscript/steam-ai-reporter.user.js`.
4. Tampermonkey shows an install page. Check that the name is "AI Reporter for Steam" (the script name from the first release) and that the permissions list only storage access and a menu command (no network access to other sites). Click Install.
5. To update after a rebuild, open the same `file:///` address again and click Reinstall.

## Violentmonkey

1. Install Violentmonkey in Chrome (Chrome Web Store) or in Firefox Nightly (addons.mozilla.org).
2. Chrome only: open `chrome://extensions`, click Details on Violentmonkey, turn on "Allow access to file URLs".
3. Open the built file by its `file:///` address in a tab, as above.
4. Violentmonkey shows "Confirm installation". Tick "Track local file" so it reloads the script from disk while that tab stays open, then click Confirm.
5. After a rebuild, switch to that tab and reload it; Violentmonkey picks up the new file.

Use only one manager at a time on a given browser, or disable the other one for the test, so the script runs once.

## What you should see

Open each page logged out first, then logged in. The first page load after installing may need a refresh.

1. App page `https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/` (Courage and Faith: Into the Dark Woods, reports AI use): a purple banner above the purchase box titled "AI use reported", quoting the developer's text, and an "AI use reported" chip under the Developer and Publisher values.
2. App page `https://store.steampowered.com/app/413150/` (Stardew Valley, no report): nothing added.
3. Search page `https://store.steampowered.com/search/?term=roguelike`: an "AI use reported" badge before the platform icons on the rows whose developers reported AI use (about ten of the first fifty at the time of writing), and nothing on the other rows.
4. Settings: click the manager's toolbar icon, then "AI Reporter for Steam", then "Settings". A dialog titled "Tag Kit for Steam" opens with switches for badges and banner, a Show, Dim or Hide choice, and a list of games you ignored. Escape or Close closes it and returns focus to the page. Change "Games that report AI use" to Hide on the search page: the badged rows vanish at once.
5. Disable the script in the manager and reload: every added element is gone.

## Reporting back

Per manager and browser, note which of the five checks passed, and for each failure the text of the first red line in the page console (F12, Console tab, filter on `[sar]`). Tampermonkey was verified before this build (plain `fetch`, storage, styles); Violentmonkey has not been run yet, so its first run is the real test.

## Renaming the userscript

The script keeps the `@name` of its first release: "AI Reporter for Steam" in English and "Marcador de IA para Steam" in Spanish, both held under `userscript_name` in `src/locales/<locale>/userscript.json`, a catalog that only the userscript header reads. Script managers tell installed scripts apart by name and namespace, so a renamed `@name` may install as a second script beside the old one and leave the stored settings and ignored games with the old copy. Run a spike in Tampermonkey and in Violentmonkey, in Chrome and in Firefox Nightly, before flipping:

1. Install the current build and change a setting, for example ignore one game.
2. Build with a different `@name` and update the way users do (the update URL, or reinstall from the file).
3. Note whether the manager updates in place, installs a second script or asks, and whether the setting survived.

Flip once both managers behave:

1. In `scripts/build.py`, set `USERSCRIPT_NAME` to `("messages.json", "ext_name")`. The `@name` and `@name:es` lines then follow the product name.
2. Delete `src/locales/en/userscript.json` and `src/locales/es/userscript.json`.
3. Update every spot that names the script. In this file: the name check in step 4 of the Tampermonkey list and step 4 of "What you should see". In `docs/store/listing.mdx`: the sentence about `@name` in the first paragraph. In `docs/design/components.mdx`: the `userscript_name` row of the message table.
4. Add a changie fragment (`mise run change-new`). If the spike showed a second script, say that the old copy needs removing and how to carry the settings over, using the backup on the settings dialog.

```
