`scripts/repo.py`:

```py
"""Shared helpers for the scripts in this folder: repository paths, Git file lists, failures."""

import json
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NoReturn

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DIST = ROOT / "dist"
ARTIFACTS = ROOT / "artifacts"
SLUG = "steam-ai-reporter"
# The extension builds, named after their browser engines: dist/<target>, manifest.<target>.json.
EXTENSION_TARGETS = ("chromium", "gecko")
ICONS_DIR = ROOT / "assets" / "icons"
ICON_SIZES = (16, 32, 48, 128)
VALIBOT_LICENSE = ROOT / "node_modules" / "valibot" / "LICENSE.md"
PNG_SIGNATURE = bytes([137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10])
PNG_HEADER_SIZE = 24


def valibot_notice() -> str:
    """valibot's license as a `/*!` comment: the userscript is one file, so it carries the text."""
    text = VALIBOT_LICENSE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    return f"/*! valibot\n{text}\n*/"


def png_size(path: Path) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """The width and height from a PNG's header bytes, or None when the file is no PNG."""
    with path.open("rb") as file:
        header = file.read(PNG_HEADER_SIZE)
    if len(header) < PNG_HEADER_SIZE or not header.startswith(PNG_SIGNATURE):
        return None
    if header[12:16] != b"IHDR":
        return None
    width, height = struct.unpack(">II", header[16:PNG_HEADER_SIZE])
    return width, height


def fail(message: str) -> NoReturn:
    print(f"error: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8"
    )
    return result.stdout


def git_paths(*args: str) -> list[str]:
    """Run a Git command that prints NUL-separated paths (`-z`) and return them."""
    return [path for path in git(*args).split("\0") if path]


def repo_files() -> list[str]:
    """Tracked files plus untracked files that are not ignored."""
    return git_paths("ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard")


def staged_files() -> list[str]:
    return git_paths("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "-z", "--diff-filter=ACMR")


def read_json(path: Path) -> object:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as file:
        result: object = json.load(file)
    return result


def json_object(value: object, where: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        fail(f"{where}: expected a JSON object")
    return {str(key): item for key, item in value.items()}


def json_string(value: object, where: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        fail(f"{where}: expected a string")
    return value


def package_version() -> str:
    package = json_object(read_json(ROOT / "package.json"), "package.json")
    return json_string(package.get("version"), "package.json version")

```

`scripts/run_browser.py`:

```py
"""Run a build in a development browser through `web-ext run`, reloading on every rebuild.

gecko: the Gecko build in Firefox Nightly only, from SAR_GECKO_BIN, with the dedicated profile
directory in SAR_GECKO_PROFILE. There is no fallback to a Firefox on PATH: a personal Firefox and
its profiles are never launched or touched. The binary must be a Nightly build (its
channel-prefs.js says "nightly"), and a profile last used by another Firefox install is refused.

chromium: the Chromium build in the browser at SAR_CHROMIUM_BIN, with the dedicated profile
directory in SAR_CHROMIUM_PROFILE.

The variables live in mise.local.toml (see mise.local.toml.example).

Usage: run_browser.py {chromium,gecko} [--check]
"""

import argparse
import configparser
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from repo import DIST, EXTENSION_TARGETS, ROOT, fail

START_URL = "https://store.steampowered.com/"
CHANNEL = re.compile(r'pref\(\s*"app\.update\.channel"\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\)')
EXAMPLE = "see mise.local.toml.example"


def env_path(name: str) -> Path:
    value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
    if not value:
        fail(f"{name} is not set; add it to mise.local.toml ({EXAMPLE})")
    path = Path(value)
    if not path.is_absolute():
        fail(f"{name} must be an absolute path, got {value!r}")
    return path


def firefox_channel(binary: Path) -> str | None:
    """Read the update channel next to the binary (Windows and Linux layout, then macOS)."""
    candidates = [
        binary.parent / "defaults" / "pref" / "channel-prefs.js",
        binary.parent.parent / "Resources" / "defaults" / "pref" / "channel-prefs.js",
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file():
            match = CHANNEL.search(candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
            return match.group(1) if match else None
    return None


def same_dir(left: str, right: Path) -> bool:
    return os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(left)) == os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(right))


def check_profile(name: str, profile: Path, binary: Path | None) -> None:
    if profile.exists() and not profile.is_dir():
        fail(f"{name} must be a profile directory, got a file: {profile}")
    compatibility = profile / "compatibility.ini"
    if binary is None or not compatibility.is_file():
        return
    parser = configparser.ConfigParser(interpolation=None)
    parser.read(compatibility, encoding="utf-8")
    last = parser.get("Compatibility", "LastPlatformDir", fallback="")
    if last and not same_dir(last, binary.parent):
        fail(
            f"{name} was last used by the Firefox in {last}, not by {binary.parent}; "
            "use a profile dedicated to Firefox Nightly"
        )


def gecko_args(check_only: bool) -> list[str]:
    binary = env_path("SAR_GECKO_BIN")
    if not binary.is_file():
        fail(f"SAR_GECKO_BIN does not exist: {binary}")
    channel = firefox_channel(binary)
    if channel != "nightly":
        found = f'channel "{channel}"' if channel else "no update channel"
        fail(f"SAR_GECKO_BIN must be Firefox Nightly; {binary} has {found}")
    profile = env_path("SAR_GECKO_PROFILE")
    check_profile("SAR_GECKO_PROFILE", profile, binary)
    if check_only:
        return []
    return [
        "--target=firefox-desktop",
        f"--source-dir={DIST / 'gecko'}",
        f"--firefox={binary}",
        f"--firefox-profile={profile}",
        "--profile-create-if-missing",
        "--keep-profile-changes",
    ]


def chromium_args(check_only: bool) -> list[str]:
    binary = env_path("SAR_CHROMIUM_BIN")
    if not binary.is_file():
        fail(f"SAR_CHROMIUM_BIN does not exist: {binary}")
    profile = env_path("SAR_CHROMIUM_PROFILE")
    check_profile("SAR_CHROMIUM_PROFILE", profile, None)
    if check_only:
        return []
    return [
        "--target=chromium",
        f"--source-dir={DIST / 'chromium'}",
        f"--chromium-binary={binary}",
        f"--chromium-profile={profile}",
        "--profile-create-if-missing",
        "--keep-profile-changes",
    ]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("target", choices=EXTENSION_TARGETS)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="only validate the settings")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    browser_args = gecko_args(args.check) if args.target == "gecko" else chromium_args(args.check)
    if args.check:
        print(f"{args.target}: development browser settings look right")
        return
    # web-ext creates a missing profile directory, but not its missing parents.
    profile_var = "SAR_GECKO_PROFILE" if args.target == "gecko" else "SAR_CHROMIUM_PROFILE"
    env_path(profile_var).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    web_ext = shutil.which("web-ext")
    if web_ext is None:
        fail("web-ext is not on PATH; run this through `mise run run-gecko` or `run-chromium`")
    command = [web_ext, "run", *browser_args, f"--start-url={START_URL}"]
    sys.exit(subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False).returncode)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`scripts/test_calver.py`:

```py
"""Unit tests for calver.py (run by `mise run release:test`)."""

import unittest
from datetime import date

from calver import MAX_SEGMENT, next_version, parse

DAY = date(2026, 10, 5)


class ParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_accepts_unpadded_versions(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(parse("2026.10.5"), (2026, 10, 5, 0))
        self.assertEqual(parse("2026.1.31.2"), (2026, 1, 31, 2))
        self.assertEqual(parse(f"2026.12.31.{MAX_SEGMENT}"), (2026, 12, 31, MAX_SEGMENT))

    def test_rejects_padding_and_bad_shapes(self) -> None:
        for text in (
            "2026.10.05",
            "2026.01.5",
            "2026.10.5.01",
            "2026.10.5.0",
            "v2026.10.5",
            "2026.10",
            "2026.10.5.1.1",
            "2026.13.1",
            "2026.2.30",
            f"2026.10.5.{MAX_SEGMENT + 1}",
            "0.0.0",
            "2026.10.5-1",
        ):
            with self.subTest(text=text):
                self.assertIsNone(parse(text))


class NextVersionTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_release_of_the_day_is_never_padded(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(next_version(DAY, []), "2026.10.5")
        self.assertEqual(next_version(date(2027, 1, 9), ["2026.10.5"]), "2027.1.9")

    def test_recut_increments_from_one(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.5"]), "2026.10.5.1")
        self.assertEqual(next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.5", "2026.10.5.1"]), "2026.10.5.2")
        self.assertEqual(next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.5.2", "2026.10.5"]), "2026.10.5.3")

    def test_earlier_days_and_other_tags_are_ignored(self) -> None:
        tags = ["2026.10.4", "2026.10.4.7", "nightly", "v1.0.0", "2026.10.05"]
        self.assertEqual(next_version(DAY, tags), "2026.10.5")

    def test_at_most_four_segments(self) -> None:
        version = next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.5", "2026.10.5.9"])
        self.assertEqual(len(version.split(".")), 4)

    def test_segments_stay_within_the_chrome_limit(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.5", f"2026.10.5.{MAX_SEGMENT}"])

    def test_a_tag_newer_than_today_fails(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            next_version(DAY, ["2026.10.6"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`scripts/test_check_i18n.py`:

```py
"""Unit tests for the literal-copy check of check_i18n.py (run by `mise run release:test`)."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from catalogs import Catalog, Entry, load, static_parts, used_placeholders
from check_i18n import (
    MIN_WILDCARD_TEXT,
    SHIPPED,
    CopyIndex,
    copy_index,
    copy_problems,
    scanned_sources,
)


def catalog(**messages: str) -> Catalog:
    return {
        key: Entry(key, message, "A description.", used_placeholders(message))
        for key, message in messages.items()
    }


ENGLISH = catalog(
    banner_undo="Undo",
    notice_settings_saved="Saved.",
    userscript_menu_settings="Settings",
    options_version="Version $version$",
    options_allow_restore_label="Stop ignoring $name$",
    banner_source="In the developer's own words:",
    options_privacy_lookup="To check a game, it asks Valve's own store servers.",
    only_placeholder="$count$",
    short_with_placeholder="$n$ ok",
    ext_description="Tags: AI Generated Content Disclosure, PvP.",
)
SPANISH = catalog(banner_undo="Deshacer", banner_source="En palabras del desarrollador:")
CATALOGS = {"en": ENGLISH, "es": SPANISH}
HIT = "catalog text in a string literal"


def keys(index: CopyIndex, *parts: str) -> list[str]:
    return [ref.label() for ref in index.matches(parts)]


class MatchTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.index = copy_index(CATALOGS)

    def test_a_literal_equal_to_a_short_message_matches(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Undo"), ["banner_undo"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Saved."), ["notice_settings_saved"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, " Undo "), ["banner_undo"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Deshacer"), ["banner_undo (es)"])

    def test_a_short_word_inside_a_longer_literal_does_not_match(self) -> None:
        for literal in ("Undo the change", "parseSettings", "Accept-Settings", "undo", "Sav"):
            with self.subTest(literal=literal):
                self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, literal), [])

    def test_a_placeholder_message_matches_when_the_whole_literal_fits(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Version 2026.10.20"), ["options_version"])
        self.assertEqual(
            keys(self.index, "Stop ignoring Some Game"), ["options_allow_restore_label"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Version"), [])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Versions of 3"), [])

    def test_a_template_expression_stands_for_a_placeholder(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Version ", ""), ["options_version"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Stop ignoring ", ""), ["options_allow_restore_label"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "", "Undo", " now"), ["banner_undo"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "", " is ", ""), [])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Versions ", ""), [])

    def test_placeholder_messages_with_little_static_text_never_match_everything(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "anything at all"), [])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "3 ok"), [])

    def test_long_catalog_text_matches_inside_a_longer_literal(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            keys(self.index, "<p>In the developer's own words: <b>x</b></p>"), ["banner_source"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            keys(self.index, "En palabras del desarrollador: x"), ["banner_source (es)"]
        )

    def test_a_detection_constant_may_repeat_a_message(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "AI Generated Content Disclosure"), [])
        self.assertEqual(
            keys(self.index, "Tags: AI Generated Content Disclosure, PvP."), ["ext_description"]
        )

    def test_a_detection_constant_still_matches_a_message_that_equals_it(self) -> None:
        index = copy_index(
            {
                "en": catalog(
                    ext_description="Tags: AI Generated Content Disclosure, PvP.",
                    banner_heading="AI Generated Content Disclosure",
                )
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(keys(index, "AI Generated Content Disclosure"), ["banner_heading"])

    def test_a_long_piece_of_a_message_matches(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "asks Valve's own store"), ["options_privacy_lookup"])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "own words"), [])

    def test_matching_is_case_sensitive(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "in the developer's own words:"), [])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "Banner_Undo"), [])

    def test_an_empty_literal_never_matches(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, ""), [])
        self.assertEqual(keys(self.index, "   "), [])


class ShippedCatalogsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_shipped_message_is_caught_as_a_string_and_as_a_template(self) -> None:
        shipped = {path.parent.name: load(path) for path in SHIPPED.glob("*/messages.json")}
        index = copy_index(shipped)
        for locale, messages in shipped.items():
            for key, entry in messages.items():
                parts = tuple(static_parts(entry.message))
                if len(parts) > 1 and len("".join(parts).strip()) < MIN_WILDCARD_TEXT:
                    # Only placeholders and punctuation: no literal can be told from it.
                    continue
                with self.subTest(locale=locale, key=key):
                    self.assertTrue(index.matches(("x".join(parts),)), entry.message)
                    self.assertTrue(index.matches(parts), entry.message)


class ScanTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_flags_a_seeded_literal_in_a_test_file(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            write(root, "src/core/ui/banner.test.ts", 'expect(button.textContent).toBe("Undo");\n')
            self.assertEqual(
                copy_problems(root, CATALOGS),
                [f"src/core/ui/banner.test.ts:1: banner_undo: {HIT}"],
            )

    def test_reports_each_literal_with_its_line_and_keys(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            write(
                root,
                "tests/helpers/a.ts",
                'const a = 1;\nconst b = `Saved.${x}`;\nf("Deshacer");\n',
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                copy_problems(root, CATALOGS),
                [
                    f"tests/helpers/a.ts:2: notice_settings_saved: {HIT}",
                    f"tests/helpers/a.ts:3: banner_undo (es): {HIT}",
                ],
            )

    def test_a_detection_constant_may_repeat_a_message(self) -> None:
        heading = "AI Generated Content Disclosure"
        catalogs = {"en": catalog(kind_ai_heading=heading)}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            write(root, "src/core/kinds/ai.ts", f'const HEADING = "{heading}";\n')
            self.assertEqual(copy_problems(root, catalogs), [])
            write(root, "src/core/ui/a.ts", f'const a = "{heading} (copy)";\n')
            self.assertEqual(
                copy_problems(root, catalogs),
                [f"src/core/ui/a.ts:1: kind_ai_heading: {HIT}"],
            )

    def test_ignores_comments_identifiers_and_type_names(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            write(
                root,
                "src/core/settings.ts",
                '// Undo the change. Saved.\ntype Settings = { parseSettings: () => "kept" };\n',
            )
            self.assertEqual(copy_problems(root, CATALOGS), [])

    def test_skips_generated_files_and_the_test_catalog_and_fixture_folders(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            seeded = 'export const text = "Undo";\n'
            write(root, "src/core/i18n/keys.gen.ts", seeded)
            write(root, "tests/locales/keys.gen.ts", seeded)
            write(root, "tests/locales/messages.ts", seeded)
            write(root, "tests/fixtures/page.ts", seeded)
            write(root, "docs/design/previews/a.ts", seeded)
            write(root, "src/locales/en/messages.json", '{"banner_undo": {"message": "Undo"}}')
            self.assertEqual(copy_problems(root, CATALOGS), [])
            self.assertEqual(scanned_sources(root), [])

    def test_scans_every_source_suffix_under_src_and_tests(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            for name in ("src/a.ts", "src/deep/b.mts", "tests/c.test.ts", "tests/helpers/d.d.ts"):
                write(root, name, "export {};\n")
            write(root, "src/notes.md", "Undo\n")
            self.assertEqual(
                [path.relative_to(root).as_posix() for path in scanned_sources(root)],
                ["src/a.ts", "src/deep/b.mts", "tests/c.test.ts", "tests/helpers/d.d.ts"],
            )


def write(root: Path, relative: str, text: str) -> None:
    path = root / relative
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`scripts/test_cws.py`:

```py
"""Unit tests for cws.py with a fake API (run by `mise run release:test`)."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path

from cws import POLL_ATTEMPTS, publish

ITEM = "publishers/pub/items/ext"


class FakeApi:
    def __init__(self, upload: str, statuses: list[str], publish_state: str = "PENDING_REVIEW"):
        self.upload = upload
        self.statuses: Iterator[str] = iter(statuses)
        self.publish_state = publish_state
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str, int]] = []
        self.sleeps = 0

    def __call__(self, method: str, path: str, body: bytes) -> dict[str, object]:
        self.calls.append((method, path, len(body)))
        if path.endswith(":upload"):
            return {"uploadState": self.upload}
        if path.endswith(":fetchStatus"):
            return {"lastAsyncUploadState": next(self.statuses)}
        return {"state": self.publish_state}

    def sleep(self, _seconds: float) -> None:
        self.sleeps += 1


class PublishTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.archive = Path(folder.name) / "chrome.zip"
        self.archive.write_bytes(b"zip-bytes")

    def run_publish(self, api: FakeApi) -> str:
        return publish(api, "pub", "ext", self.archive, api.sleep)

    def test_uploads_then_submits_when_the_upload_succeeds_at_once(self) -> None:
        api = FakeApi("SUCCEEDED", [])
        self.assertEqual(self.run_publish(api), "PENDING_REVIEW")
        self.assertEqual(
            api.calls,
            [("POST", f"/upload/v2/{ITEM}:upload", 9), ("POST", f"/v2/{ITEM}:publish", 0)],
        )
        self.assertEqual(api.sleeps, 0)

    def test_polls_an_upload_in_progress_until_it_succeeds(self) -> None:
        api = FakeApi("IN_PROGRESS", ["IN_PROGRESS", "SUCCEEDED"])
        self.run_publish(api)
        paths = [path for _, path, _ in api.calls]
        self.assertEqual(paths.count(f"/v2/{ITEM}:fetchStatus"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(paths[-1], f"/v2/{ITEM}:publish")
        self.assertEqual(api.sleeps, 2)

    def test_a_failed_upload_stops_before_publishing(self) -> None:
        for api in (FakeApi("FAILED", []), FakeApi("IN_PROGRESS", ["FAILED"])):
            with self.subTest(upload=api.upload), self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                self.run_publish(api)
            self.assertNotIn(":publish", " ".join(path for _, path, _ in api.calls))

    def test_an_upload_that_never_finishes_fails_after_the_poll_budget(self) -> None:
        api = FakeApi("IN_PROGRESS", ["IN_PROGRESS"] * POLL_ATTEMPTS)
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            self.run_publish(api)
        self.assertEqual(api.sleeps, POLL_ATTEMPTS)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

```

`scripts/test_notes.py`:

```py
"""Unit tests for notes.py (run by `mise run release:test`)."""

import unittest

from notes import AMO_LIMIT, fit

FOOTER = "Full notes: https://example.test/releases/tag/1"


class FitTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_short_notes_pass_through(self) -> None:
        notes = "### Added\n- One."
        self.assertEqual(fit(notes, AMO_LIMIT, FOOTER), notes)

    def test_long_notes_keep_whole_lines_and_the_footer(self) -> None:
        notes = "### Added\n" + "\n".join(f"- Item {n} " + "x" * 200 for n in range(40))
        result = fit(notes, AMO_LIMIT, FOOTER)
        self.assertLessEqual(len(result), AMO_LIMIT)
        self.assertTrue(result.endswith(FOOTER))
        for line in result.splitlines()[:-2]:
            self.assertTrue(line.startswith(("###", "- Item ")))
            self.assertFalse(line.startswith("- Item") and not line.endswith("x"))

    def test_a_trailing_heading_is_dropped(self) -> None:
        notes = "### Added\n- " + "a" * 40 + "\n### Changed\n- " + "b" * 3000
        result = fit(notes, 120, FOOTER)
        self.assertNotIn("### Changed", result)
        self.assertLessEqual(len(result), 120)

    def test_one_long_line_is_cut_with_an_ellipsis(self) -> None:
        result = fit("### Added\n- " + "c" * 500, 200, FOOTER)
        self.assertIn("c...\n", result)
        self.assertLessEqual(len(result), 200)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`scripts/test_ts_literals.py`:

```py
"""Unit tests for ts_literals.py (run by `mise run release:test`)."""

import unittest

from ts_literals import Literal, string_literals


def values(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """The parts of every literal, flat."""
    return [part for literal in string_literals(text) for part in literal.parts]


class QuotedTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reads_single_and_double_quotes(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values("""a("one", 'two');"""), ["one", "two"])

    def test_keeps_the_other_quote_inside(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values("""x = "it's"; y = 'say "hi"';"""), ["it's", 'say "hi"'])

    def test_decodes_escapes(self) -> None:
        text = r"""x = ["a\"b", 'c\'d', "e\nf", "\u00e1", "\u{1F600}", "\x41", "g\
h", "\q"];"""
        self.assertEqual(
            values(text), ['a"b', "c'd", "e\nf", "\u00e1", "\U0001f600", "A", "gh", "q"]
        )

    def test_keeps_a_comment_marker_inside_a_string(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            values('const url = "https://example.test/a";'), ["https://example.test/a"]
        )

    def test_reads_empty_strings(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values("""a("", '');"""), ["", ""])


class SkippedTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_skips_comments(self) -> None:
        text = """// it's "quoted"
/* 'block'
   "comment" */
const real = "kept";"""
        self.assertEqual(values(text), ["kept"])

    def test_skips_regex_literals_with_quotes(self) -> None:
        text = """const a = /["']/g; const b = x.replace(/`/, "ok"); if (/'/.test(s)) {}"""
        self.assertEqual(values(text), ["ok"])

    def test_keeps_a_slash_inside_a_regex_class(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values("""const a = /[/"]/; const b = "x";"""), ["x"])

    def test_reads_past_division(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values("""const half = total / 2; const s = "after";"""), ["after"])
        self.assertEqual(values("""const r = (a + b) / 2 + "x" / 3;"""), ["x"])

    def test_ignores_identifiers_and_type_names(self) -> None:
        text = """type Settings = { parseSettings: () => void };
function openSettingsDialog(): Settings { return create(); }"""
        self.assertEqual(values(text), [])


class TemplateTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_is_one_literal_with_a_part_per_static_chunk(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            string_literals("`Version ${version} of ${name}.`"),
            [Literal(1, ("Version ", " of ", "."))],
        )
        self.assertEqual(string_literals("`plain`"), [Literal(1, ("plain",))])

    def test_scans_expressions_and_nested_templates(self) -> None:
        text = 'x = `a${"b"}c${`d${e}f`}g`;'
        self.assertEqual(
            string_literals(text),
            [Literal(1, ("b",)), Literal(1, ("d", "f")), Literal(1, ("a", "c", "g"))],
        )

    def test_survives_braces_in_an_expression(self) -> None:
        text = "x = `a${fn({ k: 1 })}b`; y = 'after';"
        self.assertEqual(string_literals(text), [Literal(1, ("a", "b")), Literal(1, ("after",))])

    def test_decodes_escapes_in_a_template(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(values(r"x = `a\`b\${c}\n`;"), ["a`b${c}\n"])


class LineTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reports_the_line_where_a_literal_starts(self) -> None:
        text = """const a = 1;
/* two
   lines */
const b = "here";
const c = `
  multi ${d} line
`;"""
        self.assertEqual(
            string_literals(text),
            [Literal(4, ("here",)), Literal(5, ("\n  multi ", " line\n"))],
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`scripts/ts_literals.py`:

```py
"""List the string literals of a TypeScript or JavaScript source text.

A small scanner, not a parser: it skips comments and regular expression literals, reads single,
double and template literals, and decodes escapes. A template is one literal whose parts are the
static chunks around its `${}` expressions; the expressions are scanned too. Used by
check_i18n.py to find catalog text typed as a literal.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass

# What the scanner stops at: a comment, a quote, a possible regex, or a brace.
STOPS = re.compile(r"""//|/\*|["'`/{}]""")
QUOTED_END = {'"': re.compile(r'["\\\n]'), "'": re.compile(r"['\\\n]")}
TEMPLATE_END = re.compile(r"[`\\]|\$\{")
ESCAPES = {"n": "\n", "t": "\t", "r": "\r", "b": "\b", "f": "\f", "v": "\v", "0": "\0"}
HEX = re.compile(r"[0-9A-Fa-f]+")
CODE_POINT = re.compile(r"\{([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\}")
MAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF
# A `/` after one of these characters or keywords starts a regex; after anything else it divides.
REGEX_AFTER_CHARS = frozenset("(,=:[!&|?{};+-*%<>~^")
REGEX_AFTER_WORDS = frozenset(
    {
        "return",
        "typeof",
        "case",
        "do",
        "else",
        "in",
        "of",
        "void",
        "delete",
        "throw",
        "new",
        "yield",
        "await",
        "instanceof",
    }
)
LONGEST_KEYWORD = max(map(len, REGEX_AFTER_WORDS))
WORD_BEFORE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Literal:
    """A string literal: one part, or the static chunks of a template between its expressions."""

    line: int
    parts: tuple[str, ...]


def string_literals(text: str) -> list[Literal]:
    """The decoded string literals of `text` with their 1-based start lines, in line order."""
    return sorted(_Scanner(text).code(until_brace=False), key=lambda literal: literal.line)


class _Scanner:
    def __init__(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.pos = 0

    def line_at(self, index: int) -> int:
        return self.text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1

    def code(self, until_brace: bool) -> Iterator[Literal]:
        """Scan code until the end of the text, or the `}` that closes a template expression."""
        depth = 0
        text = self.text
        while (stop := STOPS.search(text, self.pos)) is not None:
            marker = stop.group()
            start = stop.start()
            self.pos = start + len(marker)
            if marker == "//":
                newline = text.find("\n", self.pos)
                self.pos = len(text) if newline < 0 else newline
            elif marker == "/*":
                close = text.find("*/", self.pos)
                self.pos = len(text) if close < 0 else close + 2
            elif marker == "/":
                if self.starts_regex(start):
                    self.skip_regex()
            elif marker == "{":
                depth += 1
            elif marker == "}":
                if until_brace and depth == 0:
                    return
                depth -= 1
            elif marker == "`":
                yield from self.template(start)
            else:
                yield self.quoted(marker, start)

    def starts_regex(self, slash: int) -> bool:
        end = slash
        while end > 0 and self.text[end - 1].isspace():
            end -= 1
        if end == 0 or self.text[end - 1] in REGEX_AFTER_CHARS:
            return True
        word = WORD_BEFORE.search(self.text[max(0, end - LONGEST_KEYWORD) : end])
        return word is not None and word.group() in REGEX_AFTER_WORDS

    def skip_regex(self) -> None:
        text = self.text
        in_class = False
        while self.pos < len(text):
            char = text[self.pos]
            self.pos += 1
            if char == "\\":
                self.pos += 1
            elif char == "\n":
                return
            elif char == "[":
                in_class = True
            elif char == "]":
                in_class = False
            elif char == "/" and not in_class:
                return

    def quoted(self, quote: str, start: int) -> Literal:
        text = self.text
        end = QUOTED_END[quote]
        chunks: list[str] = []
        while (stop := end.search(text, self.pos)) is not None:
            chunks.append(text[self.pos : stop.start()])
            self.pos = stop.end()
            if stop.group() == "\\":
                chunks.append(self.escape())
            else:
                break
        return Literal(self.line_at(start), ("".join(chunks),))

    def template(self, start: int) -> Iterator[Literal]:
        text = self.text
        chunks: list[str] = []
        parts: list[str] = []
        while (stop := TEMPLATE_END.search(text, self.pos)) is not None:
            chunks.append(text[self.pos : stop.start()])
            self.pos = stop.end()
            marker = stop.group()
            if marker == "\\":
                chunks.append(self.escape())
            elif marker == "`":
                break
            else:
                parts.append("".join(chunks))
                chunks = []
                yield from self.code(until_brace=True)
        parts.append("".join(chunks))
        yield Literal(self.line_at(start), tuple(parts))

    def escape(self) -> str:
        """Decode the escape after a backslash, leaving the position after it."""
        char = self.text[self.pos : self.pos + 1]
        self.pos += 1
        if char == "x":
            return self.hex_escape(2)
        if char == "u":
            return self.code_point_escape() or self.hex_escape(4)
        if char == "\r" and self.text.startswith("\n", self.pos):
            self.pos += 1
        if char in ("\r", "\n"):
            return ""
        return ESCAPES.get(char, char)

    def code_point_escape(self) -> str:
        """Decode the `{...}` of a `\\u{...}` escape, or return "" when there is none."""
        braced = CODE_POINT.match(self.text, self.pos)
        if braced is None:
            return ""
        self.pos = braced.end()
        code = int(braced.group(1), 16)
        return chr(code) if code <= MAX_CODE_POINT else ""

    def hex_escape(self, length: int) -> str:
        digits = self.text[self.pos : self.pos + length]
        if len(digits) != length or HEX.fullmatch(digits) is None:
            return ""
        self.pos += length
        return chr(int(digits, 16))

```

`scripts/zip_dir.py`:

```py
"""Zip a folder reproducibly: sorted entries, fixed timestamps and modes, files at the zip root.

Usage: zip_dir.py <folder> <output.zip>
"""

import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from repo import fail

FIXED_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
FILE_MODE = 0o644 << 16


def zip_dir(folder: Path, output: Path) -> None:
    files = sorted(path for path in folder.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
    if not files:
        fail(f"{folder}: no files to zip")
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(output, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9) as archive:
        for path in files:
            entry = zipfile.ZipInfo(path.relative_to(folder).as_posix(), FIXED_TIME)
            entry.external_attr = FILE_MODE
            entry.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            archive.writestr(entry, path.read_bytes())


def main() -> None:
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        fail("usage: zip_dir.py <folder> <output.zip>")
    zip_dir(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`src/core/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# src/core

The platform-free heart of Tag Kit for Steam: detection, cache, scanning, placement, rendering and i18n. The root `AGENTS.md` rules apply here; this file adds what is specific to core. The reasons are in [ADR 0002 (single codebase and tooling)](../../docs/adr/0002-single-codebase-and-tooling.mdx).

## What core must not import

- No `chrome`, `browser` or `GM` names, no `@types/chrome`, no `gm.d.ts`. `tsconfig.core.json` sets `"types": []` and never includes the platform declarations, so such a reference fails the type check. Do not work around it with a local `declare`.
- Nothing from `src/platform/`. Dependencies point inward: platform imports core, never the reverse.
- Only DOM and web standards are available: `fetch`, `DOMParser`, `MutationObserver`, `Intl`, `WeakMap`, `URL`. Anything else comes in through a port.
- No `eval`, `new Function` or dynamic remote code. No direct `JSON.parse`: use `parseJson(text): unknown` from `json.ts`.
- No user-visible or logged string literals, and no catalog text in tests. Code holds `MessageKey`s and tests take expected text from `t(key, params)`; copy lives in `src/locales/` (rule 9, i18n from day 1), and `scripts/check_i18n.py` fails on a literal that repeats it. Allowed literals: identifiers, selectors, URLs, storage keys, CSS class names, detection constants such as the heading `AI Generated Content Disclosure`.
- No `any`, no type assertions other than `as const`, no non-null assertions, no `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error` or `@ts-nocheck` (rule 10, strict static typing). Untrusted input is `unknown` until a valibot schema turns it into a typed value.
- Valve hosts only, always `credentials: "omit"` (rule 1, privacy). Core never builds a request to another host.

## Ports

Core depends on small interfaces in `ports.ts`: `Http`, `KeyValueStore`, `Clock`, `Logger`, `SettingsSource` and `MessageCatalog`. A port is one capability, as narrow as its callers need (interface segregation). Core receives implementations from a composition root and never constructs a platform object itself.

The only shipped composition roots are the extension content script and the userscript `main.ts`. `src/platform/dev/inject.ts` is a dev-only root and is never packaged.

### Adding a port

1. Check first whether an existing port or a small extension of one covers the need (rule 11, SOLID and DRY). A new port is the last resort.
2. Define the interface in `ports.ts`: methods take and return plain, `readonly` data, and return `unknown` for anything read from outside. No platform types in signatures.
3. Write the contract test in `tests/contracts/<port>.contract.ts`: a suite that takes a factory and asserts the behavior every implementation must have, including edge cases and failure modes.
4. Provide the test double in `tests/helpers/` (memory store, fake HTTP, fixed clock) and run the contract suite against it.
5. Implement the port in each platform that needs it under `src/platform/`, and run the same suite against each implementation.
6. Wire it in the composition roots only. Core code receives it by parameter.

### The contract-test rule

Every implementation of a port passes the same shared contract suite, with no per-implementation exceptions. If an implementation cannot pass a case, either the contract is wrong (change it for all implementations) or the implementation is wrong. A new implementation is not done until its suite run is in the tests.

## Extending without editing

- A new store surface is a new `Placement` entry in `scan/placements.ts`, with a fixture test. The scanner is not edited.
- A new detection source is a new `Detector` link in the chain. The chain and the scanner are not edited.
- A new message is a catalog key in `src/locales/`, never a literal in code or in a test.

### A new tag kind

A kind is data. The detectors, the chain, the cache, the settings and the ignore list read the registry, so these are the steps, and the type checker names the ones that list every kind:

1. The definition, `kinds/<id>.ts`: a `KindDefinition` with its id, `fromGetItems` (and `fromAppPage` when the English page can answer), the `stored` schema built with `storedDisclosed`, the catalog keys of its heading and chip, its settings defaults and its cache TTLs. Its disclosed type extends `DisclosedBase<"<id>">`.
2. One line in `KINDS` in `kinds/registry.ts`. The kind id, the verdict type, `perKind` and the settings defaults follow from it. `kindsFromGetItems`, the guards in `kinds/verdicts.ts` and the settings parser need no edit.
3. The catalog keys in `src/locales/en/` and `src/locales/es/`: `kind_<id>_heading` (Steam's own line for the kind, in each language), `kind_<id>_chip` and any detail line Steam shows. Each key carries a translator note.
4. A case in `kindDetails` (`ui/kind-details.ts`), which gives the hover card its lines under the heading (the banner shows only a kind's long developer text). The `switch` is exhaustive, so the type checker fails until it is there.
5. The per-kind rules in `ui/styles.css`: the badge switch, the dim and hide filters, their hover and focus rules and the hide rule list each kind by hand, because no selector joins an attribute on the root element with one on a host. `ui/styles.test.ts` fails for a kind they miss.
6. A fixture: a captured GetItems item of a game that declares the kind in `tests/fixtures/getitems/kinds.json`, and a captured app page when the kind has page-only detail (`scripts/capture_fixtures.py`, then the table in `tests/fixtures/README.md`).
7. A check in `scripts/canary.py` for the field the kind reads, so a change on Valve's side shows up before users see it.
8. The test helpers that list every kind: `FULL_DISCLOSED` and `disclosedKinds` in `tests/helpers/verdicts.ts` (typed, so the checker names them). Fixture-based tests take the captured verdicts from `tests/helpers/fixture-verdicts.ts`.
9. Tests next to the definition and in `kinds/registry.test.ts`; the settings form, the chips, the hover card and the banner pick the kind up without an edit.

### The DOM marks

Every attribute core writes on a store node starts with `data-sar-`. The scheme is per kind, so one setting change is one attribute write on the root element and no host is touched.

| Where                  | Attribute                   | Holds                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Each host              | `data-sar-appid`            | The app ID the host shows.                                                                                                                                             |
| Each host with a kind  | `data-sar-kinds`            | The ids of the kinds that are disclosed and not ignored for the game, in registry order, separated by spaces. Absent when there is none. Rules match one id with `~=`. |
| Hosts that cannot hide | `data-sar-hideable="false"` | Hiding would break the list, so hide dims instead.                                                                                                                     |
| The root element       | `data-sar-filter-<kind>`    | The kind's list filter that takes effect: `off`, `dim` or `hide`.                                                                                                      |
| The root element       | `--sar-kind-color-<kind>`   | The kind's custom color, a validated `#rrggbb`, in the root's `style`. Removed when unset.                                                                             |
| A chip                 | `data-sar-kind`             | The id of the kind it shows. A hover card entry and a banner with one tag carry it too, so the color rules reach them.                                                 |

A host with several kinds takes the strongest filter without a rule for it: a hidden host ignores a dim, and a host that cannot hide dims for either mode. A kind the game is ignored for is left out of `data-sar-kinds` and gets no chip, so it counts as absent.

## Style in this folder

- One module, one reason to change.
- `readonly` by default; discriminated unions with exhaustive `never` checks for states such as `Verdict`; branded types for domain IDs (`AppId`).
- A `Detector` answers with `KindVerdicts`, one `Verdict` per tag kind. Settings and the ignore list are stored per kind (`v2:settings`, `v2:allow`); `settings/migrate.ts` copies the `v1` keys to them the first time either is read; the `v1` keys stay.
- CSS classes and data attributes use the prefix `sar-` and `data-sar-*`; errors are `SarError` with a catalog-key `code`.
- Efficiency is a requirement (rule 13, efficiency): scan only added subtrees, batch DOM reads before writes, no per-node closures or listeners, `WeakSet` and `WeakMap` keyed by elements, bounded caches, no polling.
- Tests sit next to the module as `*.test.ts` and use the builders in `tests/helpers/`.

```

```ts
// @vitest-environment-options {"url":"https://store.steampowered.com/app/3751950/"}
import * as v from "valibot";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import kindItems from "../../tests/fixtures/getitems/kinds.json";
import { APP_PAGES, withDescriptionColumn, withSummaryBox } from "../../tests/helpers/app-page";
import { clearRoot } from "../../tests/helpers/dom";
import { fakeHttp } from "../../tests/helpers/fake-http";
import { fixedClock } from "../../tests/helpers/fixed-clock";
import { fixtureItems, getItemsRequest, getItemsRoute } from "../../tests/helpers/getitems";
import { englishI18n } from "../../tests/helpers/i18n";
import { memoryStore } from "../../tests/helpers/memory-store";
import { withKind, writeSettings } from "../../tests/helpers/settings";
import { loadPage } from "../../tests/helpers/surfaces";
import { type App, start } from "./app";
import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS } from "./settings/settings";
import { createSettingsSource } from "./settings/settings-source";
import { ALLOW_KEY } from "./storage-keys";
import { adoptPageStyles } from "./ui/styles";

// Game 3751950 declares DRM, a third-party
// account and a EULA, and no AI. Its English page can answer none of them: they come from GetItems.

const i18n = englishI18n();
const quiet = { error: vi.fn(), warn: vi.fn(), info: vi.fn(), debug: vi.fn() };
const AllowSchema = v.record(v.string(), v.record(v.string(), v.unknown()));

let app: App | undefined;

afterEach(() => {
  app?.stop();
  app = undefined;
  clearRoot();
});

const banner = () => document.getElementById("sar-banner")?.shadowRoot ?? null;
const headings = () =>
  [...(banner()?.querySelectorAll("h2") ?? [])].map((heading) => heading.textContent);
const chipKinds = () =>
  [...document.querySelectorAll(".sar-tag-section .sar-badge")].map((chip) =>
    chip.getAttribute("data-sar-kind")
  );
const control = (selector: string) => banner()?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(selector);

async function startOnDrmPage() {
  loadPage(withSummaryBox(withDescriptionColumn(APP_PAGES["3751950-drm-account-eula.html"])));
  document.documentElement.lang = "en";
  const store = memoryStore();
  const settings = createSettingsSource(store);
  const http = fakeHttp([getItemsRoute(fixtureItems(kindItems))]);
  app = await start({
    document,
    http,
    store,
    settings,
    clock: fixedClock(0),
    console: quiet,
    addPageStyles: adoptPageStyles,
  });
  await expect.poll(() => headings().length).toBe(3);
  const ignored = async (scope: string) =>
    Object.keys(v.parse(AllowSchema, (await store.get([ALLOW_KEY])).get(ALLOW_KEY))[scope] ?? {});
  return { http, settings, ignored };
}

describe("start on an English app page of a game with no AI", () => {
  it("shows its DRM, account and EULA entries, read from GetItems", async () => {
    const { http } = await startOnDrmPage();

    expect(http.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(getItemsRequest(http.calls[0] ?? "").ids).toEqual([3751950]);
    expect(headings()).toEqual([
      i18n.t("kind_drm_heading"),
      i18n.t("kind_account_heading"),
      i18n.t("kind_eula_heading"),
    ]);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["drm", "account", "eula"]);
  });

  it("ignores one kind from its entry and leaves the others", async () => {
    const { ignored } = await startOnDrmPage();

    control('.sar-banner-action[data-sar-scope="drm"]')?.click();
    await expect.poll(() => control('[data-sar-action="undo"]') !== undefined).toBe(true);
    expect(await ignored("drm")).toEqual(["3751950"]);
    expect(await ignored("all")).toEqual([]);
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_account_heading"), i18n.t("kind_eula_heading")]);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["account", "eula"]);

    control('[data-sar-action="undo"]')?.click();
    await expect.poll(() => headings().length).toBe(3);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["drm", "account", "eula"]);
    expect(await ignored("drm")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("leaves out a kind whose banner entry is switched off", async () => {
    const { settings } = await startOnDrmPage();

    await writeSettings(settings, withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "eula", { banner: false }));
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_drm_heading"), i18n.t("kind_account_heading")]);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["drm", "account", "eula"]);
    await writeSettings(settings, withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "drm", { enabled: false }));
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_account_heading"), i18n.t("kind_eula_heading")]);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["account", "eula"]);
  });

  it("draws only the chips whose badge switch is on", async () => {
    const { settings } = await startOnDrmPage();

    await writeSettings(settings, withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "account", { badge: false }));
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["drm", "eula"]);
    expect(headings()).toHaveLength(3);
    await writeSettings(settings, DEFAULT_SETTINGS);
    expect(chipKinds()).toEqual(["drm", "account", "eula"]);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import mixedStates from "../../tests/fixtures/getitems/mixed-states.json";
import { APP_PAGES } from "../../tests/helpers/app-page";
import { clearRoot } from "../../tests/helpers/dom";

import { memoryStore } from "../../tests/helpers/memory-store";

  app?.stop();
  app = undefined;

  all: v.record(v.string(), v.unknown()),
  ai: v.record(v.string(), v.unknown()),

const banner = () => document.getElementById("sar-banner")?.shadowRoot ?? null;
const control = (selector: string) => banner()?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(selector);

interface StartOptions {

  readonly initial?: ReadonlyMap<string, JsonValue>;
  /** Holds every request until `release` is called. */

async function startOnAiPage(options: StartOptions = {}) {
  const { route = getItemsRoute(fixtureItems(mixedStates)), initial = new Map() } = options;
  loadPage(APP_PAGES["5072580-ai-first.html"]);
  document.documentElement.lang = "en";
  const store = memoryStore(initial);
  const settings = createSettingsSource(store);
  const inner = fakeHttp([route]);
  const requested: string[] = [];
  let release = (): void => undefined;
  const open = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    release = resolve;
  });
  const http: Http = {
    async get(url) {
      requested.push(url);
      if (options.held === true) {
        await open;
      }
      return inner.get(url);
    },
  };
  app = await start({
    document,
    http,
    store,
    settings,
    clock: fixedClock(0),
    console: quiet,
    addPageStyles: adoptPageStyles,
  });
  const stored = async () => v.parse(AllowSchema, (await store.get([ALLOW_KEY])).get(ALLOW_KEY));
  return { http: { calls: requested }, settings, stored, release };
}

describe("start on an English app page", () => {
  it("shows the AI banner from the page at once and does not wait for GetItems", async () => {
    const { http, release } = await startOnAiPage({ held: true });

    await expect.poll(() => http.calls.length).toBe(1);
    expect(getItemsRequest(http.calls[0] ?? "").ids).toEqual([5072580]);
    const column = document.querySelector(".game_description_column");
    expect(column?.firstElementChild?.id).toBe("sar-banner");
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_ai_heading")]);
    expect(banner()?.querySelector("blockquote")?.textContent).not.toBe("");
    expect(banner()?.querySelector(".sar-banner-service")).toBeNull();
    release();
    await expect.poll(() => banner()?.querySelector(".sar-banner-service")?.textContent).toContain(
      i18n.t("badge_card_service_label"),
    );
  });

  it("asks GetItems once for the game and never fetches the page that is open", async () => {
    const { http } = await startOnAiPage({ route: getItemsRoute([]) });
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));

    expect(http.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(http.calls[0]).toContain("GetItems");
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_ai_heading")]);
  });

  it("keeps the AI banner from the page when GetItems cannot answer", async () => {
    await startOnAiPage({ route: [GETITEMS_URL, "network-error"] });
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));

    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_ai_heading")]);
  });

  it("logs a disagreement in debug mode and keeps the disclosure of the page", async () => {
    quiet.debug.mockClear();
    const none = itemAs(mixedStates, 413150, 5072580);
    const initial = new Map<string, JsonValue>([
      [SETTINGS_KEY, encodeSettings({ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, debug: true })],
    ]);
    await startOnAiPage({ route: getItemsRoute([none]), initial });

    await expect.poll(() => quiet.debug.mock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(quiet.debug).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.any(String),
      i18n.t("notice_page_disagrees", {
        kind: "ai",
        app: "5072580",
        page: "disclosed",
        data: "not-disclosed",
      }),
    );
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_ai_heading")]);
  });

  it("ignores the AI kind from its entry and brings it back with Undo", async () => {
    const { stored } = await startOnAiPage();

    control('.sar-banner-action[data-sar-scope="ai"]')?.click();
    await expect.poll(() => control('[data-sar-action="undo"]')?.getAttribute("data-sar-scope"))
      .toBe("ai");
    expect(Object.keys((await stored()).ai)).toEqual(["5072580"]);
    expect(Object.keys((await stored()).all)).toEqual([]);
    expect(banner()?.querySelector("aside")?.getAttribute("data-sar-variant")).toBe("ignored");

    control('[data-sar-action="undo"]')?.click();
    await expect.poll(() => banner()?.querySelector("blockquote") !== null).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.keys((await stored()).ai)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("ignores the game for all tags from the link below the entries", async () => {
    const { stored } = await startOnAiPage();

    control('.sar-banner-foot [data-sar-action="ignore"]')?.click();
    await expect.poll(() => control(".sar-banner-ignored-text")?.textContent).toBe(
      i18n.t("banner_ignored"),
    );
    expect(Object.keys((await stored()).all)).toEqual(["5072580"]);
    expect(Object.keys((await stored()).ai)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("follows the banner setting of the kind", async () => {
    const { settings } = await startOnAiPage();

    await writeSettings(settings, withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { banner: false }));
    expect(document.getElementById("sar-banner")).toBeNull();
    await writeSettings(settings, DEFAULT_SETTINGS);
    expect(headings()).toEqual([i18n.t("kind_ai_heading")]);
  });

  it("follows the switch of the kind", async () => {
    const { settings } = await startOnAiPage();

    await writeSettings(settings, withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { enabled: false }));
    expect(document.getElementById("sar-banner")).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

`src/core/app-page.ts`:

```ts
import type { SteamLanguage } from "./i18n/locale";
import type { IgnoredGames } from "./ignored";
import type { KindId } from "./kinds/id";
import { effectiveSettings } from "./kinds/kind-settings";
import { KINDS, perKind } from "./kinds/registry";
import {
  isKindVerdicts,
  type KindVerdict,
  type KindVerdicts,
  UNKNOWN_KINDS,
} from "./kinds/verdicts";
import type { Logger } from "./log";
import type { Detector, MessageCatalog } from "./ports";
import { perScope } from "./settings/allow-data";
import type { AllowList } from "./settings/allow-list";
import type { Settings } from "./settings/settings";
import type { AppId } from "./types";
import { type AppPageView, createAppPageUi } from "./ui/app-page";
import type { CardTriggers } from "./ui/hover-card";

/** The store app page name element, the fallback when the verdict carries no name. */
const APP_NAME_SELECTOR = "#appHubAppName";

/** The detectors the app page asks: the cached stack, and GetItems alone for a translation. */
export interface PageDetectors {
  readonly getItems: Detector;
  readonly detector: Detector;
}

/** Called when the open page and Steam's data give different answers for one kind. */
export type Disagree = (kind: KindId, page: KindVerdict, data: KindVerdict) => void;

/**
 * One kind from the page and from Steam's data. A kind the page cannot say, or Steam could not
 * answer, takes the other. When both know, a disclosure wins over none, and a disagreement is
 * reported. The data wins when it discloses, and the page when only the page does.
 */
function mergeKind(
  kind: KindId,
  page: KindVerdict,
  data: KindVerdict,
  disagree: Disagree,
): KindVerdict {
  if (page.state === "unknown" && page.reason === "missing") {
    return data;
  }
  if (data.state === "disclosed") {
    if (page.state !== "disclosed") {
      disagree(kind, page, data);
    }
    return data;
  }
  if (data.state === "unknown") {
    return page;
  }
  if (page.state === "disclosed") {
    disagree(kind, page, data);
    return page;
  }
  return data;
}

/**
 * The verdicts of an English page read from its own document, merged with Steam's data for the
 * game. Only a kind that can be read from the page (`fromAppPage`) takes the page into account.
 */
export function mergeVerdicts(
  page: KindVerdicts,
  data: KindVerdicts,
  disagree: Disagree,
): KindVerdicts {
  const merged: Partial<Record<KindId, KindVerdict>> = {};
  for (const kind of KINDS) {
    merged[kind.id] = kind.fromAppPage === undefined
      ? data[kind.id]
      : mergeKind(kind.id, page[kind.id], data[kind.id], disagree);
  }
  return isKindVerdicts(merged) ? merged : data;
}

/**
 * Whether the AI kind holds a disclosure from the API in another language than the page's. The
 * developer's notes are the only text that comes in a language.
 */
function needsTranslation(verdicts: KindVerdicts, language: SteamLanguage): boolean {
  const { ai } = verdicts;
  return ai.state === "disclosed" && ai.source === "api" && ai.language !== language;
}

/**
 * The verdicts of a page in another language than English: Steam's data, with the AI notes asked
 * for again when the cached ones are in a different language than the page's.
 */
export async function translatedVerdicts(
  id: AppId,
  language: SteamLanguage,
  detected: KindVerdicts,
  getItems: Detector,
): Promise<KindVerdicts> {
  if (!needsTranslation(detected, language)) {
    return detected;
  }
  const fresh = (await getItems.detect([id])).get(id)?.ai;
  return fresh?.state === "disclosed" ? { ...detected, ai: fresh } : detected;
}

function appName(doc: Document, verdicts: KindVerdicts, id: AppId): string {
  const { ai } = verdicts;
  const fromVerdict = ai.state === "disclosed" ? ai.name : undefined;
  const fromPage = doc.querySelector(APP_NAME_SELECTOR)?.textContent.trim();
  return fromVerdict ?? (fromPage === undefined || fromPage === "" ? String(id) : fromPage);
}

/** What the app page needs from the running app. */
export interface AppPageDeps {
  readonly language: SteamLanguage;
  readonly detectors: PageDetectors;
  /** The verdicts of the open page read from its document, when it is English. */
  readonly live: KindVerdicts | undefined;
  /** The games the user ignored, kept current by the banner's buttons. */
  readonly ignored: IgnoredGames;
  readonly allowList: AllowList;
  readonly settings: () => Settings;
  /** Called after the banner ignores or restores the game, so the capsules draw again. */
  readonly onAllowChange: (id: AppId) => void;
  readonly card: CardTriggers;
  readonly logger: Pick<Logger, "debug" | "error">;
}

/** A running app page. */
export interface AppPage {
  /** Draws again from the known verdicts and the current settings. */
  render(): void;
  /** Stops a lookup that has not finished from drawing. */
  stop(): void;
}

/**
 * Draws the game's own page: the banner with an entry per disclosed kind and the tag section.
 * An English page draws at once from its own document; Steam's data for the game, which arrives
 * later and from the cache when it can, fills in the other kinds and draws again.
 */
export function startAppPage(
  doc: Document,
  id: AppId,
  i18n: MessageCatalog,
  deps: AppPageDeps,
): AppPage {
  const { detectors, live, logger } = deps;
  let known: KindVerdicts = live ?? UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing;
  let stopped = false;

  function view(): AppPageView {
    const { kinds } = deps.settings();
    return {
      verdicts: known,
      ignored: perScope((scope) => deps.ignored[scope].has(id)),
      badge: perKind((kind) => effectiveSettings(kinds[kind.id]).badge),
      banner: perKind((kind) => effectiveSettings(kinds[kind.id]).banner),
    };
  }

  const ui = createAppPageUi(doc, i18n, {
    async ignore(scope) {
      await deps.allowList.add(scope, id, appName(doc, known, id));
      deps.ignored[scope].add(id);
      deps.onAllowChange(id);
      render();
    },
    async restore(scope) {
      await deps.allowList.remove(scope, id);
      deps.ignored[scope].delete(id);
      deps.onAllowChange(id);
      render();
    },
  }, { card: deps.card });

  function render(): void {
    ui.render(view());
  }

  function disagree(kind: KindId, page: KindVerdict, data: KindVerdict): void {
    logger.debug("notice_page_disagrees", {
      kind,
      app: String(id),
      page: page.state,
      data: data.state,
    });
  }

  async function settle(): Promise<void> {
    const detected = (await detectors.detector.detect([id])).get(id) ?? UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing;
    const next = live === undefined
      ? await translatedVerdicts(id, deps.language, detected, detectors.getItems)
      : mergeVerdicts(live, detected, disagree);
    if (!stopped) {
      known = next;
      render();
    }
  }

  render();
  settle().catch((problem: unknown) => {
    logger.error(problem);
  });
  return {
    render,
    stop() {
      stopped = true;
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { appId } from "../../tests/helpers/app-ids";
import { APP_PAGES } from "../../tests/helpers/app-page";
import { fakeDetector } from "../../tests/helpers/fake-detector";
import { capturedVerdicts } from "../../tests/helpers/fixture-verdicts";
import { aiVerdicts, disclosedVerdict, NOT_DISCLOSED } from "../../tests/helpers/verdicts";
import { mergeVerdicts, translatedVerdicts } from "./app-page";
import { parseAppPage } from "./detect/app-page";
import { KINDS } from "./kinds/registry";
import { UNKNOWN_KINDS } from "./kinds/verdicts";
import { UNKNOWN } from "./types";

const ID = appId(5072580);
const PAGE_URL = "https://store.steampowered.com/app/5072580/?l=english";

/** What the open English page says about itself: only the AI kind can be read from it. */
function pageOf(name: "5072580-ai-first.html" | "413150-no-block.html") {
  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(APP_PAGES[name], "text/html");
  return parseAppPage(doc, PAGE_URL);
}

const none = () => undefined;

describe("mergeVerdicts", () => {
  it("takes every kind from Steam's data when both disclose", () => {
    const data = capturedVerdicts(1808500);
    const disagree = vi.fn();
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(pageOf("5072580-ai-first.html"), data, disagree);
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      expect(merged[kind.id]).toBe(data[kind.id]);
    }
    expect(merged.ai).toBe(data.ai);
    expect(disagree).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("prefers a disclosure from Steam's data, which also names the AI service", () => {
    const named = aiVerdicts(disclosedVerdict({ service: "Midjourney" }));
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(pageOf("5072580-ai-first.html"), named, none);
    expect(merged.ai).toMatchObject({ source: "api", service: "Midjourney" });
  });

  it("keeps the page's disclosure when Steam's data has none, and reports the disagreement", () => {
    const disagree = vi.fn();
    const page = pageOf("5072580-ai-first.html");
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(page, aiVerdicts(NOT_DISCLOSED), disagree);
    expect(merged.ai).toBe(page.ai);
    expect(disagree).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ai", page.ai, NOT_DISCLOSED);
  });

  it("keeps Steam's disclosure when the page shows none, and reports the disagreement", () => {
    const disagree = vi.fn();
    const data = aiVerdicts(disclosedVerdict());
    const page = pageOf("413150-no-block.html");
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(page, data, disagree);
    expect(merged.ai).toBe(data.ai);
    expect(disagree).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(disagree).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ai", page.ai, data.ai);
  });

  it("keeps Steam's disclosure when the page hid the store, and reports it", () => {
    const disagree = vi.fn();
    const data = aiVerdicts(disclosedVerdict());
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(UNKNOWN_KINDS.gated, data, disagree);
    expect(merged.ai).toBe(data.ai);
    expect(disagree).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ai", UNKNOWN.gated, data.ai);
  });

  it("uses Steam's answer when the page's is unknown, without a report", () => {
    const disagree = vi.fn();
    const data = aiVerdicts(disclosedVerdict());
    expect(mergeVerdicts(UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing, data, disagree).ai).toBe(data.ai);
    expect(disagree).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("keeps the page's answer when Steam's data could not answer", () => {
    const page = pageOf("5072580-ai-first.html");
    expect(mergeVerdicts(page, UNKNOWN_KINDS.error, none).ai).toBe(page.ai);
    const quiet = pageOf("413150-no-block.html");
    expect(mergeVerdicts(quiet, UNKNOWN_KINDS["rate-limited"], none).ai).toBe(quiet.ai);
  });

  it("settles a page that shows none and data that has none as not disclosed", () => {
    const data = aiVerdicts(NOT_DISCLOSED);
    expect(mergeVerdicts(pageOf("413150-no-block.html"), data, none).ai).toBe(NOT_DISCLOSED);
  });

  it("never lets the page speak for a kind that cannot be read from it", () => {
    const data = capturedVerdicts(813230);
    const page = { ...UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing, kernel: capturedVerdicts(1808500).kernel };
    expect(mergeVerdicts(page, data, none).kernel).toBe(data.kernel);
  });

  it("holds a verdict for every kind", () => {
    const merged = mergeVerdicts(UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing, UNKNOWN_KINDS.error, none);
    expect(Object.keys(merged)).toStrictEqual(KINDS.map((kind) => kind.id));
  });
});

describe("translatedVerdicts", () => {
  it("takes Steam's data as it is when the AI notes are in the page's language", async () => {
    const detected = aiVerdicts(disclosedVerdict({ language: "german" }));
    const getItems = fakeDetector(() => UNKNOWN_KINDS.error);
    expect(await translatedVerdicts(ID, "german", detected, getItems)).toBe(detected);
    expect(getItems.calls).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("asks GetItems again when the stored AI notes are in another language", async () => {
    const stored = capturedVerdicts(1808500);
    const fresh = disclosedVerdict({ language: "german", notes: "Deutsche Hinweise." });
    const getItems = fakeDetector(() => aiVerdicts(fresh));

    const verdicts = await translatedVerdicts(ID, "german", stored, getItems);

    expect(verdicts.ai).toBe(fresh);
    expect(verdicts.kernel).toBe(stored.kernel);
    expect(getItems.calls).toEqual([[ID]]);
  });

  it("keeps the stored verdicts when the second answer is no disclosure", async () => {
    const stored = capturedVerdicts(1808500);
    const getItems = fakeDetector(() => UNKNOWN_KINDS.error);
    expect(await translatedVerdicts(ID, "german", stored, getItems)).toBe(stored);
  });
});
```
