`src/core/kinds/verdicts.ts`:

```ts
import type { ExtraDetails, StoreItem } from "../detect/getitems.schema";
import type { SteamLanguage } from "../i18n/locale";
import { type DisclosedBase, UNKNOWN, type UnknownReason, type Verdict } from "../types";
import type { KindId } from "./id";
import type { KindDefinition, TagKind } from "./kind";
import { holdsEveryKind, KINDS, perKind } from "./registry";

type DisclosedOf<Kind> = Kind extends KindDefinition<infer Disclosed> ? Disclosed : never;

/** The disclosed verdict of any registered kind. */
export type AnyDisclosed = DisclosedOf<TagKind>;

/** A verdict of any registered kind, for code that does not know which kind it holds. */
export type KindVerdict = Verdict<AnyDisclosed>;

/**
 * What core knows about one app: a verdict for every registered kind, in the shape of that kind.
 * A verdict has the three states of rule 4. A missing answer is unknown, never not disclosed.
 */
export type KindVerdicts = {
  readonly [Id in KindId]: Verdict<Extract<AnyDisclosed, DisclosedBase<Id>>>;
};

function sitsUnderItsKind(id: KindId, verdict: KindVerdict): boolean {
  return verdict.state !== "disclosed" || verdict.kind === id;
}

/**
 * Whether the verdicts hold an answer for every registered kind. A disclosed verdict must sit in
 * the slot of its own kind.
 */
export function isKindVerdicts(
  verdicts: Partial<Record<KindId, KindVerdict>>,
): verdicts is KindVerdicts {
  return holdsEveryKind(verdicts, sitsUnderItsKind);
}

/** Whether two lists hold the very same verdict objects in the same order. */
export function sameVerdicts(a: readonly AnyDisclosed[], b: readonly AnyDisclosed[]): boolean {
  return a.length === b.length && a.every((verdict, index) => verdict === b[index]);
}

function allUnknown(reason: UnknownReason): KindVerdicts {
  return perKind(() => UNKNOWN[reason]);
}

/** One shared object per unknown reason, so an app nobody could settle costs no allocation. */
export const UNKNOWN_KINDS: Readonly<Record<UnknownReason, KindVerdicts>> = {
  "gated": allUnknown("gated"),
  "missing": allUnknown("missing"),
  "malformed": allUnknown("malformed"),
  "error": allUnknown("error"),
  "rate-limited": allUnknown("rate-limited"),
};

/** Every kind's verdict for a GetItems item with `extra_details`. */
export function kindsFromGetItems(
  item: StoreItem,
  details: ExtraDetails,
  language: SteamLanguage,
): KindVerdicts {
  const verdicts: Partial<Record<KindId, KindVerdict>> = {};
  for (const kind of KINDS) {
    verdicts[kind.id] = kind.fromGetItems(item, details, language);
  }
  return isKindVerdicts(verdicts) ? verdicts : UNKNOWN_KINDS.error;
}

```

`src/core/log.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { englishI18n } from "../../tests/helpers/i18n";
import { SarError } from "./errors";
import { createLogger } from "./log";

const i18n = englishI18n();

function setup(debug = false) {
  const sink = { error: vi.fn(), warn: vi.fn(), info: vi.fn(), debug: vi.fn() };
  const logger = createLogger(i18n, sink, debug);
  return { sink, logger };
}

describe("SarError", () => {
  it("carries a catalog key and params, not prose", () => {
    const cause = new TypeError();
    const error = new SarError("error_unexpected", {}, { cause });
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
    expect(error.name).toBe("SarError");
    expect(error.code).toBe("error_unexpected");
    expect(error.message).toBe("error_unexpected");
    expect(error.params).toStrictEqual({});
    expect(error.cause).toBe(cause);
  });
});

describe("createLogger", () => {
  it("logs a SarError as catalog text with the [sar] prefix", () => {
    const { sink, logger } = setup();
    const error = new SarError("error_unexpected", {});
    logger.error(error);
    expect(sink.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith("[sar]", i18n.t("error_unexpected"), error);
  });

  it("logs any other value under error_unexpected", () => {
    const { sink, logger } = setup();
    logger.error(42);
    expect(sink.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith("[sar]", i18n.t("error_unexpected"), 42);
  });

  it("writes warnings and info by key", () => {
    const { sink, logger } = setup();
    logger.warn("ext_short_name", {});
    logger.info("ext_name", {});
    expect(sink.warn).toHaveBeenCalledWith("[sar]", i18n.t("ext_short_name"));
    expect(sink.info).toHaveBeenCalledWith("[sar]", i18n.t("ext_name"));
  });

  it("writes debug lines only when debug logging is on", () => {
    const quiet = setup(false);
    quiet.logger.debug("ext_name", {});
    expect(quiet.sink.debug).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    const verbose = setup(true);
    verbose.logger.debug("ext_name", {});
    expect(verbose.sink.debug).toHaveBeenCalledWith("[sar]", i18n.t("ext_name"));
  });
});
```

`src/core/log.ts`:

```ts
import { SarError } from "./errors";
import type { MessageKey, MessageParams } from "./i18n/keys.gen";
import type { I18n } from "./i18n/t";

/** The part of `console` the logger writes to. */
export interface ConsoleSink {
  error(...data: readonly unknown[]): void;
  warn(...data: readonly unknown[]): void;
  info(...data: readonly unknown[]): void;
  debug(...data: readonly unknown[]): void;
}

/** Logs catalog messages by key (rule 9), each line prefixed with `[sar]`. */
export interface Logger {
  /** A `SarError` logs its own message; anything else logs `error_unexpected` and the value. */
  error(problem: unknown): void;
  warn<K extends MessageKey>(code: K, params: MessageParams[K]): void;
  info<K extends MessageKey>(code: K, params: MessageParams[K]): void;
  /** Written only when debug logging is on (`settings.debug`). */
  debug<K extends MessageKey>(code: K, params: MessageParams[K]): void;
}

const LOG_PREFIX = "[sar]";

export function createLogger(i18n: I18n, sink: ConsoleSink, debug: boolean): Logger {
  return {
    error(problem) {
      if (problem instanceof SarError) {
        sink.error(LOG_PREFIX, i18n.t(problem.code, problem.params), problem);
      } else {
        sink.error(LOG_PREFIX, i18n.t("error_unexpected"), problem);
      }
    },
    warn(code, params) {
      sink.warn(LOG_PREFIX, i18n.t(code, params));
    },
    info(code, params) {
      sink.info(LOG_PREFIX, i18n.t(code, params));
    },
    debug(code, params) {
      if (debug) {
        sink.debug(LOG_PREFIX, i18n.t(code, params));
      }
    },
  };
}

```

`src/core/ports.ts`:

```ts
import type { JsonValue } from "./json";
import type { KindVerdicts } from "./kinds/verdicts";
import type { AppId } from "./types";

// The capabilities core receives from a composition root (see src/core/AGENTS.md, "Ports"). Each
// port is one capability. Every implementation passes the suite in tests/contracts/.

/** The message catalog port: typed lookup of catalog text by key. */
export type { I18n as MessageCatalog } from "./i18n/t";
export type { Logger } from "./log";

/** Stops a subscription. Calling it again does nothing. */
export type Unsubscribe = () => void;

/** A readable HTTP answer, whatever its status. The body is read in full. */
export interface HttpResponse {
  readonly kind: "response";
  readonly status: number;
  /** The final URL after redirects; the HTML fallback checks it for gates. */
  readonly url: string;
  /** Response headers by lower-case name, as far as CORS exposes them. */
  readonly headers: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
  readonly body: string;
}

/**
 * No readable answer: a network failure, or an error answer without CORS headers, which `fetch`
 * reports as a `TypeError` with no status (rq6, S1). `cause` is the rejection, for debug logs.
 */
export interface HttpFailure {
  readonly kind: "failed";
  readonly cause: unknown;
}

/** The request was not sent, because a breaker is open (the throttle decorator holds it back). */
export interface HttpWithheld {
  readonly kind: "withheld";
}

export type HttpResult = HttpResponse | HttpFailure | HttpWithheld;

/**
 * GET requests to the two Valve hosts (rule 1), always without credentials. Never rejects: every
 * outcome is an `HttpResult`. Decorators such as a throttle wrap an `Http` and are one themselves.
 */
export interface Http {
  get(url: string): Promise<HttpResult>;
}

/**
 * Batched key-value storage (`storage.local`, `GM.*`, memory). Reads are `unknown` until a schema
 * validates them. Values are copied in and out, so later mutation of either side has no effect.
 */
export interface KeyValueStore {
  /** The stored values of the keys that exist; absent keys are absent from the map. */
  get(keys: readonly string[]): Promise<ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>>;
  /** Writes every entry, replacing existing values. */
  set(entries: ReadonlyMap<string, JsonValue>): Promise<void>;
  /** Removes the keys; keys that do not exist are ignored. */
  remove(keys: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  /** Every stored key, in no particular order. */
  keys(): Promise<readonly string[]>;
}

/** Wall-clock time. Timers use the web-standard `setTimeout`, which tests fake. */
export interface Clock {
  /** Milliseconds since the Unix epoch. */
  now(): number;
}

/** The stored settings value and its changes, unvalidated; core's settings module validates it. */
export interface SettingsSource {
  /** The stored settings value, or undefined when none is stored. */
  read(): Promise<unknown>;
  /**
   * Calls `listener` with the new stored value when the settings change in any tab. Where the
   * platform cannot observe changes, it never calls it, and settings apply on the next page load.
   */
  subscribe(listener: (value: unknown) => void): Unsubscribe;
}

/**
 * One source of verdicts: GetItems, the HTML fallback, or a chain or decorator of them. Its
 * contract (tests/contracts/detector.contract.ts): it never rejects, and the result holds exactly
 * one `KindVerdicts` per distinct requested ID, with `unknown` for anything it could not settle.
 */
export interface Detector {
  detect(ids: readonly AppId[]): Promise<ReadonlyMap<AppId, KindVerdicts>>;
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { appIdFromDataAttribute, appIdFromHref } from "./appid";

const STORE = "https://store.steampowered.com/search/?term=roguelike";
const COMMUNITY = "https://steamcommunity.com/id/someone/wishlist/";

describe("appIdFromDataAttribute", () => {
  it("reads a single numeric ID", () => {
    expect(appIdFromDataAttribute("5072580")).toBe(5072580);
    expect(appIdFromDataAttribute(" 413150 ")).toBe(413150);
  });

  it("skips comma lists, which belong to packages and bundles", () => {
    expect(appIdFromDataAttribute("1245620,2778580")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("skips values that are not app IDs", () => {
    for (const value of ["", "abc", "12abc", "-5", "1.5", "0", "4294967296"]) {
      expect(appIdFromDataAttribute(value)).toBeUndefined();
    }
  });
});

describe("appIdFromHref", () => {
  it("reads relative and absolute store links, with or without a trailing slash", () => {
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500/", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("https://store.steampowered.com/app/1808500", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("https://store.steampowered.com/app/1808500/", COMMUNITY)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("//store.steampowered.com/app/1808500", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
  });

  it("allows a slug, a query and a hash after the ID", () => {
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500/ARC_Raiders/?snr=1_7_7_151_150_1", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500?curator_clanid=1", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500/#app_reviews_hash", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500#app_reviews_hash", STORE)).toBe(1808500);
  });

  it("ignores steamcommunity.com and other hosts", () => {
    expect(appIdFromHref("https://steamcommunity.com/app/1808500", STORE)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(appIdFromHref("/app/1808500", COMMUNITY)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(appIdFromHref("https://example.com/app/1808500", STORE)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("ignores store paths that are not an app page", () => {
    for (
      const href of [
        "/agecheck/app/1808500/",
        "/apps/1808500",
        "/app/",
        "/app/12abc",
        "/app/0",
        "/sub/12345/",
        "/bundle/232/",
        "javascript:void(0)",
        "",
      ]
    ) {
      expect(appIdFromHref(href, STORE)).toBeUndefined();
    }
  });
});
```

`src/core/scan/appid.ts`:

```ts
import { type AppId, toAppId } from "../types";

const STORE_HOST = "store.steampowered.com";
const DIGITS = /^\d+$/;
/** `/app/<id>`, then a slash or the end: slugs, queries and hashes pass, `/app/12abc` does not. */
const APP_PATH = /^\/app\/(\d+)(?:\/|$)/;

/**
 * The app ID in a `data-ds-appid` value. Only a single numeric ID counts: a comma list belongs to
 * a package or bundle capsule and names no single app.
 */
export function appIdFromDataAttribute(value: string): AppId | undefined {
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  return DIGITS.test(trimmed) ? toAppId(Number(trimmed)) : undefined;
}

/**
 * The app ID an `href` links to, when it resolves to a store app page. Relative links resolve
 * against `base` (the document's base URL). Other hosts, steamcommunity.com included, and store
 * paths such as `/agecheck/app/<id>` name no app.
 */
export function appIdFromHref(href: string, base: string): AppId | undefined {
  const url = URL.parse(href, base);
  if (url === null || url.hostname !== STORE_HOST) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const digits = APP_PATH.exec(url.pathname)?.[1];
  return digits === undefined ? undefined : toAppId(Number(digits));
}
```

`src/core/scan/candidates.ts`:

```ts
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import { appIdFromDataAttribute, appIdFromHref } from "./appid";
import { SAR_NODE } from "./marks";

// Elements that name an app (rq6, S5): classic surfaces put a `data-ds-appid` on the capsule
// itself; React surfaces carry only `/app/<id>` links.

const DATA_APPID = "data-ds-appid";

/** Capsules that say their app ID in a `data-ds-appid`. A comma list is a package or bundle. */
export const DATA_CANDIDATE = `[${DATA_APPID}]`;
/** Links that may lead to an app page; `appIdFromHref` decides. */
export const LINK_CANDIDATE = "a[href*='/app/']";
/** Links to store items that are not apps: packages, bundles and events. They name `several`. */
const OTHER_ITEM_LINK = "a[href*='/sub/'], a[href*='/bundle/'], a[href*='/news/']";
const OTHER_ITEM_PATH = /\/(?:sub|bundle|news)\//;
export const ANY_CANDIDATE = `${DATA_CANDIDATE}, ${LINK_CANDIDATE}, ${OTHER_ITEM_LINK}`;

/**
 * Regions whose app links are never capsules: the classic and React footers, the app page
 * breadcrumbs, and our own nodes. The global header root is not here: it holds the search
 * suggestions, and its navigation links carry no image, so the host rule drops them.
 */
export const SKIPPED = `#footer, [data-featuretarget='footer'], .breadcrumbs, ${SAR_NODE}`;

/** What an element names: one app ID, `several` (a comma list or another item), or nothing. */
export type Naming = AppId | "several" | undefined;

/**
 * The app an element names. A `data-ds-appid` wins over the element's own `href`; a comma list
 * names several apps; a link names its app when it leads to a store app page. A link to a package,
 * bundle or event names `several`, so a capsule never grows to take in such a tile.
 */
export function namingOf(element: Element, base: string): Naming {
  const data = element.getAttribute(DATA_APPID);
  if (data !== null) {
    const id = appIdFromDataAttribute(data);
    if (id !== undefined) {
      return id;
    }
    if (data.includes(",")) {
      return "several";
    }
  }
  if (element.localName !== "a") {
    return undefined;
  }
  const href = element.getAttribute("href");
  if (href === null) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return appIdFromHref(href, base) ?? (OTHER_ITEM_PATH.test(href) ? "several" : undefined);
}

/** Whether `root` or an element inside it still names `appId`. */
export function namesApp(root: Element, appId: AppId, base: string): boolean {
  if (namingOf(root, base) === appId) {
    return true;
  }
  for (const element of root.querySelectorAll(ANY_CANDIDATE)) {
    if (namingOf(element, base) === appId) {
      return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * The single app every naming element in `root` (`root` included) names, `several` when they
 * disagree, or undefined when none names an app. Stops at the first disagreement.
 */
export function uniformNaming(root: Element, base: string): Naming {
  let found = namingOf(root, base);
  if (found === "several") {
    return found;
  }
  for (const element of root.querySelectorAll(ANY_CANDIDATE)) {
    const naming = namingOf(element, base);
    if (naming === undefined) {
      continue;
    }
    if (naming === "several" || (found !== undefined && naming !== found)) {
      return "several";
    }
    found = naming;
  }
  return found;
}

```

`src/core/scan/hosts.ts`:

```ts
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import { DATA_CANDIDATE, type Naming, uniformNaming } from "./candidates";
import { firstImage } from "./image";

// The host rule rq6 (S5) chose on the tag hub: the lowest image-bearing ancestor that names one
// app, then a short climb that joins image and title blocks that are siblings.

/** How far above a link its capsule image may sit (the link itself is level 0). */
export const MAX_IMAGE_LEVELS = 8;
/** How many more levels a host may climb while everything inside still names its app. */
export const MAX_JOIN_LEVELS = 3;

/** Finds capsule hosts during one scan. Its memos live as long as the scan; never keep one. */
export interface HostFinder {
  /** The capsule host for a candidate that names `appId`, or undefined when it has none. */
  hostOf(candidate: Element, appId: AppId): Element | undefined;
}

/**
 * A host finder for one scan of `document`. A `data-ds-appid` element is its own host: Steam puts
 * the attribute on the capsule. A link's host is found by the rule above, and never climbs to
 * `body`; a link with no image-bearing ancestor (text links, navigation) has none.
 */
export function createHostFinder(document: Document): HostFinder {
  const base = document.baseURI;
  const images = new Map<Element, boolean>();
  const namings = new Map<Element, Naming>();

  function hasImage(element: Element): boolean {
    let known = images.get(element);
    if (known === undefined) {
      known = firstImage(element) !== undefined;
      images.set(element, known);
    }
    return known;
  }

  function naming(element: Element): Naming {
    if (namings.has(element)) {
      return namings.get(element);
    }
    const value = uniformNaming(element, base);
    namings.set(element, value);
    return value;
  }

  /** The parent, unless it is `body` or the root, which are never hosts. */
  function parentOf(element: Element): Element | undefined {
    const parent = element.parentElement;
    return parent === null || parent === document.body || parent === document.documentElement
      ? undefined
      : parent;
  }

  return {
    hostOf(candidate, appId) {
      if (candidate.matches(DATA_CANDIDATE)) {
        return candidate;
      }
      let host: Element | undefined = candidate;
      for (let level = 0; !hasImage(host); level++) {
        host = level < MAX_IMAGE_LEVELS ? parentOf(host) : undefined;
        if (host === undefined) {
          return undefined;
        }
      }
      if (naming(host) !== appId) {
        return undefined;
      }
      for (let level = 0; level < MAX_JOIN_LEVELS; level++) {
        const parent = parentOf(host);
        if (parent === undefined || naming(parent) !== appId) {
          break;
        }
        host = parent;
      }
      return host;
    },
  };
}
```

`src/core/scan/image.ts`:

```ts
import { isInSarNode } from "./marks";

/**
 * What counts as a capsule image (rq6, S5): an `img`, or an element with an inline
 * `background-image`, which is all the home page's main carousel capsule has. Steam's lazy
 * backgrounds carry `data-background-image-url` before the style is set; they count too, because
 * setting the style later is an attribute change the observer does not see.
 *
 * React store capsules mount their image box empty and add the `img` inside the app link later.
 * That added subtree holds no link, so the box itself counts as the image.
 */
export const IMAGE = [
  "img",
  "[style*='background-image']",
  "[data-background-image-url]",
  ".CapsuleImageCtn",
  ".HeroCapsuleImageContainer",
].join(", ");

/** The first capsule image in `root` (`root` included), skipping anything inside our own nodes. */
export function firstImage(root: Element): Element | undefined {
  if (root.matches(IMAGE)) {
    return root;
  }
  for (const image of root.querySelectorAll(IMAGE)) {
    if (!isInSarNode(image)) {
      return image;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * The box a capsule image sits in: the image element itself when it paints a background, else
 * the `img`'s parent. This is where a compact badge is overlaid.
 */
export function imageBox(image: Element): Element | undefined {
  return image.localName === "img" ? (image.parentElement ?? undefined) : image;
}
```

`src/core/scan/marks.ts`:

```ts
// What core writes on store nodes and how it recognizes its own nodes (docs/design/components.mdx,
// "DOM ownership and state"). The scanner, the renderers and the stylesheet share these names.

/** Every element core injects carries a class starting with `sar-`; the scanner skips them. */
export const SAR_NODE = "[class^='sar-'], [class*=' sar-']";

/** On each host: the app ID it shows. */
export const HOST_APPID = "data-sar-appid";
/**
 * On each host once its verdicts are known: the kinds it carries, as kind ids separated by spaces
 * in registry order. A kind that is not disclosed, unknown or ignored for the game is absent. The
 * list filter and the layout rules match one id with `~=`.
 */
export const HOST_KINDS = "data-sar-kinds";
/** On hosts whose placement must not be hidden (`"false"`); the list filter dims them instead. */
export const HOST_HIDEABLE = "data-sar-hideable";

/** Whether the element is one of ours: a badge, a banner host or anything else core injected. */
export function isSarNode(element: Element): boolean {
  return element.matches(SAR_NODE);
}

/** Whether the element is one of ours or sits inside one. */
export function isInSarNode(element: Element): boolean {
  return element.closest(SAR_NODE) !== null;
}
```

`src/core/scan/placements.ts`:

```ts
import { LINK_CANDIDATE } from "./candidates";
import { firstImage, imageBox } from "./image";

// Where a host's badge goes, per store surface (rq6, S5; docs/design/components.mdx, sections 1,
// 2 and 5). A new surface is a new entry here, never a scanner edit (rule 11).

/** Chips a row with room for words shows beside its title. */
const ROW_CHIPS = 3;
/** Chips a capsule overlay shows: the image is narrow and the store's own flags sit on it. */
const OVERLAY_CHIPS = 2;
/** Chips a search suggestion shows: its row is the smallest. */
const SUGGESTION_CHIPS = 2;

/** Finds the element a badge attaches to inside a host, or undefined when it does not fit. */
export type AnchorRule = (host: Element) => Element | undefined;

interface PlacementBase {
  /** A stable name for tests and debug logs. */
  readonly id: string;
  /** A selector the host must match (`Element.matches`, so descendant combinators work). */
  readonly host: string;
  /**
   * False where hiding the host would break the list (virtualized or carousel lists); the list
   * filter dims those hosts instead, through `data-sar-hideable="false"`.
   */
  readonly hideable: boolean;
  /**
   * How many kind chips the surface shows before one "+N" chip stands for the rest. A constant to
   * tune by the room the surface leaves.
   */
  readonly maxChips: number;
  /** Reads only: it runs in the scan's read phase. */
  readonly anchor: AnchorRule;
}

/** A compact badge overlaid on the capsule image; the anchor is the image's box. */
export interface OverlayPlacement extends PlacementBase {
  readonly badge: "compact";
  readonly slot: "overlay";
}

/**
 * A full badge in a row with room for words. `after` makes it the anchor's next sibling. `end`
 * makes it the anchor's last child, after its text.
 */
export interface RowPlacement extends PlacementBase {
  readonly badge: "full";
  readonly slot: "after" | "end";
}

export type Placement = OverlayPlacement | RowPlacement;

/** The box of the host's first capsule image. */
export const capsuleImage: AnchorRule = (host) => {
  const image = firstImage(host);
  return image === undefined ? undefined : imageBox(image);
};

/** The first element in the host matching `selector`. */
export function inside(selector: string): AnchorRule {
  return (host) => host.querySelector(selector) ?? undefined;
}

function hasText(element: Element): boolean {
  return element.textContent.trim() !== "";
}

/** The host's first element without child elements that shows text: a row's title line. */
export const firstTextLeaf: AnchorRule = (host) => {
  for (const element of host.querySelectorAll("*")) {
    if (element.childElementCount === 0 && hasText(element)) {
      return element;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
};

/** The host's first app link without an image, even before its text arrives. */
const imagelessLink: AnchorRule = (host) => {
  for (const link of host.querySelectorAll(LINK_CANDIDATE)) {
    if (firstImage(link) === undefined) {
      return link;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
};

/**
 * The wishlist row's title link, only when the host is a wishlist row (its drag ID says so). A row
 * mounts with empty links and fills them later, so the title link may still be empty here.
 */
const wishlistTitle: AnchorRule = (host) =>
  host.querySelector("[data-rfd-draggable-id^='WishlistItem-']") === null
    ? undefined
    : imagelessLink(host);

/** The default: a compact badge over the capsule image of any host. */
export const GENERIC: OverlayPlacement = {
  id: "generic",
  host: "*",
  hideable: true,
  maxChips: OVERLAY_CHIPS,
  badge: "compact",
  slot: "overlay",
  anchor: capsuleImage,
};

/** Every placement, most specific first; the first whose host and anchor match wins. */
export const PLACEMENTS: readonly Placement[] = [
  {
    // Classic search rows: right after the title. The title line clips its overflow, so CSS
    // turns it into a flex row where the title shrinks and the badge stays whole.
    id: "search-row",
    host: "a.search_result_row",
    hideable: true,
    maxChips: ROW_CHIPS,
    badge: "full",
    slot: "after",
    anchor: inside(".search_name .title"),
  },
  {
    // The virtualized React wishlist mounts and unmounts rows, so hiding would make it jump.
    id: "wishlist-row",
    host: "[data-index]",
    hideable: false,
    maxChips: ROW_CHIPS,
    badge: "full",
    slot: "after",
    anchor: wishlistTitle,
  },
  {
    // Search suggestions inside the header root: images too small for a compact badge.
    id: "search-suggestion",
    host: "[id^='searchSuggestions'] *",
    hideable: true,
    maxChips: SUGGESTION_CHIPS,
    badge: "full",
    slot: "after",
    anchor: firstTextLeaf,
  },
  {
    // DLC rows on an app page; most have no image. The row spreads its children apart. The
    // badge goes inside the name, so it follows the text.
    id: "dlc-row",
    host: "a.game_area_dlc_row",
    hideable: true,
    maxChips: ROW_CHIPS,
    badge: "full",
    slot: "end",
    anchor: inside(".game_area_dlc_name"),
  },
  {
    // The home page's main carousel: the image is a CSS background on a child.
    id: "home-main-carousel",
    host: "a.store_main_capsule",
    hideable: false,
    maxChips: OVERLAY_CHIPS,
    badge: "compact",
    slot: "overlay",
    anchor: capsuleImage,
  },
  {
    // The discovery queue preview: one overlay link names the first queued app over a stack of
    // capsule images. The badge goes on that first capsule, and hiding would remove the queue.
    id: "queue-preview",
    host: ".discovery_queue_content_ctn",
    hideable: false,
    maxChips: OVERLAY_CHIPS,
    badge: "compact",
    slot: "overlay",
    anchor: inside(".dq_item"),
  },
  {
    // The large carousel capsule on React sale pages (tag, category and specials hubs).
    id: "hub-carousel",
    host: ".LibraryAssetExpandedDisplay, .LibraryAssetExpandedDisplay *",
    hideable: false,
    maxChips: OVERLAY_CHIPS,
    badge: "compact",
    slot: "overlay",
    anchor: capsuleImage,
  },
  GENERIC,
];

/** A host's placement and the element its badge attaches to. */
export interface Placed {
  readonly placement: Placement;
  readonly anchor: Element;
}

/** The first placement that fits the host, or undefined when none does. Reads only. */
export function placeHost(host: Element, placements: readonly Placement[]): Placed | undefined {
  for (const placement of placements) {
    if (host.matches(placement.host)) {
      const anchor = placement.anchor(host);
      if (anchor !== undefined) {
        return { placement, anchor };
      }
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}
```

`src/core/scan/renderer.ts`:

```ts
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import type { Placement } from "./placements";

// The seam between the scanner and the UI. The scanner finds and marks hosts; whatever implements
// `CapsuleRenderer` (the app's verdict and badge code) decides what they show. Neither imports
// the other's internals.

/** A capsule host the scanner marked, with what its placement found during the read phase. */
export interface CapsuleHost {
  /** The host element; it carries `data-sar-appid`. */
  readonly element: Element;
  readonly appId: AppId;
  readonly placement: Placement;
  /** The element the badge attaches to, as `placement.slot` says. */
  readonly anchor: Element;
}

/** What one scan found. Both lists may be empty; a scan with nothing to report is not sent. */
export interface ScanBatch {
  /** Hosts marked for the first time. */
  readonly found: readonly CapsuleHost[];
  /**
   * Known hosts that received new content: a re-render may have dropped their badge, or the
   * anchor may be a new element. `anchor` is read again for them.
   */
  readonly changed: readonly CapsuleHost[];
}

/**
 * Receives the scanner's batches. `render` runs in the scan's animation frame after the scanner's
 * own writes, so it must not read layout synchronously; it schedules its own read and write
 * phases. It must be idempotent per host: a host whose badge is in place stays unchanged, and any
 * badge it inserts sits inside the host and carries a `sar-` class.
 */
export interface CapsuleRenderer {
  render(batch: ScanBatch): void;
}
```

`src/core/scan/scanner.test.ts`:

```ts
// @vitest-environment-options {"url":"https://store.steampowered.com/search/?term=roguelike"}
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { countDomWork, type DomWork } from "../../../tests/helpers/dom-work";
import {
  type RecordingRenderer,
  recordingRenderer,
} from "../../../tests/helpers/recording-renderer";
import { loadPage, nodes, setBody, SURFACES, the } from "../../../tests/helpers/surfaces";
import { HOST_APPID, HOST_HIDEABLE, HOST_KINDS } from "./marks";
import type { CapsuleHost } from "./renderer";
import { createScanner, DEBOUNCE_MS, type Scanner, type ScanReport } from "./scanner";

const SEARCH_URL = "https://store.steampowered.com/search/?term=roguelike";
/** One animation frame under fake timers. */
const FRAME_MS = 16;

let renderer: RecordingRenderer;
let reports: ScanReport[];
let scanner: Scanner;

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.useFakeTimers({
    toFake: ["setTimeout", "clearTimeout", "requestAnimationFrame", "cancelAnimationFrame"],
  });
  history.replaceState(null, "", SEARCH_URL);
});

afterEach(() => {
  scanner.stop();
  vi.useRealTimers();
});

/** Starts a scanner on the current page and lets its first page scan run. */
async function startScanner(options: { readonly badges?: boolean; } = {}): Promise<void> {
  renderer = recordingRenderer(options);
  reports = [];
  scanner = createScanner({ document, renderer, onReport: (report) => reports.push(report) });
  scanner.start();
  await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(FRAME_MS);
}

/** Lets a debounced scan run after the last mutation. */
async function settle(): Promise<void> {
  await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DEBOUNCE_MS + FRAME_MS);
}

function found(): readonly CapsuleHost[] {
  return renderer.batches.flatMap((batch) => batch.found);
}

/** Each found host as `[appId, placement id]`, in order. */
function mapping(): (readonly [number, string])[] {
  return found().map((host) => [host.appId, host.placement.id] as const);
}

function hostElements(): readonly Element[] {
  return found().map((host) => host.element);
}

describe("per-surface hosts", () => {
  it("search: each result row, badge right after the title", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.search);
    await startScanner();
    const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll("a.search_result_row")];
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(8);
    expect(hostElements()).toStrictEqual(rows);
    expect(mapping()).toStrictEqual(
      [4075620, 3934270, 3784030, 1045010, 3432110, 3664320, 4461450, 2624160].map(
        (id) => [id, "search-row"] as const,
      ),
    );
    for (const host of found()) {
      expect(host.anchor).toBe(the(".search_name .title", host.element));
    }
  });

  it("home: main carousel with a CSS background, discount capsules and tab rows", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.home);
    await startScanner();
    expect(mapping()).toStrictEqual([
      [4356430, "home-main-carousel"],
      [1867240, "home-main-carousel"],
      [466560, "generic"],
      [1121640, "generic"],
      [1091500, "generic"],
      [1174180, "generic"],
    ]);
    expect(hostElements()).toStrictEqual([
      ...document.querySelectorAll("a.store_main_capsule"),

/** A search row like the captured ones, for app `id`. */
function searchRow(id: number): HTMLElement {
  const row = document.createElement("a");
  row.className = "search_result_row";
  row.href = `https://store.steampowered.com/app/${String(id)}/Game/`;
  row.dataset["dsAppid"] = String(id);
  row.append(
    ...nodes(
      `<div class="search_capsule"><img></div><div class="search_name">`
        + `<span class="title"></span></div><div class="search_platforms"></div>`,
    ),
  );
  return row;
}

/** A bfcache page transition; happy-dom's `PageTransitionEvent` is a plain `Event`. */
function pageTransition(type: "pagehide" | "pageshow"): Event {
  return Object.assign(new Event(type), { persisted: true });
}

describe("observing", () => {
  it("scans 50 appended search rows once, touching only the new rows", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.search);
    await startScanner();
    const container = the("#search_resultsRows");
    const added: HTMLElement[] = [];
    for (let burst = 0; burst < 5; burst++) {
      for (let n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        const row = searchRow(1_000_000 + burst * 10 + n);
        added.push(row);
        container.append(row);
      }
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DEBOUNCE_MS / 4);
    }
    expect(renderer.batches).toHaveLength(1);
    await settle();
    expect(renderer.batches).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(renderer.batches[1]?.found.map((host) => host.element)).toStrictEqual(added);
    expect(renderer.batches[1]?.changed).toStrictEqual([]);
    expect(reports[1]).toStrictEqual({
      kind: "added",
      roots: 50,
      candidates: 50,
      found: 50,
      changed: 0,
    });
  });

  it("scans within the maximum wait while the page keeps changing", async () => {
    setBody("<main></main>");
    await startScanner();
    const main = the("main");
    for (let n = 0; n < 12; n++) {
      main.append(searchRow(100 + n));
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DEBOUNCE_MS / 2);
    }
    expect(reports.filter((report) => report.kind === "added").length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    await settle();
    expect(found()).toHaveLength(12);
  });

  it("ignores mutations made only of our own nodes", async () => {

  });

    expect(host.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(0);
    await settle();
    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.found).toStrictEqual([]);
    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.changed.map((changed) => changed.element)).toStrictEqual([
      host,
    ]);
    expect(host.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(the(".sar-badge", host).parentElement).toBe(the(".CapsuleImageCtn", host));
  });

  it("resets a host reused for another app and finds the new app's host", async () => {
    setBody(
      `<main><div class="other"><a href="/app/99/"><img></a></div>`
        + `<div class="slot"><div class="slide"><a href="/app/10/"><img></a>`
        + `<a href="/app/10/">Ten</a></div></div></main>`,
    );
    await startScanner({ badges: true });
    const slot = the(".slot");
    expect(slot.getAttribute(HOST_APPID)).toBe("10");
    the(".slide", slot).replaceWith(
      ...nodes(
        `<div class="slide"><a href="/app/20/"><img></a><a href="/app/20/">Twenty</a></div>`,
      ),
    );
    await settle();
    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.changed).toStrictEqual([]);
    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.found.map((host) => [host.element, host.appId])).toStrictEqual([
      [slot, 20],
    ]);
    expect(slot.getAttribute(HOST_APPID)).toBe("20");
    expect(slot.querySelectorAll(`[${HOST_APPID}]`)).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(slot.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("finds a capsule whose image arrives inside its link after the scan", async () => {

    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.found.map((host) => host.element)).toStrictEqual([
      the(".card"),
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps the badge in place when the store adds a hover popup inside the host", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES["tag-hub"]);

    const box = the(".CapsuleImageCtn", host);
    expect(box.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);

    );
    the(".ImpressionTrackedElement", host).prepend(...popup);

    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.changed.map((changed) => changed.anchor)).toStrictEqual([box]);
    expect(box.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(the(".popup", host).querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(0);
    the(".popup", host).remove();

    expect(box.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);

  it("gives a carousel clone its own host and removes the copied badge", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.home);
    await startScanner({ badges: true });
    const original = the("a.sale_capsule");

    if (!(clone instanceof Element)) {
      throw new TypeError();
    }
    expect(clone.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);

    await settle();
    expect(renderer.batches.at(-1)?.found.map((host) => host.element)).toStrictEqual([clone]);
    expect(original.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);

  it("cleans marks and badges left by a previous instance", async () => {

    row.setAttribute(HOST_KINDS, "ai");
    row.append(...nodes(`<span class="sar-badge"></span><span class="sar-badge"></span>`));
    await startScanner({ badges: true });
    expect(hostElements()).toContain(row);
    expect(row.hasAttribute(HOST_KINDS)).toBe(false);
    expect(row.querySelectorAll(".sar-badge")).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("disconnects on pagehide and rescans the page on a bfcache pageshow", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.search);
    await startScanner();

    const row = searchRow(42);

    expect(reports).toHaveLength(1);
    globalThis.dispatchEvent(pageTransition("pageshow"));
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(FRAME_MS);

  });
});

describe("work budget", () => {
  // Scan cost as counted DOM calls, which do not depend on the machine running the tests. Each
  // limit is per scanned capsule, a little above what the scanner does today, so a change that
  // makes the scan superlinear or re-reads old content fails here. The real time budget (under
  // 4 ms per mutation batch) is the manual sale-page profile in the checklist.

  const LIMITED = [
    "querySelectorAll",
    "queried",
    "querySelector",
    "closest",
    "matches",
    "parentSteps",
  ] as const;
  type Limits = Readonly<Record<(typeof LIMITED)[number], number>>;

  /** Per capsule on a page scan; measured 7, 6, 0, 3, 10 and 46. */
  const PAGE_LIMITS: Limits = {
    querySelectorAll: 8,
    queried: 8,
    querySelector: 1,
    closest: 4,
    matches: 12,
    parentSteps: 60,
  };

  /**
   * Per appended row; measured 4, 0, 1, 2, 5 and 20. `queried` stays under one per new row, so
   * the scan never lists the rows that were already there.
   */
  const ADDED_LIMITS: Limits = {
    querySelectorAll: 5,
    queried: 1,
    querySelector: 1,
    closest: 3,
    matches: 6,
    parentSteps: 30,
  };

  function expectWithin(work: DomWork, limits: Limits, count: number): void {
    for (const name of LIMITED) {
      expect.soft(work[name], name).toBeLessThanOrEqual(limits[name] * count);
    }
  }

  /** A React sale grid of `count` tag hub capsules, each for its own app. */
  function capsuleGrid(count: number): Element {
    const page = new DOMParser().parseFromString(SURFACES["tag-hub"], "text/html");
    const capsule = the(".capsule_index_0", page).parentElement;
    if (capsule === null) {
      throw new TypeError();
    }
    const grid = document.createElement("div");
    grid.className = "SaleSectionContainer";
    for (let n = 0; n < count; n++) {
      const copy = capsule.cloneNode(true);
      if (copy instanceof Element) {
        for (const link of copy.querySelectorAll("a")) {
          link.setAttribute("href", `https://store.steampowered.com/app/${String(500_000 + n)}/X`);
        }
        grid.append(copy);
      }
    }
    return grid;
  }

  it("scans a 200-capsule page with bounded DOM work, in one frame", async () => {
    document.body.replaceChildren(capsuleGrid(200));
    const work = countDomWork();
    await startScanner();
    expect(found()).toHaveLength(200);
    expect(renderer.batches).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(reports).toHaveLength(1);
    const done = work();
    expectWithin(done, PAGE_LIMITS, 200);
    expect(done.setAttribute).toBe(200);
    expect(done.removeAttribute).toBe(0);
  });

  it("scans 50 appended search rows with bounded DOM work", async () => {
    loadPage(SURFACES.search);
    await startScanner();
    const container = the("#search_resultsRows");
    const rows = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, n) => searchRow(2_000_000 + n));
    const work = countDomWork();
    for (const row of rows) {
      container.append(row);
    }
    await settle();
    expect(found()).toHaveLength(58);
    expect(renderer.batches).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(reports).toHaveLength(2);
    const done = work();
    expectWithin(done, ADDED_LIMITS, 50);
    expect(done.setAttribute).toBe(50);
    expect(done.removeAttribute).toBe(0);
  });
});

```

`src/core/scan/scanner.ts`:

```ts
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import { appIdFromHref } from "./appid";
import {
  ANY_CANDIDATE,
  DATA_CANDIDATE,
  LINK_CANDIDATE,
  namesApp,
  namingOf,
  SKIPPED,
} from "./candidates";
import { createHostFinder } from "./hosts";
import { HOST_APPID, HOST_HIDEABLE, HOST_KINDS, isInSarNode, isSarNode, SAR_NODE } from "./marks";
import { placeHost, type Placement, PLACEMENTS } from "./placements";
import type { CapsuleHost, CapsuleRenderer } from "./renderer";

/** Quiet time after the last mutation before a scan. */
export const DEBOUNCE_MS = 200;
/** The longest a mutation waits for its scan while the page keeps changing. */
export const MAX_WAIT_MS = 1000;

/** What one scan did; for debug logs and tests. */
export interface ScanReport {
  /** `page`: the whole body (start, bfcache restore). `added`: only added subtrees. */
  readonly kind: "page" | "added";
  /** Subtrees scanned. */
  readonly roots: number;
  /** Distinct elements that named an app and were checked for a host. */
  readonly candidates: number;
  readonly found: number;
  readonly changed: number;
}

export interface ScannerOptions {
  readonly document: Document;
  readonly renderer: CapsuleRenderer;
  /** Defaults to `PLACEMENTS`. */
  readonly placements?: readonly Placement[];
  readonly onReport?: (report: ScanReport) => void;
}

export interface Scanner {
  /** Scans the page in the next animation frame, then scans added subtrees as they come. */
  start(): void;
  /** Disconnects the observer and drops pending work. `start` may be called again. */
  stop(): void;
}

interface HostRecord {
  readonly appId: AppId;
  readonly placement: Placement;
  /** The element the badge attaches to, kept while it stays in the host. */
  readonly anchor: Element;
}

/** What the read phase decided; the write phase only applies it. */
interface ScanPlan {
  readonly found: CapsuleHost[];
  readonly changed: CapsuleHost[];
  /** Marked elements to reset: clones, old instance hosts, hosts reused for another app. */
  readonly stale: Element[];
  readonly report: ScanReport;
}

/**
 * Finds capsule hosts (rq6, S5) and hands them to the renderer. One `MutationObserver` on `body`
 * collects added subtrees, debounced by `DEBOUNCE_MS` up to `MAX_WAIT_MS`; each scan reads the DOM
 * first and writes after, in one animation frame. Hosts are remembered in a `WeakMap`, so a
 * rescan finds nothing new. The observer disconnects on `pagehide` and resumes on a bfcache
 * `pageshow`.
 */
export function createScanner(options: ScannerOptions): Scanner {
  const { document, renderer, onReport } = options;
  const placements = options.placements ?? PLACEMENTS;
  const view = document.defaultView;
  const hosts = new WeakMap<Element, HostRecord>();
  const observer = new MutationObserver(onMutations);
  let pending = new Set<Element>();
  let pageScanDue = false;
  let debounceTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  let maxWaitTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  let frame: number | undefined;

  function onMutations(records: readonly MutationRecord[]): void {
    let added = false;
    for (const record of records) {
      for (const node of record.addedNodes) {
        if (node instanceof Element && !isSarNode(node)) {
          pending.add(node);
          added = true;
        }
      }
    }
    if (added) {
      clearTimeout(debounceTimer);
      debounceTimer = setTimeout(requestFrame, DEBOUNCE_MS);
      maxWaitTimer ??= setTimeout(requestFrame, MAX_WAIT_MS);
    }
  }

  function clearTimers(): void {
    clearTimeout(debounceTimer);
    clearTimeout(maxWaitTimer);
    debounceTimer = undefined;
    maxWaitTimer = undefined;
  }

  function requestFrame(): void {
    clearTimers();
    frame ??= requestAnimationFrame(runScan);
  }

  function runScan(): void {
    frame = undefined;
    clearTimers();
    const kind = pageScanDue ? "page" : "added";
    const roots = pageScanDue ? [document.body] : liveRoots(pending);
    pageScanDue = false;
    pending = new Set();
    if (roots.length === 0) {
      return;
    }
    const plan = read(kind, roots);
    write(plan);
    onReport?.(plan.report);
  }

  /** The known host that is `element` or encloses it, for `appId` or for any app. */
  function knownHostAround(
    element: Element,
    appId?: AppId,
    replaced: ReadonlySet<Element> = new Set(),
  ): Element | undefined {
    for (let node: Element | null = element; node !== null; node = node.parentElement) {
      const record = hosts.get(node);
      if (
        record !== undefined && !replaced.has(node)
        && (appId === undefined || record.appId === appId)
      ) {
        return node;
      }
    }
    return undefined;
  }

  /** Whether `host` holds a known host of the same app, which then stays the host. */
  function holdsKnownHost(host: Element, appId: AppId, replaced: ReadonlySet<Element>): boolean {
    for (const marked of host.querySelectorAll(`[${HOST_APPID}='${String(appId)}']`)) {
      if (hosts.get(marked)?.appId === appId && !replaced.has(marked)) {
        return true;
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  function read(kind: ScanReport["kind"], roots: readonly Element[]): ScanPlan {
    const base = document.baseURI;
    const pageAppId = appIdFromHref(document.URL, document.URL);
    const finder = createHostFinder(document);
    const candidates = new Set<Element>();
    const changedHosts = new Set<Element>();
    const stale: Element[] = [];
    for (const root of roots) {
      // A root added inside an app link (an image that arrives late) makes that link a candidate.
      const around = root.closest(ANY_CANDIDATE);
      if (around !== null) {
        candidates.add(around);
      }
    }
    for (const selector of [DATA_CANDIDATE, LINK_CANDIDATE]) {
      for (const root of roots) {
        for (const element of root.querySelectorAll(selector)) {
          candidates.add(element);
        }
      }
    }
    for (const root of roots) {
      const known = kind === "added" ? knownHostAround(root) : undefined;
      if (known !== undefined) {
        changedHosts.add(known);
      }
      if (root.hasAttribute(HOST_APPID) && !hosts.has(root)) {
        stale.push(root);
      }
      for (const marked of root.querySelectorAll(`[${HOST_APPID}]`)) {
        if (!hosts.has(marked)) {
          stale.push(marked);
        }
      }
    }
    // A host that no longer names its app was reused for other content, as carousel slides are.
    const replaced = new Set<Element>();
    for (const element of changedHosts) {
      const record = hosts.get(element);
      if (record !== undefined && !namesApp(element, record.appId, base)) {
        replaced.add(element);
        stale.push(element);
      }
    }
    for (const element of replaced) {
      changedHosts.delete(element);
    }

    const fresh = new Map<Element, AppId>();
    let checked = 0;
    for (const candidate of candidates) {
      const appId = namingOf(candidate, base);
      if (typeof appId !== "number" || appId === pageAppId || candidate.closest(SKIPPED) !== null) {
        continue;
      }
      checked++;
      const host = finder.hostOf(candidate, appId);
      if (host === undefined || fresh.has(host)) {
        continue;
      }
      const known = knownHostAround(host, appId, replaced);
      if (known !== undefined) {
        if (kind === "added") {
          changedHosts.add(known);
        }
        continue;
      }
      fresh.set(host, appId);
    }

    const found: CapsuleHost[] = [];
    for (const [element, appId] of fresh) {
      if (enclosedByFresh(element, appId, fresh) || holdsKnownHost(element, appId, replaced)) {
        continue;
      }
      const placed = placeHost(element, placements);
      if (placed !== undefined) {
        found.push({ element, appId, placement: placed.placement, anchor: placed.anchor });
      }
    }
    const changed: CapsuleHost[] = [];
    for (const element of changedHosts) {
      const record = hosts.get(element);
      if (record === undefined) {
        continue;
      }
      // Keep the anchor while it is still in the host: a store popup added inside the host must
      // not pull the badge into itself. Look it up again only when a re-render replaced it.
      const kept = record.anchor.isConnected && element.contains(record.anchor);
      const anchor = kept ? record.anchor : record.placement.anchor(element);
      if (anchor !== undefined) {
        changed.push({ element, appId: record.appId, placement: record.placement, anchor });
      }
    }
    const report: ScanReport = {
      kind,
      roots: roots.length,
      candidates: checked,
      found: found.length,
      changed: changed.length,
    };
    return { found, changed, stale, report };
  }

  function write(plan: ScanPlan): void {
    for (const element of plan.stale) {
      hosts.delete(element);
      element.removeAttribute(HOST_APPID);
      element.removeAttribute(HOST_KINDS);
      element.removeAttribute(HOST_HIDEABLE);
      for (const copy of element.querySelectorAll(SAR_NODE)) {
        copy.remove();
      }
    }
    for (const host of plan.found) {
      host.element.setAttribute(HOST_APPID, String(host.appId));
      if (!host.placement.hideable) {
        host.element.setAttribute(HOST_HIDEABLE, "false");
      }
      hosts.set(host.element, {
        appId: host.appId,
        placement: host.placement,
        anchor: host.anchor,
      });
    }
    for (const host of plan.changed) {
      hosts.set(host.element, {
        appId: host.appId,
        placement: host.placement,
        anchor: host.anchor,
      });
    }
    if (plan.found.length > 0 || plan.changed.length > 0) {
      renderer.render({ found: plan.found, changed: plan.changed });
    }
  }

  function connect(): void {
    observer.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    pageScanDue = true;
    requestFrame();
  }

  function disconnect(): void {
    observer.disconnect();
    clearTimers();
    if (frame !== undefined) {
      cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
      frame = undefined;
    }
    pending = new Set();
    pageScanDue = false;
  }

  function onPageShow(event: PageTransitionEvent): void {
    if (event.persisted) {
      connect();
    }
  }

  return {
    start() {
      disconnect();
      connect();
      view?.addEventListener("pagehide", disconnect);
      view?.addEventListener("pageshow", onPageShow);
    },
    stop() {
      disconnect();
      view?.removeEventListener("pagehide", disconnect);
      view?.removeEventListener("pageshow", onPageShow);
    },
  };
}

/** The pending roots still in the page and outside our own nodes. */
function liveRoots(pending: ReadonlySet<Element>): Element[] {
  const roots: Element[] = [];
  for (const root of pending) {
    if (root.isConnected && !isInSarNode(root)) {
      roots.push(root);
    }
  }
  return roots;
}

/** Whether a fresh host of the same app encloses `element`: the outer one is the host. */
function enclosedByFresh(
  element: Element,
  appId: AppId,
  fresh: ReadonlyMap<Element, AppId>,
): boolean {
  for (let node = element.parentElement; node !== null; node = node.parentElement) {
    if (fresh.get(node) === appId) {
      return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

```

`src/core/serial.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { createSerial } from "./serial";

/** A promise the test settles by hand. */
function gate() {
  let open = (): void => undefined;
  const opened = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    open = resolve;
  });
  return { opened, open };
}

describe("createSerial", () => {
  it("starts a task only when the one before it has settled", async () => {
    const serial = createSerial();
    const log: string[] = [];
    const first = gate();
    const one = serial(async () => {
      log.push("one starts");
      await first.opened;
      log.push("one ends");
    });
    const two = serial(() => {
      log.push("two starts");
      return Promise.resolve();
    });
    await Promise.resolve();
    expect(log).toEqual(["one starts"]);
    first.open();
    await Promise.all([one, two]);
    expect(log).toEqual(["one starts", "one ends", "two starts"]);
  });

  it("hands each task's result to its own caller", async () => {
    const serial = createSerial();
    expect(await Promise.all([serial(() => Promise.resolve(1)), serial(() => Promise.resolve(2))]))
      .toEqual([1, 2]);
  });

  it("rejects the failed task and still runs the next one", async () => {
    const serial = createSerial();
    const failed = serial(() => Promise.reject(new Error()));
    const next = serial(() => Promise.resolve("ran"));
    await expect(failed).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(Error);
    expect(await next).toBe("ran");
  });
});

```

`src/core/serial.ts`:

```ts
/** Runs the tasks it is given one after another. A task that fails does not stop the next. */
export type Serial = <T>(task: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>;

/** A queue of one: each task starts when the one before it has settled. */
export function createSerial(): Serial {
  let tail: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
  return (task) => {
    const result = tail.then(task);
    tail = result.catch(() => undefined);
    return result;
  };
}
```

`src/core/settings/allow-data.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { appId } from "../../../tests/helpers/app-ids";
import { KIND_IDS } from "../kinds/id";
import {
  ALLOW_ALL,
  ALLOW_SCOPES,
  decodeAllow,
  decodeAllowScope,
  encodeAllow,
  perScope,
  toAllowScope,
} from "./allow-data";

const T = 1_000_000_000_000;
const ENTRY = { name: "Game", added: T };

describe("perScope", () => {
  it("makes one result for the scope for all kinds and one for each kind", () => {
    const seen: string[] = [];
    const result = perScope((scope) => {
      seen.push(scope);
      return scope.length;
    });
    expect(seen).toStrictEqual([ALLOW_ALL, ...KIND_IDS]);
    expect(Object.keys(result).toSorted()).toStrictEqual([ALLOW_ALL, ...KIND_IDS].toSorted());
  });
});

describe("toAllowScope", () => {
  it("lists the scope for all kinds first, then each kind in registry order", () => {
    expect(ALLOW_SCOPES).toStrictEqual([ALLOW_ALL, ...KIND_IDS]);
  });

  it.each([ALLOW_ALL, ...KIND_IDS])("reads %s as a scope", (scope) => {
    expect(toAllowScope(scope)).toBe(scope);
  });

  it.each([null, "", "kinds", "all ", "__proto__"])("reads %j as no scope", (value) => {
    expect(toAllowScope(value)).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("decodeAllowScope", () => {
  it("reads an object from app ID to name and date", () => {
    expect(decodeAllowScope({ "10": ENTRY })).toStrictEqual(new Map([[appId(10), ENTRY]]));
  });

  it("reads anything else as no games", () => {
    for (const stored of [undefined, null, "x", 3, true]) {
      expect(decodeAllowScope(stored)).toStrictEqual(new Map());
    }
  });
});

describe("decodeAllow and encodeAllow", () => {
  it("round trip the games of every scope", () => {
    const entries = decodeAllow({ all: { "20": ENTRY }, ai: { "10": ENTRY } });
    expect(entries.all.get(appId(20))).toStrictEqual(ENTRY);
    expect(entries.ai.get(appId(10))).toStrictEqual(ENTRY);
    expect(decodeAllow(encodeAllow(entries))).toStrictEqual(entries);
  });

  it("read the games of the scope of any kind, and nothing for a kind not stored", () => {
    const entries = decodeAllow({ drm: { "30": ENTRY } });
    expect(entries.drm.get(appId(30))).toStrictEqual(ENTRY);
    for (const id of KIND_IDS) {
      expect(entries[id].size).toBe(id === "drm" ? 1 : 0);
    }
    expect(entries.all.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it("encode every scope, empty ones too", () => {
    expect(encodeAllow(decodeAllow(undefined))).toStrictEqual(
      Object.fromEntries([ALLOW_ALL, ...KIND_IDS].map((scope) => [scope, {}])),
    );
  });

  it("do not take a v1 list, which kept the games at the top level, for a scope", () => {
    const entries = decodeAllow({ "10": ENTRY });
    expect(entries.ai.size + entries.all.size).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

`src/core/settings/allow-data.ts`:

```ts
import * as v from "valibot";
import type { JsonValue } from "../json";
import type { KindId } from "../kinds/id";
import { KINDS, perKind } from "../kinds/registry";
import { type AppId, toAppId } from "../types";

/** One ignored game: its store name at the time and when the user ignored it. */
export interface AllowEntry {
  readonly name: string;
  /** Milliseconds since the Unix epoch. */
  readonly added: number;
}

/** The scope that ignores a game for every kind. */
export const ALLOW_ALL = "all";

/** Where an ignore applies: one tag kind, or every kind. */
export type AllowScope = typeof ALLOW_ALL | KindId;

/** Every scope, in the order a list shows them: all kinds, then each kind in registry order. */
export const ALLOW_SCOPES: readonly AllowScope[] = [ALLOW_ALL, ...KINDS.map((kind) => kind.id)];

/** The scope a stored or attribute value names, or undefined when it is none. */
export function toAllowScope(value: string | null): AllowScope | undefined {
  return ALLOW_SCOPES.find((scope) => scope === value);
}

/** The ignored games of each scope, keyed by app ID. */
export type AllowEntries = Readonly<Record<AllowScope, ReadonlyMap<AppId, AllowEntry>>>;

/** One `make(scope)` result for every scope. */
export function perScope<T>(make: (scope: AllowScope) => T): Readonly<Record<AllowScope, T>> {
  return { [ALLOW_ALL]: make(ALLOW_ALL), ...perKind((kind) => make(kind.id)) };
}

const EntrySchema = v.pipe(
  v.object({ name: v.string(), added: v.pipe(v.number(), v.finite()) }),
  v.readonly(),
);

const RecordSchema = v.record(v.string(), v.unknown());

/**
 * The entries of one scope's stored value, an object from app ID to name and date. Anything but an
 * object yields nothing, and an entry that is invalid, or whose key is not an app ID, is dropped
 * on its own.
 */
export function decodeAllowScope(stored: unknown): ReadonlyMap<AppId, AllowEntry> {
  const entries = new Map<AppId, AllowEntry>();
  const record = v.safeParse(RecordSchema, stored);
  if (!record.success) {
    return entries;
  }
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(record.output)) {
    const id = /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(key) ? toAppId(Number(key)) : undefined;
    const entry = v.safeParse(EntrySchema, value);
    if (id !== undefined && entry.success) {
      entries.set(id, entry.output);
    }
  }
  return entries;
}

/** The ignored games in a stored value, scope by scope; a scope it lacks has none. */
export function decodeAllow(stored: unknown): AllowEntries {
  const record = v.safeParse(RecordSchema, stored);
  const scopes = record.success ? record.output : {};
  return perScope((scope) => decodeAllowScope(scopes[scope]));
}

function encodeScope(entries: ReadonlyMap<AppId, AllowEntry>): JsonValue {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    [...entries].map(([id, entry]) => [String(id), { name: entry.name, added: entry.added }]),
  );
}

/** The stored value of the ignored games: one object per scope. */
export function encodeAllow(entries: AllowEntries): JsonValue {
  return perScope((scope) => encodeScope(entries[scope]));
}

```

`src/core/settings/allow-list.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { appId } from "../../../tests/helpers/app-ids";
import { countingStore } from "../../../tests/helpers/counting-store";
import { fixedClock } from "../../../tests/helpers/fixed-clock";
import { memoryStore } from "../../../tests/helpers/memory-store";
import type { JsonValue } from "../json";
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import { type AllowEntry, type AllowScope, perScope } from "./allow-data";
import { createAllowList } from "./allow-list";

const T = 1_000_000_000_000;
/** The stored ignore list with no game in any scope. */
const NO_GAMES = perScope(() => ({}));
/** The ignored games of every scope, none. */
const NO_ENTRIES = perScope(() => new Map());

function setup(initial: ReadonlyMap<string, JsonValue> = new Map()) {
  const store = countingStore(memoryStore(initial));
  const clock = fixedClock(T);
  return { store, clock, allow: createAllowList(store, clock) };
}

/** The ignored games of one scope. */
async function scoped(
  allow: ReturnType<typeof setup>["allow"],
  scope: AllowScope,
): Promise<ReadonlyMap<AppId, AllowEntry>> {
  return (await allow.list())[scope];
}

describe("two quick changes", () => {
  it("both apply when two games stop being ignored at once", async () => {
    const { allow } = setup();
    await allow.add("drm", appId(1), "One");
    await allow.add("drm", appId(2), "Two");
    await allow.add("drm", appId(3), "Three");
    await Promise.all([allow.remove("drm", appId(1)), allow.remove("drm", appId(2))]);
    expect([...(await scoped(allow, "drm")).keys()]).toEqual([3]);
  });

  it("keep every game added at once, in two scopes", async () => {
    const { allow } = setup();
    await Promise.all([
      allow.add("drm", appId(1), "One"),
      allow.add("eula", appId(1), "One"),
      allow.add("all", appId(2), "Two"),
    ]);
    const listed = await allow.list();
    expect([listed.drm.size, listed.eula.size, listed.all.size]).toEqual([1, 1, 1]);
  });

  it("run the next change after one that failed", async () => {
    const { allow, store } = setup();
    store.break();
    const failed = allow.add("drm", appId(1), "One");
    await expect(failed).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(Error);
    store.heal();
    await allow.add("drm", appId(2), "Two");
    expect([...(await scoped(allow, "drm")).keys()]).toEqual([2]);
  });
});

describe("createAllowList", () => {
  it("starts empty in every scope", async () => {
    expect(await setup().allow.list()).toStrictEqual(NO_ENTRIES);
  });

  it("adds a game with its name and the time it was added", async () => {
    const { allow, clock } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "Counter-Strike");
    clock.advance(5_000);
    await allow.add("ai", appId(20), "Team Fortress");
    expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(
      new Map([
        [10, { name: "Counter-Strike", added: T }],
        [20, { name: "Team Fortress", added: T + 5_000 }],
      ]),
    );
  });

  it("keeps a game's ignore apart in each scope", async () => {
    const { allow } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "A");
    await allow.add("all", appId(20), "B");
    expect([...(await scoped(allow, "ai")).keys()]).toStrictEqual([10]);
    expect([...(await scoped(allow, "all")).keys()]).toStrictEqual([20]);
    await allow.remove("all", appId(10));
    expect((await scoped(allow, "ai")).has(appId(10))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("stores one object per scope, each from app ID to name and date", async () => {
    const { allow, store } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "Counter-Strike");
    expect(await store.get(["v2:allow"])).toStrictEqual(
      new Map([["v2:allow", { ...NO_GAMES, ai: { "10": { name: "Counter-Strike", added: T } } }]]),
    );
  });

  it("replaces the entry of a game that is added again", async () => {
    const { allow, clock } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "Old name");
    clock.advance(1_000);
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "New name");
    expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(
      new Map([[10, { name: "New name", added: T + 1_000 }]]),
    );
  });

  it("removes a game and keeps the others", async () => {
    const { allow } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "A");
    await allow.add("ai", appId(20), "B");
    await allow.remove("ai", appId(10));
    expect([...(await scoped(allow, "ai")).keys()]).toStrictEqual([20]);
    await allow.remove("ai", appId(20));
    expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(new Map());
  });

  it("ignores removing a game that is not listed, without writing", async () => {
    const { allow, store } = setup();
    await allow.remove("ai", appId(10));
    expect(store.calls.set).toBe(0);
  });

  it("is shared by every list over the same store", async () => {
    const { allow, store, clock } = setup();
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "A");
    expect((await scoped(createAllowList(store, clock), "ai")).has(appId(10))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("reads only the v2 key once the list is stored, and writes once per change", async () => {
    const { allow, store } = setup(
      new Map<string, JsonValue>([
        ["v2:allow", { all: {}, ai: {} }],
        ["v1:allow", { "10": { name: "Old", added: T } }],
      ]),
    );
    await allow.add("ai", appId(10), "A");
    expect(store.gets).toStrictEqual([["v2:allow"]]);
    expect(store.calls.set).toBe(1);
    await allow.list();
    expect(store.gets).toStrictEqual([["v2:allow"], ["v2:allow"]]);
  });

  it("reads the v1 key only when the v2 key is absent", async () => {
    const { allow, store } = setup();
    await allow.list();
    expect(store.gets).toStrictEqual([["v2:allow"], ["v1:allow"]]);
  });

  describe("a v1 list", () => {
    const V1 = {
      "10": { name: "Counter-Strike", added: T },
      "20": { name: "Team Fortress", added: T },
    };

    it("is copied to the AI scope on the first read, and left in place", async () => {
      const { allow, store } = setup(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v1:allow", V1]]));
      expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(
        new Map([[10, V1["10"]], [20, V1["20"]]]),
      );
      expect(await scoped(allow, "all")).toStrictEqual(new Map());
      expect((await store.get(["v2:allow"])).get("v2:allow")).toStrictEqual({
        ...NO_GAMES,
        ai: V1,
      });
      expect((await store.get(["v1:allow"])).get("v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1);
    });

    it("is copied once: later changes go to v2 and the list is not copied again", async () => {
      const { allow, store } = setup(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v1:allow", V1]]));
      await allow.remove("ai", appId(10));
      expect([...(await scoped(allow, "ai")).keys()]).toStrictEqual([20]);
      expect([...(await scoped(createAllowList(store, fixedClock(T)), "ai")).keys()]).toStrictEqual(
        [20],
      );
    });

    it("keeps the entries it can read when part of the list is corrupt", async () => {
      const { allow } = setup(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v1:allow", { "10": V1["10"], "20": 7, "abc": V1["20"] }]]),
      );
      expect([...(await scoped(allow, "ai")).keys()]).toStrictEqual([10]);
    });

    it("adds to the AI scope after the copy and keeps the copied games", async () => {
      const { allow } = setup(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v1:allow", V1]]));
      await allow.add("ai", appId(30), "New");
      expect([...(await scoped(allow, "ai")).keys()].toSorted((a, b) => a - b)).toStrictEqual([
        10,
        20,
        30,
      ]);
    });
  });

  describe("invalid stored values", () => {
    it("discards a value that is not an object", async () => {
      for (const stored of ["x", 3, null, true, [["10", { name: "A", added: T }]]]) {
        const { allow } = setup(new Map([["v2:allow", stored]]));
        expect(await allow.list()).toStrictEqual(NO_ENTRIES);
      }
    });

    it("discards the entries of a scope that is not an object", async () => {
      const { allow } = setup(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v2:allow", {
          all: "x",
          ai: { "10": { name: "A", added: T } },
        }]]),
      );
      expect(await scoped(allow, "all")).toStrictEqual(new Map());
      expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(new Map([[10, { name: "A", added: T }]]));
    });

    it("drops invalid entries and keeps the valid ones", async () => {
      const { allow } = setup(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([[
          "v2:allow",
          {
            ai: {
              "10": { name: "Good", added: T },
              "20": { name: "No date" },
              "30": { name: 5, added: T },
              "40": "text",
              "50": null,
              "0": { name: "Zero", added: T },
              "-5": { name: "Negative", added: T },
              "abc": { name: "Not an ID", added: T },
              "1.5": { name: "Fraction", added: T },
              "4294967296": { name: "Too big", added: T },
            },
          },
        ]]),
      );
      expect(await scoped(allow, "ai")).toStrictEqual(
        new Map([[10, { name: "Good", added: T }]]),
      );
    });

    it("drops scopes it does not know", async () => {
      const { allow } = setup(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v2:allow", { future: { "10": { name: "A", added: T } } }]]),
      );
      expect(await allow.list()).toStrictEqual(NO_ENTRIES);
    });

    it("repairs the stored object on the next change", async () => {
      const { allow, store } = setup(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([[
          "v2:allow",
          { ai: { "10": { name: "Good", added: T }, "20": 7 }, future: { "5": 1 } },
        ]]),
      );
      await allow.add("ai", appId(30), "New");
      expect(await store.get(["v2:allow"])).toStrictEqual(
        new Map([[
          "v2:allow",
          {
            ...NO_GAMES,
            ai: { "10": { name: "Good", added: T }, "30": { name: "New", added: T } },
          },
        ]]),
      );
    });
  });
});
```

`src/core/settings/allow-list.ts`:

```ts
import type { Clock, KeyValueStore } from "../ports";
import { createSerial } from "../serial";
import { ALLOW_KEY } from "../storage-keys";
import type { AppId } from "../types";
import {
  type AllowEntries,
  type AllowEntry,
  type AllowScope,
  decodeAllow,
  encodeAllow,
} from "./allow-data";
import { readAllowValue } from "./migrate";

/** The games the user chose to ignore, per scope: one tag kind, or all kinds. */
export interface AllowList {
  /** The ignored games of every scope. */
  list(): Promise<AllowEntries>;
  /** Adds the game to the scope, or replaces its entry. */
  add(scope: AllowScope, id: AppId, name: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Removes the game from the scope; an ID that is not listed is ignored. */
  remove(scope: AllowScope, id: AppId): Promise<void>;
}

/**
 * The allow-list over a `KeyValueStore`, stored as `v2:allow`, an object per scope. Changes read
 * and write the whole object, one after another in this context, so two quick changes both apply;
 * two tabs at once can still lose one. A read copies a `v1:allow` list.
 */
export function createAllowList(store: KeyValueStore, clock: Clock): AllowList {
  async function read(): Promise<AllowEntries> {
    return decodeAllow(await readAllowValue(store));
  }

  async function write(entries: AllowEntries): Promise<void> {
    await store.set(new Map([[ALLOW_KEY, encodeAllow(entries)]]));
  }

  const serial = createSerial();

  function change(
    scope: AllowScope,
    update: (entries: Map<AppId, AllowEntry>) => boolean,
  ): Promise<void> {
    return serial(async () => {
      const entries = await read();
      const scoped = new Map(entries[scope]);
      if (update(scoped)) {
        await write({ ...entries, [scope]: scoped });
      }
    });
  }

  return {
    list: read,

    add: (scope, id, name) =>
      change(scope, (entries) => {
        entries.set(id, { name, added: clock.now() });
        return true;
      }),

    remove: (scope, id) => change(scope, (entries) => entries.delete(id)),
  };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { migrationContract } from "../../../tests/contracts/migration.contract";

/** The stored ignore list with no game in any scope. */

// What the version that stored layout v1 wrote: one flat settings object, and one object from app
// ID to name and date. `ARC` and `COURAGE` are two games the user ignored.

  badges: true,

  locale: "auto",
  debug: false,

  badges: false,
  banner: true,
  listFilter: "hide",
  locale: "es",
  debug: true,
};
const V1_ALLOW: JsonValue = { "1808500": ARC, "5072580": COURAGE };

async function stored(store: KeyValueStore, key: string): Promise<unknown> {
  return (await store.get([key])).get(key);
}

migrationContract("memory", () => memoryStore());

/** A store that logs its calls and runs `before(call)` ahead of the nth `get`, to interleave. */
function loggingStore(
  inner: KeyValueStore,
  log: string[],
  before: (getCall: number) => Promise<void> = () => Promise.resolve(),
): KeyValueStore {
  let gets = 0;
  return {
    async get(keys) {
      gets += 1;
      await before(gets);
      log.push(`get ${keys.join(",")}`);
      return inner.get(keys);
    },
    set(entries) {
      log.push(`set ${[...entries.keys()].join(",")}`);
      return inner.set(entries);
    },
    remove(keys) {
      log.push(`remove ${keys.join(",")}`);
      return inner.remove(keys);
    },
    keys: () => inner.keys(),
  };
}

/** The key lists of a store's `get` calls, in order. */
function keysRead(log: readonly string[]): readonly string[] {
  return log.filter((line) => line.startsWith("get ")).map((line) => line.slice("get ".length));
}

describe("migrateStorage", () => {
  it("checks, re-checks and verifies each key on its own, and never removes", async () => {
    const log: string[] = [];
    const inner = memoryStore(new Map([["v1:settings", V1_CUSTOM], ["v1:allow", V1_ALLOW]]));
    await migrateStorage(loggingStore(inner, log));
    expect(log).toStrictEqual([
      "get v2:settings",
      "get v1:settings",
      "get v2:settings",
      "set v2:settings",
      "get v2:settings",
      "get v2:allow",
      "get v1:allow",
      "get v2:allow",
      "set v2:allow",
      "get v2:allow",
    ]);
  });

  it("reads no v1 key where v2 holds a usable value", async () => {
    const log: string[] = [];
    const inner = memoryStore(
      new Map<string, JsonValue>([
        ["v2:settings", encodeSettings(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)],
        ["v2:allow", { all: {}, ai: {} }],
        ["v1:settings", V1_CUSTOM],
        ["v1:allow", V1_ALLOW],
      ]),
    );
    expect(await migrateStorage(loggingStore(inner, log))).toBe("current");
    expect(keysRead(log)).toStrictEqual(["v2:settings", "v2:allow"]);
  });

  it("skips a key that another context wrote after the first read", async () => {
    const log: string[] = [];
    const inner = memoryStore(new Map([["v1:settings", V1_CUSTOM], ["v1:allow", V1_ALLOW]]));
    const changed = encodeSettings(withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { banner: false }));
    // The user changes the v2 settings between this run's first read and its re-read.
    const store = loggingStore(inner, log, async (call) => {
      if (call === 3) {
        await inner.set(new Map([["v2:settings", changed]]));
      }
    });
    expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
    expect(await stored(inner, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(changed);
    expect(log).not.toContain("set v2:settings");

  });

  it("changes nothing when another context finished the whole migration meanwhile", async () => {
    const log: string[] = [];
    const inner = memoryStore(new Map([["v1:settings", V1_CUSTOM], ["v1:allow", V1_ALLOW]]));
    const store = loggingStore(inner, log, async (call) => {
      if (call === 3) {

      }

    expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
    expect(log.filter((line) => line.startsWith("set"))).toStrictEqual([]);
    expect(await stored(inner, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(settings);
  });

  it("agrees with itself when two contexts migrate at once", async () => {

    await Promise.all([migrateStorage(inner), migrateStorage(inner)]);
    expect(await stored(inner, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(
      encodeSettings(settingsFromV1(V1_CUSTOM)),
    );
    expect(await stored(inner, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(allowFromV1(V1_ALLOW));
    expect(await stored(inner, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_CUSTOM);
    expect(await stored(inner, "v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1_ALLOW);
  });
});
```
