`tests/contracts/key-value-store.contract.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { JsonValue } from "../../src/core/json";
import type { KeyValueStore } from "../../src/core/ports";

/**
 * The behavior every `KeyValueStore` must have (src/core/AGENTS.md, "The contract-test rule").
 * `make` returns a new, empty store for each case.
 */
export function keyValueStoreContract(
  name: string,
  make: () => KeyValueStore | Promise<KeyValueStore>,
): void {
  describe(`KeyValueStore contract: ${name}`, () => {
    it("returns nothing for keys that were never set", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      expect(await store.get(["a", "b"])).toStrictEqual(new Map());
      expect(await store.keys()).toStrictEqual([]);
    });

    it("returns what was set, for the requested keys only", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", { n: 1, list: ["x"] }], ["b", "two"], ["c", 3]]),
      );
      expect(await store.get(["a", "c", "missing"])).toStrictEqual(
        new Map<string, unknown>([["a", { n: 1, list: ["x"] }], ["c", 3]]),
      );
    });

    it("keeps falsy values apart from absent ones", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["null", null], ["false", false], ["zero", 0], ["empty", ""]]),
      );
      const got = await store.get(["null", "false", "zero", "empty"]);
      expect(got).toStrictEqual(
        new Map<string, unknown>([["null", null], ["false", false], ["zero", 0], ["empty", ""]]),
      );
    });

    it("replaces existing values", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", 1]]));
      await store.set(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", { replaced: true }]]));
      expect(await store.get(["a"])).toStrictEqual(new Map([["a", { replaced: true }]]));
    });

    it("removes keys and ignores keys that do not exist", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", 1], ["b", 2]]));
      await store.remove(["a", "missing"]);
      expect(await store.get(["a", "b"])).toStrictEqual(new Map([["b", 2]]));
      expect(await store.keys()).toStrictEqual(["b"]);
    });

    it("lists every stored key", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(
        new Map<string, JsonValue>([["v1:a:10", 1], ["v1:settings", {}], ["v1:meta", []]]),
      );
      expect([...(await store.keys())].sort()).toStrictEqual(["v1:a:10", "v1:meta", "v1:settings"]);
    });

    it("copies values in and out", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      const value = [1];
      await store.set(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", value]]));
      value.push(2);
      const first = (await store.get(["a"])).get("a");
      expect(Array.isArray(first)).toBe(true);
      if (Array.isArray(first)) {
        first.push(3);
      }
      expect(await store.get(["a"])).toStrictEqual(new Map([["a", [1]]]));
    });

    it("treats empty batches as no-ops", async () => {
      const store = await make();
      await store.set(new Map<string, JsonValue>([["a", 1]]));
      await store.set(new Map());
      await store.remove([]);
      expect(await store.get([])).toStrictEqual(new Map());
      expect(await store.keys()).toStrictEqual(["a"]);
    });
  });
}
```

`tests/contracts/migration-faults.contract.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { JsonValue } from "../../src/core/json";
import { perKind } from "../../src/core/kinds/registry";
import type { KeyValueStore } from "../../src/core/ports";
import { perScope } from "../../src/core/settings/allow-data";
import { migrateStorage } from "../../src/core/settings/migrate";
import { noFaults, type StorageFaults } from "../helpers/storage-faults";

const T = 1_000_000_000_000;
const V1_SETTINGS: JsonValue = {
  badges: false,
  banner: true,
  listFilter: "hide",
  locale: "es",
  debug: true,
};
const V1_ALLOW: JsonValue = { "1808500": { name: "ARC Raiders", added: T } };
const SETTINGS_V2 = {
  locale: "es",
  debug: true,
  kinds: {
    ...perKind(() => ({ enabled: true, badge: true, banner: true, filter: "off" })),
    pvp: { enabled: false, badge: true, banner: true, filter: "off" },
    ai: { enabled: true, badge: false, banner: true, filter: "hide" },
  },
};
const ALLOW_V2 = {
  ...perScope(() => ({})),
  ai: { "1808500": { name: "ARC Raiders", added: T } },
};

const MIGRATION_ERROR = { code: "error_settings_load" };

/**
 * What the migration does when the storage under a port fails, on the real port wrappers. `make`
 * returns a new, empty store whose layer reads the given faults.
 */
export function migrationFaultContract(
  name: string,
  make: (faults: StorageFaults) => KeyValueStore,
): void {
  describe(`migration fault contract: ${name}`, () => {
    async function seeded() {
      const faults = noFaults();
      const store = make(faults);
      await store.set(new Map([["v1:settings", V1_SETTINGS], ["v1:allow", V1_ALLOW]]));
      return { faults, store };
    }

    async function stored(store: KeyValueStore, key: string): Promise<unknown> {
      return (await store.get([key])).get(key);
    }

    async function expectV1Intact(store: KeyValueStore): Promise<void> {
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_SETTINGS);
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1_ALLOW);
    }

    it("copies the v1 keys and removes nothing, even where removing would fail", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.rejectRemove = true;
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
      await expectV1Intact(store);
    });

    it("keeps the settings copy when the ignore-list copy does not read back", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.dropWrites.add("v2:allow");
      await expect(migrateStorage(store)).rejects.toMatchObject(MIGRATION_ERROR);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toBeUndefined();
      await expectV1Intact(store);

      faults.dropWrites.clear();
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
    });

    it("keeps the ignore-list copy when the settings copy does not read back", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.dropWrites.add("v2:settings");
      await expect(migrateStorage(store)).rejects.toMatchObject(MIGRATION_ERROR);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toBeUndefined();
      await expectV1Intact(store);
    });

    it("accepts any usable v2 value on read-back, as another context may edit it", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      const other = { all: {}, ai: { "42": { name: "Written by another context", added: T } } };
      faults.replaceWrites.set("v2:allow", other);
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(other);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
    });

    it("fails on an unusable value, leaves it, and replaces it from v1 next time", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.replaceWrites.set("v2:allow", "garbage");
      await expect(migrateStorage(store)).rejects.toMatchObject(MIGRATION_ERROR);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toBe("garbage");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      await expectV1Intact(store);

      faults.replaceWrites.clear();
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
    });

    it("keeps the copy that landed when the next write rejects, and finishes later", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.rejectWrite = faults.writes + 2;
      await expect(migrateStorage(store)).rejects.toThrow();
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toBeUndefined();
      await expectV1Intact(store);

      faults.rejectWrite = undefined;
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(SETTINGS_V2);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
    });

    it("keeps the v1 data when the first write rejects, and copies the other key", async () => {
      const { faults, store } = await seeded();
      faults.rejectWrite = faults.writes + 1;
      await expect(migrateStorage(store)).rejects.toThrow();
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toBeUndefined();
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(ALLOW_V2);
      await expectV1Intact(store);
    });
  });
}
```

`tests/contracts/migration.contract.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { JsonValue } from "../../src/core/json";
import { perKind } from "../../src/core/kinds/registry";
import type { KeyValueStore } from "../../src/core/ports";
import { perScope } from "../../src/core/settings/allow-data";
import { allowFromV1, migrateStorage, settingsFromV1 } from "../../src/core/settings/migrate";
import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS, encodeSettings, parseSettings } from "../../src/core/settings/settings";
import { withKind } from "../../tests/helpers/settings";

const T = 1_000_000_000_000;

// What the version that stored layout v1 wrote: one flat settings object, and one object from app
// ID to name and date. `ARC` and `COURAGE` are two games the user ignored.
const ARC = { name: "ARC Raiders", added: T };
const COURAGE = { name: "Courage and Faith: Into the Dark Woods", added: T + 86_400_000 };

const V1_DEFAULTS: JsonValue = {
  badges: true,
  banner: true,
  listFilter: "off",
  locale: "auto",
  debug: false,
};
const V1_CUSTOM: JsonValue = {
  badges: false,
  banner: true,
  listFilter: "hide",
  locale: "es",
  debug: true,
};
const V1_ALLOW: JsonValue = { "1808500": ARC, "5072580": COURAGE };

const PLAIN_AI = { enabled: true, badge: true, banner: true, filter: "off" };
// PvP starts off.
const DEFAULT_KINDS = { ...perKind(() => PLAIN_AI), pvp: { ...PLAIN_AI, enabled: false } };
const CUSTOM_AI = { enabled: true, badge: false, banner: true, filter: "hide" };
/** The stored ignore list with no game in any scope. */
const NO_GAMES = perScope(() => ({}));

async function seed(
  store: KeyValueStore,
  entries: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue>>,
): Promise<void> {
  await store.set(new Map(Object.entries(entries)));
}

async function stored(store: KeyValueStore, key: string): Promise<unknown> {
  return (await store.get([key])).get(key);
}

/**
 * What the move from the v1 settings and ignore list to the v2 keys does on every storage port,
 * from realistic v1 samples: defaults, customized, partial, corrupt and empty. `make` returns a
 * new, empty store for each case.
 */
export function migrationContract(name: string, make: () => KeyValueStore): void {
  describe(`migration contract: ${name}`, () => {
    it("copies default v1 settings and an empty list to the v2 keys", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_DEFAULTS, "v1:allow": {} });
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual({
        locale: "auto",
        debug: false,
        kinds: DEFAULT_KINDS,
      });
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(NO_GAMES);
      expect([...(await store.keys())].toSorted()).toStrictEqual([
        "v1:allow",
        "v1:settings",
        "v2:allow",
        "v2:settings",
      ]);
    });

    it("maps customized v1 settings into the AI kind and keeps the global ones", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual({
        locale: "es",
        debug: true,
        kinds: { ...DEFAULT_KINDS, ai: CUSTOM_AI },
      });
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_CUSTOM);
    });

    it("puts every ignored game in the AI scope, and none in the scope for all kinds", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual({
        ...NO_GAMES,
        ai: { "1808500": ARC, "5072580": COURAGE },
      });
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1_ALLOW);
    });

    it("migrates a customized install as the settings read it", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM, "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect(parseSettings(await stored(store, "v2:settings"))).toStrictEqual(
        withKind({ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, locale: "es", debug: true }, "ai", {
          badge: false,
          filter: "hide",
        }),
      );
    });

    it("fills the fields a partial v1 object lacks with their defaults", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": { badges: false, locale: "es" } });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect(parseSettings(await stored(store, "v2:settings"))).toStrictEqual(
        withKind({ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, locale: "es" }, "ai", { badge: false }),
      );
    });

    it("falls back per field on corrupt v1 settings and drops corrupt list entries", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, {
        "v1:settings": { badges: "no", banner: false, listFilter: "blur", locale: "x y", debug: 1 },
        "v1:allow": {
          "1808500": ARC,
          "20": { name: "No date" },
          "abc": ARC,
          "5072580": "text",
        },
      });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect(parseSettings(await stored(store, "v2:settings"))).toStrictEqual(
        withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { banner: false }),
      );
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual({
        ...NO_GAMES,
        ai: { "1808500": ARC },
      });
    });

    it("turns values that are not objects into defaults and an empty list", async () => {
      for (const junk of ["garbage", 7, null, true, [], [V1_CUSTOM]]) {
        const store = make();
        await seed(store, { "v1:settings": junk, "v1:allow": junk });
        expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
        expect(parseSettings(await stored(store, "v2:settings"))).toStrictEqual(DEFAULT_SETTINGS);
        expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(NO_GAMES);
      }
    });

    it("writes nothing when the store holds no v1 data", async () => {
      const store = make();
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await store.keys()).toStrictEqual([]);
    });

    it("never removes a key", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM, "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      const before = [...(await store.keys())].toSorted();
      await migrateStorage(store);
      expect([...(await store.keys())]).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(before));
    });

    it("is idempotent: a second run changes nothing", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM, "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      const settings = await stored(store, "v2:settings");
      const allow = await stored(store, "v2:allow");
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(settings);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(allow);
    });

    it("keeps v2 data the user changed, and leaves the v1 keys as they are", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM, "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      const changed = encodeSettings(withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { banner: false }));
      await seed(store, { "v2:settings": changed, "v1:settings": V1_DEFAULTS });
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(changed);
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_DEFAULTS);
    });

    it("replaces a corrupt v2 value with the v1 data and keeps the v1 keys", async () => {
      for (const corrupt of ["garbage", 7, null, true, ["x"]]) {
        const store = make();
        await seed(store, {
          "v2:settings": corrupt,
          "v2:allow": corrupt,
          "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM,
          "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW,
        });
        expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
        expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(
          encodeSettings(settingsFromV1(V1_CUSTOM)),
        );
        expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual(allowFromV1(V1_ALLOW));
        expect(await stored(store, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_CUSTOM);
        expect(await stored(store, "v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1_ALLOW);
      }
    });

    it("leaves a corrupt v2 value alone when there is no v1 data to copy", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v2:settings": "garbage", "v2:allow": 7 });
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toBe("garbage");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toBe(7);
    });

    it("keeps a usable v2 value over any v1 value, even one that is mostly defaults", async () => {
      const store = make();
      await seed(store, { "v2:settings": {}, "v2:allow": {}, "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM });
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("current");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual({});
      expect(parseSettings(await stored(store, "v2:settings"))).toStrictEqual(DEFAULT_SETTINGS);
    });

    it("finishes a run that stopped after one key, converting only the missing one", async () => {
      const store = make();
      const done = encodeSettings(withKind(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "ai", { badge: false }));
      await seed(store, { "v2:settings": done, "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM, "v1:allow": V1_ALLOW });
      expect(await migrateStorage(store)).toBe("migrated");
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:settings")).toStrictEqual(done);
      expect(await stored(store, "v2:allow")).toStrictEqual({
        ...NO_GAMES,
        ai: { "1808500": ARC, "5072580": COURAGE },
      });
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:settings")).toStrictEqual(V1_CUSTOM);
      expect(await stored(store, "v1:allow")).toStrictEqual(V1_ALLOW);
    });

    it("leaves verdicts, the meta record and the breaker alone", async () => {
      const store = make();
      const others = {
        "v1:a:1808500": { time: T, kinds: { ai: { state: "not-disclosed", source: "api" } } },
        "v1:meta": { schema: 2, sweptAt: T },
        "v1:breaker": { openUntil: T },
      };
      await seed(store, { ...others, "v1:settings": V1_CUSTOM });
      await migrateStorage(store);
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(others)) {
        expect(await stored(store, key)).toStrictEqual(value);
      }
    });
  });
}
```

`tests/fixtures/README.md`:

```md
# Test fixtures

Captured from the live store on 2026-10-20 from a European location (prices in EUR). GetItems and app page captures were cookie-less (`credentials: "omit"`). Surface captures came from the live DOM; `wishlist/` and `search-suggestions/` needed a signed-in session, and no capture contains account data. Spike notes: `docs/research/steam-ai-disclosure/rq6-verification-spikes.md`. The tag kind fixtures (`getitems/kinds.json` and the four pages named in the app-page table) were captured the same way on 2026-10-24.

These files are data, not code we own: formatters and the line width rule skip `tests/fixtures/**`.

## Sanitizing

Every file was reduced before it was saved:

- Removed: `script`, `style`, `link`, `noscript`, `iframe`, `svg`, `template`, `video`, `object` and `embed` elements, comments, `on*` handler attributes, `srcset`, `data-props` (React mount payloads), `data-panel`, every `data-ds-*` attribute except `data-ds-appid`, `data-ds-packageid`, `data-ds-bundleid` and `data-ds-itemkey`, `#application_config`, session ID inputs, and anything matching `[class*="avatar"]` or `[data-miniprofile]`. No account names, avatars or Steam IDs remain (the captures were logged out).
- Trimmed: page chrome (global header, menus, footer, modals), media carousels, reviews, related items, language tables and the long tail of the "About this game" text. The app page structure around `#appHubAppName` and `.game_description_column` is kept as served.
- Whitespace: whitespace-only text nodes became a single newline, and runs of spaces and tabs in other text collapsed to one space, except inside `#game_area_content_descriptors`, which keeps the server's exact whitespace (the developer text starts with a newline and tabs).
- Encoding: every file is ASCII. JSON uses `\uXXXX` escapes; HTML uses numeric character references (`&#8217;`, `&#9;` for a tab). Both parse to the same strings as the original.
- GetItems JSON keeps every field Steam returned except the bulky ones listed per file below. Each fixture was checked byte for byte against a SHA-256 of the captured object.

## getitems/

Request shape: `GET https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1?input_json=...` with `data_request.include_extra_details: true`, keyless. Responses were 200 with `x-eresult: 1`.

| File | Request | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mixed-states.json` | 5072580, 1808500, 1938090, 413150, 339800, 99999999, 50300; `english`, `US` | Disclosed with `ai_generation_service` (5072580); disclosed without it (1808500, 1938090); not disclosed (413150); adult-only, `success: 1` with mature notes in `content_survey_notes` only (339800); invalid ID, `success: 15`, `appid: 0`, no `extra_details` (99999999); delisted, `unlisted: true` (50300). Removed: `related_items`, `best_purchase_option`, and the `extra_details` keys `system_requirements`, `early_access`, `partner_awards_bbcode`, `links_and_info`, `press_review`, `legal_notice_bbcode`, `eula`, `section`. |
| `german-context.json` | 1938090, 5072580; `german`, `DE` | 1938090 returns German notes; 5072580 (no translation) returns the English text. Same removals as above. |
| `search-roguelike-50.json` | The 50 rows of `/search/?term=roguelike`; `english`, `US` | 10 disclosed. Response order equals request order. Trimmed to the item keys `item_type`, `id`, `success`, `visible`, `name`, `appid`, `type`, `is_free`, `is_early_access`, `is_coming_soon`, `content_descriptorids`, `unlisted` and the `extra_details` keys `vetted`, `ai_generation_service`, `content_survey_ai_notes`. Notes include `\r\n` line breaks, trailing spaces and zero-width spaces (U+200B), kept verbatim. |
| `kinds.json` | 3751950, 2807960, 1808500, 813230, 730, 570, 105600, 1245620, 1172470, 271590, 1145360, 413150, 504230, 367520, 2379780, 620, package 320795, bundle 1, 99999999; `english`, `US` | One batch for the tag kinds (captured 2026-10-24). DRM, account and EULA (3751950); kernel anti-cheat with boot protection, no vendor name, account and EULA (2807960); kernel anti-cheat named Denuvo, EULA and AI notes (1808500); no declaration of any kind and no PvP category (813230, 1145360, 413150, 504230, 367520, 2379780, 620); non-kernel VAC anti-cheat (730, 570); PvP categories 49 and 36 (105600, 1245620, 1172470); kernel anti-cheat named Easy Anti-Cheat, account and EULA (1172470); delisted, kernel anti-cheat named BattlEye (271590); a package, which has `categories` and no `extra_details` (320795); a bundle and an ID that does not exist, `success: 15` with neither (1, 99999999). No item has `drm_activation_limit`. Removed: `related_items`, `best_purchase_option`, and the `extra_details` keys `system_requirements`, `early_access`, `partner_awards_bbcode`, `links_and_info`, `press_review`, `legal_notice_bbcode`, `section`; the `eula` links stay. |
| `empty-response.json` | `ids: []`, or a request without `context` | Steam answers 200 with this body; without `context` the `x-eresult` header is `8` (invalid parameter). |

## app-page/
```

```html
&#9;&#9;&#9;The game contains dark fantasy violence, combat involving weapons and supernatural creatures, descriptions of injuries and death, and scenes involving a cult. There is no sexual content or graphic gore.&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;</i>
```

```ts
import * as v from "valibot";
import { type AppId, AppIdSchema } from "../../src/core/types";

/** The values as app IDs. Throws on a value that is not one, so a typo fails the test. */
export function appIds(...values: readonly number[]): readonly AppId[] {
  return values.map((value) => v.parse(AppIdSchema, value));
}

/** The value as an app ID; throws when it is not one. */
export function appId(value: number): AppId {
  return v.parse(AppIdSchema, value);
}
```

`tests/helpers/counting-store.ts`:

```ts
import type { KeyValueStore } from "../../src/core/ports";

export interface CountingStore extends KeyValueStore {
  /** How many calls of each method the store has seen. */
  readonly calls: { get: number; set: number; remove: number; keys: number; };
  /** The keys of every `get` call, in order. */
  readonly gets: (readonly string[])[];
  /** Makes the next calls to `get` and `set` reject, until `heal()`. */
  break(): void;
  heal(): void;
}

/** Wraps a store and counts its calls, so tests can assert one `get` and one `set` per batch. */
export function countingStore(inner: KeyValueStore): CountingStore {
  const calls = { get: 0, set: 0, remove: 0, keys: 0 };
  const gets: (readonly string[])[] = [];
  let broken = false;
  return {
    calls,
    gets,
    break() {
      broken = true;
    },
    heal() {
      broken = false;
    },
    get(keys) {
      calls.get += 1;
      gets.push(keys);
      return broken ? Promise.reject(new Error()) : inner.get(keys);
    },
    set(entries) {
      calls.set += 1;
      return broken ? Promise.reject(new Error()) : inner.set(entries);
    },
    remove(keys) {
      calls.remove += 1;
      return inner.remove(keys);
    },
    keys() {
      calls.keys += 1;
      return inner.keys();
    },
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/dom-work.ts`:

```ts
import { vi } from "vitest";

/** DOM calls made while counting: a deterministic measure of scan cost, unlike wall-clock time. */
export interface DomWork {
  readonly querySelectorAll: number;
  /** Elements the `querySelectorAll` calls returned, summed. */
  readonly queried: number;
  readonly querySelector: number;
  readonly closest: number;
  readonly matches: number;
  /** `parentElement` reads: ancestor steps. */
  readonly parentSteps: number;
  readonly setAttribute: number;
  readonly removeAttribute: number;
}

/**
 * Starts counting DOM calls on every element (the spies call through). The returned function
 * reads the counts so far; vitest restores the spies after the test.
 */
export function countDomWork(): () => DomWork {
  const element = Element.prototype;
  const querySelectorAll = vi.spyOn(element, "querySelectorAll");
  const querySelector = vi.spyOn(element, "querySelector");
  const closest = vi.spyOn(element, "closest");
  const matches = vi.spyOn(element, "matches");
  const setAttribute = vi.spyOn(element, "setAttribute");
  const removeAttribute = vi.spyOn(element, "removeAttribute");
  const parentElement = vi.spyOn(Node.prototype, "parentElement", "get");
  return () => ({
    querySelectorAll: querySelectorAll.mock.calls.length,
    queried: querySelectorAll.mock.results.reduce(
      (sum, result) => sum + (result.type === "return" ? result.value.length : 0),
      0,
    ),
    querySelector: querySelector.mock.calls.length,
    closest: closest.mock.calls.length,
    matches: matches.mock.calls.length,
    parentSteps: parentElement.mock.calls.length,
    setAttribute: setAttribute.mock.calls.length,
    removeAttribute: removeAttribute.mock.calls.length,
  });
}
```

`tests/helpers/fake-area.ts`:

```ts
import type { JsonValue } from "../../src/core/json";
import type { StorageArea } from "../../src/platform/extension/ext";
import { failsWrite, type StorageFaults, storedValue } from "./storage-faults";

/** A typed `storage.local` fake that clones values in and out, as the browsers serialize them. */
export function fakeArea(): StorageArea & { readonly calls: string[]; } {
  const items = new Map<string, JsonValue>();
  const calls: string[] = [];
  return {
    calls,
    get(keys) {
      calls.push("get");
      const found: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      for (const [key, value] of items) {
        if (keys === null || keys.includes(key)) {
          found[key] = structuredClone(value);
        }
      }
      return Promise.resolve(found);
    },
    set(entries) {
      calls.push("set");
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(entries)) {
        items.set(key, structuredClone(value));
      }
      return Promise.resolve();
    },
    remove(keys) {
      calls.push("remove");
      for (const key of keys) {
        items.delete(key);
      }
      return Promise.resolve();
    },
  };
}

/** A `storage.local` fake that injects the given faults, for the migration's failure cases. */
export function faultyArea(faults: StorageFaults): StorageArea {
  const inner = fakeArea();
  return {
    get: (keys) => inner.get(keys),
    set(items) {
      if (failsWrite(faults)) {
        return Promise.reject(new Error());
      }
      const kept: Record<string, JsonValue> = {};
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(items)) {
        const stored = storedValue(faults, key, value);
        if (stored !== undefined) {
          kept[key] = stored;
        }
      }
      return inner.set(kept);
    },
    remove: (keys) => faults.rejectRemove ? Promise.reject(new Error()) : inner.remove(keys),
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/fake-detector.ts`:

```ts
import type { KindVerdicts } from "../../src/core/kinds/verdicts";
import type { Detector } from "../../src/core/ports";
import type { AppId } from "../../src/core/types";

export interface FakeDetector extends Detector {
  /** The IDs of every `detect` call, in order. */
  readonly calls: readonly (readonly AppId[])[];
}

/**
 * A `Detector` that answers each ID with `verdictsFor(id)` on a later microtask, so calls that are
 * not awaited overlap, and records what it was asked.
 */
export function fakeDetector(verdictsFor: (id: AppId) => KindVerdicts): FakeDetector {
  const calls: (readonly AppId[])[] = [];
  return {
    calls,
    async detect(ids) {
      calls.push(ids);
      await Promise.resolve();
      return new Map([...new Set(ids)].map((id): [AppId, KindVerdicts] => [id, verdictsFor(id)]));
    },
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/fake-http.ts`:

```ts
import type { Fetch } from "../../src/core/http";
import type { Http, HttpResult } from "../../src/core/ports";

/** What a fake server answers to one request. */
export type Reply =
  | {
    readonly status?: number;
    readonly body?: string;
    readonly headers?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    /** The final URL after redirects; the requested URL when absent. */
    readonly url?: string;
  }
  /** `fetch` rejects with a `TypeError`, as for a network failure or an answer without CORS. */
  | "network-error"
  /** The headers arrive, then reading the body fails. */
  | "body-error";

/** A URL prefix or pattern, and the reply (or a function of the requested URL giving it). */
export type Route = readonly [match: string | RegExp, reply: Reply | ((url: URL) => Reply)];

/** Unrouted URLs get this, like a server that has no such page. */
const NOT_FOUND: Reply = { status: 404 };

function replyFor(routes: readonly Route[], url: string): Reply {
  for (const [match, reply] of routes) {
    const hit = typeof match === "string" ? url.startsWith(match) : match.test(url);
    if (hit) {
      return typeof reply === "function" ? reply(new URL(url)) : reply;
    }
  }
  return NOT_FOUND;
}

function lowerCaseHeaders(headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): ReadonlyMap<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    Object.entries(headers).map(([name, value]): [string, string] => [name.toLowerCase(), value]),
  );
}

/** The `HttpResult` an `Http` gives for `reply` to a request for `url`. */
export function httpResult(reply: Reply, url: string): HttpResult {
  if (typeof reply === "string") {
    return { kind: "failed", cause: new TypeError() };
  }
  return {
    kind: "response",
    status: reply.status ?? 200,
    url: reply.url ?? url,
    headers: lowerCaseHeaders(reply.headers ?? {}),
    body: reply.body ?? "",
  };
}

export interface FakeHttp extends Http {
  /** Every requested URL, in order. */
  readonly calls: readonly string[];
  /** The most requests that were in flight at the same time. */
  readonly maxInFlight: number;
}

/** A fake `Http` answering from routes; the first matching route wins. */
export function fakeHttp(routes: readonly Route[]): FakeHttp {
  const calls: string[] = [];
  let inFlight = 0;
  let maxInFlight = 0;
  return {
    calls,
    get maxInFlight() {
      return maxInFlight;
    },
    async get(url) {
      calls.push(url);
      inFlight += 1;
      maxInFlight = Math.max(maxInFlight, inFlight);
      // Answer on a later microtask, so requests sent without awaiting overlap.
      await Promise.resolve();
      inFlight -= 1;
      return httpResult(replyFor(routes, url), url);
    },
  };
}

export interface FetchCall {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly init: RequestInit;
}

export interface FakeFetch {
  readonly fetch: Fetch;
  /** Every call, with the options it was made with. */
  readonly calls: readonly FetchCall[];
}

/** A fake `fetch` answering from the same routes, with real `Response` objects. */
export function fakeFetch(routes: readonly Route[]): FakeFetch {
  const calls: FetchCall[] = [];
  const fetch: Fetch = (url, init) => {
    calls.push({ url, init });
    const reply = replyFor(routes, url);
    if (reply === "network-error") {
      return Promise.reject(new TypeError());
    }
    if (reply === "body-error") {
      const response = new Response("");
      Object.defineProperty(response, "text", { value: () => Promise.reject(new TypeError()) });
      return Promise.resolve(response);
    }
    const { status = 200, body = "", headers = {} } = reply;
    const response = new Response(body, { status, headers });
    // A constructed Response has an empty `url`; a fetched one carries its final URL.
    Object.defineProperty(response, "url", { value: reply.url ?? url });
    return Promise.resolve(response);
  };
  return { fetch, calls };
}

```

`tests/helpers/fixed-clock.ts`:

```ts
import type { Clock } from "../../src/core/ports";

export interface FixedClock extends Clock {
  /** Moves the time forward by `ms`. */
  advance(ms: number): void;
  /** Sets the time to `t`, in milliseconds since the epoch. */
  set(t: number): void;
}

/** A `Clock` that stands still at `t` until a test moves it. */
export function fixedClock(t: number): FixedClock {
  let time = t;
  return {
    now: () => time,
    advance(ms) {
      time += ms;
    },
    set(next) {
      time = next;
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { parseAppPage } from "../../src/core/detect/app-page";
import { GETITEMS_URL, parseGetItems } from "../../src/core/detect/getitems";
import { KIND_IDS } from "../../src/core/kinds/id";
import { KINDS } from "../../src/core/kinds/registry";
import type { AnyDisclosed, KindVerdicts } from "../../src/core/kinds/verdicts";
import kinds from "../fixtures/getitems/kinds.json";
import { appId, appIds } from "./app-ids";
import { APP_PAGES, type AppPageName } from "./app-page";
import { httpResult } from "./fake-http";
import { fixtureItems, getItemsResponse } from "./getitems";

/** The apps of the batch captured for the tag kinds (tests/fixtures/README.md). */
const CAPTURED = [3751950, 2807960, 1808500, 813230, 730, 570, 105600, 1245620, 1172470, 271590];

const captured = parseGetItems(
  appIds(...CAPTURED),
  httpResult(getItemsResponse(fixtureItems(kinds)), GETITEMS_URL),
  "english",
);

/** The verdicts GetItems gave for an app of the captured kinds batch. Throws for any other. */
export function capturedVerdicts(id: number): KindVerdicts {
  const found = captured.get(appId(id));
  if (found === undefined) {
    throw new TypeError(String(id));
  }
  return found;
}

/** The verdicts read from a captured English app page, with the URL it was served from. */
export function pageVerdicts(name: AppPageName, id: number): KindVerdicts {
  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(APP_PAGES[name], "text/html");
  return parseAppPage(doc, `https://store.steampowered.com/app/${String(id)}/?l=english`);
}

/** The kinds a verdict list discloses, in registry order. */
export function disclosedIds(verdicts: KindVerdicts): readonly string[] {
  return KIND_IDS.filter((id) => verdicts[id].state === "disclosed");
}

/** The disclosed verdicts of every kind, in registry order, as the banner lists them. */
export function disclosedList(verdicts: KindVerdicts): readonly AnyDisclosed[] {
  return KINDS.flatMap((kind) => {
    const verdict = verdicts[kind.id];
    return verdict.state === "disclosed" ? [verdict] : [];
  });
}
```

`tests/helpers/getitems.ts`:

```ts
import * as v from "valibot";
import { GETITEMS_URL } from "../../src/core/detect/getitems";
import {
  type ExtraDetails,
  type StoreItem,
  StoreItemSchema,
} from "../../src/core/detect/getitems.schema";
import type { SteamLanguage } from "../../src/core/i18n/locale";
import { parseJson } from "../../src/core/json";
import type { KindDefinition } from "../../src/core/kinds/kind";
import { type AppId, AppIdSchema, type DisclosedBase, type Verdict } from "../../src/core/types";
import type { Reply, Route } from "./fake-http";

/** A plain store item as GetItems returns it: listed, `success: 1`, no AI notes. */
export function storeItem(
  id: number,
  overrides: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> = {},
): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
  return {
    item_type: 0,
    id,
    success: 1,
    visible: true,
    name: `App ${String(id)}`,
    appid: id,
    type: 0,
    extra_details: { vetted: true },
    ...overrides,
  };
}

/** A store item whose developer disclosed AI use with these notes. */
export function disclosedItem(
  id: number,
  notes: string,
  service?: string,
): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
  return storeItem(id, {
    extra_details: {
      vetted: true,
      content_survey_ai_notes: notes,
      ...(service === undefined ? {} : { ai_generation_service: { name: service, url: "" } }),
    },
  });
}

/** What GetItems answers for an invalid ID (rq6, S2). */
export function invalidItem(id: number): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
  return { item_type: 0, id, success: 15, visible: false, name: "", appid: 0 };
}

export interface ResponseOptions {
  readonly status?: number;
  /** The `x-eresult` header; `null` leaves it out. Default `1`. */
  readonly eresult?: string | null;
}

/**
 * A GetItems reply holding `items`, or a body without `store_items` when `items` is undefined
 * (what Steam sends for an empty or context-less request).
 */
export function getItemsResponse(
  items: readonly unknown[] | undefined,
  options: ResponseOptions = {},
): Reply {
  const { status = 200, eresult = "1" } = options;
  const response = items === undefined ? {} : { store_items: items };
  return {
    status,
    body: JSON.stringify({ response }),
    headers: eresult === null ? {} : { "x-eresult": eresult },
  };
}

const RequestSchema = v.object({
  ids: v.array(v.object({ appid: v.number() })),
  context: v.object({ language: v.string() }),
});

export interface GetItemsRequest {
  readonly ids: readonly number[];
  readonly language: string;
}

/** The IDs and language a GetItems URL asks for. Throws when the URL is not one. */
export function getItemsRequest(url: URL | string): GetItemsRequest {
  const input = new URL(url).searchParams.get("input_json") ?? "";
  const request = v.parse(RequestSchema, parseJson(input));
  return { ids: request.ids.map(({ appid }) => appid), language: request.context.language };
}

const ItemIdSchema = v.looseObject({ id: AppIdSchema });

/** The `id` of each item. Throws on an item without a valid one. */
export function itemIds(items: readonly unknown[]): readonly AppId[] {
  return items.map((item) => v.parse(ItemIdSchema, item).id);
}

/**
 * A route that answers GetItems from a pool of items, in request order, the way Steam does.
 * Requested IDs absent from the pool get no item. `items` may be fixture JSON.
 */
export function getItemsRoute(items: readonly unknown[], options: ResponseOptions = {}): Route {
  const pool = new Map<number, unknown>();
  for (const item of items) {
    pool.set(v.parse(ItemIdSchema, item).id, item);
  }
  return [GETITEMS_URL, (url) => {
    const found = getItemsRequest(url).ids.flatMap((id) => {
      const item = pool.get(id);
      return item === undefined ? [] : [item];
    });
    return getItemsResponse(found, options);
  }];
}

const FixtureSchema = v.object({
  response: v.object({ store_items: v.exactOptional(v.array(v.unknown())) }),
});

/** The `store_items` of a GetItems fixture. */
export function fixtureItems(fixture: unknown): readonly unknown[] {
  return v.parse(FixtureSchema, fixture).response.store_items ?? [];
}

/** A store item and its extra details, as the schema parses them. */
export interface ParsedItem {
  readonly item: StoreItem;
  readonly details: ExtraDetails;
}

/**
 * Parses a plain store item with these extra details through the real schema, after a JSON round
 * trip like a response body, so a kind sees what it sees in production. `overrides` replace item
 * keys such as `name` or `categories`; an undefined value leaves the key out.
 */
export function parsedItem(
  details: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> = {},
  overrides: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> = {},
): ParsedItem {
  const body = JSON.stringify(storeItem(1, { extra_details: details, ...overrides }));
  const item = v.parse(StoreItemSchema, parseJson(body));
  if (item.extra_details === undefined) {
    throw new TypeError();
  }
  return { item, details: item.extra_details };
}

/** What a kind answers for a store item with these extra details (see `parsedItem`). */
export function verdictOf<Disclosed extends DisclosedBase>(
  kind: KindDefinition<Disclosed>,
  details: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> = {},
  overrides: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> = {},
  language: SteamLanguage = "english",
): Verdict<Disclosed> {
  const parsed = parsedItem(details, overrides);
  return kind.fromGetItems(parsed.item, parsed.details, language);
}

const ItemRecordSchema = v.record(v.string(), v.unknown());

/**
 * The item of a GetItems fixture for the app `from`, as another app: the same name, categories
 * and extra details under the ID `to`. Throws when the fixture has no such item.
 */
export function itemAs(
  fixture: unknown,
  from: number,
  to: number,
): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
  const found = fixtureItems(fixture).find((item) => v.parse(ItemIdSchema, item).id === from);
  return { ...v.parse(ItemRecordSchema, found), id: to, appid: to };
}
```

`tests/helpers/gm-fake.ts`:

```ts
import { type JsonValue, parseJson } from "../../src/core/json";
import type { GmStorage } from "../../src/platform/userscript/gm-storage";
import { failsWrite, type StorageFaults, storedValue } from "./storage-faults";

export interface FakeGm extends GmStorage {
  /** The `GM.setValue` calls, in order. */
  readonly writes: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * A typed fake of the `GM` storage calls. Like the managers, it stores serialized values: what
 * goes in and out is a copy, and a name with no value reads as `undefined`.
 */
export function fakeGm(): FakeGm {
  const values = new Map<string, string>();
  const writes: string[] = [];
  return {
    writes,
    getValue(name) {
      const text = values.get(name);
      // The managers serialize values as JSON, so reading one back is a parse
      return Promise.resolve(text === undefined ? undefined : parseJson(text));
    },
    setValue(name: string, value: JsonValue) {
      writes.push(name);
      values.set(name, JSON.stringify(value));
      return Promise.resolve();
    },
    deleteValue(name) {
      values.delete(name);
      return Promise.resolve();
    },
    listValues() {
      return Promise.resolve([...values.keys()]);
    },
  };
}

/** A GM fake that injects the given faults. Each `setValue` is one write, as in the managers. */
export function faultyGm(faults: StorageFaults): GmStorage {
  const inner = fakeGm();
  return {
    getValue: (name) => inner.getValue(name),
    setValue(name, value) {
      if (failsWrite(faults)) {
        return Promise.reject(new Error());
      }
      const stored = storedValue(faults, name, value);
      return stored === undefined ? Promise.resolve() : inner.setValue(name, stored);
    },
    deleteValue: (name) =>
      faults.rejectRemove ? Promise.reject(new Error()) : inner.deleteValue(name),
    listValues: () => inner.listValues(),
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/helpers.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { LIST_FILTERS } from "../../src/core/kinds/kind-settings";
import { httpContract } from "../contracts/http.contract";
import { keyValueStoreContract } from "../contracts/key-value-store.contract";
import { fakeHttp } from "./fake-http";
import { fixedClock } from "./fixed-clock";
import { memoryStore } from "./memory-store";
import { strongestFilter } from "./settings";

keyValueStoreContract("memoryStore", () => memoryStore());
httpContract("fakeHttp", fakeHttp);

describe("memoryStore", () => {
  it("starts from initial values", async () => {
    const store = memoryStore(new Map([["v1:settings", { badges: true }]]));
    expect(await store.get(["v1:settings"])).toStrictEqual(
      new Map([["v1:settings", { badges: true }]]),
    );
  });
});

describe("fakeHttp", () => {
  it("records calls and answers unrouted URLs with 404", async () => {
    const http = fakeHttp([]);
    const got = await http.get("https://store.steampowered.com/nothing");
    expect(got.kind === "response" ? got.status : undefined).toBe(404);
    expect(http.calls).toStrictEqual(["https://store.steampowered.com/nothing"]);
  });

  it("counts overlapping requests", async () => {
    const http = fakeHttp([]);
    await Promise.all([http.get("https://a.test/"), http.get("https://b.test/")]);
    expect(http.maxInFlight).toBe(2);
  });
});

describe("fixedClock", () => {
  it("stands still until moved", () => {
    const clock = fixedClock(1_000);
    expect(clock.now()).toBe(1_000);
    clock.advance(500);
    expect(clock.now()).toBe(1_500);
    clock.set(10);
    expect(clock.now()).toBe(10);
  });
});

describe("strongestFilter", () => {
  it("is off for no kind at all", () => {
    expect(strongestFilter([])).toBe("off");
  });

  it.each(LIST_FILTERS)("is %s for a single %s", (mode) => {
    expect(strongestFilter([mode])).toBe(mode);
  });

  it("lets hide win over dim over off, whatever the order", () => {
    expect(strongestFilter(["dim", "hide", "off"])).toBe("hide");
    expect(strongestFilter(["hide", "off", "dim"])).toBe("hide");
    expect(strongestFilter(["off", "off", "dim", "off"])).toBe("dim");
    expect(strongestFilter(new Set<"off" | "dim" | "hide">(["dim", "off"]))).toBe("dim");
  });
});
```

`tests/helpers/host-view.ts`:

```ts
import type { AiVerdict } from "../../src/core/kinds/ai";
import type { KindId } from "../../src/core/kinds/id";
import { perKind } from "../../src/core/kinds/registry";
import type { KindVerdicts } from "../../src/core/kinds/verdicts";
import type { BadgeSlot, HostView } from "../../src/core/ui/host";
import { aiVerdicts, disclosedVerdict } from "./verdicts";

export interface HostViewOptions {
  /** The AI kind's verdict; disclosed unless a test says otherwise. */
  readonly verdict?: AiVerdict;
  /** Every kind's verdict, instead of the AI verdict and nothing else known. */
  readonly verdicts?: KindVerdicts;
  /** Whether the game is on the allow-list, for every kind. */
  readonly allowed?: boolean;
  /** Kinds the game is ignored for, whatever `allowed` says. */
  readonly ignored?: readonly KindId[];
  /** Kinds whose badges are switched off in the settings. */
  readonly unbadged?: readonly KindId[];
  /** Chips the placement shows before the "+N" chip. */
  readonly maxChips?: number;
  readonly slot?: BadgeSlot | undefined;
  readonly hideable?: boolean;
}

/** Chips a view shows before the "+N" chip unless a test says otherwise. */
export const MAX_CHIPS = 3;

/** What a renderer receives for one host, with the AI kind's verdict and nothing else known. */
export function hostView(host: Element, options: HostViewOptions = {}): HostView {
  const { verdict = disclosedVerdict(), allowed = false, ignored = [] } = options;
  const { slot, hideable = true, verdicts = aiVerdicts(verdict) } = options;
  const { unbadged = [], maxChips = MAX_CHIPS } = options;
  return {
    host,
    verdicts,
    allowed: perKind((kind) => allowed || ignored.includes(kind.id)),
    badged: perKind((kind) => !unbadged.includes(kind.id)),
    maxChips,
    slot,
    hideable,
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/recording-renderer.ts`:

```ts
import type { CapsuleRenderer, ScanBatch } from "../../src/core/scan/renderer";

export interface RecordingRenderer extends CapsuleRenderer {
  /** Every batch the scanner sent, in order. */
  readonly batches: ScanBatch[];
}

/**
 * A renderer that records batches. With `badges`, it also does what a real renderer must: it puts
 * one `span.sar-badge` into each found or changed host's anchor unless the host already has one.
 */
export function recordingRenderer(options: { readonly badges?: boolean; } = {}): RecordingRenderer {
  const batches: ScanBatch[] = [];
  return {
    batches,
    render(batch) {
      batches.push(batch);
      if (options.badges !== true) {
        return;
      }
      for (const host of [...batch.found, ...batch.changed]) {
        if (host.element.querySelector(".sar-badge") === null) {
          const badge = document.createElement("span");
          badge.className = "sar-badge";
          host.anchor.append(badge);
        }
      }
    },
  };
}
```

`tests/helpers/settings.ts`:

```ts
import type { KindId } from "../../src/core/kinds/id";
import {
  type KindSettings,
  LIST_FILTERS,
  type ListFilter,
} from "../../src/core/kinds/kind-settings";
import { KINDS } from "../../src/core/kinds/registry";
import { applyPatch, type Settings, type SettingsPatch } from "../../src/core/settings/settings";
import type { StoredSettings } from "../../src/core/settings/settings-source";

/** The settings with `patch` applied to one kind's settings. */
export function withKind(settings: Settings, id: KindId, patch: Partial<KindSettings>): Settings {
  return applyPatch(settings, { kinds: { [id]: patch } });
}

/**
 * A patch that names every field, so applying it sets the settings to exactly `settings`. An unset
 * color is named as `undefined`, which clears a stored one.
 */
function wholePatch(settings: Settings): SettingsPatch {
  return {
    locale: settings.locale,
    debug: settings.debug,
    kinds: Object.fromEntries(
      KINDS.map((kind) => {
        const own = settings.kinds[kind.id];
        return [kind.id, { ...own, color: own.color }];
      }),
    ),
  };
}

/** Stores exactly these settings, telling the source's subscribers, as another tab's save does. */
export function writeSettings(source: StoredSettings, settings: Settings): Promise<Settings> {
  return source.patch(wholePatch(settings));
}

/**
 * The mode that wins when several kinds match one host: hide over dim over off. The style rules
 * reach the same result without a function, because a hidden host ignores a dim and a host that
 * cannot hide dims for both, so tests use this as their oracle.
 */
export function strongestFilter(modes: Iterable<ListFilter>): ListFilter {
  let strongest: ListFilter = "off";
  for (const mode of modes) {
    if (LIST_FILTERS.indexOf(mode) > LIST_FILTERS.indexOf(strongest)) {
      strongest = mode;
    }
  }
  return strongest;
}

```

`tests/helpers/storage-faults.ts`:

```ts
import type { JsonValue } from "../../src/core/json";

/**
 * Faults that a storage layer under a `KeyValueStore` injects. A test sets them after seeding the
 * store, and the layer reads them on every call.
 */
export interface StorageFaults {
  /** The write calls so far: an area `set`, or a GM `setValue`. */
  writes: number;
  /** Keys the layer accepts and does not store. */
  readonly dropWrites: Set<string>;
  /** Keys the layer stores with another value than the one written. */
  readonly replaceWrites: Map<string, JsonValue>;
  /** The write call with this number rejects without storing. */
  rejectWrite: number | undefined;
  /** Removing rejects. */
  rejectRemove: boolean;
}

export function noFaults(): StorageFaults {
  return {
    writes: 0,
    dropWrites: new Set(),
    replaceWrites: new Map(),
    rejectWrite: undefined,
    rejectRemove: false,
  };
}

/** Counts a write call. Returns whether it rejects. */
export function failsWrite(faults: StorageFaults): boolean {
  faults.writes += 1;
  return faults.rejectWrite === faults.writes;
}

/** What the layer stores for a write of `value` to `key`; undefined when it drops the key. */
export function storedValue(
  faults: StorageFaults,
  key: string,
  value: JsonValue,
): JsonValue | undefined {
  return faults.dropWrites.has(key) ? undefined : faults.replaceWrites.get(key) ?? value;
}
```

```ts
/** Replaces the global document's head and body with those of `html`. */
export function loadPage(html: string): void {
  const parsed = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html");
  document.head.replaceChildren(...parsed.head.childNodes);
  document.body.replaceChildren(...parsed.body.childNodes);
}

/** The nodes `markup` parses to, as a body's children. */
export function nodes(markup: string): readonly Node[] {
  return [...new DOMParser().parseFromString(markup, "text/html").body.childNodes];
}

/** Replaces the global document's body with `markup`. */
export function setBody(markup: string): void {
  document.body.replaceChildren(...nodes(markup));
}

/** The element `selector` matches, failing the test when there is none. */
export function the(selector: string, root: ParentNode = document): Element {
  const element = root.querySelector(selector);
  if (element === null) {
    throw new TypeError(selector);
  }
  return element;
}
```

```ts
import type { AccountDisclosed } from "../../src/core/kinds/account";
import type { AiDisclosed, AiVerdict } from "../../src/core/kinds/ai";
import type { AnticheatDisclosed } from "../../src/core/kinds/anticheat";
import type { DrmDisclosed } from "../../src/core/kinds/drm";
import { type EulaDisclosed, eulaLink, type EulaUrl } from "../../src/core/kinds/eula";

/** The link of a EULA entry, when the address is one the store hosts. */
function linked(address: string): { readonly url?: EulaUrl; } {
  const url = eulaLink(address);
  return url === undefined ? {} : { url };
}

/** A disclosed verdict with the optional fields filled in; override what a test cares about. */
export function disclosedVerdict(overrides: Partial<AiDisclosed> = {}): AiDisclosed {
  return {
    state: "disclosed",
    kind: "ai",

/** An app's verdicts where the AI kind has this verdict and no other kind has an answer. */
export function aiVerdicts(ai: AiVerdict): KindVerdicts {
  return { ...UNKNOWN_KINDS.missing, ai };
}

interface FullDisclosed {
  readonly ai: AiDisclosed;
  readonly kernel: KernelDisclosed;
  readonly anticheat: AnticheatDisclosed;
  readonly drm: DrmDisclosed;
  readonly account: AccountDisclosed;
  readonly eula: EulaDisclosed;
  readonly pvp: PvpDisclosed;
}

/** Each kind's disclosed verdict, with every field of its payload set. */
export const FULL_DISCLOSED: FullDisclosed = {
  ai: disclosedVerdict(),
  kernel: {
    state: "disclosed",
    kind: "kernel",
    source: "api",
    name: "Easy Anti-Cheat",
    nameToken: "#Store_AntiCheat_Type_easyac",
    uninstallsCompletely: true,
    bootProtection: { token: "secureboot_tpm2" },
  },
  anticheat: {
    state: "disclosed",
    kind: "anticheat",
    source: "api",
    name: "VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat)",
    nameToken: "#Store_AntiCheat_Type_vac",
  },
  drm: {
    state: "disclosed",
    kind: "drm",
    source: "api",
    text: "Denuvo Anti-tamper",
    activationLimit: "5 a day",
  },
  account: {
    state: "disclosed",
    kind: "account",
    source: "api",
    text: "Ubisoft Account",
    linksToSteam: true,
  },
  eula: {

    kind: "eula",
    source: "api",
    items: [
      { name: "Game EULA", ...linked("https://store.steampowered.com/eula/1_eula_0") },
      { name: "Publisher terms" },
    ],
  },
  pvp: { state: "disclosed", kind: "pvp", source: "api", categoryIds: [49, 36] },
};

/** Every kind in the same state, so a test sees the TTL or the storage of that state alone. */
export function uniformVerdicts(
  state: "disclosed" | "not-disclosed" | UnknownReason,
): KindVerdicts {
  if (state === "disclosed") {
    return FULL_DISCLOSED;
  }
  return state === "not-disclosed" ? perKind(() => NOT_DISCLOSED) : UNKNOWN_KINDS[state];
}

/** The kinds in `kinds` disclosed with a full payload, every other kind not disclosed. */
export function disclosedKinds(kinds: readonly KindId[]): KindVerdicts {
  const pick = <T>(id: KindId, verdict: T) => kinds.includes(id) ? verdict : NOT_DISCLOSED;
  return {
    ai: pick("ai", FULL_DISCLOSED.ai),
    kernel: pick("kernel", FULL_DISCLOSED.kernel),
    anticheat: pick("anticheat", FULL_DISCLOSED.anticheat),
    drm: pick("drm", FULL_DISCLOSED.drm),
    account: pick("account", FULL_DISCLOSED.account),
    eula: pick("eula", FULL_DISCLOSED.eula),
    pvp: pick("pvp", FULL_DISCLOSED.pvp),
  };
}
```
